units.la: DAVID PAREVS S.
units.tr: DAVID PAREUS, GREETINGS

units.la: CEssi tandem flagitationibus amicorum, qui me obtundere per literas & coram non destiterunt, ut explicationes cate-chet[?]icas D. Zachariæ Vrsini, felicis memoriæ, præceptoris mei colendi, in hac scho-la olim à discipulis exceptas, ac post obitum eius diversis locis evulgatas, in ecclesiæ usum retexerem. Quere-bantur enim, editiones alias, studio quidem non malo, adornatas, sed ita tamen non magno satis iudicio videri consarcinatas, passimque sententiis & verbis vel hiantes, vel redundantes, vel depravatas, ut vix summa vestigia Vrsinianæ illius ἀνομοιότητος[?] in iis apparerent, opusque ipsum tyrone magis, quàm tanto dignum Theologo videretur. Ac versari illud quidem in manibus multorum, sed suo iudicio, non satis magna cum authoris laude, ac legentium fructu. Spondebant etiam illi, molestiam me
units.tr: At last I have yielded to the entreaties of friends, who did not cease to pester me by letter and in person, that I should bring out for the use of the Church the catechetical explanations of Dr. Zacharias Ursinus, of happy memory, my revered teacher. These were once taken down by his students in this school, and after his death were published in various places. My friends complained that the other editions, prepared with no ill intent, seemed to have been patched together without much judgement, and that in them the sense and the words were everywhere either gapped, or swollen, or corrupted, so that scarcely any trace of that Ursinian manner was visible in them, and the work seemed fitter for a beginner than for so great a theologian. The book was indeed in many people's hands, but in their judgement it brought neither great credit to the author nor much profit to its readers. They also promised that the trouble I would take would not be heavy, since the task called only for arrangement, not for the discovery of new matter; and they said that I knew Ursinus's manner thoroughly, and besides that I was now lecturing on this same catechism in the same school.

units.la: subiturum non grauem: quandoquidem digestione tan- tum, non noua rerum inuentione opus foret : ego vero & Vrsinianā probe perspecta haberem, & alioqui nunc in eadem schola Catech tica ista tractare. Sic igitur ad laborem illi me induxerunt. Et ipse quidem initio leuiter eo me defunct urum exist imaban. Sed certe in progressu l nge is meam & aliorum opinionem superauit, ac saepe optaslem de meo potius aliquid commentari, quam alienum aurum quasi ex luto eruere. Accesserunt molestiae aliae, quae parum abfuit, quin laborem, iam pene absoluti m mihi e manib. excuterent. Quia vero semel me amicis obstrinxeram, quiduis deuorare malui, quam fidem non liberare.
units.tr: So they persuaded me to take up the labour. At first I myself thought I would finish it lightly. But in the course of the work it far outstripped both my expectation and that of others, and I often wished that I had rather written something of my own than dug up another's gold, as it were, out of mud. Other troubles came too, which very nearly wrested the work from my hands when it was almost finished. But since I had once bound myself to my friends, I preferred to swallow anything rather than fail to keep my word.

units.la: Nunc, quam secutus sim rationem, propter eos breuiter est indicandum, quibus familiare est quoutis modo aliena carpere. Adhibui & contuli exemplaria nō pauca, sed eas cum primis notas, quas ipsemet olim per annos fere sex exceperam, quasi pro Cynosura habui, quoniam has tutius sequi potui. In locorum explicatione quaestionum numerum & ordinem non unum semper, sed aliis annis alij proposuisse, omnes discipuli eius norunt. Itaque in eo secutus sum, quod methodo rerum magis conuenire est visum. Norunt quoque dictionem eam, quae in exemplaribus circumfertur, magna ex parte Vrsinianam non esse. Sed cum vel submissius vel in diuiutationum feruore concitatius diceret, inter festinandum quisque, suis fere verbis, dictorum summas celeri calamo excepit, vel certe, vt potuit, praeceptoris orationem interpolauit. Postea pro Vrsinianis omnia descripta & sparsa sunt. Ego taq. verbis vulgo exceptis minime me adstrinxi: sed satis habui, sententias mentemque authoris simplici, proprio ac tali sermone, qui ad ipsius stylum accederet quam proxime fideliter explicare: retentis interim atque expressis vbique, quatum fieri potuit, terminis, phrasibus, ac idiotismis ipsi consuetis: in obiectionibus vero etiam rectè eftenfis solutionum fontibus ac neruis, quibus ille breuibus, & ad artis normas accommodatis delectabatur, & vtebatur felicissime. Denique sic singula digessi v: sperem, commentarios hoc catecheticos satis a barbarie & consu[?]ione vindicatos:id quod collatio istorum cum aliis, ut confido,ostendet.
units.tr: Now, the method I have followed must be briefly explained, for the sake of those who are accustomed to carp at the work of others in any way. I consulted and compared not a few copies, but above all I held as my Cynosure the notes which I myself had taken down over nearly six years under him; these I could follow more safely. As to the explanation of the places, all his students know that he did not always propose the number and order of the questions in the same way, but in different years differently. So I followed what seemed better suited to the method of the subject. They also know that the wording which circulates in the copies is for the most part not Ursinus's. When he spoke either rather quietly, or more vehemently in the heat of disputation, each student, while hurrying, took down the gist of what was said in a rapid hand, usually in his own words; or at any rate, as best he could, he reshaped the teacher's speech. Afterwards everything was copied out and scattered about as if it were Ursinus's. I, for my part, did not bind myself at all to the words commonly taken down. It was enough for me to set out the opinions and mind of the author, as faithfully as possible, in a plain, my own and suitable style that comes as close as possible to his own manner; while retaining and expressing everywhere, as far as could be done, the terms, phrases and idioms customary to him. In the objections, moreover, I have also brought out the sources and sinews of the solutions, correctly stated, in which he took delight, and which he used most happily, being brief and suited to the rules of the art. Finally, I have arranged each thing in this way, so that I hope these catechetical commentaries will be seen to be sufficiently freed from barbarism and confusion; as I trust the comparison of these with others will show.

units.la: Eos vero tum cæteris S.S.Theologiæ studiosis, tũ vobis cum primis, Discipuli carissimi, legendos, terendos, ac familiariter cognoscendos commendo. Etenim in ea vos nunc schola versamini,in qua illi olim sunt nati. Vos in eorum successistis locum, quibus illi olim tradi-ti,propriiq.dicati fuerunt. Ad vos igitur iure quasi hœre-ditario pertinent. Per vos illi vestramque diligentiam ad familiam & fundos auitos redibunt, domisque quasi consenescent. Optatis,ni fallor,omnes,magno illo VR-SINO, ut vobis ut præceptore licuerit. En vos, per me, voti compotes. VRSINVM enim exhibeo,nō quidem seuerum illum,qualis in hac schola fuit,disciplinę vindi-cem,morumque ac vitæ informatorem : sed accuratum ac fidum Catecheten, à quo rudimenta pietatis dextrè accipiatis:sed διδακτικὸν[?]& magnum ac sincerum Theologum, à quo præcipua veræ Theologiæ monimenta methodo comprehendere, & recte secare λόγον[?] discatis:sed acutum & breuem disputatorem, à quo verum Logicæ vsum in retexendis & dissoluendis aduersariorum argutiis petere valeatis. Habent magni commenta-rii suam laudem & vsum. Vobis ego hæc catechetica comprimis commendo,dum ad [illegible, ~8 letters] veniatis, in qua ipsa eriam horum vsum recte experieminiac scitote amicis ita me gratificatum esse, ut magis tamen vobis prodesse voluerim. Hæc tradam, & hæc à vobis reposcam. Est quidem, ut Aristot.ait, [illegible, ~10 letters] sed placet hic Socraticum illud, [illegible, ~8 letters] quod & Apostolo non displicuit dicenti: Eadem scribere vobis me quidem haud piget, vobis autem est tutum.
units.tr: I commend them to be read, used and thoroughly known, both to the other students of Holy Theology and above all to you, my dearest students. For you are now living in the same school in which they were born. You have taken the place of those to whom they were once handed down and to whom they were properly dedicated. They therefore belong to you, as if by hereditary right. Through you they will return to their family and ancestral estates, and grow old there as in their own home. I think you all wish, unless I am mistaken, for that great Ursinus, so that you might have him as your teacher. See, through me, you have your wish: for I present Ursinus to you, not that stern figure who was here in this school, the guardian of discipline and the moulder of morals and life; but a careful and faithful catechist, from whom you may receive the rudiments of piety properly; a teacher, and a great and sincere theologian, from whom you may learn to grasp the chief monuments of true theology by method and to divide the word rightly; and a sharp and brief disputant, from whom you may draw the true use of logic in unravelling and dissolving the subtleties of opponents. Great commentaries have their own praise and use. To you I commend these catechetical writings above all, while you come to [illegible] in which very place you may also test the use of these rightly; and know that I have so obliged my friends, yet have wished rather to be of service to you. I shall hand these on, and these I shall ask back from you. It is indeed, as Aristotle says, [illegible]; but that saying of Socrates pleases me here, [illegible], which also did not displease the Apostle, who said: "To write the same things to you is indeed no trouble to me, but for you it is safe."

units.la: Valete, Heidelbergæ Calen. Martij, Anno 1591.
units.tr: Farewell. Heidelberg, the Calends of March, in the year 1591.

units.la: AD ILLVSTREM ET GENEROSVM DN. IOHANNEM Dionysium Zerotinum, PRÆFATIO.
units.tr: TO THE ILLUSTRIOUS AND NOBLE LORD JOHANN DIONYSIUS ZEROTIN, PREFACE.

units.la: ETsi, generose D. Iohannes Dionysi, sub id fere tempus, quo extremam huic operi manum adhibui, incertus huc nuncius veniret, te, relicta Basilea, cum fratre Carolo per Italiam in Morauos rediisse, vel, ut alij aiebant, in Italia subsistisse: ego tamen consilium meum, de hac altera catecheticarum explicationum parte generoso nomini tuo consecranda, mutare nec debui, nec volui. Non sane debui, ne pollicitationi meæ non satisfacerem: nec volui, ne nulla hoc tempore obseruā-tiq in te meę gratiqúe animi testificatio publicè exstaret. Etenim, ex quo a nobis discessisti, verè testari ausim, vix mihi diem abiisse, qua non cum grata recordatione in mente versaretur venustissima indoles tua, ad virtutes summas, & res, si male non auguror, maximas a natura tibi tributa, & elegantissima (si quæ in ætatem tuam cadere potest) gravitas, vel certe gravissima modestia tua, & suavissimum contubernium, quo tibi biennio mecum vti visum fuit, & iucundissimus conuictus noster, quem extremo semestri vna habuimus quam familiariter. Horum, inquam, recordatio interim semper mihi iucunda fuit: maxime quod præter alia tuæ in me meosque beneuolentiæ argumenta, μνημόσυνον longe clarissimum, quaeque obsidem domesticum mihi in oculis reliquisti, Iohannem Georgium filiolum meum prope iam trimulum, quem vnâ cum clarissimo piæ memoriæ viro, D.GEORGIO SO-N, collecta dilecto, ex sacro baptismi fonte suscipere, réque compaternitatis iure mecum obstringere non fuisti grauatus: quo sane beneficio clarissimo & maximo vicissim tibi ad sempiterna officia devinctum me teneri agnosco, sempérque agnoscam.
units.tr: Although, noble Lord Johann Dionysius, at about the time when I was putting the final hand to this work, an uncertain report came here that you had left Basel and returned with your brother Karl through Italy to Moravia, or, as others said, that you had stayed on in Italy, I nevertheless neither ought to nor wished to change my plan of dedicating this second part of the catechetical explanations to your noble name. I certainly ought not to, lest I fail to keep my promise; and I did not wish to, lest at this time no public testimony of my respect and gratitude toward you should exist. For, since you parted from us, I may truly declare that scarcely a day has gone by on which your most charming disposition did not come to my mind with pleasant remembrance: your natural aptitude for the highest virtues and for great things, which, if I do not augur wrongly, nature has bestowed upon you; your most refined seriousness (if such a quality can belong to your age), or rather your most serious modesty; the very pleasant companionship we enjoyed for two years together; and the most agreeable society we had in the last half-year, when we were so intimately together. I say that the remembrance of these things has always been pleasant to me, especially because, besides your other tokens of goodwill toward me and mine, you left in my sight a memorial by far the most distinguished, and a domestic hostage: my little son Johann Georg, now nearly three years old, whom you did not hesitate to take up from the sacred font of baptism together with the most distinguished man of pious memory, Lord Georg Sonnius, our dear colleague, and to bind me to you by the right of co-parenthood. For this very great and distinguished kindness I acknowledge that I am bound to you in return to everlasting duties, and I shall always acknowledge it.

units.la: En igitur tibi, generose Zerotine, hoc qualecunque studij in te mei, gratiq; animi testimonium, explicationum catecheticarum partem alteram, nō meam quidem illam, sed mea tamen opera sic elaboratam, vt illius nunc esse, cuius est, vere dici mereatur: quam si acceperis clementer, mihi laetabor. Si etiam cognoscere, & inis animi sensibus reponere studio habueris, tibi gratulabor, nec dubitabo in verae pietatis ac fidei doctrina, cuius tum domesticis carissimorum exemplis inde à puero, Timothei exéplo, es quasi innutritus: tu vero Amandi Po-lani à Polanstorff S.S. Theologiae Doctoris, viri pietatis iuxta & humanitatis ac eruditionis, laude praeclari, mihiq; amicissimi, fidelissima institutione, totum te tradere didicisti, accessionem & incrementa facturum esse magis ac magis haud poenitenda. Macte igitur Generose D. Iohan Dionysi, quam virtutis viam ingredi coepisti feliciter perfice, & me meo isque, in primis tuu Iohannem Georgium eo quo solebas, fauore compleki perge. Sic te Dominus Iesus Spiritu coelestis sapientiae magis magisque instruat, tuaeque institutioni porrò, in gloriae suae laudem, & Ecclesiarum, quas Dominus sub praesidio Illustrium Moraviae procerum voce Euangelij sibi colligit, & quibus ego gratiam à Domino & pacem precor, incrementum, & Reipub. Christianae ornamentum, cumulatissime benedicat: reque, cum illustri Zerorinorum familia, ab omni malo incolumem diu seruet. Vale. Heidelbergae ex collegio Sapientiae 5. Calend. Mart. Anno reparatae salutis humanae MDXCIV[?].
units.tr: Here, then, noble Zerotin, is this second part of the catechetical explanations, which is a testimony of my zeal for you and of my grateful feeling, whatever its worth may be. It is not that part of mine, indeed, but it has been so worked out by my labour that it deserves to be truly called his whose it is. If you accept it kindly, I shall rejoice. If you are willing to read it and to lay it up in your mind and heart, I shall congratulate you, and I do not doubt that you will make progress more and more in the teaching of true piety and faith, in which, from boyhood, you have been as it were nourished by the domestic examples of your most beloved relatives, like Timothy, and under the most faithful instruction of Lord Amandus Polanus of Polansdorf, Doctor of Sacred Theology, a man distinguished for his piety as well as for his humanity and learning, and most friendly to me; you have learned to give yourself wholly to that teaching, which is by no means to be regretted. Therefore, noble Lord Johann Dionysius, go on happily to complete the course of virtue you have begun to enter upon, and continue to embrace me and mine, and above all your Johann Georg, with the favour you were wont to show. So may the Lord Jesus instruct you more and more by the Spirit of heavenly wisdom, and may he bless abundantly your instruction henceforth, to the praise of his glory and the increase of the Churches which the Lord gathers to himself by the voice of the Gospel under the protection of the illustrious nobles of Moravia, and for whom I pray grace and peace from the Lord, and may he make them an ornament to the Christian commonwealth; and together with the illustrious house of Zerotin may he keep you safe from all evil for a long time. Farewell. Heidelberg, from the college of Sapientia, 5th day before the Calends of March, in the year of restored human salvation 1594[?].

units.la: IN TERTIAM EXPLICAT. catecheticarum partem, De Sacramentis: AD ILLVSTREM AC GENEROSVM D. PHILIPPVM BA-ronem in VVinnenburg & Beilstein,&c. Electoralis Palatinatus consilia-rium, Burggrauium Al-zeanum, &c. PRÆFATIO:
units.tr: ON THE THIRD PART OF THE CATECHETICAL EXPLANATIONS, On the Sacraments: TO THE ILLUSTRIOUS AND NOBLE LORD PHILIP, BARON OF WINNENBURG AND BEILSTEIN, etc., Councillor of the Electoral Palatinate, Burgrave of Alzey, etc. PREFACE

units.la: QVA SATYRICA DECLAMATIO Roberti Bellarmini Jesuitae, secundo tomo disputationum de Sacramentis praefi-xa, excutitur.
units.tr: IN WHICH THE SATIRICAL DECLAMATION OF ROBERT BELLARMINE, JESUIT, PREFIXED TO THE SECOND VOLUME OF HIS DISPUTATIONS ON THE SACRAMENTS, IS EXAMINED.

units.la: TERTIA explicationum Catecheticarum pars, quam generoso nomini tuo, Baro illustris, consecrare est visum, doctrinam orthodoxam de Sacramentis breui compendio sic repetit, ut fontes eius latissimè aperiat, & controuersias nostri temporis praecipuas, maximè de paedobaptismo, de transsubstantiatione, de consubstantiatione, nec non de excommunicatione, (quae doctrina sacramentorum appendix est) non ad captum modo juniorum explicet, sed ita persequatur, ut etiam diligen-tioribus sufficere possit. Sophistarum quaestiones & lites [illegible, ~9 letters] de sacramenti definitione, natura, vi, differentiis, &c. quibus simplicem veritatis doctrinam invol-verunt, non quidem ex professo discutiuntur. Quid e-nim attinebat discentes his fatigare, de quibus inter ipsos sophistas nondum convenire potuit? Imo quid ex lente unguentum? Ex istis tamen sanae doctrinae fundamentis haud difficulter judicari poterit, quàm sint vanae, & à verbo Dei alienae, vtut ementito vetustatis dibapho coram imperitis pallientur. Est enim veritas & sui & falsitatis index. Erit vero deinceps, cur de his etiam in scholis non omninò taceamus.
units.tr: The third part of my Catechetical Explanations, which I have thought fit to dedicate to your noble name, illustrious Baron, sets out the orthodox doctrine of the sacraments in a brief summary, so as to open up its sources very widely. It explains the principal controversies of our time, above all concerning infant baptism, transubstantiation, consubstantiation, and also excommunication (which is an appendix to the doctrine of the sacraments), not only in a way suited to the understanding of the young, but pursues them so thoroughly that they may also satisfy the more diligent. The questions and disputes of the sophists about the definition, nature, power, differences, etc., of the sacrament, by which they have wrapped the simple doctrine of truth, are not discussed here as a matter of course. For what was the point of wearing out the learners with things about which the sophists themselves have not yet been able to agree? Or rather, what is this but ointment from a lentil? Nevertheless, from the foundations of sound doctrine it will not be difficult to judge how empty and alien to the Word of God these things are, however they are dressed up before the unlearned with a falsely claimed antiquity. For truth is the measure both of itself and of falsehood. Yet there will be a reason later why we should not altogether keep silent about these things even in the schools.

units.la: Eò enim impudentiae Jesuitarum se nunc jactat audacia, ut nihil tam absurdè fit à scholasticis disputatum, quod ista suâ sophistică non confidant se pingere sic posse, vt & scholis & vulgo, tanquam Catholicum, placeat. Si qua vero (vt sunt complura) tam crasse à vero sint absona, vt fucum nullum admittant, ea isti loue lapidem iurare non erubescunt, à suis Catholicis nūquam scripta vel probata fuisse. Hi enim sunt (nisi fallor) tres illi impuri spiritus, quos Draco ad dementandos orbis monarchas, & ad quouis modo fulciendas Papatus ruinas nuper euomuit.
units.tr: For the audacity of the Jesuits now boasts of such impudence that nothing is disputed by the schoolmen so absurdly that they do not trust they can paint it with their sophistry in such a way that it pleases both the schools and the common people as Catholic. But if some things (as there are many) are so grossly discordant with the truth that they admit no disguise, they are not ashamed to swear by Jove the stone that these were never written or approved by their Catholics. For these are (unless I am mistaken) those three impure spirits which the Dragon has lately vomited forth to drive mad the monarchs of the world and to prop up in any way the ruins of the Papacy.

units.la: Rursus ergo iam disputant, an sacramentum sit ens rationis, an reale, an ens aggregatum, quid per accidens, ex rebus & verbis constans: & an ideo proprie definiri possit: & si possit, an vulgata definitio, quod sit mutabilis gratia visibilis forma, vniuocè omnibus coueniat. Frigi-dè docent, sacramenta esse signa sensibilia & visibilia, significantia rem sacram, cum aliqua analogia: sed proterue negant, ad ea requiri mandatum Dei expressum in scripturis: negat esse sigilla promissionis gratiæ: immo negant in eis esse promissionem gratiæ & remissionis peccatorum, vel saltem, esse signis annexa ordinatione diuina: negant denique ad excitandam, alendam & confirmandam fidem esse institutas, &c. Contendunt vero esse causam gratiæ, conferre gratiam, esse instrumenta iusti-ficationis, vi sua efficere gratiam, iustificationem & san-ctificationem ex opere operato, vt loquuntur: hoc est, naturali aptitudine ac vi ipsius actionis sacramentalis à Deo ad id institutæ: vel, vt alij volunt, per modum assistentiæ virtutis diuinæ ad signata ex pacto, etiam sine fide, & interno motu vtentis. Et hanc quidem efficaciam in solis nouæ legis sacramentis comminiscuntur. Veteris vero legis sacramentis alij nudā significationem iustificationis reliquerunt: alij etiam sanctificationis effectum concedunt, sed ex opere operantis, hoc est, ex deuotione & merito vtentis. Et hic rursus circumcisionem alij excipiunt, quasi etiam ex opere operato iustificantem: alij in turbam coniiciunt. Hanc rancidam scholasticorum crambem, noui isti cupediarij opiparè nunc recoquunt, & mundo pro deliciis apponunt.
units.tr: Again, then, they now dispute whether a sacrament is a being of reason, or a real being, or an aggregate being, consisting of things and words, accidentally, and whether it can therefore be properly defined; and if it can, whether the common definition, that it is a changeable visible form of grace, applies univocally to all. They coldly teach that sacraments are sensible and visible signs, signifying a holy thing with some analogy; but they shamelessly deny that for them an express command of God in the Scriptures is required; they deny that they are seals of the promise of grace; indeed they deny that there is in them a promise of grace and remission of sins, or at least that they are attached to signs by divine ordinance; they deny finally that they were instituted to arouse, nourish and confirm faith, etc. But they contend that they are the cause of grace, that they confer grace, that they are instruments of justification, that by their own power they effect grace, justification and sanctification ex opere operato, as they say: that is, by the natural aptitude and power of the sacramental action itself instituted by God for this purpose; or, as others wish, by way of a sort of assistance of divine power to the things signified by covenant, even without faith and the inward movement of the recipient. And this efficacy they devise only in the sacraments of the New Law. Of the sacraments of the Old Law, however, some have left only the bare signification of justification; others also concede an effect of sanctification, but ex opere operantis, that is, from the devotion and merit of the recipient. And here again some exempt circumcision, as if it also justified ex opere operato; others throw it into the crowd. This rancid crumb of the schoolmen these new delicacy-sellers now reheat lavishly, and set before the world as dainties.

units.la: In primis Bellarminus, ille sophistarū hodie princeps, adeò sibi in his argutiis placet, vt vel Soli tenebras offundere se posse, persuasum habeat. Petulanter igitur, planéque contra tanti difputatoris officium, Doctorib; nostris,plerisque vita functis,ranquam surdis,maledicit & insultat,non paralogifmos ostendes, vel eis obiiciés, sed tantū mendacia,mendacia,médacia crepās : qui feré nouus rabularum istorum disputandi mos est. Sed superbissimi hominis futilitatem clarissimi Theologi, VVitekerus, Danæus, Sibrandus aliique in plerisque disputationibus ita iam dexerunt, vt vel ipsos Iesuitas sui Goliathi pudere, & disputationum nimis libere editarum pœnitere incipiat.
units.tr: First of all Bellarmine, that prince of the sophists today, is so pleased with himself in these subtleties that he is persuaded he could cast darkness even over the Sun. Wantonly, therefore, and plainly contrary to the duty of so great a disputant, he reviles and insults our teachers, most of whom have died, as though they were deaf, not showing their paralogisms or objecting them to them, but merely crying out "lies, lies, lies"; which is nearly the new custom of these wranglers in disputing. But the vanity of this most proud man, the most distinguished theologians Wittich, Danaeus, Sibrandus and others have by now in most of their disputations so mauled that even the Jesuits themselves, like their own Goliath, begin to be ashamed and to repent of disputations published too freely.

units.la: Præfixit is secundo disputationum tomo, quem nuper de sacramentis emisit, declamatione planè satyricam, in cuius exordio non dissimulat, se velle histrionem agere, & spectaculum exhibere auditorio Romano, de hæreticorum furiosis concertationibus, non iniucundum. Hoc ergo cum primis agit, vt Doctores nostros inter se committat, ac præcipuè sacramentorum vsum, de obsignatione promissionis gratiæ, & confirmatione fidei, noua sua sophistica nobis excutiat. Quā vero agat pterueè, operæ pretium est duxi hoc loco breuiter oftedere.
units.tr: In the second volume of his disputations, which he recently issued on the sacraments, he prefixed a declamation that is plainly satirical, in the opening of which he does not conceal that he wishes to play the buffoon and to put on a show before the Roman audience, not unpleasing, of the frenzied contentions of heretics. He therefore chiefly aims at setting our teachers against one another, and especially, with his new sophistry, at tearing apart for us the use of the sacraments, their sealing of the promise of grace, and the confirmation of faith. How perversely he does this, I have thought it worth while to show briefly in this place.

units.la: Principiò nomen Sacramenti & à diuersis, & ab iisdē nostris modò receptū, modò explosum esse, ex Luthero, Carolostadio, Melanchthone, Zwinglio & Caluino ostendere conatur. Quasi vero de sacramenti origine, significatione, proprietate & vsu, inter ipsos scholasticos nunquam dubitatum sit vel disputatum. Quòd si à nostris de voce quæsitum aliquando est: constat nihilominus, omnium consensu hactenus in ecclesiis nostris receptam esse, & in hunc vsque diem sine controuersia retineri. Quæ itaque de Luthero & Philippo narrat, planè sunt friuola. Carolostadij hominis à Luthero exacerbati sententiam nemo admodū secutus est. Zwinglium manifestè calumniatur. Is enim cuperet vocem sacramenti Germanis nunquam receptam fuisse. Sed cur? certè non aliam ob causam, quàm quia horribilem sacramenti abusum in deierationibus, nimis, proh dolor, familiarem Germanis detestatur. De Caluino, quòd nomen hoc parum probet, ac reprehendat, nec tamen existimet operæ pretium de eo litigare: impudens Iesuitæ figmentum est, quod Romæ in suo theatro, vbi Caluini Institutio Christiana exsulat, sine rubore effutire potuit. Qui totam sectionem 13. ad quam Iesuita infrà digitum intendit, recte legerint, videbunt Calvinum non reprehendere vocabulum sed argutias sophistarum, qui ex vocabuli Latina significatione, confirmationem fidei per sacramenta oppugnant.
units.tr: First, he tries to show that the name Sacrament has been received at one time and rejected at another, both by different people and by these same men of ours, from Luther, Karlstadt, Melanchthon, Zwingli and Calvin. As if indeed the origin, meaning, property and use of the sacrament had never been doubted or disputed among the schoolmen themselves! But if at some time the word was questioned by our men, it is nonetheless clear that by the agreement of all it has hitherto been received in our churches and is retained without controversy to this day. Therefore what he relates about Luther and Philip is plainly frivolous. Karlstadt's opinion, a man exasperated by Luther, has been followed by almost no one. He manifestly slanders Zwingli. For Zwingli would wish that the word sacrament had never been received by the Germans. But why? Certainly for no other reason than that he detests the horrible abuse of the sacrament in oaths, which, alas, is too familiar to the Germans. As for Calvin, that he approves this name little and finds fault with it, yet does not think it worth the trouble to quarrel about it: this is a shameless fiction of the Jesuit, which he could blurt out without blushing at Rome in his theatre, where Calvin's Christian Institution is an exile. Those who read rightly the thirteenth section, to which the Jesuit points his finger below, will see that Calvin does not find fault with the word but with the subtleties of the sophists, who, from the Latin meaning of the word, attack the confirmation of faith through the sacraments.

units.la: Hinc ad sacramenti naturâ accedens, Lutherū, Zwin-glium & Calvinum, quasi de ea inter se conflgentes, in scenam producit. Et Lutherum quidem voluisse dicit, sacramenta tantum esse testimonia diuinitus ad excitandam fidem instituta: Zwinglium contrà, tantum esse oppignorationem quandam nostri erga Deum: Calvinum denique, utriusque sententia quasi in unam conflata, esse symbola benevolentiae Dei fidem obsignantia, & testimonia ad pietatem vicissim nos obligantia. En conflictum. Sed profectò nodum in scirpo Iesuita auditoribus suis ostendit.
units.tr: Hence, coming to the nature of the sacrament, he brings forward Luther, Zwingli and Calvin on the stage, as if they were fighting among themselves about it. And he says that Luther indeed wanted the sacraments to be only testimonies divinely instituted to arouse faith; Zwingli on the contrary, only a certain pledge of our own towards God; and Calvin finally, as if the opinion of both had been fused into one, to be symbols of the goodwill of God sealing faith, and testimonies binding us in turn to piety. Behold the conflict! But the Jesuit has surely shown his hearers a knot in a bulrush.

units.la: De Lutheri & Calvini in hac parte consensu, res est manifestior, ac notior, quàm ut ostendi mereatur. Zwinglio per calumniam tribui opinionem de meris obligationis & professionis nostrae notis, ipse Iesuita paulò post imprudens testatur, cum scribit Carolostadianam & Anabaptisticam opinionem de meris notis professionis fuisse tum ab aliis, tum etiam à Zwinglio confutatam, & penitus ferè sepultam: & verè hoc scribit. Sententiam namque suam ZVVINGLIVS, tum alibi, tum in libello ad Principes Germaniae scripto, satis aperte declarat, sic scribens: Signa ipsa sic à Christo ipsa sunt instituta, ut etiam analogia sua plurimum polleant ad inducendum in rem fide & contemplatione praesentem. Ex mox clarius: Frustra non sunt sacramenta. Praedicat enim salutem à Deo datâ: sensus huc convertit, & subinde FIDEM EXERCENT, quam & proximo pollicetur, atque ad fraternâ caritatem trahunt. Atque haec omnia dum fiunt, Spiritus, qui inspirando nunc citra instrumento trahit, nunc cum instrumento, quo, quantum & quae vult. Haftenus ille. Quid verò clarius ad consensum cum LVTHERO & CALVINO dici potuit, quàm sacramenta ad hoc instituta esse, ut analogia nos inducant in rem fide praesentem, praedicare salutem, sensus convertere, fidem exercere, denique esse instrumēta Spiritus sancti? Hoc-cine est meras notas, profeßionis vel obligationis nostrę erga Christum & ecclesiam eius ex sacramentis facere? Iniuriam ergo nostris Doctoribus Iesuita manifestam facit.
units.tr: Concerning the agreement of Luther and Calvin on this point, the matter is too plain and well known to deserve demonstration. That Zwingli is slanderously credited with the opinion of mere marks of obligation and profession of our own, the Jesuit himself, a little later and unwittingly, bears witness when he writes that the Karlstadtian and Anabaptist opinion of mere marks of profession was refuted, and almost wholly buried, both by others and also by Zwingli; and this he writes truly. For ZWINGLI declares his own view quite openly, both elsewhere and in the little book written to the Princes of Germany, writing thus: The signs themselves were so instituted by Christ that their analogy also greatly avails to lead into the thing present by faith and contemplation. And a little more clearly: The sacraments are not in vain. For they proclaim the salvation given by God; they turn the senses towards it, and thereupon they exercise FAITH, which they also pledge to the neighbour and draw to brotherly love. And while all these things are done, the Spirit, who inspires, now draws without the instrument, now with the instrument by which, as much as and whatever he wills. So far he. What could be said more clearly in agreement with LUTHER and CALVIN than that sacraments were instituted for this purpose, that by their analogy they lead us into the thing present by faith, proclaim salvation, turn the senses, exercise faith, and finally are instruments of the Holy Spirit? Is this to make from the sacraments mere marks of our obligation or profession towards Christ and his Church? The Jesuit therefore does manifest injustice to our teachers.

units.la: Nec tamen hic ceßat, sed amplius singulos ordine insectatur. Clamat sententiam Lutheri, quòd sacramenta confirment fidem, tam esse absurdam vt absurdius nihil cogitari possit. Cur? Quia nimirum ista sit miraculorum vsus. Hæc enim summa.
units.tr: Nor does he stop there, but goes after the individual points one by one. He cries out that Luther's view, that the sacraments confirm faith, is so absurd that nothing more absurd can be imagined. Why? Because, of course, that is the use of miracles. For this is his whole argument.

units.la: Atqui absurdus est Iesuita, ideò remouens differentiam generica am ab vna specie, quia conuenit alteri; cum <bl>ςωικῷ</bl> omnibus speciebus communiter insit, non ignoret. An non omnium diuinorum signorum communis est vsus, vt homines de voluntate ac beneficiis Dei commonefaciant, & fidem promissionum obsignent? Imò enim Deus verbis addit signa, vt infirmitati nostrę consulat, & promissi nes nobis confirmet. Si dubitat Iesuita, percurrat scripturam à primo immortalitatis sacramento in Paradiso, vsque ad extrema signa vltimi aduentus Christi: & omnia in hoc scopo conuenire deprehendet, tam vniuersalia, quàm particularia, tam in rebus naturalibus, quàm in miraculis exhibita, tam denique ordinaria, quàm extraordinaria. Atqui miraculum signum diuinum esse, non puto inficias ibit. Sacramentum verò etiam esse diuinorum signorum speciem, ipse Lombardus eum docere potest. Conueniunt ergo in hoc vsu miracula & sacramenta: nisi quòd illa vel in genere totius doctrinæ, vel cerræ alicuius promissionis, hæc verò in specie promissionis gratiæ sigilla sunt.
units.tr: Yet the Jesuit is absurd, since he removes the generic difference from one species because it belongs to another, though he cannot be unaware that the Stoic element is common to all species. Is it not the common use of all divine signs to remind men of God's will and benefits, and to seal the promises by faith? Indeed God adds signs to his words so that he may provide for our weakness and confirm his promises to us. If the Jesuit doubts this, let him run through Scripture from the first sacrament of immortality in Paradise to the final signs of Christ's last coming, and he will find that everything agrees in this purpose: universal and particular things alike, things shown in natural events and in miracles, things ordinary and extraordinary. And surely he will not deny that a miracle is a divine sign. That a sacrament is also a kind of divine sign, Lombard himself can teach him. So miracles and sacraments agree in this use, except that the miracles are signs of the whole doctrine in general or of some particular promise as a pledge, while the sacraments are seals of the promise of grace in particular.

units.la: Neque ad rem facit, quòd fingit miracula ex se nota esse, nec à prædicatione vlla ratione dependere. Sacramenta verò nō intelligi, nisi verbi testimonio confirmentur. Vanum est enim, quod de miraculorum vi dicit: possunt siquidem ea ex se quorumuis infidelium sensus percellere: sed docere & confirmare doctrinam cœlestem, cuius sunt sigilla, ex se non magis possunt, quàm sacramenta, si doctrinę explicatio non accedat. Tu, quæ hæc est consequentia? Sacramenta non obsignant gnant promissiones ex se, vt miracula. Ergo non obsi-gnant.Ponamus miraculaex se vim habere.Hoc no,impedit, quin sacramenta ex instituto Dei vim habeant. Nam & naturalia, & miraculosa, & voluntaria signa significat:etsi aliter fumo incédiu, aliter miraculo virtus diuina, aliter sacramento promissio gratiæ significetur.
units.tr: Nor does it help him that he pretends miracles are known in themselves and depend on no preaching at all, whereas sacraments are not understood unless they are confirmed by the testimony of the Word. His claim about the power of miracles is empty: they may indeed strike the senses of any unbelievers by themselves, but they cannot by themselves teach and confirm the heavenly doctrine, of which they are the seals, any more than sacraments can, if an explanation of the doctrine does not accompany them. What kind of inference is this? "Sacraments do not seal promises by themselves, as miracles do. Therefore they do not seal." Let us grant that miracles have power in themselves. This does not prevent sacraments from having power by the institution of God. For natural, miraculous and voluntary signs all signify alike, although smoke signifies fire in one way, divine power signifies itself by a miracle in another way, and the promise of grace is signified by a sacrament in yet another way.

units.la: Ridet deinde,vt ineptam comparationem illam, qua verbum diplomati, sacramentum sigillo à nostris confertur:& contra contendit, verbum potius sigillum sacramenti,quàm sacramentum sigillum verbi dicendum esse.Quid ita?Quia,inquit,vt sigillu etiá sine diplomate sim sua habet,diploma,sine sigillo no ite:Sic verbum Dei etiá sine sacramento authoritate summa habet,sacramentu sine verbo nulla. Atqui bis ridiculus & ineptus est lefuita.Primo,tribuens vim sigillo sine diplomate:diplomati nullam sine sigillo. Deinde faciens ex verbo,sigillum,eò quod ex se authoritatem habeat. Quaelo enim te,Bellarmine,quàm vim habet,vel quid vobis obsignat plumbum Papæ à diplomate indulgentiario auulsum? Quod negas diplomata sine sigillo agnosci,id nec vniuersale est,nec καθ' αὑτὸ [?] Quid enim? An tu nulla chirographa,nullas syngraphas,nullas apochas,nulla rescripta Principum rata vidisti sine sigillis? Per se bonorum virorum,nedum Principum,nedum Dei tabulæ authoritatem habent,& fidem merentur:vt constat olim imperatorias tabulas signis subscriptis potius, quàm sigillis cereis muniri solitas esse : ex accidenti verò,hoc est,ob lubricam hominum fidem vitámque est factum , vt vix multis sigillis munitæ tabulæ ratæ nunc habeantur. Et quàm est ineptû,te ideo ex verbo sigillum facere, quia sine sacramento authoritatem habet? An vero tibi mox sigillum erit,quicquid ex se est authenticum? Sigillum est signum visibile tabularum,non tam authoritatis addendæ,quàm fidei faciendæ vsum habens. Tale signum non est verbum Dei. Rectius vero tabulis comparatur: quia in eo Deus de voluntate sua ecclesiam erudit, & certa bona ei nuncupat. Habet authoritatem ex se,propter authorem Deum, Sacramenta pro sigillis ei sunt addita,minimè,vt tu putas,quo ex his authoritatem accipiat,sed vt languori nostro per ea Deus consulat:sunt enim visibiles picturæ promissionum, seu potius promissiones ipsæ cæremoniis vestitæ, & quasi verba visibilia, ut ab Augustino scitè appellantur: quia nimirum eadem beneficia pingunt & significant oculis, quæ verbum sonat auribus. Firmius vero credutur visa, quàm tantu audita.
units.tr: Next he mocks the comparison which our people make, that the Word is to a diploma as the sacrament is to a seal, and he argues on the contrary that the Word should rather be called the seal of the sacrament than the sacrament the seal of the Word. Why so? "Because," he says, "a seal has its authority even without the diploma, but a diploma does not without the seal. So the Word of God has supreme authority even without a sacrament, but a sacrament has none without the Word." But the Jesuit is doubly ridiculous and absurd. First, in giving power to a seal without a diploma, and to a diploma nothing without a seal. Second, in making the Word into a seal because it has authority from itself. For I ask you, Bellarmine, what power does the lead of the Pope, torn off from an indulgence diploma, have, or what does it seal for you? As for your claim that diplomas are not recognised without a seal, this is neither universal nor true in itself. For what? Have you never seen handwritten documents, notes of obligation, receipts, or rescripts of princes that are valid without seals? Documents of good men, let alone of princes, and still less of God, have authority in themselves and deserve belief, as it is known that imperial documents were once customarily secured by signatures rather than by wax seals. It is only by accident, that is, because of the slippery faith and life of men, that documents secured by many seals are now scarcely held valid. And how absurd it is that you make the Word into a seal because it has authority without a sacrament! Or will whatever is authentic in itself immediately be a seal for you? A seal is a visible sign of documents, serving not so much to add authority as to make belief, and such a sign is not the Word of God. It is more correctly compared to the documents themselves, because in it God teaches the Church about his will and names certain goods for it. It has authority in itself, on account of its author God. The sacraments have been added to it as seals, not, as you think, so that it may receive authority from them, but so that God may provide for our weakness through them. For they are visible pictures of the promises, or rather the promises themselves clothed in ceremonies, and, as Augustine rightly calls them, visible words: because they paint and signify to the eyes the same benefits that the word sounds to the ears. Things seen are indeed believed more firmly than things only heard.

units.la: Argumentatur tertio contra Luth. Si sacramentum nihil est aliud, nisi excitandæ vel alendæ fidei instrumentum: quorsum infantes, amentes & dormientes interdum in ecclesia baptizantur? At cur non etiam de campanis, templis & altaribus quærit? Amentes & dormientes vestra sanè ecclesia baptizet. De infantibus ecclesiæ Christi respondemus, baptizari eos, licet vsu rationis carentes, propter mandatum & promissionem Dei. At, inquis, non credunt. Non ergo baptismus eis confirmat fidem. Quod nescis, noli negare. Non credunt, ut adulti. Ergo non credunt: si verum hoc, cur non etiam verum? Non sunt rationales, ut adulti: Ergo non sunt rationales? Promissio est eis Spiritus sanctus fidei effector, gratia fœderis, & regnum Dei. Si actu non credunt, cur non crederent inclinatione per gratiam: sicut peccant inclinatione per naturam? Ut ergo credunt: ita baptismus eis est sigillum gratiæ fidem obsignans. Quis vero dixit, sacramentum nihil esse aliud, nisi excitandæ aut fovendæ fidei instrumentum? Plures sunt sacramenti usus. Esto ergo: Baptismus fide non confirmat infantibus. At confirmabit aliquando adultis. Neque enim ad unum momentum restringendus est baptismi fructus, ipso Magistro & Augustino testibus. Et tamen baptizandi sunt, ut adoptio & regeneratio eis obsignetur, & ab infidelibus ipsi discernantur, quæ sane, ut non sunt nihil, ita per baptismum infantium ecclesiæ conferri & obsignari, non, ut vos docetis, ex opere operato, sed ex institutione Christi, non dubitamus. Habet ergo Iesuita quomodo pædobaptismus confirmationem fidei non tollat.
units.tr: Thirdly, he argues against Luther: "If a sacrament is nothing but an instrument for awakening or nourishing faith, why are infants, the mad and the sleeping sometimes baptised in the Church? But why does he not also ask about bells, temples and altars? Your Church, certainly, baptises the mad and the sleeping." To the infants of the Church of Christ we reply that they are baptised, although they lack the use of reason, on account of God's command and promise. "But," you say, "they do not believe. Therefore baptism does not confirm their faith." What you do not know, do not deny. They do not believe as adults do. Therefore they do not believe? If that is true, why is it not also true that... ? They are not rational as adults are. Therefore they are not rational? The promise is that the Holy Spirit, the author of faith, the grace of the covenant and the kingdom of God, is theirs. If they do not believe in act, why should they not believe by inclination through grace, just as they sin by inclination through nature? So, as they believe, baptism is to them a seal of grace sealing their faith. But who said that a sacrament is nothing but an instrument for awakening or fostering faith? A sacrament has several uses. Grant then that baptism does not confirm faith in infants. Yet it will sometimes confirm it in adults. For the fruit of baptism is not to be confined to a single moment, as both the Master and Augustine testify. And yet they are to be baptised, so that adoption and regeneration may be sealed to them, and so that they may be distinguished from unbelievers. That these things, since they are not nothing, are conferred and sealed to the infants of the Church through their baptism, not, as you teach, by the work worked, but by the institution of Christ, we do not doubt. So the Jesuit has no way to show that infant baptism does not take away the confirmation of faith.

units.la: IV. Hic vero totus Anabaptistica indutus larua, Infantes, inquit, qui dum baptizantur, eiulant, & obluctantur, id vel intelligunt, vel non. Si non intelligunt, nec credunt, & perperam baptizantur: sic Vicerunt An abaptista. Si intelligunt, sunt fa-cri legi: & Vicerunt Anabaptistæ. Satis vero elegantèr persequam suam agit histrio. Quid si dicam dilemmate, ut ipse vocat, ipse vocat, similiter armato: Iesuita hoc scribens aut est vir bonus, aut calumniator. Si vir bonus, non debuit sic mentiri, & nos vicimus: si calumniator, non meretur fidem eius sophistica: & nos vicimus. Nunquid hic par ratio? Sophisticum est utrumque Iesuitae cornu: & prius quidem duplicitèr: nam fallacia est a secundum quid, cum sic colligit: Infantes non intelligunt. Ergo non credunt. De fidei ἐπιστήμη[?] datur: de ἀγνωσία[?] non item. Loquor autem de ἀνάγκῃ[?], non quàm à natura, sed quàm à gratia habent promissionis: Ero Deus tuus, & seminis tui. Est etiā paralogismus non causae: Infantes non credunt actu, Ergo non sunt baptizandi. Causa enim praecobaptismi, non est intellectus, vel fides actualis infantum, sed promissio ad ipsos tanquam ad filios foederis & ecclesiae pertinēs, testante Petro Apostolo, Baptizetur unusquisque in nomine Iesu Christi, &c. quia vobis & liberis vestris facta est promissio.
units.tr: IV. Here, indeed, he is wholly dressed in an Anabaptist mask. "Infants," he says, "who cry out and struggle while they are baptised, either understand this or do not. If they do not understand, they do not believe either, and they are wrongly baptised: thus the Anabaptists have won. If they understand, they are fit for the sacred law: and the Anabaptists have won." But how elegantly the actor carries out his farce! What if I say, with a dilemma, as he calls it, armed in the same way: the Jesuit, writing this, is either a good man or a slanderer. If a good man, he ought not to lie thus, and we have won. If a slanderer, his sophistical arguments deserve no trust, and we have won. Is the reasoning not the same here? Both horns of the Jesuit's dilemma are sophistical, and the first in a twofold way. For it is a fallacy of "in a certain respect" (a secundum quid) when he infers as follows: "Infants do not understand. Therefore they do not believe." Knowledge of faith is given; ignorance is not given likewise. I am speaking of the necessity which infants have not by nature but by the grace of the promise: "I will be your God and the God of your seed." There is also a paralogism of non-cause: "Infants do not believe in act. Therefore they are not to be baptised." For the cause of baptism is not the understanding or actual faith of infants, but the promise made to them as children belonging to the covenant and to the Church, as the Apostle Peter testifies: "Let each one be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ, etc., because the promise has been made to you and to your children."

units.la: In posteriore cornu, est idem sophisma. Eiulant, obluctantur, & motus distortos aliquando edunt infantes baptizandi. Cur? An quia sacrae actioni obluctantur? Minime: sed quia dolent, vel affectum aliquem tenellae aetati aduersum patiuntur. Quid putat Iesuita infantibus in crueta illa circumcisione? imo quid seni Abrahamo? quid familiae eius masculę? quid denique Sichemitis civibus factum esse? An ibi nullus motus distortus? An infantes vocabit sacrilegos magis, quā suas vestales adolescentulas, quae inter confitendum, poenitendum, vel communicandum, a fraterculis sic doctae, lacrymulas saepe profundunt quàm miserìcorditer? Et quis magis distortos motus in sacris edit, quàm sacrificus missificā? Imo an nunquam ipse flens prae devotione missam fecit, atque ita sacrilegus fuit? Pudeat tantum Doctorem naeniarum istarum. Audiatur de hoc Augustinus: Quod sociis & motibus, quibus possunt, relictā[?] infantes, nō eis imputatur, atque omnis renitsum ipsorum nihil penditur, &c. quia in tantum nesciunt quid faciunt, ut nec facere iudicetur. Similia habet Epist.23. & lib.4.cap.23.de Bapt. contra Donatistas.
units.tr: The same sophism is in the second horn. Infants who are to be baptised cry out, struggle, and sometimes make distorted movements. Why? Is it because they struggle against the sacred action? By no means: rather because they feel pain, or suffer some feeling of aversion proper to tender age. What does the Jesuit think happened to the infants in that cruel circumcision? Indeed, what happened to the old man Abraham? To his male household? And finally, to the citizens of Shechem? Was there no distorted movement there? Will he call infants more sacrilegious than his own vestal girls, who, while confessing, doing penance, or receiving communion, taught by their little friars, often pour out tears as pitifully as they can? And who makes more distorted movements in the sacred rites than the priest at Mass? Indeed, has he himself never wept out of devotion while saying Mass, and so been a sacrilegious man? Let us be ashamed of such a teacher of these trifles. Let Augustine be heard on this: "Infants, left with the movements and gestures by which they are able, are not held guilty for them, and all their resistance is accounted as nothing, etc., because they so little know what they do that it is not judged even to be doing." Similar things are found in Epistle 23, and in book 4, chapter 23, of On Baptism, against the Donatists.

units.la: Tandem Lutherum cum hoc sarcasmo dimittit: In Sacramē-quonam evangelio, vel apostolo, vel propheta legerit: sacra-ta esse figil[?] meta noua legis esse testimonia vel sigilla verbi Dei? An forte in euangelio secundum Lutherum? Esse sigilla verbi Dei, veteratorie dixit, pro esse sigilla promissionis gratiae: vt videamur omne verbi authoritatem a sacramentis suspendere, quod supra est refutatum. Sic mortuo leoni barbam vellicare audet, cuius viui aspectu vix suffinereret. At vero tu prius dic nobis, in quonam euangelio? an in Loyolano? an potius Calendario Gregoriano legeris, sacramenta nō esse sigilla promissionis gratiae, non confirmare fidem: sed conferre gratiam, iustificare, sanctificare: vetera quidem ex opere operantis, noua vero ex opere operato, etiam sine fide & bono motu venentium: cum scriptura contra clamet: circumcisione prodesse legi seruantibus: nō seruatibus fieri praecipiuntur baptizati credentes seruanti cum probatione suis edendum esse de panes facere. Iam audi contrà, vbi Lutherus legerit, sacramenta esse sigilla promissionis gratiae. De circumcisione dicit Deus: Vt sit signum foederis inter me et vos. Foedus vero interpretatur Paulus, gratiam seu iustitiam fidei: signum accepit circumcisione, signaculum iustitiae fidei. De Pascha: Sanguis ille pro vobis erit in signum super illas domos, vbi eritis, et videns sanguinem illum, transeam prater vos. Hic vero trāsitus seu hoc Pascha significabat Christi gratiā. De Baptismo: Baptizate omnes gentes, in nomine (hoc est authoritate, iussu & vice) patris, filii, et Spiritus sancti. Et Surge, ablue peccata tua. Et Baptismus est lauacrum regenerationis: Baptismus nos seruat, nō quo carnis sordes abstinentur, sed quo fit, et bona conscientia Deum interroget. De Coena: Hoc poculum est nouum Testamentum in meo sanguine. Item: Hoc facite in mei commemorationem. Haec si intelligis, habes quod petis, vtriusque legis sacramenta esse signa gratiae. Cur enim nouae quam veteris legis, vt vos loquimini, esset deterior conditio? Si non intelligis, indignus es, qui voceris magister in Israel, & nescias omnium sacramentorum formam [?] esse, promissionem gratiae significare & obsignare fidelibus. Sed & audi ecclesiae homiines: Basilium, qui expresse confitetur, quod tu sine fronte negas: [?] hoc est, Est enim baptismus, signum fidei, [?]. Et Tertullianum sic de baptismo loquentem: Lauacrum illud obsiobsignatio est fidei, &c. Et Augustinum, qui sacramenta vocat visibilia rerum diuinarum, signacula, &c. Et tu, vbi Lutherus hoc legerit, quærere non erubescis? Sic dimisso Luthero, Zuinglium aggreditur, & opinionem scilicet eius de signis oppignorationis nostræ erga Deum flagellâdam sumit. Sed calumniatorem hic agere histrionem, iam supra ostensum est.
units.tr: Finally he dismisses Luther with this sneer: "In what gospel, or apostle, or prophet did he read that the sacraments of the new law are testimonies or seals of the Word of God?" Is it perhaps in the gospel according to Luther? He sly-ly said that they are seals of the Word of God, instead of seals of the promise of grace, so that we seem to make the whole authority of the Word depend on the sacraments, which has been refuted above. Thus he dares to pluck the beard of a dead lion, whose living aspect he could scarcely endure. But you, tell us first: in what gospel did you read it? In the Loyolan one? Or rather in the Gregorian calendar, that the sacraments are not seals of the promise of grace, do not confirm faith, but confer grace, justify and sanctify: the old ones indeed by the work wrought by the one who works, but the new ones by the work wrought, even without faith and good motion in those who come? When Scripture cries out against this: "Circumcision profits those who keep the law, but if they do not keep it, their circumcision is made uncircumcision"; the baptized, believing, are commanded to keep ... (the text here is corrupt). Now hear the contrary: where Luther read that the sacraments are seals of the promise of grace. God says of circumcision: "that it may be a sign of the covenant between me and you." Paul interprets the covenant as the grace or righteousness of faith: "he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith." Of the Passover: "That blood will be for you a sign upon those houses where you are, and when I see the blood I will pass over you." Yet that passing over, or this Passover, signified the grace of Christ. Of Baptism: "Baptize all nations in the name (that is, by the authority, command and in the place) of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit." And "Arise, wash away your sins." And "Baptism is the washing of regeneration: baptism saves us, not because the filth of the flesh is put away, but because the conscience asks God with a good answer." Of the Supper: "This cup is the new testament in my blood." Likewise: "Do this in remembrance of me." If you understand these things, you have what you seek: the sacraments of both laws are signs of grace. For why should the condition of the new law be worse than that of the old, as you put it? If you do not understand, you are unworthy to be called a teacher in Israel, and you do not know that the form of all the sacraments is to signify and seal the promise of grace to the faithful. But hear also the men of the Church: Basil, who expressly confesses what you shamelessly deny: "For baptism is a sign of faith." And Tertullian, speaking thus of baptism: "That washing is a sealing of faith," etc. And Augustine, who calls the sacraments visible signs of divine things, seals, etc. And you, when Luther has read this, are not ashamed to ask where? Having thus dismissed Luther, he attacks Zwingli, and takes up for flogging his opinion about signs of our pledge toward God. But that he here plays the buffoon as a slanderer has already been shown above.

units.la: Tandem in Caluinum grauius insurgens; Inter Lutherum, inquit, & Caluinum, hoc interest, quod cùm vtrque sacramenta faciat testimonia vel sigilla diuinæ promissionis: eam promissionē esse sult[?] Lutherus iustificationis præsentis: Caluinus electionis æternæ. Et ne mentiri videatur, citat Caluinum in Antidoto Có. Trid. sess.6.c.5 quod ibi infantes baptizari dicat, nō vt in adoptione filiorum Dei recipiantur, sed vt obsignetur promissio vitæ: quæ ad eos per gratiam prædestinationis iam ante pertinebat. Et sess.7.can.7. quòd id ad eum finem sacramenta referenda esse affirmet, vt certos nos reddat perpetuæ adoptionis & gratiæ, ad quâ videlicet ante mundi constitutionem prædestinati sumus. Hæc Iesuita: Sed absque fronte omnia. Vtroque loco de æterna electione vel prædestinationis gratia Caluinus ne iota quidem. In priore hoc tantum dicit: Ideo infantes iure ad baptismum admitti, & baptizari, quia sint promissionis heredes: quia, nisi iam ante ad eos pertineret vitæ promissio, baptismum profanaret quisquis illis daret. In posteriore hæc sunt eius verba: Tametsi baptismus chirographum est mutuæ inter nos & Deum obligationis: hoc tamen habet præcipuum, vt de gratuita peccatorum remissione, perpetuaq; adoptionis gratia nos certiores reddat. Hoccine negare est, sacramenta esse sigilla promissionis de iustificatione præsente? Hoccine vero est, sacramenta solùm ad præteritum, id est, ad gratiam electionis referre? Hæc nimirum est fides Bellarmini in citandis patrum & nostrorum Doctorum verbis & sententiis. Talia sunt disputationum eius duo lumina: farragines nempe malè compilatæ, quæ vbi à doctis ad candorem reuocabuntur, nec ipse disputator manebit Agrippa sterilior. Sed ad rem.
units.tr: Finally, rising more heavily against Calvin: "Between Luther and Calvin," he says, "there is this difference: while both make the sacraments testimonies or seals of the divine promise, Luther says that promise is of present justification, Calvin that it is of eternal election." And lest he seem to lie, he cites Calvin in the Antidote to the Council of Trent, session 6, chapter 5, where he says that infants are baptized not so that they may be received into adoption as sons of God, but so that the promise of life may be sealed, which already belonged to them beforehand through the grace of predestination. And in session 7, canon 7, that he affirms the sacraments are to be referred to this end, that they make us certain of the perpetual adoption and grace into which we were predestined before the foundation of the world. Thus the Jesuit; but all of it without shame. In both places Calvin says not one jot about eternal election or the grace of predestination. In the former he says only this: "Therefore infants are rightly admitted to baptism and baptized, because they are heirs of the promise: because, unless the promise of life already belonged to them, whoever gave them baptism would profane it." In the latter these are his words: "Although baptism is a bond of mutual obligation between us and God, yet it has this chief purpose, that it makes us more certain of the free remission of sins and of the perpetual grace of adoption." Is this to deny that the sacraments are seals of the promise of present justification? Or is this to refer the sacraments only to the past, that is, to the grace of election? This, surely, is the faith of Bellarmine in citing the words and opinions of the Fathers and of our teachers. Such are the two lights of his disputations: indeed hodgepodges badly compiled, which, when they are called back to clarity by learned men, the disputant himself will not remain less barren than Agrippa. But to the matter.

units.la: Sacramenta esse sigilla electionis æternæ, etsi in usu legitimo verum est: tamen non memini à Caluino usquam scriptum esse.Imò Vbiquitarij hodiè contrariam calũ-niam Caluino & Bezæ intentant,quasi sacramēta electionis sigilla esse negét: quod ipsum etiam falsum est.
units.tr: That the sacraments are seals of eternal election is true, if taken in lawful use; yet I do not remember that it was ever written anywhere by Calvin. Indeed, today the Ubiquitarians bring the contrary calumny against Calvin and Beza, as if they denied that the sacraments are seals of election; which itself is also false.

units.la: « Hæc vero simplex doctrina Caluini est:Sacramenta pro-desse,hoc est,exhibere & obsignare gratiā in vero vsu, « non ex opere operato,vel operantis,vt sophistæ volút,sed « ex promissione instituentis,& fide vtentis. Gratia vero intelligit ipsam salutè nostram, cum omnibus antece-dētibus,mediis, & causis,hoc est,gratuitam electionem remissionem peccatorum,regenerationem ,sanctifica-tionem & vitam æternam. Completitur ergo gratiam præteritā,præsentem,& futuram:cum primis vero præ-sentem.Nā & æterna electio obsignatur sacramentis,nö vt est æternū in Deo decretum vel præteritum quid, sed vt est præses & cōstās Dei volūtas de nobis in Chri-sto feruādis in Euāgelio reuelata:& vita æterna iifdē cō-firmatur,nō vt est bonū futurū,sed vt fide iā possidetur.
units.tr: "This is the simple doctrine of Calvin: the sacraments benefit, that is, exhibit and seal grace in true use, not by the work wrought, either of the one who works, as the sophists wish, but by the promise of the one who institutes and by the faith of the one who uses. Now by grace he understands our salvation itself, with all its antecedents, means and causes, that is, gratuitous election, remission of sins, regeneration, sanctification and eternal life. He therefore completes grace as past, present and future, but chiefly as present. For eternal election is sealed by the sacraments, not as it is an eternal decree in God or something past, but as it is the constant and steadfast will of God concerning our preservation in Christ, revealed in the gospel; and eternal life is confirmed by the same, not as it is a future good, but as it is already possessed by faith."

units.la: Possem ex institutione Christiana infinita produce-re,quibus hæc confirmem.Sed ex ipso Antidoto Con-cilij calumniâ Iesuitæ refutare satis erit,Canone 7. de sacramentis dicit Caluinus,Deū in sacramētis promitte-re gratiam:vtique non electionis modo,sed & iustifica-tionis:Can. 4.Sacramenta esse sigilla euangelij. Euāgeliū vero nonne est promissio iustificationis præsentis per fidem?Canon.8.In Baptismo,inquit,Deus nos filij sui san-guine abluit,suo spiritu nos regenerat. In cœna carne san-guineque Christi nos pascit.&c. Cano.7.de Bapt.Baptis-mus hoc habet præcipuū,vt de gratuita peccatorū remissio-ne nos certiores faciat.Hoc vero quid est aliud,quàm præ-sens iustificatio?Ex his satis liquet calumnia Iesuitæ de sigillis æternæ electionis,id est,de præterito tantum.
units.tr: I could bring forth endless passages from the Christian Institutes to confirm these things. But from the Antidote of the Council itself it will be enough to refute the Jesuit's calumny: in canon 7 on the sacraments Calvin says that God promises grace in the sacraments, surely not only of election but also of justification. Canon 4: the sacraments are seals of the gospel. And is the gospel not the promise of present justification through faith? Canon 8: "In Baptism," he says, "God washes us in the blood of his Son, and regenerates us by his Spirit. In the Supper he feeds us with the flesh and blood of Christ," etc. Canon 7 on Baptism: baptism has this chief purpose, that it makes us more certain of the free remission of sins. But what is this other than present justification? From these things it is clear enough that the Jesuit's calumny about seals of eternal election, that is, about the past only, is false.

units.la: Quàm vero absurdè etiam colligit,sacramenta nō fore sigilla iustificationis præsentis,si ītatuantur sigilla electionis æternæ?Annō enim electio & iustificatio sūt [illegible, ~7 letters] ? quæ se mutuò non tollunt?Potius igitur contrarium sequitur:sunt sigilla electionis æternæ:Ergo iustificationis & gratiæ præsentis.Est enim iustificatio electionis effectus ita proprius, vt nulla huius absq; illa certitudo esse possit: siquidem quicunque in Christo iustificantur, in eodem electi sunt ante iacta mundi fundamendamenta:& quos Deus prædestinauit, hos etiam vocauit,iustificauit, & glorificauit.
units.tr: But how absurdly he also infers that the sacraments would not be seals of present justification if they are established as seals of eternal election! For are election and justification not things that do not cancel each other out? Rather, the opposite follows: they are seals of eternal election; therefore of justification and of present grace. For justification is so proper an effect of election that no certainty of it can exist without that: since whoever are justified in Christ are chosen in him before the foundation of the world; and whom God predestined, these he also called, justified and glorified.

units.la: Eat nunc Iesuita,& sententiam Caluini falsam,abfur-dam,perniciosam & impiam esse clamet.
units.tr: Let the Jesuit now go and cry out that Calvin's opinion is false, absurd, pernicious and impious.

units.la: Cur vero falsam? Quia, inquit, sacramenta solum ad præteritum, hoc est, ad gratiam electionis æternæ refert contra scripturam. At hæc calumnia iam refutata.
units.tr: Why false? Because, he says, it refers the sacraments only to the past, that is, to the grace of eternal election, contrary to Scripture. But this calumny has already been refuted.

units.la: Cur verò absurdam? Quia, inquit,per sacrament a vbfi-gnari cæfciētis promissiones,& infantes rectè baptizari docet: cum tamen paruuli rationis vsu & conscientiis carent. Sed nec paruulos ecclesiæ simpliciter vel ἀλόγως [?] vel ἀπαθῶς [?] esse, si promissam gratiam spectemus, licet actu nec ratiocinentur,nec credant, vt adulti: quin etiam si maximè non crederent non ideò tolli pædobaptismum, & confirmationem fidei per sacramenta,cùm plures sint fines:supra satis ostensum est.
units.tr: Why absurd? Because, he says, it teaches that the promises are sealed by the sacraments to those who believe, and that infants are rightly baptized; yet infants lack the use of reason and consciousness. But if we look at the promised grace, infants are not simply without reason or without feeling, though in act they neither reason nor believe as adults do; indeed, even if they did not believe at all, paedobaptism would not for that reason be abolished, nor the confirmation of faith through the sacraments, since there are several ends: this has been shown sufficiently above.

units.la: Cur verò perniciosam? Quia,inquit,filios fidelium iustos ac sanctos nasci docet,eisque sacramenta ad accipiendâ Christi gratiâ minimè necessaria esse,multis persuasit. Vnde consecutu est, vt non pauci eadem sacramenta contenat,atque interim multorum animæ paruulorū nō expiata salutaribus aquis,in æternis sordibus perseuerent. An verò perniciosum docere infantes fidelium nasci sanctos,hoc est,non alienos, sed hæredes fœderis,iuxta promissionem: Ero Deus tuus & seminis tui? Perniciosum ergo,quod docet Apostolus: Si radix sancta est,etiam rami. Et, Vxor infidelis sanctifi-cata est viro: alioqui certè liberi vestri impuri essent: nunc autem sancti sunt. Atqui hæc prima consolatio est piorum parentum, quòd sciunt, ramum cum radice sanctum esse, hoc est, & se & prolem suam ab vtero habere ius fœderis cum Deo, vi gratuitæ promissionis sibi & feminî suo factæ.
units.tr: Why do I call it pernicious? Because, he says, he taught that the children of believers are born just and holy, and he persuaded many that the sacraments are by no means necessary for receiving the grace of Christ. From this it followed that not a few neglect the sacraments, and meanwhile the souls of many infants, not cleansed by the saving waters, remain in eternal filth. But is it pernicious to teach that the infants of believers are born holy, that is, not strangers but heirs of the covenant, according to the promise: "I will be your God and the God of your seed"? Pernicious, then, is what the Apostle teaches: "If the root is holy, so are the branches." And: "The unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband; otherwise your children would certainly be unclean, but now they are holy." Indeed this is the first consolation of godly parents, that they know the branch is holy along with the root, that is, that both they and their offspring have from the womb a right of covenant with God, by virtue of the free promise made to them and to their seed.

units.la: At sunt natura filij iræ? Quis nescit? Vtrumque docet Caluinus: esse filios iræ, si naturam: & filios pacti, si gratiam spectes: iuxta illud Petri: Vos estis filij prophetarum, & pacta, &c. Illud contra Pelagianos, negantes peccatum originale: hoc contra sophistas, alligantes gratiam sacramentis: neutrum perniciosè: quia vtrumque verè, & cum scriptura. Consulatur eius Institutio Christiana: Et commentarius in verba Pauli: sumus omnes natura filij iræ. Inde petat Iesuita, & Selneccerus, & Hunnius, & omnis Caluinomastyx, quomodo peccatum originale omnibus naturaliter insit, non secus ac serpentes suum venenum ex utero afferunt: & nihilominus fidelium liberi ab utero sint semel benedictū: Quin si malunt, audiant, & concilient Dauidem confitentem de se: Ecce, in iniquitate genitus sum, & in peccato cocepit me mater mea: Et alibi tamen sic se erigēt: super te pro-tectum [?] sum ab utero, de uetre [?] matrū mea, Deus meus es tu: uel ipsum Deū sic de natura hominis queretem: Cogitatio cordis humani praua est a pueritia sua: Et tamē apud Ieremiam testatur: Priusquam formarem te in utero, noui: & antequam ires e uetre, sanctificaui te. Habet quomodo Caluinus fidelium infantes nascantur sancti, nempe secundum quid, non simpliciter. Iustos nasci, apud Caluinum reperiri, vix crediderim, nisi Iesuita ostendat. Neque enim sanctum & iustum esse, idem sunt in hac vita.
units.tr: But are they by nature children of wrath? Who does not know it? Calvin teaches both: that they are children of wrath if you look to nature, and children of the covenant if you look to grace, in line with that saying of Peter: "You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant," etc. The former is against the Pelagians, who deny original sin; the latter is against the sophists, who bind grace to the sacraments. Neither is pernicious, because both are true and agree with Scripture. Let the Jesuit, Selneccer, Hunnius, and every Calvin-scourger consult his Christian Institutes and his commentary on Paul's words, "we are all by nature children of wrath." Let them ask how original sin naturally clings to all, just as serpents bring their venom from the womb, and yet the children of believers are blessed from the womb once for all. Indeed, if they prefer, let them hear and reconcile David confessing of himself: "Behold, I was born in iniquity, and in sin my mother conceived me," and yet elsewhere he raises himself up thus: "I have been protected from the womb, from my mother's belly; you are my God." Or let them hear God himself speaking of the nature of man: "The thought of the human heart is evil from its youth." And yet to Jeremiah he testifies: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I sanctified you." Here is how Calvin holds that the infants of believers are born holy, namely in a certain respect, not absolutely. That they are born just, I could hardly believe is found in Calvin unless the Jesuit shows it. For to be holy and to be just are not the same thing in this life.

units.la: Iam quod affuit: Caluinum sacramenta ad accipiendam Christi gratiam minime necessaria esse multis persuasisse [?], indeque baptismi contemtum cum multarum animarum pernicie consecutum esse: id partim calumniosum est, partim aperte sophisticum. Calumniosum est, quod omnem sacramentorum necessitatem Caluinus negauerit: sophisticum quod baptismi contemtum, quem inde consecutum fingit Iesuita, doctrinae eius imputat.
units.tr: Now as to what he alleges: that Calvin has persuaded many that the sacraments are by no means necessary for receiving the grace of Christ, and that from this a contempt of baptism followed with the destruction of many souls: this is partly slanderous, partly plainly sophistical. It is slanderous, because Calvin denied all necessity of the sacraments; it is sophistical, because the contempt of baptism which the Jesuit imagines followed from it he imputes to Calvin's doctrine.

units.la: Non alligat Deum & gratiam sacramentis, nec fingit in his absolutam necessitatem, vt sophistae. Cum Bernhardo autem contemtum sacramenti, non priuatione damnare statuit. Hoccine vero est multis persuadere, sacramenta minime necessaria esse? Audiatur quaeso ipse in Institutione hac de re scribens: Iam, inquit, & ex eo explodendum esse eorum commentum, palam est, qui omnes nobaptizatos aeterna morti adiudicant, &c. Clara est Domini promissio: Quicunque in filium credit, non uidebit mortem, nec in iudicium uenietur, sed transiit a morte in uitam, nondum baptizatum nullibi damnasse reperitur. Quod in ea parte accipi nolo, (perinde, ac si baptismum contemni impune posse innuerem, quo contemtu violatur Domini foedus affirmo: tantum abest vt excusare sufficiat) tantum euincere iussit, non esse adeo necessarium, vt periisse protinus existimentur, cuius eius obtinendi ademta fuerit facultas. Atqui si eorum commento assentimur, eos omnes citra exceptionem damnabimus, quos a baptismo casus aliquis prohibuerit, quatacumque aliqua fide praditos, per qua Christus ipse possidetur? Et in antidoto. Facile, inquit, patiar, & quæ nobis Christus dedit salutis adiumenta, eorum [?]quæ necessarius dicatur, quàdo scilicet datur facultas. Quaquà semper admonendi sunt fideles, nō alia esse cuiusuis sacramenti necessitatem, quàm causa instrumentalis, cui nequaquam alligāda est Dei virtus. Voce sanè illâ nemo pius est, qui nō toto pectore exhorreat. Sacramenta: RES ESSE SUPERFLUAS, &c. Hæc ille: quæ Iesuitæ calumniam plus satis retundunt.
units.tr: Calvin does not bind God and grace to the sacraments, nor does he invent in them an absolute necessity as the sophists do. With Bernard, he has determined to condemn contempt of the sacrament, not its privation. Is this really to persuade many that the sacraments are by no means necessary? Let him be heard, I beg, writing on this matter himself in the Institutes: "Now, he says, it is also clear that the fiction of those who condemn all the unbaptized to eternal death must be exploded, etc. The promise of the Lord is clear: 'Whoever believes in the Son will not see death, nor come into judgment, but has passed from death into life'; nowhere is it found that he condemned the unbaptized who is not yet baptized. What I do not want to be accepted in that part" (as if I suggested that baptism may be despised with impunity, by whose contempt the covenant of the Lord is violated, I affirm; so far is it from sufficing to excuse it) "he ordered only to prove that it is not so necessary that those are thought to have perished at once, from whom the opportunity of obtaining it has been taken away. Yet if we assent to their fiction, we shall condemn without exception all whom some chance has prevented from baptism, however endowed with some faith by which Christ himself is possessed?" And in the Antidote: "I will easily bear," he says, "that the aids to salvation which Christ gave us be called necessary, namely when the opportunity is given. Yet the faithful are always to be admonished that the necessity of any sacrament is nothing other than an instrumental cause, to which the power of God must by no means be bound. Surely no one who is godly does not shudder from his whole heart at that voice: 'Sacraments are superfluous things,' etc." These are his words, which quite sufficiently refute the Jesuit's slander.

units.la: At liberi nascuntur sancti: Nō est ergo, cur baptizentur: & sequitur baptismi contemtus. Imò contrà: quia nascantur sancti, hoc est, filij & hæredes fœderis, est cur baptizentur. Neque enim, inquit alibi Calvinus, alio iure per baptismū aggregātur in ecclesiam, nisi quia ad corpus Christi tam antea pertinebant, quàm in luce ederentur. Secus certè non magis Christianorū quàm Turcarū liberi baptismo initiandi essent. Hinc Petrus Iudæos hortatur, vt baptizentur in nomine Iesu Christi: Cur? Quia inquit, Vestra & liberorum Vestrorum est promissio. Quòd ergo liberis nostris debetur, Turcarum liberis non debetur baptismus, hæc causa est: quòd illi inde ab vtero sunt, illi non sunt filij promissionis. Minimè itaque baptismi contemtus sequi potest ex eo, in quo piis prima baptismi petendi & conferendi causa est: nec pernicies animarum metuenda ex eo, in quo parentum iuxtà & liberorum prima consolatio, ac iustum baptismi desiderium fundatur. Quod si Iesuita pergat inanem arbitrari Pædobaptismum per hoc, quòd liberi ecclesiæ inde ab vtero fœderi accensentur, discat quæso ex suo magistro Lō-bardo, baptismum, qui datur etiam iam iustis, remissionis anæ per fidem darę, sacramentū esse.
