Sed ô duram magistri sententiam sic pronunciantis: Paruuli si absque Baptismo suerint defuncti, etiā cū deferuntur ad baptismū, damnantur: ô non perniciosam modò, sed impiā & crudelem Iesuitarum theologiam! quæ Deum elementis subiicit, eiusque virtutem (nolit velit) absolutā necessitate signis alligat, & multa infantum millia quibus baptismus, nullā ipsorū culpā contingere nequiuit, liano quasi imperio ad orcum relegat, quatumuis Chri-stus ipse regnum coelorum eis adiudicet. Scio praetexi Augustini authoritatem, qui infantes absque baptismo mortuos, necessario damnari, attamen in mitissima damnatione futuros alicubi scripserit. Sed si hic sanctissimi & doctissimi alioqui patris naevus ad ò eis placet, cur non alterum eiusdem, simili plane nitetem causa itidem defendunt: infantes etiam sine eucharistiae sumtione non posse seruari? Ambrosium quoque huc rapiunt. Sed libros, quibus hoc exstat, Prosperi potius quàm Ambrosij esse, eruditi non sine causa censen. Nam quid Ambrosius senserit, vel ex oratione de obitu Valentiniani li-quet. Quàm vero etiam pie Bernardus de pio nō baptizato: Propter ius sit mihi Deus, inquit, quia huc ego ob solā aquam, si defuerit, nequaquam omnino possim desperare salutem, nec vacuam credere fidem, nec confundere spem, nec excidere charitatem: tantum si aquam non contemtu, sed sola prohibeat impossibilitas.
units.tr: "But children are born holy: there is therefore no reason why they should be baptized, and contempt of baptism follows." On the contrary: because they are born holy, that is, sons and heirs of the covenant, there is reason why they should be baptized. "For," Calvin says elsewhere, "they are not otherwise admitted into the Church through baptism by any other right, except that they already belonged to the body of Christ before they were born into the light." Otherwise the children of Christians would be no more to be initiated by baptism than the children of Turks. Hence Peter exhorts the Jews to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ: "Why? Because," he says, "the promise is yours and your children's." What is owed to our children, the children of Turks are not owed baptism; the reason is this: that the former are from the womb, the latter are not children of the promise. Least of all, then, can contempt of baptism follow from that in which the first cause of seeking and conferring baptism lies for the godly, nor should the destruction of souls be feared from that in which the first consolation of parents and children, and the just desire for baptism, is founded. But if the Jesuit persists in thinking that paedobaptism is empty because the children of the Church are counted in the covenant from the womb, let him learn, I beg, from his own master Lombard that baptism, which is given even to the already just, is the sacrament of giving remission of sins through faith. But oh, the harsh pronouncement of the master, who declares thus: "Infants, if they have died without baptism, are condemned even though they are brought to baptism." Oh, the theology of the Jesuits, not merely pernicious but impious and cruel! It subjects God to the elements, binds his power by absolute necessity to signs, and by this quasi-command consigns many thousands of infants, to whom baptism could not come through no fault of their own, to hell, although Christ himself adjudges the kingdom of heaven to them. I know Augustine's authority is put forward, who wrote that infants who died without baptism are necessarily condemned, yet that they will be in the mildest condemnation somewhere. But if this blemish of an otherwise most holy and learned father pleases them so much, why do they not defend another of his, resting on exactly the same reason: that infants also cannot be saved without partaking of the Eucharist? They also drag in Ambrose. But scholars not without cause judge that the books in which this stands are by Prosper rather than by Ambrose. For what Ambrose thought is clear even from the oration on the death of Valentinian. How piously, indeed, Bernard speaks of the godly unbaptized: "God is my witness," he says, "that for the sake of water alone, if it be lacking, I can by no means utterly despair of salvation, nor believe faith empty, nor confound hope, nor fall from love, provided that impossibility, not contempt, prevents the water."

units.la: Denique impiam esse Caluini sententiam, clamat Iesuita. Quid ita? Quia, inquit, sacramentū falsum, ministros sacrilegos, Deū mendaces, & quasi periurium facit. Etenim si sacramentū diminutum est, tuēdū atque sigillū, quo electionis aeterna promissio obsignatur, quotes contingit (contingit autē frequentissimè) et reprobi baptizētur: totīes itē contingit, ut sacramenta alia verba sint falsa, & ore ministri mentiatur Deus. Haec calumnia caeteris acerbior & impudentior. Sed caput eius de sigillis non praesentis gratiae, sed raeteritae ratium electionis, supra est refutatum. Caetera uno verbo expediuntur: Sacramenta promittere & obsignare gratiam in usu legitimo: qui non est, cum a reprobis suscipiuntur. Hoc solum vniuersam calumniam in fumum dissipare poterat. Sed respondebo distinctius.
units.tr: Finally, the Jesuit cries out that Calvin's opinion is impious. Why so? Because, he says, "it makes the sacrament false, the ministers sacrilegious, and God a liar, and as it were a perjurer. For if the sacrament is diminished, the guarantee and seal by which the promise of eternal election is sealed, as often as it happens (and it happens very frequently) that the reprobate are baptized, so often it also happens that the other sacraments are false words, and God lies through the mouth of the minister." This slander is more bitter and more shameless than the rest. But its main point, about seals not of present grace but of past decree of election, has been refuted above. The rest is disposed of in one word: the sacraments promise and seal grace in lawful use, which does not occur when they are received by the reprobate. This alone could have dissolved the whole slander into smoke. But I will answer more distinctly.

units.la: Sacramentum non fit falsum, licet aliquando reprobis fidem simulantibus frustrà detur. Manet enim in se sigillum gratiae, licet ipsis non sit, quia non credunt: vt sol manet lucidus, licet caecis non luceat, quia non vident. Est enim signum pactionale, sic offerens & obsignans gratiam, vt simul fidem, & conuersionem postulet, quae non afferentibus nec confert aliquid vel obsignat, nec est ipsis sacramentum, hoc est, sigillum gratiae ipsorum vitio:quia non vsus,sed horribilis profanatio est sacramenti,cū à reprobis sine fide sumitur.Extra vero vsum diuinitus institutum, nihil habere sacramenti ratione, scriptura passim docet:Si fueris transgressor legis,circuci- sio tua facta est præputium. Et: Hoc non est dominica cœna edere. Et:Qui manducat bouē,est quasi qui cane cædat. Baptismus Simonis magi verum fuit sacramentū:sed ipsi nō fuit,propter hypocrisin,teste Petro:Non est tibi pars, neque sors in hoc negotio,cor enim tuum non est rectum,&c. Bu-celia dominica verum fuit sacramentum,sed Iudæ fuit venenum,non quia malum fuit,sed quia bonum malus male accepit.Denique ipso Lombardo teste,baptismus æque sanctus est datus bono vel malo.Ergo & æque verus.
units.tr: The sacrament does not become false, even though it is sometimes given in vain to the reprobate who feign faith. The seal of grace remains in itself, though it does not reach them, because they do not believe: just as the sun remains bright, though it does not shine for the blind, because they do not see. For it is a covenant sign, offering and sealing grace in such a way that it also requires faith and conversion; to those who do not bring these, it confers and seals nothing, and it is not a sacrament to them, that is, a seal of grace, because of their own fault. For it is not a use, but a horrible profanation of the sacrament, when it is received by the reprobate without faith. Outside the use divinely instituted, Scripture everywhere teaches that there is no sacrament at all: "If you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision" (Rom. 2.). And: "This is not to eat the Lord's Supper" (1 Cor. 11.). And: "He who eats an ox is as one who kills a dog" (Isa. 66.). The baptism of Simon Magus was a true sacrament, but it was not one for him, because of his hypocrisy, as Peter testified: "You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right," etc. (Acts 8.). The Lord's Supper was a true sacrament for Judas, yet it was poison to him, not because it was evil, but because the evil man received what was good in an evil way. Finally, by the testimony of Lombard himself, baptism is given equally holy to the good and to the bad. Therefore it is equally true.

units.la: Tu ne vero Petrum dices sacrilegum,quod Simoni mago homini reprobo,sed fidem apostolicam profitenti,Dei nomine gratiam obtulit,& quantum in se fuit,ob signauit per baptismum? Atqui id nō fecit absolutè,sed ex hypothesi,si vere crederet:sicut Philippus dicit Eunucho:Licet tibi baptizari,si credis toto corde. Non vere credenti igitur nihil obsignauit,vt recte Lombardus verster:Simoni mago,inquit, Visibilis baptismus nihil profuit, quia invisibilis non affuit. Tu etiā,fecit ex officio,quod non erat,scrutari arcana cordium: vel diuinæ prædestinationis abyssum:Sed baptizare fidem profitentes,siue hypocritæ essent,sine non.De occultis enim non iudicat ecclesia,sed solus Deus καρδιογνώστης [?]. Par est ratio aliorum ministrorum omnium,qui de baptizandis nō ex prædestinatione Dei,sed ex professione hominū,& Christi mandato iudicare debēt:quod cum faciunt,nō ipsi,sed reprobi hypocritæ,sacramentis se ingerentes sacrilegi existunt.
units.tr: But will you call Peter a sacrilegious man because he offered grace in God's name to Simon Magus, a reprobate man, who professed apostolic faith, and, as far as lay in him, sealed it through baptism? Yet he did not do this absolutely, but on a condition: if he truly believed, just as Philip says to the eunuch: "You may be baptized, if you believe with all your heart." Therefore he sealed nothing for one who did not truly believe, as Lombard rightly puts it: "Visible baptism," he says, "did nothing for Simon Magus, because the invisible was not present." You also, it was not his office to search out the secrets of hearts or the abyss of divine predestination; but to baptize those who profess faith, whether they were hypocrites or not. For the Church does not judge hidden things, but God alone, the knower of hearts [καρδιογνώστης]. The same reasoning holds for all other ministers, who must judge concerning baptism not by God's predestination but by men's profession and Christ's command. When they do this, it is not they, but the reprobate hypocrites, who push themselves upon the sacraments, who become sacrilegious.

units.la: Apage vero etiam blasphemiam,Deum per os ministrorum mentiri,si reprobis hypocritis nondum patefactis sacramenta conferant.Tibi-ne Deus per os Petri Simonem baptizantis mentitus est?Serio ac veraciter omnibus tam verbo,quam symbolis adoptionem & gratiam suam offert ac donare vult,sed cum conditione si credant:ac præcipit,vt credant,& fide gratiam oblatam accipiant.Infidelibus vero & hypocritis adeo non promittit vel obsignat adoptionis & electionis gratia, cum sacramenta ad se rapiunt,vt etiam iudictum minetur. Manet ergo verax in offerendo, licet infidelibus gratia oblata pereat.
units.tr: Away also with the blasphemy that God lies through the mouth of the ministers if they confer the sacraments on reprobate hypocrites not yet revealed. Did God lie through the mouth of Peter baptizing Simon? In earnest and truly, God offers and wills to give his adoption and grace to all, both by word and by signs, but with the condition: if they believe. He commands them to believe and to receive the offered grace by faith. Yet to unbelievers and hypocrites he does not promise or seal the grace of adoption and election, when they snatch the sacraments to themselves; indeed he threatens judgment. Therefore he remains true in offering, although the grace offered perishes for unbelievers.

units.la: At non offert tantum, clamat Iesuita, sed etiā reipsa praebet, cum reipsa homines baptizantur. Quidni? Nā & hoc fatetur Calvinus in Antidoto Artic. Parif.sic[?] inquiens: Offerri nobis in baptismo & exhiberi tu remissionem peccatorum, tu Spiritus sancti gratiam pij omnes confitentur. Sed, inquit alibi, hic boni patres pro sua crassitie non animaduertunt, quicquid nobis gratia per sacramenta confertur, nihilominus fidei imputandū. Qui enim a sacramentis fidem separat, perinde facit ac si anima a corpore tolleret. Praebet ergo Deus, quae offert, sed credentibus. Incredulis nec promittit nec praebet aliquid, quandiu tales manent. Idque ipsorum culpa, quia oblata bona, infidelitate respuunt, & offerentem Deum, quantum in se est, iudifi-cantur. Est ergo calumnia haec Iesuitae nō minus impu-dens, & in Deum blasphemia, quam erat Iudaeorum accusantium Deum perfidię, nisi etiam incredulis pactum praestaret: quam retundens apostolus: Num, inquit, incredulitas eorum fidem Dei inanem reddet? Absit. Esto Deus verax, omnis homo mendax.
units.tr: "But he not only offers," the Jesuit shouts, "he also actually gives, since men are actually baptized." Why not? For Calvin also confesses this in his Antidote to the Articles of Paris, saying: "That the forgiveness of sins and the grace of the Holy Spirit are offered and exhibited to us in baptism, all the godly confess. But, he says elsewhere, these good fathers, in their dullness, do not notice that whatever grace is conferred on us through the sacraments is nonetheless to be imputed to faith. For he who separates faith from the sacraments does just as one who would take the soul from the body." God therefore gives what he offers, but to believers. To unbelievers he neither promises nor gives anything, as long as they remain such, and this is by their own fault, because they reject the good things offered by unbelief, and, as far as in them lies, they make God, the one offering, unworthy of faith. This calumny of the Jesuit is therefore no less shameless, and a blasphemy against God, than the accusation of the Jews, who charged God with perfidy, unless he also kept his covenant with unbelievers. The apostle refutes this, saying: "What then? If some did not believe, will their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid. Let God be true, but every man a liar" (Rom. 3.).

units.la: Sed age in Iesuitae caput blasphemiā retorqueamus. Docet ipse cum Lombardo magistro, reprobatione esse, & nihil aliud esse, quam Deum nolle aliquorum misereri. Sic enim magister eam definit. Fac ergo Iesuita opero[?] operato baptismi vel missae gratiam sanctificationis conferre Simoni mago, vel simili reprobo. An non hic & ipse sacrilegus erit, & sacramentum faciet sacrilegii, conferens gratiam reprobo, cuius Deus misereri nolit? Imo an non ipsum Deum faciet mendacem, & sibi contrarium eius nomine conferens, seu eum conferre testificans (si modo Deum a sacramentis penitus non excludit) gratiam sanctificationis reprobo, cui tamen nihil conferre ab aeterno decreuerit, & cuius misereri nolit Deus? Ab hac blasphemia, quomodo stante opinione operis operati[?] se expediat Iesuita, ipse viderit. Quomodo-cunque tamen expediet, simul calumniam suam Calvino abstergeret.
units.tr: But come, let us turn this blasphemy back upon the head of the Jesuit. He himself teaches with the master Lombard that reprobation is nothing other than God's unwillingness to show mercy to some. For the master defines it so. Suppose then, the Jesuit, that by the work wrought (ex opere operato) of baptism or of the Mass he confers the grace of sanctification on Simon Magus or a similar reprobate: will he not himself be sacrilegious here, and will he not make the sacrament an instrument of sacrilege, by conferring grace on a reprobate, on whom God is unwilling to have mercy? Indeed, will he not make God himself a liar, and contrary to himself, if in God's name he confers, or testifies that God confers (if indeed he does not wholly exclude God from the sacraments), the grace of sanctification on a reprobate, for whom God from eternity decreed nothing of the kind, and on whom God is unwilling to have mercy? How the Jesuit will extricate himself from this blasphemy, while the doctrine of the work wrought stands, he himself will see. However he extricates himself, he would at the same time wipe away his calumny against Calvin.

units.la: Atque hactenus theatrici huius declamatoris proter-uitas breuiter respondisse sufficiat. Quae porro ad finem ibi disputat, nihil nos attinent: in eos vero, in quos dicuntur, Schwenkfeldivm & huius fraterculos Vbiquitarios, communes doctrinæ de persona Christi & sacramentis depravatores, sane valeant.
units.tr: Let it suffice to have answered briefly thus far the impudence of this theatrical declaimer. As for what he further discusses about the end, it does not concern us; but against those against whom it is said, Schwenkfeld and his little brothers, the Ubiquitarians, corruptors of the common doctrine about the person of Christ and the sacraments, let it indeed be applied.

units.la: Tibi vero, illustris & generose Domine, Vrsinianas hasce de sacramentis explicationes consecrare visum est, quòd sciam, te non modò pr[?] accuratissimo iudicio tuo, necnon singulari cœlestis doctrinæ scientia, quam lectione, meditatione & tractatione sacrarum literarum indefessa comparatam, ceu verum nobilitatis decus, cum generis splendore coniunxisti, de hac tota Disputatione optimè iudicare posse: sed & infaustam illa sophistarum de sacramentis placita, cum reliquo papatus fermento, toto pectore auersari: sincerâm vero ecclesiarum nostrarum doctrinam, hoc libello exegetico repetitâ & illustratam ex animo ampleƈi: nec ampleƈi modò, sed & incredibili pietatis zelo in celeberrima præfectura tua Alceana, ad Dei gloriam & subditorum utilitatem tueri ac propagare: quo sane nomine inter Palatinatus Heroas ab Illustrissimis Principibus nostris proxima laus tibi merito debetur.
units.tr: To you, illustrious and noble Lord, it has seemed fitting to dedicate these explanations of the sacraments from Ursinus, because I know that you, joining the splendour of your lineage with the true glory of nobility, a learning of heavenly doctrine gained by the tireless reading, meditation and handling of the sacred letters, are able not only through your most accurate judgment to judge well of this whole disputation, but also with your whole heart to turn away from the unhappy opinions of the sophists about the sacraments, together with the rest of the leaven of Popery; and that you have embraced with your whole soul the sincere doctrine of our churches, repeated and illustrated in this exegetical little book, and not only embraced it, but also, with an incredible zeal for piety, defend and propagate it in your most famous prefecture of Alzey, to the glory of God and the benefit of your subjects; for which reason, among the heroes of the Palatinate, the next praise is rightly due to you from our most illustrious princes.

units.la: Accessit, quòd non modò clarissimum Vrsini, Theologi magni, & olim quasi cuiusdam ecclesiarum nostrarum Iosephi nomen, eruditissimaque scripta, plurimi semper fecisti, sed & me tuo indignum fauore, nunc benignè complecteris, parique beneuolentia hanc scholam nostram, in cuius vsum hæc ἐξηγήματα[?] olim ab Vrsino tradita, & nunc à me qualicunque studio sic elaborata sunt, vt forte me alterum ab illo parentem agnoscere possint, amanter proseque-ris: quorum omnium tum indicia non obscura ipse aliquando coram dedisti, tum testem locupletem habeo Marcum Beumlerum, ecclesiæ vestræ pastorem atque ephorum, virum doctissimum iuxta & studiosissimum Generositatis tuæ, meiq. amantissimum, qui honorificum tuum de studiis meis iudicium mihi non semel exposuit: quod licet non merear, tamen officiis meis conseruare atq. augere debeo & percupio. Accipe igitur hoc qualecunq. obseruantiæ in te meæ verum ἐνδηγήματα[?], mèque & scholam nostram, ea, qua facis, clementia & fauore complecti perge. Dominus Iesvs G. T. cum illustri familia vniuersa Ecclesiæ & Reipubl.diu incolumem feruet. Amen. Heidelbergæ Dominica Inuocauit. Anno reparatæ salutis cIↄ Iↄ.xci.
units.tr: Add to this that you not only have always held in the highest regard the most famous name of Ursinus, a great theologian and once, as it were, the Joseph of our churches, and his most learned writings, but also now kindly embrace me, unworthy of your favour, and with equal goodwill you lovingly support this school of ours, for whose use these explanations, once delivered by Ursinus and now worked out by me with whatever diligence, may perhaps recognise me as a second father after him. Of all these things you yourself have once before given me clear indications in person, and I have a worthy witness in Marcus Beumler, pastor and superintendent of your church, a man most learned and most zealous, and most devoted both to your Nobility and to me, who has more than once set forth to me your honourable judgment of my studies. Although I do not deserve it, yet I ought, and greatly desire, to preserve and increase it by my services. Accept therefore this little work, whatever it is, as a true token of my respect for you, and continue to embrace me and our school with the clemency and favour that you show. May the Lord Jesus Christ, God our Saviour, keep the whole illustrious family, the Church and the Commonwealth, safe for a long time. Amen. Heidelberg, Sunday Invocavit. In the year of restored salvation 1591.

units.la: David Parevs.
units.tr: David Pareus.

units.la: IN QVARTAM EXPLICAT.] catecheticarum partem, de gratitudine,
units.tr: On the Fourth Part of the Catechetical Explanation, concerning gratitude

units.la: AD AMPLISSIMOS ET CLARISSIMOS VIROS, D. IVSTVM REVBERVM, Electoralis Palatinatus Cancellarium: & D. NICOLAVM DOBBINVM, curiæ augustæ consiliarium. Dominos & fautores suos perpetua obseruantia colendos, PRÆFATIO: QVA DE FVNESTIS QVORVNDAM Theologorum seculi huius fcriptionibus disseritur: & Iohannes Caluinus fortissimus Christi gloriæ assertor à calumnia Arianisfmi paucis vindicatur.
units.tr: PREFACE: TO THE MOST DISTINGUISHED AND ILLUSTRIOUS MEN, Sir Justus Reuber, Chancellor of the Electoral Palatinate, and Sir Nicolaus Dobbin, councillor of the Augsburg court, to be honoured with perpetual respect as my lords and patrons. IN WHICH IS DISCUSSED THE DEADLY WRITINGS OF CERTAIN THEOLOGIANS OF THIS CENTURY, AND JOHN CALVIN, THE VALIANT CHAMPION OF CHRIST'S GLORY, IS BRIEFLY VINDICATED FROM THE CALUMNY OF ARIANISM.

units.la: Cogit me, viri amplissimi, fautores colendi, argumentum huius partis, quæ est de gratitudine hominis erga Deum, in communem bonorum querelam descendere de Bruto mundi stupore, fœdáque ingratitudine pro summis bonis, quibus Deus Optim. Max. extremum hoc seculum nostrum quasi cumulo facto adbruit: nec tamen aliud fere proficit, quàm quòd ingrati homines quotidie in peius ruunt, quasi qui cum optimo benefactore suo bellum susceperint. Quanta enim quæso diuinæ benignitatis testium nubes nos vndique circumstat? Quid huic seculo negatum est, quod homines ad bene beatèque transfigendam vitam expetât? Taceo communia bona. Singularia quot sunt, & quàm eximia? Renascens euangelij lux, & doctrinæ sincéritas: sacramentorum puritas: verus Dei cultus & inuocatio: restituta scripturæ sacræ lectio: antichristi detectio: tenebrarum difcuffio: superstitionum fuga: idolorum interitus: ecclesiæ denique quasi postliminio reparata libertas. Hos verò tam inæstimabiles thesauros quotusquisque satis curat? ac non potiùs vel bruto stupore præterit, vel turpiter
units.tr: Gentlemen, most distinguished and honoured patrons, I am driven to take up, in this part of the catechism, which concerns man's gratitude towards God, the common complaint about the brutish dullness of the world and its foul ingratitude for the greatest blessings with which God, the best and greatest, has heaped up, as it were, this last age of ours. Yet this achieves almost nothing beyond the fact that ungrateful men fall daily into worse ways, as though they had declared war upon their best benefactor. For, I ask you, how great a cloud of divine kindness's witnesses surrounds us on every side? What has been denied to this age that men might need in order to pass their life well and happily? I say nothing of the common blessings. How many and how outstanding are the particular ones? The renewed light of the gospel and the purity of doctrine; the purity of the sacraments; the true worship and invocation of God; the restored reading of Holy Scripture; the unmasking of the Antichrist; the dispelling of darkness; the flight from superstitions; the destruction of idols; and finally the liberty of the Church, restored as if by a return of rights. Yet how few take sufficient care for these priceless treasures? Rather, people either pass them by with brutish dullness, or shamefully trample them underfoot.

units.la: Lines run as printed; no footnotes on this page. Iupiter[?] conculcat? In Athenienses olim dicebat ille, cire[?] eos, quid rectum sit, sed non facere. At quanto turpius, nos Christianos non modo non facere, quæ recta scimus, & scimus non, ut illi, ex naturæ tantum luce, sed ex Christi doctrina: verum etiam facere, quæ nō recta intelligimus? Grassatur vulgo cū profanitate securitas, ambitio, luxus, inuidia, doctrinæ contemptus, sacramentorum abusus, concionum fastidium, & quid non? Quan-tus numerus, qui veritatem in iniustitia detinet? quantus eorum, qui Deum se scire profitentur, factis negat? quantus denique apostatarum, qui vel ingenij leuitate impulsi, ad illas Ægyptias respectant, vel à spiritibus deceptoribus seducti, à Christo ad antichri-stum quotidie desciscunt, canum instar ad vomitum redeuntes? Sed hæc fortassis popularis est ingra-titudo.
units.tr: Lines run as printed; no footnotes on this page. Iupiter[?] tramples? Of the Athenians that man once said that they knew what was right but did not do it. But how much more shameful it is for us Christians not only not to do what we know to be right, and know it not, as they did, from the light of nature alone, but from the teaching of Christ, and yet actually to do what we do not understand to be right! Carelessness, ambition, luxury, envy, contempt for doctrine, abuse of the sacraments, weariness of sermons, and what not, rage commonly along with profanity. How great is the number of those who hold the truth captive in unrighteousness? How great is the number of those who profess that they know God, yet deny him by their deeds? How great, finally, is the number of apostates who, either driven by lightness of mind, look back to those Egyptian fleshpots, or, seduced by deceiving spirits, fall away daily from Christ to the Antichrist, returning like dogs to their vomit? But perhaps this ingratitude is that of the common people.

units.la: Utinam vero antistitum maior pars ad has fraćturas ascenderet, ac sepem pro domo Israelis obduceret: nec vulpium instar per ecclesiæ vastitates & scandala publica sagi-nam quæreret, quod de sui temporis prophe-tis Ezechiel querebatur. Magna ecclesiæ pestis semper fuit, cauponari verbum Dei, vel inflectere ad hominū affectus, ad potentium libidinem & gratiam, ad fastū & inanem gloriam, ad quæstum & luxum. At longè nocentior pestis, quæ hodie cum multitudinis applausu ecclesiæ viscera depascit, quòd ecclesiastica iudicia fere iacet: & interim per ambitionē, per auaritiā, per inuidiā, nihilque non mouendi libidinem, quo quisque est impudentior & dicacior eò digniorem in ecclesia locū affectat, & per gratiam popularem obtinet. Hinc infaustę illę digladiationes inter ἱεροφάντας[?], qui magna ex parte bellum non pacem meditantes, ac litem de lite feretes in ecclesia, summo cauere videntur studio, ne cōtrouersiæ ecclesiasticæ legitimè cognoscantur, disceptentur, vel etiam sopiantur, ex quibus illi rem & gloriam sibi parare studio habent. Hinc & funestæ tot scriptiones, nullo mansuetudinis vel caritatis spiritu tinctæ, sed atro virulentiæ sale perfusæ, ac venenatis maledicentię[?] aculeis infestæ, quib. sacrosancta Theologia nunc scilicet exor-[?] natur, & pietatis doctrina ad posteritatem transmittere-[?] tur. Hoc mali caput est: quod vt intelligatur magis, dico duo maxime earum scriptionum prodire nunc genera.
units.tr: Would that the greater part of the bishops would climb up to these breaches and set a hedge before the house of Israel, and not, like foxes, seek their prey amid the devastations and public scandals of the Church, as Ezekiel complained of the prophets of his own time! The word of God has always been a great plague of the Church when it is peddled like merchandise, or bent to men's passions, to the lust and favour of the powerful, to pride and empty glory, to gain and luxury. But a far more harmful plague is that which today, with the applause of the multitude, devours the vitals of the Church, namely that ecclesiastical judgment lies almost prostrate, and meanwhile, through ambition, through avarice, through envy, and through a lust for stirring up everything, whoever is the more shameless and more abusive seeks a more honourable place in the Church, and obtains it through popular favour. Hence those unhappy brawls among the hierophants, who, for the most part meditating war rather than peace and heaping strife upon strife in the Church, seem to take the utmost care that ecclesiastical controversies should not be properly examined, debated, or even laid to rest, since they are eager to win for themselves reputation and glory from them. Hence also come so many baleful writings, tinged with no spirit of gentleness or charity, but drenched in the black salt of virulence and hostile to others with the venomous stings of slander, by which, forsooth, the most sacred theology is now adorned, and the teaching of piety is handed down to posterity. This is the head of the evil; and so that it may be understood better, I say that two chief kinds of those writings now come forth.

units.la: Vnum est mere συκοφαντικὸν, quo defunctorum iuxta & superstitum, fidelium Christi seruorum, deque ecclesiae praeclare meritorum, Zwinglij, Caluini, Buceri, Martyris, Vrsini, Zanchij, Bezae, Grynaei, & aliorum, qui σωμα-[illegible, ~6 letters] corporis Christi ab euangelio alienam esse docent, cineres foedè conspurcantur, fama laceratur, commentaria (quae alioqui plagiarij illi priuatim in mufeis post pulpita sua nefarie suppilant) Theonino dente roduntur, sententiae depraauantur, verba per calumniam torquentur, ipsi denique tetetrimarum haeresium authores proclamantur.
units.tr: One is purely calumnious, by which the ashes of the dead as well as of the living—of faithful servants of Christ and of men who deserved well of the Church, such as Zwingli, Calvin, Bucer, Martyr, Ursinus, Zanchius, Beza, Grynaeus, and others who teach that the body of Christ is alien to the gospel—are foully defiled, reputations are torn to pieces, commentaries (which those plagiarists otherwise secretly and wickedly steal in their private studies behind their pulpits) are gnawed with a Theonine tooth, opinions are perverted, words are twisted by calumny, and the authors themselves are finally proclaimed as originators of the most abominable heresies.

units.la: In hoc post magistrum illum Vbiquitariae factionis Schmidlinum nuper excellebat Selneccerus, & nunc excellit Hunius, & alter Heilbrunnerus: quorum primus centones duodecim capitum scelerate compilatos, fere absque librorum & paginarum notis pridem in vulgus disseminauit: tertius quindecim capita errorum Caluinisticorum cosimili farragine nuper eunlgauit: medius ille quaestionarius scriptor, Caluino praecipue Arianismi crimen, pari compilatione locorum, quae Patres de Christo interpretati sunt, ille paulo aliter accepit, impingere non est veritus. Atqui scelceratior nulla est ingratitudo quam maledicere illis, quorum labore profeceris, quorumque tam praeclara in ecclesiam extant merita, nulla petulantia intolerabilior, quam mordere & verberare conseruos: conuiciis lacessere surdos: nihil theologis indignum magis, quam συκοφαντεῖν.
units.tr: In this respect, after that master of the Ubiquitarian faction, Schmidlin, Selnecker recently excelled, and now Hunnius excels, and another, Heilbrunner. The first of these long ago spread among the public twelve chapters of centones wickedly compiled, almost without notes of books and pages; the third recently published fifteen chapters of Calvinistic errors in a similar hodgepodge; and that middle one, the questioning writer, did not hesitate to lay against Calvin especially the charge of Arianism, by a similar compilation of passages which the Fathers interpreted about Christ, though he took them in a somewhat different way. Yet there is no more wicked ingratitude than to speak ill of those by whose labour you have profited, and whose merits to the Church are so distinguished; no petulance is more intolerable than to bite and beat fellow servants, to assail the deaf with abuse; nothing is more unworthy of theologians than to slander.

units.la: Exemplo sit vel vnus ille locus Gen. 3. de femine mulieris contrituro caput serpentis: quod horribiliter a Caluino depravatum vociferantur, quòd femē mulieris nō indiuiduē de solo Christo, sed collectiuē de tota mulieris posteritate atque ecclesia interpretatur. Atqui si frontem haberent, & Caluini interpretationem non truncatam, sed integram recitarent, facile illos tam crassae calumniae puderet. Vt enim tacea, multos ante Caluinum veteres, & in his Chrysostomum sic interpretari. Primo negare nunquam audebunt femen serpentis, cui femen mulieris opponitur, propria significatione colleïctivé i-stic intelligi. Deinde, calunia manifesta in eo est, quòd inimicitias ad homines & serpentes externos à Caluino restringi scribant. Expressè enim addit, Deû sub nomi-ne serpentis, Sathana hic maximè petere, & in eû stringere iudicij fulmen. Tertia, semen mulieris sic eum de ecclesia interpretari, vt tamen Christum ecclesiæ caput, extra quod nulla est victoria, præcipuè includat: testantur eius verba, quæ illi sceleratè detruncant, cùm addit: Cùm experientia doceat, multû abesse, quàm supra diabolum emergant omnes filij Adæ: ad caput vnû venire necesse est, & reperiamus, ad quos pertineat victoria: Sic Paulus à se-mine Abraha ad Christû nos deducit, &c. Hoccine verò est, in externo hominum & serpentû dissidio subsistere? victoriam ad homines restringere? Christum excludere?
units.tr: Let the one passage Genesis 3 concerning the seed of the woman who shall bruise the serpent's head serve as an example. They loudly cry out that it was horribly distorted by Calvin, because he interprets the seed of the woman not individually of Christ alone, but collectively of the whole posterity of the woman and of the Church. Yet if they had any shame, and had recited Calvin's interpretation not mutilated but whole, such a gross calumny would easily make them blush. For, to say nothing of the many ancient writers before Calvin, and among them Chrysostom, who so interpret it. First, they will never dare to deny that the seed of the serpent, to which the seed of the woman is opposed, is there understood collectively in its proper meaning. Second, the calumny is plain in this, that they write that Calvin restricts the enmity to men and external serpents. For he expressly adds that under the name of serpent, God chiefly aims at Satan here, and hurls the thunderbolt of judgment against him. Third, that he so interprets the seed of the woman of the Church, that nevertheless he especially includes Christ, the head of the Church, outside whom there is no victory: his words testify this, which they wickedly cut short, when he adds: "Since experience teaches that it is far from true that all the sons of Adam rise above the devil, it is necessary to come to one head, and we find to whom the victory belongs. Thus Paul leads us from the seed of Abraham to Christ, etc." Is this indeed to remain in an external quarrel between men and serpents? To restrict victory to men? To exclude Christ?

units.la: Et pergit tamen Hunius calumniari: nihilominus alia complura euidentissima Caluinum eludere oracula de Christo : Iudæorum blasphemiis patrocinari: Arianorum hæresim promouere: argumenta ecclesiæ eneruare: patres orthodoxos de ponte præcipitare. Grauia hæc sunt crimina, quæ diluerem hic facilè, si paucis dilui vellent. Sed ex primis duobus criminationum exemplis cætera iudicentur.
units.tr: And yet Hunnius goes on slandering; nevertheless he also mocks Calvin with several other most evident oracles about Christ: that he defends the blasphemies of the Jews, promotes the heresy of the Arians, weakens the arguments of the Church, and throws the orthodox Fathers headlong from the bridge. These are grave charges, which I would easily refute here if they wished to be refuted in a few words. But from the first two examples of these accusations let the rest be judged.

units.la: An quæso euidentissimum oraculum est, cùm Moses dicit: Bara Elohim: verbum singulare cû nomine plurali constructum, vnitatem essentiæ diuinæ, & trinitatem personarum denotare? Hanc parum solidam tantæ rei probationem videri sibi Caluinus scripsit. At si tam firmum & tam euidens hoc est trinitatis argumentum, cur, tu Huni, in tractatu tuo de trinitate illud primo loco non posuisti, cur totum omisisti?
units.tr: Is it, I ask you, a most evident oracle when Moses says: Bara Elohim—a singular verb constructed with a plural noun—denoting the unity of the divine essence and the trinity of persons? Calvin wrote that this proof of so great a matter seemed to him rather weak. But if this argument for the Trinity is so firm and so evident, why, Hunnius, did you not place it first in your treatise on the Trinity? Why did you omit it altogether?

units.la: Verba Heuæ, Gen. 4. Canithischath Iehouah: Caluinus reddidit: Acquisiui virum Domino, clamat ille, depraua-tionem esse euidentissimi testimonij deitatis Messiæ: quia Heua dicat: Acquisiui virum Dominum: quoniam ath Hebræis perpetuò nota fit quarti casus. At si hoc verum, cùm LXX. reddiderunt: [illegible, ~6 letters] Thargum: coram Domino? vetus Latina, & Melanchthon, per Deû, Luthe-ri germanica versio ante 45. annum: desz Herren, Domini? An & isti cum Caluino iudaizant? Exempla plura non addam.
units.tr: The words of Eve, Gen. 4: Canithischath Iehouah: Calvin rendered them: I have gotten a man from the Lord. He cries out that this is a corruption of the most evident testimony to the deity of the Messiah, because Eve says: I have gotten a man the Lord; since ath is always a sign of the accusative case among the Hebrews. But if this is true, why did the LXX render [illegible, ~6 letters], and the Chaldee paraphrast Onkelos before the Lord? The old Latin version and Melanchthon, through God; Luther's German version before the 45th year: des Herren, of the Lord. Do these too Judaize with Calvin? I will not add more examples.

units.la: Quid ergo? Hæc & alia nonnulli à patribus contra hæreticos vsurpata, non simpliciter approbans Caluinus, anne hæreticus erit? Arianus & Iudæus erit? Calumnia grauis in tātum Dei seruum. Quis enim obsecro doctrinam ecclesiæ de adorando sacrosanctæ Trinitatis mysterio, deque æterna Christi deitate contra fanaticos doctius & fortius hoc ipso viro asseruit? Quis rabiosos illos canes, Seruetum, Gentilem, & scelerum socios Alciatum, Blandratam, &c. acrius repressit?
units.tr: What then? If Calvin, who does not simply approve of some of these and other arguments used by the Fathers against the heretics, will be a heretic? Will he be an Arian and a Jew? A grave calumny against so great a servant of God. For who, I ask, has asserted the Church's teaching on adoring the mystery of the most holy Trinity, and on the eternal deity of Christ, against the fanatics more learnedly and more forcefully than this very man? Who has more sharply repressed those raving dogs, Servetus, Gentile, and Alciati, accomplices in crime, Blandrata, etc.?

units.la: Quòd si nonnulla à veteribus in certamine aduersus hæreticos adhibita, non satis euidentia vel firma esse obseruauit: quid tum? nihilominus centum alia de æterna Christi deitate contra Iudæorum & hæreticorum quasuis argutias fortissimè asseruit: idque ne cuiquam sit dubium, exemplo vno & altero ex commentariis eius ostendere non grauabor.
units.tr: But if he observed that some things employed by the ancients in the contest against the heretics were not sufficiently evident or firm, what of it? Nevertheless, he most strongly asserted a hundred other things about the eternal deity of Christ against any subtleties of the Jews and heretics; and, so that no one may doubt this, I will not hesitate to show it by one or two examples from his commentaries.

units.la: Gen. i. verf. 3. Quod Ѓnum, inquit (mundi creationem per Dei verbum intelligens) ad refutandam Serueti blasphemiam sufficit. Latrat hic obscenus canis, hoc primum fuisse verbi initiū, cum Deus mandauit, vt lux esset. Quasi vero causa effectu suo prior non sit. Imò cum Dei verbo repete extiterint, quæ non erant, potius colligēda est æterna eius essentia. Quare merito Apostoli, Christi diuinitatem inde probant, quòd cum sit Dei sermo, per eū creata sint omnia.
units.tr: Gen. 1, verse 3. Since he, he says, understanding the creation of the world through the word of God, is sufficient to refute the blasphemy of Servetus. This obscene dog barks that this was the first beginning of the word, when God commanded that there be light. As if the cause were not prior to its effect! Indeed, since things which were not came into being through the word of God, his eternal essence should rather be inferred. Therefore the Apostles rightly prove Christ's deity from this, that, since he is the Word of God, all things were created through him.

units.la: Exod. 3. ver. 2. Angelum Iehouæ ostendens Christum fuisse, sic scribit: Recte senserunt veteres ecclesiæ doctores, æternū Dei filiū ita vocari, respectu personæ mediatoris. Et mox: Itaque nihil mirum, si æternus Dei sermo, Ѓnius cum patre deitatis, & essentiæ, nomen angeli mutuatum sit futuræ legationis repetitum. Duo oracula Iesaiæ ca. 7. ver. 14. de virginis partu Immanuele: & cap. 9. ver. 6. de filio nobis dato, ita extorquet Iudæis, ac de vnigenito Dei filio ex Maria nato intelligenda esse demonstrat, vt nemo facile illustrius. Ieremiæ 23. ver. 5. de germine Dauidi suscitado: Deus ergo hic reuocat eos ad Messiam. Et mox: Nemini autem dubium est quin loquatur hic propheta de Christo. Ibique Iudæos prolixè refutat, germen illud ad omnes Dauidis posteros extendere conantes. Addit posteà contra eosdem: Vocatur idem & Ѓnus redemptor tam filius Dauidis. vidis, quâ Iehouah. Quomodo vocatur filius Dauidis?nempe quia oportuit illum nasci ex genere illo. Quomodo igitur est Iehouah? Hinc colligitur, aliquid esse humana carne in illo excellentius: & vocatur Iehouah : quia Unigenitus sit filius Dei: Unius cum patre essentia, & gloria, & aeternitatis, & diuinitatis.
units.tr: Exod. 3, verse 2. Showing that the Angel of Jehovah was Christ, he writes thus: The ancient doctors of the Church rightly judged that the eternal Son of God is so called with respect to the person of the Mediator. And soon after: Therefore it is no wonder if the eternal Word of God, one with the Father in deity and essence, had the name of angel borrowed and repeated for his future embassy. He wrests the two oracles of Isaiah, ch. 7, verse 14, on the virgin's childbirth, Immanuel, and ch. 9, verse 6, on the Son given to us, from the Jews, and demonstrates that they are to be understood of the only-begotten Son of God born of Mary, so that no one could do so more clearly. Jeremiah 23, verse 5, on the Branch raised up for David: God therefore here recalls them to the Messiah. And soon after: Yet no one doubts that the prophet here speaks of Christ. And there he refutes the Jews at length, who strive to extend that Branch to all the posterity of David. He adds afterward against the same: The same is called also the one Redeemer, as the son of David. You see how he is called Jehovah. How is he called the son of David? Surely because he had to be born from that stock. How then is he Jehovah? From this it is gathered that there is something in him more excellent than human flesh, and he is called Jehovah because he is the only-begotten Son of God, of one essence with the Father, and of the same glory, eternity, and divinity.

units.la: Hofe.12 verf. 4. quomodo idem fit Iehoua, & angelus explicans: Christus, inquit, aeterna Dei sapientia induit personam mediatoris, antequam induer et[?] carnem nostram. Fuit ergo tunc mediator, & eo respectu fuit et iam Angelus. Interea fuit et am Iehouah, qui nunc est Deus manifestatus in carne. Et postea: Ita hic est locus memoratu dignus ad testandam Christi deitatem.
units.tr: Hosea 12, verse 4: how the same is Jehovah, and the angel, explaining: Christ, he says, the eternal wisdom of God, put on the person of the Mediator before he put on our flesh. He was therefore then Mediator, and in that respect he was already the Angel. Meanwhile he was also Jehovah, who now is God manifested in the flesh. And afterward: Thus here is a place worth remembering for attesting the deity of Christ.

units.la: Michæ 4.verf.3. Loquitur Michæas de ipso Deo, non expressa mentione Christi: quia nondum erat manifestatus in carne, sed tamen scimus, hoc fuisse impletum in persona eius, quod Deus gubernauit orbe, & sibi populos totius mundi subegit. Statuimus ergo Christum esse verum Deum, quia nō tātum minister fuit patri sicuti Moyses, vel alius ex prophetis quispiam, sed fuit ipse summus rex ecclesiae suae. Ibidem ver.7. Tametsi[?] Christus fuit verum semen Dauidis: tamen simul etiam fuit Iehouah, nempe Deus manifestatus in carne.
units.tr: Micah 4, verse 3: Micah speaks of God himself, without express mention of Christ, because he was not yet manifested in the flesh; yet we know that this was fulfilled in his person, that God governed the world and subdued to himself the peoples of the whole world. We therefore hold that Christ is true God, because he was not merely a minister to the Father, as Moses or some other of the prophets, but was himself the supreme king of his Church. In the same place, verse 7: although Christ was the true seed of David, yet at the same time he was also Jehovah, namely God manifested in the flesh.

units.la: Zacha.1.ver.19. Tenendum memoria est, quod prius dixi: hunc primarium angelum fuisse mediatorem & caput ecclesiae. Est autem idem Iehouah, quia scimus Christum esse Deum manifestatum in carne.
units.tr: Zech. 1, verse 19: It must be kept in memory, as I said before, that this chief angel was the Mediator and head of the Church. He is, however, the same Jehovah, because we know that Christ is God manifested in the flesh.

units.la: Zach.2.ver.8. Hinc colligimus introduci Christum qui servus est Iehouah, & tamen simul est angelus ac legatus Patris. Ibidem ver.10. Videmus ergo, nomen Iehouae aptari Christo: & nullum esse discrimen patris & filij, quoad essentiam: sed tantum in ipsis personis debere distingui. Quoties ergo Christus suam diminutatem asserit, usurpat nomen Iehouae: Sed postea ostendit sibi aliquid esse proprium & distinctum, nempe quod est legatus Patris.
units.tr: Zech. 2, verse 8: From this we gather that Christ is introduced, who is the servant of Jehovah, and yet at the same time is the angel and legate of the Father. In the same place, verse 10: We see therefore that the name of Jehovah is applied to Christ, and that there is no difference between Father and Son as to essence, but that they ought to be distinguished only in the persons themselves. Whenever therefore Christ asserts his lowliness, he takes the name of Jehovah; but afterward he shows that something is proper and distinct to himself, namely that he is the legate of the Father.

units.la: Zach.3.v.3. Iam videmus vocari angelum, qui sapius dicitur Iehouah. Nō dubito igitur, quantum ad me spectat, quin nomen tam angeli, quam Iehouae debeat referri ad Christum: personam, qui verus & unicus est Deus.
units.tr: Zech. 3, verse 3: Now we see that the angel is called, who is often called Jehovah. I do not doubt, therefore, as far as I am concerned, that both the name of angel and the name of Jehovah ought to be referred to Christ, the person who is the true and only God.

units.la: Zac.11. ver.14. Tenendum est illud principium, Christum fuisse verum Iehouā ab initio. Quoniā ergo filius Dei eiusdem est cum patre essentia, & Dnus etiā cum ipso Deus, &c.
units.tr: Zech. 11, verse 14: That principle must be held, that Christ was the true Jehovah from the beginning. Since therefore the Son of God is of the same essence with the Father, and Lord also is God together with him, etc.

units.la: Nec minùs fideliter & aperte in commentariis Noui Testamenti æternam Christi deitatem & ὁμοούσιαν cùm patre paßim adstruxit.
units.tr: No less faithfully and openly in his commentaries on the New Testament he everywhere asserted the eternal deity of Christ and his homoousia with the Father.

units.la: Coloß.1.ver.15.Est interea locus memorabilis ad probandam Christi deitatem, & unam cum patre essentiam. Nam præfatus de notitia Dei mox tam ad filium, quàm ad patre accommodat. Vnde sequitur, filiu cu patre eudé esse Deu.
units.tr: Col. 1, verse 15: There is meanwhile a memorable place for proving the deity of Christ and one essence with the Father. For the author, having spoken of the knowledge of God, soon applies it both to the Son and to the Father. Whence it follows that the Son is the same God with the Father.

units.la: Vide, lector candide, quid scribat in verba apostoli, Deus manifestatus est in carne, &c. Post multa: Ita, inquit, hoc uno testimonio vera & orthodoxa fides aduersus Arium, Marcionem, Nestorium & Eutychen egregiè munitur.
units.tr: See, candid reader, what he writes on the words of the Apostle, God was manifested in the flesh, etc. After much: Thus, he says, by this one testimony the true and orthodox faith is excellently fortified against Arius, Marcion, Nestorius and Eutyches.

units.la: Ioh.5. ver.10. Tamen si hunc locum eludere Ariani conati sunt, & illis hodie subscribunt quidam: hic tamen insigne habemus diminutatis Christi elogium.
units.tr: John 5, verse 10: Although the Arians have tried to elude this place, and some today subscribe to them, yet here we have a notable elogy of the deity of Christ.

units.la: Act.7.ver.30. Ita hic locus æterna Christi diuinitati lucidentum testimonium reddit, & eiusdem cum patre essentia esse docet. Sed pluribus in re manifesta quid est opus? Similia fexcenta in aureis huius viri commentariis quibusque passim sunt obuia, quæ rabidos canum latratus ad omnem postertitatem abundè refutabunt.
units.tr: Acts 7, verse 30: So here this place bears a shining testimony to the eternal divinity of Christ, and teaches that he is of the same essence with the Father. But what need is there of more in a matter so manifest? Six hundred similar passages are everywhere at hand in the golden commentaries of this man, which will abundantly refute the raving barks of the dogs for every posterity.

units.la: Cæterùm, vt eò, vnde disgreßus sum, redeam, si Caluinus in certamine nō obuia quæuis arripuit, & nonnulla ex iis, quæ patribus olim placuerunt, hæreticorum cauillis hodie nimis obnoxia esse ostendit, fortißimus ceteroquin æternæ maiestatis Christi assertor, quam ei palam ipsos etiam hostes inter maledicendum (vel ii rupantur) porrigere conscientia cogit: an ideo Arianus proclamandus vel Arianorum patronus? an dignus, quæ sic lacerent, quasi venditandæ sapientiæ studio, captandæque gloriæ cupiditate abreptus, euidentißima scripturæ oracula de trinitatis mysterio, vel de æterna filij & Spiritus sancti deitate, data opera deprauet? Christianis sua tela eripiat? Arianorum gloßas suo calculo suffragiqué manifeftißimè coprobet? Vtinam, vtinam vos Vbiquitarij hoc non faciatis, scabiémque Arianam vestram ecclesiæ affricare desinatis. Dele& u rationum est vsus, haud temerè, aut libidine tali abrepti, vt vestra vult calumnia. Hoc vnum fe agere ac velle non semel testatur, vtnihil habeamus, nisi solidum.
units.tr: Moreover, to return to where I digressed: if Calvin in the contest did not seize upon whatever was at hand, and showed that some of the things that once pleased the Fathers are today too exposed to the cavils of heretics, yet he is otherwise the most vigorous asserter of the eternal majesty of Christ, which conscience compels even his enemies, while reviling him, to hold out (though they burst)—shall he therefore be proclaimed an Arian or a patron of the Arians? Is he worthy to be torn apart in this way, as if, carried away by a desire to display his wisdom and a greed for glory, he deliberately distorts the most evident oracles of Scripture on the mystery of the Trinity, or on the eternal deity of the Son and the Holy Spirit? Does he snatch weapons from Christians? Does he deliberately approve the glosses of the Arians with his vote and suffrage? Would that you Ubiquitarians would not do this, and would cease to rub your Arian scab into the Church. The use of arguments is discriminating, not rashly, nor carried away by such a lust, as your calumny would have it. He testifies more than once that he has this one aim and wish: that we have nothing but what is solid.

units.la: Expertus nimirum erat in congreßibus cum Serueto, Gentile,& similibus monstris, quæ valida & euidentia, quæ secus essent: quæ fortius hostem constringerent, quæ minus. Pondere igitur, non numero argumentorum sibi certandum esse vidit, aliósque suo exemplo certare docuit contra hæreticos, longè profecto nunc argutos & lubricos magis, quàm olim ipse Samosatenus, Arius, vel alij ipsorum patriarchæ fuerunt. Aduersarius enim vetus est & hostis antiquus, qui per istos Christi gloriam impugnat. Sex millia annorum pene cöplentur, ex quo, vt verbis vtar Cypriani, hoc certamen diabolus contra Deum gerit. Omnia iam genera tentandi, & artes atque insidias deiiciendi, vsu ipso vetustatis hæreticos docuit. Denique, cum spiritus Prophetarum subiecti sint prophetis: scripsit, non præscripsit ecclesiæ interpretationes & sententias suas præclarus & eximius ille Dei seruus. Desinant ergo maledicentiæ suæ virus in eum despumare ingratissimi Stentores post pulpita, quæ sine eo plerique parum magnificè tuerentur.
units.tr: Certainly he had gained experience in his encounters with Servetus, Gentile and similar monsters, and he knew which arguments were strong and conclusive and which were weaker and would bind the enemy less firmly. He therefore saw that one must contend with weight of argument, not with number of arguments, and by his own example taught others to contend in the same way against heretics, who are now far more subtle and slippery than Samosatenus, Arius, or their other patriarchs ever were. The adversary is indeed old and an ancient enemy, who through these men attacks the glory of Christ. Nearly six thousand years have passed since, in the words of Cyprian, the devil has waged this struggle against God. Long practice has taught the heretics every kind of attempt, and every art and snare for overthrowing others. Finally, since the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets, that distinguished and eminent servant of God wrote his interpretations and opinions but did not prescribe them to the Church. Let those most ungrateful stentors therefore cease to spew the poison of their slander against him from behind the pulpits, which for the most part would be defended with little splendour without him.

units.la: Verùm istis nunc missis, ad alterum scriptionum genus venio, quod est [illegible, ~9 letters], planéque [illegible, ~8 letters], quo monstrosa dogmata monstrosioribus adstruunt, euidentia theologiæ principia conuelluntur, aperta scripturæ dicta proteruè deprauantur, hæreses iam olim damnatæ, inani dicacitate postliminio in ecclesiam reducuntur, ac pro euangelica veritate misero popello obtruduntur: In hoc facile nunc dominatur Archilochius ille disputator Huberus, apostata impudentissimus: quem odium certò agnitæ, abnegatæ, & petulanter impugnatæ veritatis in tantam maledicendi & calumniandi rabiem magis ac magis abripit, vt non obscurum exemplum sit à Deo in reprobum sensum traditi. Largiatur ei Dominus saniorem mentem, si non est ἀνίατος[?]: vel certè furoris eius modum statuat, ne secum alios exitio miserè inuol-uat.
units.tr: But now, setting those aside, I come to the other kind of writing, which is [illegible], and plainly [illegible], by which monstrous doctrines are supported by still more monstrous ones, the evident principles of theology are overthrown, the plain words of Scripture are shamelessly distorted, heresies condemned long ago are brought back into the Church under the guise of empty wit, and are thrust upon the wretched people in the name of evangelical truth. In this field that Archilochian disputant Huber now holds easy sway, the most shameless apostate, whom hatred of a truth he has recognised, renounced and wantonly attacked drives into such a frenzy of slander and calumny, more and more, that he is an obvious example of one given over by God to a reprobate mind. May the Lord grant him a saner mind, if he is not [incurable?]; or at least may He set a limit to his frenzy, lest he wretchedly drag others with him into ruin.

units.la: Hic iam quasi Pelagij quidam alumnus, ac Stentor Epicureus horrendis vociferationibus Germaniam implet: Omnes homines citra exceptionem, fideles & infi-deles, damnatos & damnandos, reprobos aque ac quoslibet alios, puta canes & porcos, aque atque omnes Christi, Nerones & Heliogabalos aeque atque Dauides & Iosaphatos, Iudas aeque atque Petrum Christi morte Deo reconciliatos, sanctificatos, iustificatos, remissionem peccatorum conse-cutos, in finum & gratiam Dei receptos, denique saluatos esse, (applaudite vos canes & porci, patrono,) o portam a-theifmo apertam! neminem damnari propter peccata, sed propter solam incredulitatem: electionis & repro-batiouis decretum aeternum in Deo nullum esse: nullum esse certum apud Deum saluandorum numerum: omnes homines post lapsum demum Adami esse in Christo ele-ctos: electionem, gratiam, & remissionem peccatorum esse generalem, specialem electionem nullam esse quo-ad Deum: sed tantum quoad homines, qui universalem gratiam sibi applicant: scivisse Deum ab aeterno, qui essent recepturi gratiam, & permansuri, qui non: eligere idem esse quod allegere genus humanum: multos elec-tos perire: qui perierunt traditos fuisse Christo in ado-ptionem: vanam esse illam certitudinem donorum Dei, quam iactamus ex Rom.11. Dona Dei esse ἀμεταμέλητα[?]: electionem in Christo factam esse cum hypothesi Si credamus: niti fide nostra: fidem non contingere quidem sine Dei gratia, sed media, per quae detur, esse ἐφ' ἡμῖν: non renatos in suo arbitrio habere, ut currant ad verbum Dei: posse intelligere & animadvertere vocem Dei vocantis: quod ex multis, qui iisdem utuntur mediis, alij credunt & perseuerant, alij non credunt, vel non perseuerant, causam esse rectum vel non rectum mediorum usum, qui fit ἐφ' ἡμῖν: cap.9. ad Rom. non agere de praedestinatione ad vitam vel ad mortem: praedestinationem hanc facere Deum mendacem, crudelem, [illegible, ~8 letters], iniustum, tol-lere ministerium, hortationes afferre securitatem & de-sperationem: & talia sexcenta: cum quibus si veteres Pe-lagij & Coeleftij furores conferas, non ouum ouo similius esse videbis. Sic enim Pelagiani docebant, ut tum ex Au-guftini scriptis, tum vero ex epistolis Prosperi & Hilarij ad eundem, de reliquiis Pelagianae haeresseos in Gallia con-stat: omnes quidem homines in Adamo peccasse, & neminem per opera sua, sed per Dei gratiam regeneratio-ne saluari: universis tamen propitiationem sanguinis Christi esse propositam sine exceptione, ut quicunque ad fidem & baptismum accedere voluerint, salui esse possint. Qui autem crediturî sint, & in fide permansuri, praescisse Deu ante mundi constitutionem, & eos praedestinasse in regnum suum, quos gratis vocatos dignos futuros electione, & de hac vita bono fine excessuros praeuiderit: ideo-que omnes ad credendum & bene operandum admonen-ri, vt de salute apprehendenda nemo desperet. Negabant praedestinatum esse certum electorum numerum apud Deum: ne hortationes essent superuacuae, & omnis praedicandi vigor tolleretur: Aiebant remoueri omnem industriam, tollique virtutes. si Dei constitutio humanas[?] praeue-niat voluntates, & sub hac praedestinationis nomine fatalem induci necessitatem: epistolam ad Rom. cap. 9. à patrib. antiquis ecclesiasticis nunquam sic fuisse intellectam de gratuita electione praeuenente voluntates & merita: doctrina hanc aedificationi docetium contrariam esse: ac si vera etiam sit, non promendam: quia praebeat causam desperationi: turbari hac disputatione imperitorum corda sine causa: quia fides catholica etiam sine ea possit tradi & defendi. Faustus quoque humano labori adiungebat gratiae adiutorium, vt videlicet gratia & labor humanus pariter sociati reliqua perficiant operari. Deum quidem per scripturas suas operari vt velimus, quas vel legimus vel audiimus: sed eis consentire vel non consentire ita nostrum esse, vt si velimus, fiat: si autem nolimus, nihil in nobis operationem Dei valere faciamus, &c.
units.tr: Here now, like a certain disciple of Pelagius, an Epicurean stentor, he fills Germany with horrendous shouting: that all men without exception, faithful and unbelieving, the damned and those destined to damnation, the reprobate as well as any others, say dogs and pigs, just as all of Christ's, Neros and Heliogabaluses just as much as Davids and Jehoshaphats, Judas just as much as Peter, have been reconciled to God by the death of Christ, sanctified, justified, have obtained forgiveness of sins, have been received into the bosom and grace of God, and finally have been saved (applaud, you dogs and pigs, your patron!). O gate opened to atheism! That no one is damned on account of sins, but only on account of unbelief; that there is no eternal decree of election and reprobation in God; that there is no certain number of the saved with God; that all men after the fall of Adam are elect in Christ; that election, grace and forgiveness of sins are general, and that there is no special election as regards God, but only as regards men, who apply to themselves the universal grace; that God knew from eternity who would receive grace and persevere and who would not; that to elect is the same as to choose the human race; that many of the elect perish; that those who perished were handed over to Christ for adoption; that that certainty of God's gifts which we boast of from Romans 11 is vain, the gifts of God being [irrevocable?]; that election in Christ was made under the hypothesis "if we believe"; that we rest on our faith; that faith does not come without the grace of God, but the means by which it is given are in our power (ἐφ' ἡμῖν); that the unregenerate have it in their own will to run to the Word of God; that they can understand and take notice of the voice of God calling; that of many who use the same means, some believe and persevere, others do not believe or do not persevere, and the cause is the right or wrong use of the means, which lies in our power; on Romans chapter 9, that it does not treat of predestination to life or to death; that this predestination makes God a liar, cruel, [illegible], unjust; that it abolishes the ministry, that exhortations bring security and despair; and six hundred such things. If you compare these with the old frenzies of the Pelagians and Caelestius, you will see that egg is not more like egg. For the Pelagians taught in such a way, as is clear both from the writings of Augustine and from the letters of Prosper and Hilary to him about the remnants of the Pelagian heresy in Gaul: that indeed all men sinned in Adam, and no one is saved through his own works but by the grace of God through regeneration; yet the propitiation of the blood of Christ is set before all without exception, so that whoever are willing to come to faith and baptism may be saved. But as for those who would believe and persevere in faith, God foreknew them before the foundation of the world, and predestined them into his kingdom, those whom he foresaw would be called freely, would be worthy of election, and would depart from this life with a good end; and therefore all are admonished to believe and to act well, so that no one should despair of laying hold of salvation. They denied that a certain number of the elect was predestined with God, lest exhortations be superfluous and all vigour of preaching be taken away. They said that all effort would be removed and virtues abolished if God's decree should go before human wills, and that under this name of predestination a fatal necessity would be introduced. They maintained that the Epistle to the Romans chapter 9 was never so understood by the ancient Fathers of the Church, as concerning a gratuitous election that goes before wills and merits; that this doctrine is contrary to edification, and even if it were true, should not be put forward, since it gives occasion to despair, and since the hearts of the unlearned are troubled by this disputation without cause, because the catholic faith can be taught and defended even without it. Faustus too added the help of grace to human labour, so that grace and human labour, joined together, would accomplish the rest of the work. God indeed works through his Scriptures that we may will, which we either read or hear; but to consent or not to consent to them is so much in our power that, if we will, it happens; but if we are unwilling, we make it so that God's working has no effect in us, etc.

units.la: Haec & similia fuerunt insaniae Pelagianae deliria, quae infelicem hunc hominem quasi verbotim[?] descripta pro nouis oraculis nobis nunc edere: neminem tam esse in religione Christiana hospitem arbitror, qui non intelligat.
units.tr: These and similar were the delusions of the Pelagian madness, which this unhappy man, as if copied almost word for word, now publishes to us as new oracles. I think there is no one so much a stranger to the Christian religion as not to understand this.

units.la: Et iurabit tamen scio, Pelagij lacunas se nunquam gustasse, sed exsecrari. Verum satis proditur à Puccio illo Pelagiano, apostata similiter leuissimo, qui nuper conculcata euangelij veritate ad Iesuitas transitum simulans, aperte adeo & impudenter Pelagianas furores interpolauit defenditque, vt ipsos Iesuitas Pragenses ab editione monstrosissimi eius libri conscientia & pudor abstterruerit. Is cum apostata hoc nostro omnia illa confirmat: neque ipse tamen videri vel audire vult Pelagianus. In plerisque vero est nostro apertior. Nam quod hoc toties factarum se simulat, nec vspiam tamen facere pet conscientiam audet: ille praedestinationem egregie definit hoc modo: quod sit ordo pravisus & propositus Deo, quo decrevit ab omni aeternitate, quid eventurum sit singulis personis, quas creavit omnes, Servatoris participes & haereditatis aeternae haeredes, relinquens singulis in hac vita libertate voluntatis, ut ab eo non deficerent, aut deficerent prout {g}nusquisque eligeret, postquam sum rationis haberet. Voluit enim, ut quicunque non deficerent a creatore, servarentur: quia vero constantes in fide, & obsequio eius permanerent, & adversarius acriter resisteret, probati & electi eius haberentur, nec solum servarentur, sed regnarent in regno Christi & vita aterna. At qui ad tempus deficeret, temporariis pœnis monerentur & purgarentur: & qui demum generatim & obstinate ipsi repugnarent, euaderent reprobi & indociles. Hæc ille.
units.tr: And yet he will swear, I know, that he never tasted the Pelagian pools, but abhors them. But it is sufficiently revealed by that Pelagian Puccius, likewise a most shallow apostate, who, after trampling underfoot the truth of the gospel, feigning a passage to the Jesuits, so openly and shamelessly interpolated and defended the Pelagian frenzies that the Jesuits of Prague were deterred from publishing his most monstrous book by conscience and shame. He, being an apostate, confirms all those things along with this man of ours; yet he himself does not wish to be seen or heard as a Pelagian. In most respects, however, he is more open than ours. For while this man pretends that he has often disavowed these things, yet nowhere dares to disavow them with a clear conscience, the other defines predestination admirably in this way: that there is an order foreseen and proposed by God, by which he decreed from all eternity what would happen to each person, whom he created all as sharers in the Saviour and heirs of eternal inheritance, leaving to each in this life freedom of will, so that they either would not fall away from him, or would fall away, as each chose, after they had reached the use of reason. For he willed that whoever did not fall away from the Creator should be saved; because those who remained steadfast in faith and obedience to him, and the adversary resisted fiercely, were held to be proven and elect, and were saved not only but would reign in the kingdom of Christ and in eternal life. But those who fell away for a time would be admonished and purged by temporal punishments; and those who finally and obstinately resisted him would become reprobate and unteachable. So he.

units.la: Contendit idem, Christus pariter omnium & singulorum hominum, ut conditorem, ita & redemptorem esse: & omnes nasci in statu salutis & gratiæ, ac proinde felices, modo non accersant sibi exitium sua infidelitate: electionem & gratia esse generalem: fidem esse generale & commune omnibus hominibus Dei donum: imo esse naturale: & omnes homines aptos natos ad pietatem: discrimen bonorum & malorum super terram esse ex cognitionis Dei bono vel malo usu: ratione in iudiciis de religione REGINAM esse: ac doctrinam hanc cum doctrina apostoli (Rom.9.10.11.) bene congruere, tantum repugnare disputationibus Augustini, & quibusdam conciliis atque scholasticis, utpote ex solius Augustini sententia pendentib. Obsecrat Iesuitas, & in his Bellarmino, ne Augustini & scholasticorum definitionibus & interpretationibus nimis adhæreant: nec suam istam præclaram rationem interpretandi & intelligendi sacras literas, humano generi diutius invideant, &c.
units.tr: The same author contends that Christ is equally the Creator and the Redeemer of all and of each human being; that all are born in a state of salvation and grace, and therefore happy, provided they do not bring ruin on themselves by their unbelief; that election and grace are general; that faith is a general and common gift of God to all human beings, indeed that it is natural; and that all human beings are born fit for piety; that the distinction between good and evil men on earth arises from a good or bad use of the knowledge of God; that reason is queen in judgments about religion; and that this doctrine agrees well with the teaching of the Apostle (Rom. 9, 10, 11), and conflicts only with the disputations of Augustine and certain councils and scholastics, which, as he says, depend on Augustine's opinion alone. He begs the Jesuits, and Bellarmine among them, not to cling too closely to the definitions and interpretations of Augustine and the scholastics, nor to begrudge the human race any longer their own splendid method of interpreting and understanding the sacred letters, etc.

units.la: Iam quæro ex apostata, & purpurato eius præside Tubingensi, ecquid hic Pelagianum videant. Sentinam sordium Pelagianarum hanc esse clamabunt scio. Audite igitur porro Franciscum illum Puccium vestrum. Is capiti 33. libelli sui tale præfixit argumentum: Ostendam Vvitembergenses theologos Lutheri successores, nostra sententia accedere: at Bezam cum cæteris Caluini successoribus in sua peruicacia[?] perseverare, ac diversos locos scripturæ corrumpere. pere.Postea laudes vestras præclarósque in doctrina profectus sic prædicat: Dum hac scriberemus, incidimus in re-fpofione[?] Theod. Beza successoris Caluini, ad acta colloquij Montisp. Tubinga edita, impressam Geneua Anno 1588. in qua videmus, quàm acriter certét Caluiniani cū Lutheranis theologis, de aliu dogmatib. ac de prædestinatione: & quàm miserè confligentur, qui extra sepța Ecclesiæ & successionis apostolicæ vagantur & errant. Tamè studiū veritatis quo accensi sumus, fecit vt lataremur, videntes, VVirtebergenses Theologos multum demisse de Lutherana fausta & absurditate ab hac sententia: & nobiscum in rei summa consentire, licet in interpretatione scripturarum & sacramentorum hæreant & errent. Hæc ille de nostris bonis vicinis VVirtembergenfibus. O funestum consensum! ô nefandam coniurationem! Iurabunt coelum & maria, hæc nihil ad se: & à nobis sua refutari volent: vt iam pridem rabiosus ille apóstata exoptauit antagonistam, cui dentes infigeret, & sic nomen inueniret. Sed sciat ille neminem sic insanire, qui cum homine furioso αὐτοκρα-χρίτω manus conferre velit. Me quidem frustra ille lacessit. Interim scio, me domi in retexenda eius farragine discipulis & veritati non defuisse. Nec de est officio in argumento illo de redemptionis vniuersalitate publicis lectionibus solidissimè pertractando clarissimus vir D.IACOBVS KIMENDONCIVS Rector Academiæ nostræ magnificus, quem honoris causa nomino. In cæteris quid actum agere est opus?
units.tr: Now I ask this apostate and his purple-robed president at Tübingen whether they see anything Pelagian here. I know they will cry out that this is a sink of Pelagian filth. Listen, then, to your Franciscus Puccius. In chapter 33 of his little book he prefixed this argument: I will show that the Wittenberg theologians, the successors of Luther, agree with our opinion; but that Beza with the other successors of Calvin persists in his obstinacy and corrupts various passages of Scripture. Afterwards he proclaims your praises and your remarkable progress in doctrine in this way: While we were writing this, we came upon the reply of Theodore Beza, successor of Calvin, to the Acts of the Colloquy of Montbéliard, published at Tübingen and printed at Geneva in the year 1588, in which we see how bitterly the Calvinists contend with the Lutheran theologians about other doctrines and about predestination, and how wretchedly they clash, who wander and err outside the fold of the Church and of apostolic succession. Yet the zeal for truth with which we are inflamed made us rejoice, seeing that the Württemberg theologians have greatly moderated their Lutheran boasting and absurdity on this point, and agree with us in the substance of the matter, although they cling to and err in the interpretation of Scripture and the sacraments. Thus he speaks of our good neighbours, the Württembergers. O baneful agreement! O accursed conspiracy! They will swear heaven and seas that these things have nothing to do with them, and they will wish their own errors to be refuted by us, as that raging apostate long ago desired an opponent on whom he might sink his teeth and so win a name. But let him know that no one is so mad as to join hands with a furious man who is a self-taught lunatic. As for me, he attacks me in vain. Meanwhile I know that at home I have not failed my students and the truth in unravelling his medley. Nor has the most distinguished man, Mr. JACOB KIMENDONCK, the magnificent Rector of our Academy, whom I name out of respect, failed in his duty, treating that topic of the universality of redemption most solidly in public lectures. What else needs to be done in the rest?

units.la: Augustinus olim, cum Alipio socio, vt Hieronymus epistola ad eosdem ostendit, in confutanda hæresi Pelagiana plurimum studij & laboris sustinuit, scripsitque diuersis titulis totos XXX. libros cum aliquot epistolis, quibus ex professo Pelagianam insaniam confutauit. Prosper affirmat, trecentos fuisse, qui contra eam hæresin scripserint. Testatur & Augustinus, quinque concilis Africanis damnatum fuisse. Exstat Fulgentij præclarus liber ad Monimum primus de duplici prædestinatione Dei, vna bonorum ad gloriam, altera malorum ad pœnam. Extant Maxentij similia capitula aduersus Pelagianos. Exstat aureus Lutheri libell. de SERVO ARBITRIO contra semipelagianam Erasmi diatriben. Exstant denique recentium Theologorum orthodoxæ de his disputationes, Brentij, Heshusij, Schnepffij, & cum primis Here-[?] brandi[?]. Et apostata exspectab[?] t,dum nostrum aliquis os e maledicum compescat? Hæc lega, refutet: vel si non potest, veritatem insectari desinat.
units.tr: Augustine once, together with his colleague Alypius, as Jerome shows in a letter to them, devoted great zeal and labour to refuting the Pelagian heresy, and he wrote, under various titles, whole books, thirty in number, together with several letters, in which he expressly refuted the Pelagian madness. Prosper affirms that there were three hundred who wrote against that heresy. Augustine also testifies that it was condemned by five African councils. There survives Fulgentius's excellent first book to Monimus on the twofold predestination of God: one of the good to glory, the other of the wicked to punishment. There survive similar chapters of Maximus against the Pelagians. There survives Luther's golden little book, On the Bondage of the Will, against Erasmus's semi-Pelagian diatribe. Finally there survive the orthodox disputations on these matters by recent theologians: Brenz, Heshusius, Schnepf, and above all Herebrand[?]. And does the apostate wait for one of us to silence his slanderous mouth? Let him read these, let him refute them; or, if he cannot, let him cease to attack the truth.

units.la: Stabit contra hos latratus & inferorum portas inuicta veritas scri[?]turæ: Dei[?] redemptione per Christum. Qui credit in Filium, habet vitam æternam: qui vero non credit Filio, non videbit vitam: sed ira Dei manet (manet, manet) super eum. De prædestinatione & gratia. Elegit nos in Christo ante te [?] iacta mundi fundamenta. Quos prædestinauit, hos vocauit. Nondum natis pueris dictum est: Maior seruiet minori: sicut scriptum est: Iacob dilexi, Esau odio habui. Itaque cuius vult miseretur, quem vult indurat. Electio consecuta est, reliqui occalluerunt. De Fide. Non omnium est fides. Vobis datum est in Christi negotio, non solum in eum credere, sed etiam pro eo affligi. Deus operatur & st[?] ἐνεργεῖν perficere. Et crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam. De perseuerantia. Firmum stat fundamentum Dei habens sigillum hoc: Nouit Dominus qui sunt sui. Ego ouibus meis do vitam æternam (æterna inquit Christus, non triduana) nec peribunt in æternum: neque rapiet eas quisquam e manu mea. Ego rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua. Pseudoprophetæ edet signa magna & miracula, ita ut si fieri possit, etiam electos seducant. Confiteor tibi, pater domine cœli & terræ, quia abscondisti hæc à sapientibus & intelligentibus: & reuelasti ea infantibus. Etiam pater, quia sic LACVIT TIBI. Hæc & similia cœlestis veritatis mysteria, discant prius ac ostare, quam ad sui cerebri phantasias examinare, ut hodie in cœlum os inferunt.
units.tr: Against these barkings the invincible truth of Scripture will stand, and the gates of hell: the redemption of God through Christ. He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who does not believe the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains (remains, remains) upon him. Concerning predestination and grace: He chose us in Christ before [the foundation of the world was laid]. Those whom he predestined, these he also called.
