units.la: Procul igitur à nostro scopo, nimis procul aberramus,nisi certò statuimus, quòd non tam in hunc finé in his Christi myrmeciis & alueari bus opus feruere debeat, vt literis culiiores,quã vt bonis& sanctis moribus ornatiores,Deóq.& hominibus gratiores efficiamur. Costat autem in ecclesia omnem de virtute præceptionem sine doctrina pietatis nihil esse,nisi aberrationé & abductioné àDeo,à veris bonis,vera iustitia,vera salute.Quid quid enim nō ad gloriam Dei : quidquid nō in nomine Christi Iesu,quidquid nō ex fide facimus,peccatū & abieɛtum ac dānatū à Deo esse, Spiritus sanctus pronunciat.Nō solum igitur,à scholis ecclefię doctrinā remotā,de vera & integra virtute,qualé Deus postulat,nihil diceretur,sed etiā,quæ restaret,exigua & obscura cula,non suo quidé accessu.sed eorum sine quibus nihil est sanctum aut sanum, defectione, nos ex malis deteriores redderet. Sed hic omniū sanorū cōsensus etsi satisfacere nobis debet,maioris tamen sint nobis mandata diuina,quæ scrutari scripturas,attendere lectioni,ὁ῾ρώτα[?]-μὲν verbum Dei,iubet.Cùm autē sine doctrina & exercitatione scholastica,explicare sermone prophetico & apostolicum,doctrinæ partes recte,ordine & perspicue discernere & exponere nemo possit, quis nō videt,quã arcto studia pietatis vinculo scholis copulata sint?Quod igitur opus in genere humano summū est,ac sine scholasticis operis à nobis præstari nō potest,præcipuū in scholis esse iudicemus,librorū videlicet propheticorū & apostolicorū intellectum & explicationem.Cũmque nobis accuratiùs doctrinā cognoscendi maior quàm cẽteris hominibus,facultas & occasio detur,eā certè si negligimus,& suspectam pietate nostram facimus, & maiores negligentiæ & iustitiæ pœnas dabimus. Neque verò nostra solum,sed aliorum etiam causa, nobis praecipuè scholastici curam hanc & custodiā doctrinę Deus mandatam esse voluit. A literatis enim, sermonis genus intelligentibus & seriem [?] doctrinæ intuentibus, institutio & interpretatio reliquis expectanda est.
units.tr: We therefore stray far, far from our aim, unless we firmly resolve that in these hives and beehives of Christ the effort should be directed not so much to this end, that we be made more refined in letters, as that we be made more adorned with good and holy morals, and more pleasing to God and to men. Now it is agreed in the Church that any instruction in virtue without the doctrine of piety is nothing but a straying and a turning away from God, from true goods, true righteousness, and true salvation. For whatever we do that is not to the glory of God, whatever we do not in the name of the Lord Jesus, whatever we do not from faith, the Holy Spirit pronounces to be sin and rejected and condemned by God. Therefore, if the doctrine of the Church were removed from the schools, not only would nothing be said about true and complete virtue, such as God demands, but also what remained, meagre and obscure, would make us worse from bad, not by its approach indeed, but by the defection of those things without which nothing is holy or sound. But although the consensus of all sound men ought to satisfy us, the divine commands are nevertheless greater for us, which bid us search the Scriptures, attend to reading, and first of all [the] word of God. Since, however, no one can explain the prophetic and apostolic discourse, nor rightly, in order and clearly discern and set forth the parts of doctrine, without scholastic teaching and exercise, who does not see how closely the pursuits of piety are joined to the schools by a tight bond? What is therefore the highest task in the human race, and cannot be accomplished by us without scholastic labour, we judge to be chiefly in the schools: namely, the understanding and explanation of the prophetic and apostolic books. And since we are given a greater opportunity and occasion of learning doctrine more accurately than other men, if we neglect it and make our piety suspect, we shall pay greater penalties for negligence and injustice. Moreover, God wished this care and guardianship of doctrine to be entrusted especially to us scholars, not only for our own sake but also for the sake of others. For instruction and interpretation are to be expected by the rest from the learned, who understand the kind of speech and observe the sequence of doctrine.

units.la: Cum igitur in scholis religio tradenda sit, ut pueris, idque recte tradi possit, catechesis necessaria est. Nec enim sine brevitate discit hæc ætas, nec ullius disciplinę partes tam à docentibus quàm à discentibus dextrè & ἀλλοιωτικὰς [?] tractari possunt, cuius non utique summam quandà animo conceperint. Horū utrūque causa est, cur toties in sacris libris summæ repetitæ legātur, ut, Agite pœnitentiam, & credite evangelio. Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Milita bonam militiam, retinens fidem & bonam conscientiam &c. Cùm autè dictū sit, Colos.3.16. Sermo Christi habitet inter vos opulenter in omni sapientia: addendæ sunt explicationes cum prophetarum & apostolorum sententiis congruentes. Nec aliud est catechismus, quàm talium sententiarum brevis declaratio. At talis cum sit libellus EXAMINIS, qui vobis proponitur, & autor proprio & perspicuo verborum genere, summa fide & dexteritate, Christianismi capita complexus sit, similem denique catechesēos formam in multis ecclesiis extare non paulum referat: vos ipsos ad discendum excitetis & has nostras miseras chartas existimetis esse fascias, in quibus involutus Christus anobis inveniri vult. Eas verò fascias, quæ vobis commendant, quæ vos ad eas amplectandas hortantur serió, per quæ vos obtestor, ut illæ vobis cordi sint, multa videtis esse. Mandatum Dei, vestram salutem, officium, quod debemus posteris, exemplum purioris ecclesiæ, vestrum vitæ genus, vestram statem, vestrorum voluntates & spes, imminentia pericula, præmia & pœnas à Deo expectandas. Sed ut nostræ admonitiones sunt necessariæ, sic illas absque Spiritus sancti moribus scimus nihil proficere. Ad Deum igitur conversi, quod in hac evangelij luce nos nasci voluit, agamus ei gratias, & ab ipso doceri & gubernari petamus. DIXI.
units.tr: Since, therefore, religion is to be taught in the schools, and so that it may be taught rightly to boys, catechesis is necessary. For this age does not learn without brevity, nor can the parts of any discipline be handled skilfully and in a way suited to the mind, either by teachers or by learners, unless they have first conceived in their minds some summary of it. Each of these is the reason why the summaries are so often repeated in the sacred books, as: "Repent, and believe the gospel." "He who believes and is baptized will be saved." "Fight the good fight, holding faith and a good conscience," etc. Since it has been said (Col. 3.16): "Let the word of Christ dwell richly among you in all wisdom," explanations agreeing with the sayings of the prophets and apostles must be added. Nor is a catechism anything other than a brief declaration of such sayings. But since the little book of EXAMINATION which is set before you is of such a kind, and its author, in a proper and clear manner of words, with great faithfulness and skill, has embraced the heads of Christianity, and since indeed a similar form of catechesis is found in many churches, it refers no little: may you rouse yourselves to learning, and regard these our wretched papers as swaddling-bands, in which Christ, wrapped up, wishes to be found by us. Yet you see that there are many things which recommend those swaddling-bands to you, which urge you to embrace them seriously, and through which I beseech you that they may be dear to your hearts: the command of God, your salvation, the duty we owe to posterity, the example of a purer Church, your way of life, your station, the wishes and hopes of your people, impending dangers, and rewards and punishments to be expected from God. But just as our admonitions are necessary, so we know that without the moral working of the Holy Spirit they profit nothing. Therefore, turning to God, who willed us to be born in this light of the gospel, let us give him thanks, and ask to be taught and governed by him. I have spoken.

units.la: III. DE VERBI INCARNATIONE, Symbolum Patrum Antiochenorum aduersus Paulum Samosatenum, Ex actis concilij Ephesini primi.
units.tr: III. ON THE INCARNATION OF THE WORD, the Creed of the Antiochene Fathers against Paul of Samosata, from the acts of the First Council of Ephesus.

units.la: CONFITEMVR dominum nostrum Iesum Christum ante secula quidem ex patre, per Spiritū sanctum vero nouissimis temporibus ex virgine fecundum carnē natum,vna dūtaxat persona ex cœlesti diuinitate & humana carne conflata,subsistentem.Totum Deum & totum hominem. Totum Deum etiam cum corpore, sed non fecundum corpus Deum. Totum hominem etiam cum diuinitate,sed nō fecundum diuinitatem homine. Totum rursum adorabilem etiam cum corpore,sed non fecundum corpus adorabilem.Totum adorantem etiam cum diuinitate,sed non fecundum diuinitatem, adorātem. Totum increatum etiam cum corpore, sed non fecundum corpus, increatum. Totum formatum etiam cum diuinitate, sed non fecundum diuinitatem formatum. Totum Deo <bl>ὁμοούσιον</bl> etiam cum corpore, sed non fecundum corpus <bl>ὁμοούσιον</bl>; quemadmodum neque fecundum diuinitatem quoque hominibus coessentialis est: est autem nobis fecundum carnem <bl>ὁμοούσιος</bl>, etiam in diuinitate existens. Etenim cum illum fecundum Spiritū Deo consubstantialem dicimus,nō dicimus hominibus fecundum Spiritum coessentialem. Contra autem cum illum fecundum carnem hominibus consubstantialem prædicamus,non prædicamus illum fecundum carnem Deo coessentialem. Vt enim fecundum spiritum nobis <bl>ὁμοούσιος</bl> non est:(Nam fecundum hunc Deo <bl>ὁμοούσιος</bl> est:) ita vicissim Deo fecundum carnē coessentialis non est: fecundum hanc autem nobis consubstantialis est. Quēadmodum autem hæc diftinēta, & inter fe secreta pronunciamus,non ad inducendam vnius indiuisæ perfonę diuisionem,sed ad denotandam naturarum & proprietatum verbi & carnis distinctionem, & incōfusibilitatem; ita illa,quæ ad indiuisæ vnionis compositionisve rationem faciunt,vnita prædicamus & veneramur.
units.tr: We confess that our Lord Jesus Christ was indeed born before all ages from the Father, but in the last times, through the Holy Spirit, was born of the virgin according to the flesh, one person subsisting, compounded of heavenly divinity and human flesh. Whole God and whole man. Whole God, even with the body, but not God according to the body. Whole man, even with the divinity, but not man according to the divinity. Whole, again, adorable, even with the body, but not adorable according to the body. Whole adoring, even with the divinity, but not adoring according to the divinity. Whole uncreated, even with the body, but not uncreated according to the body. Whole formed, even with the divinity, but not formed according to the divinity. Whole homoousios with God, even with the body, but not homoousios according to the body; just as neither is he co-essential with men according to the divinity: yet he is homoousios with us according to the flesh, existing also in the divinity. For when we say that he is consubstantial with God according to the Spirit, we do not say that he is co-essential with men according to the Spirit. On the other hand, when we proclaim that he is consubstantial with men according to the flesh, we do not proclaim that he is co-essential with God according to the flesh. For just as he is not homoousios with us according to the Spirit (for according to this he is homoousios with God), so again he is not co-essential with God according to the flesh; yet according to this he is consubstantial with us. Just as we pronounce these things as distinct and separate from one another, not to introduce a division of the one undivided person, but to denote the distinction and the unconfused character of the natures and properties of the Word and of the flesh; so we proclaim and venerate, as united, those things which pertain to the manner of the undivided union and composition.

units.la: Vigilius lib.4. aduersus Eutychen.
units.tr: Vigilius, book 4, against Eutyches.

units.la: Si verbi & carnis vna natura est, quomodo, cum ver-bum vbique sit,non vbique inueniatur & caro?Namque quando in terra fuit,non erat vtique in cœlo : & nunc, quia in cœlo est,non est vtique in terra,& in tantū non est, vt secundùm ipsam Christum spectemus venturum de cœlo, quem secundùm verbum nobiscum esse credi-mus in terra. Igitur secundùm vos,aut verbum cum carne sua loco continetur, aut caro cum verbo vbique est, quando vna natura contrarium quid & diuersum non recipit in seipsa. Diuersum est autem & longè dissimili circumscribi loco,& vbique esse:& quia verbum vbique est,caro autem vbique non est,apparet,vnum eumdemque Christum vtriusque esse naturæ:& esse quidem vbique secundùm naturam diuinitatis suæ, & loco contineri,secundùm naturam humanitatis suæ:creatum esse, & initium non habere:morti subiacere, & mori nõ posse:quod vnum illi est ex natura verbi,qua Deus est:aliud ex natura carnis,qua idem Deus homo est. Igitur vnus Dei filius,idémque hominis factus filius,habet initium ex natura carnis suæ,& non habet initium ex natura diuinitatis suæ:creatus est per naturam carnis suæ,& non est creatus per naturam diuinitatis suæ: circumscriptus loco est per naturam carnis suæ,& non loco capitur per naturam diuinitatis suæ: minor est etiã angelis per naturam carnis suæ, & ꝗqualis est patri secundū naturam diuinitatis suæ:mortuus est natura carnis suæ, & nõ est mortuus natura diuinitatis suæ. HAEC EST FIDES & confessio catholica,quam apostoli tradiderunt, martyres roborauerunt,& fideles hucusque custodiunt.Vnde impiissimè & Eutychianæ hæreseos veneno infectus Leonem audes reprehendere,dum ex diuersitate gestorum vnius domini Christi, veritatem edoceat vtriusq. eius naturæ:vt quod ille ad demonstrationem vtrarum-que protulit naturarum,professionem calum-nieris duarum esse perso-narum?
units.tr: If the Word and the flesh are one nature, how is it that, since the Word is everywhere, the flesh is not also found everywhere? For when he was on earth, he was certainly not in heaven; and now, since he is in heaven, he is certainly not on earth, and to such a degree that we look for him to come from heaven according to Christ himself, whom we believe to be with us on earth according to the Word. Therefore, according to you, either the Word is contained in place together with his flesh, or the flesh is everywhere together with the Word, since one nature does not receive in itself what is contrary and diverse. But to be circumscribed by place is quite different from being everywhere; and since the Word is everywhere, while the flesh is not everywhere, it is clear that the one and the same Christ is of both natures: that he is indeed everywhere according to the nature of his divinity, and is contained in place according to the nature of his humanity; that he was created and has no beginning; that he is subject to death and cannot die: the one belongs to him from the nature of the Word, by which he is God; the other from the nature of the flesh, by which the same is God and man. Therefore the one Son of God, who is also made the Son of man, has a beginning according to the nature of his flesh, and has no beginning according to the nature of his divinity; he was created according to the nature of his flesh, and was not created according to the nature of his divinity; he is circumscribed by place according to the nature of his flesh, and is not contained by place according to the nature of his divinity; he is even less than the angels according to the nature of his flesh, and equal to the Father according to the nature of his divinity; he died according to the nature of his flesh, and did not die according to the nature of his divinity. THIS IS THE FAITH AND THE CATHOLIC CONFESSION, which the apostles handed down, the martyrs confirmed, and the faithful have kept until now. Whence, most impiously, and tainted with the poison of the Eutychian heresy, do you dare to reprehend Leo, since from the diversity of the deeds of the one Lord Christ he teaches the truth of each of his natures; so that what he brought forward to demonstrate both natures, you twist into a profession that there are two persons?

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: EPISTOLA D. ZACHARIÆ VRSINI AD AMICVM, DE PRAEDESTINATIO-ne: totam de ea disputationem erudite & breuiter explicans: & consilium, quod infirmi hic sequantur, ostendens:
units.tr: Letter of Dr. Zacharias Ursinus to a Friend, on Predestination: explaining the whole disputation about it learnedly and briefly, and showing the course that the weak should follow here:

units.la: HACTENVS ne quidem legendi tempus habui tuam de præ-destinatione disputationem. Imò ne nunc quidem habeo, sed eripio tantum temporis aliis negotiis dilatis, vt semel me liberem tua postulatione, quæ mihi videtur non ita necessaria, si D. Bezæ & Martyris scripta legisti, quę tibi me nominasse credo. Volui etiam hoc testatum facere, non animum hactenus, sed facultatem tibi gratificandi mihi defuisse. Postulo autem abs te vt ne disputando alios turbes, qui vel nolunt aliud audire, atque ipsi semel animo coeperunt, vel nō possunt subito doceri de rebus, quas antea nunquam sunt meditati, & quarum principia seu fundamenta falsa pro veris cum lacte imbiberunt. Nisi sperarem te tibi hac in parte Christiana prudentia & infirmorum tolerantia temperaturum, verbum ad te non scriberem.
units.tr: Until now I have not even had time to read your disputation on predestination. Indeed, I do not even have time now, but I snatch time from other business, postponed, so that I may at last free myself from your request, which does not seem so necessary to me, if you have read the writings of Dr. Beza and of Martyr, whom I believe you have named to me. I wished also to make this known: that it was not my will that has been lacking until now, but the opportunity to oblige you. I ask, however, that you not disturb others by disputing, those who either do not wish to hear anything else, having once made up their minds, or cannot suddenly be taught about matters which they have never before considered, and whose false principles or foundations they have drunk in, as it were, with their milk in place of true ones. Unless I hoped that you would, in this matter, temper your zeal with Christian prudence and with patience toward the weak, I would not be writing to you at all.

units.la: Non videtur mihi, vt tu scribis, difficillima pars doctrinæ Christianæ ea, quæ est de prædestinatione: si modo sine præiudiciis, & sine affectibus & serio studio non reformandi Deū ad nostras φιλαυτίας[?], sed ab ipso de ipso discendi, & omnem gloriam ipsi tribuendi, atque à nobis ad ipsum transferendi, scripturam sacram legamus. Sic mihi facta sunt facilia, quæ videbantur difficilia dū ex authoritate hominum pendebam, qui neque seipsos, « neque me expediebant. Nullus est locus doctrinæ sacræ, « de quo plura sint scripta in libris propheticis & apostolicis, « quàm hic ipse de prouidentia, electione, libero arbitrio: vt mirer, homines doctos & Christianos in eo hærere.
units.tr: The part of Christian doctrine concerning predestination is not, as you write, the most difficult. This holds if only we read Holy Scripture without prejudices, without passions and without a serious study not to reshape God according to our own self-love, but to learn about Him from Himself, to ascribe all glory to Him and to transfer it from ourselves to Him. For me, things that seemed difficult became easy when I depended on the authority of men, who neither explained themselves nor me. There is no place in sacred doctrine about which more has been written in the prophetic and apostolic books than here, concerning providence, election and free will; so that I marvel that learned and Christian men cling to this point.

units.la: Facias, quod ego feci, qui propter istam solam causam vt colligerem, expenderem, conferrem, quicquid de ea tam in concionibus, quàm in exemplis scripturæ continetur, perlegi diligentissimè Biblia à Genesi vsque ad finem Apocalypseos. Hoc vbi fecissem, partim ridebam, partim exsecrabar ista σκύβαλα[?] disputationum,& fumos sophismatum,qui frustra offunduntur huic fulgori. Poteris hoc per otium facere in Italia,vbi non habebis religionis exercitia, praeter lectionem Bibliorum, & precationem priuatam.Quidam etiam boni non habebant tantum otij,vt hoc facerent,alioqui nõ sic se implicassent.Istud autem semper tene,quod antea monui. Si nõ statim fiant tibi omnia peruia & perspicua,non turbari te sinas,sed paulatim sedulo animo mediteris inuocans Deum, & fundamentum tenens quod apud pios est extra controuersiam:nõ reipsum, sed Deũ esse authore totius tuę salutis,& quicquid es,habes,facis boni,siue magni,siue parui.Sic nõ errabis cũ aliquo periculo cõscientiæ aut salutis,etsi non omnia possis enodare & extricare,quæ cupéres.Scientia inflat,dilectio vero ædificat.
units.tr: Do what I did. For this one reason, in order to gather, weigh and compare whatever is contained about it, both in sermons and in the examples of Scripture, I read through the Bible most diligently from Genesis to the end of the Apocalypse. When I had done this, I partly laughed and partly cursed those dregs of disputations and the smoke of sophisms that are vainly poured over this brightness. You can do this at leisure in Italy, where you will not have the exercises of religion beyond the reading of the Bible and private prayer. Some good men did not have so much leisure as to do this, otherwise they would not have entangled themselves so. But always hold to what I advised earlier: if not everything becomes clear and transparent to you at once, do not allow yourself to be troubled, but gradually meditate with a diligent mind, calling upon God and holding the foundation that is beyond dispute among the godly: that it is not oneself but God who is the author of your whole salvation, and whatever you are, have, or do of good, whether great or small. Thus you will not err with any danger to conscience or salvation, even if you cannot unravel and disentangle all the things you would wish. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

units.la: Distingue Prouidentiam & prædestinationem tàquam totum & partem.Prouidentia enim est æternum & immutabile & optimum consilium seu decretum Dei, secundū quod omnia ad gloriā creatoris, & salutem electorum eueniunt.Prædestinatio est consilium Dei æternum de electorum salute inchoanda & perficienda:& de reproborum defectione, & abiectione in poenas:ideoque Electionem & Reprobationem tanquam partes complectitur.
units.tr: Distinguish providence and predestination as the whole and the part. For providence is the eternal, immutable and best counsel or decree of God, according to which all things come to pass for the glory of the Creator and the salvation of the elect. Predestination is God's eternal counsel concerning the beginning and completion of the salvation of the elect, and concerning the defection and rejection of the reprobate into punishment; and therefore it embraces election and reprobation as its parts.

units.la: Discerne item prouidentiam bonorum & malorum culpæ (nã mala poenæ habent rationem boni,id est,iustitiæ,ac proinde eatenus sunt à Deo:) Bona prouidet, hoc est,ab æterno decreuit & vult Deus efficere decreto tempore,ordine,modo.Horū igitur est causa, effector, author. Hæc fiunt nõ modò secundū prouidentiam, sed etiam à prouidentia Dei.Mala siue peccata,prouidet ab æterno,id est,decreuit & vult permittere,seu,nõ obstare,cauere,impedire,quo minus fiat ab aliis:nequaquam autè efficere in ipsis aut per ipsos, Horū igitur nequaquam est causa,sed alios causam earū esse finit, iusto & optimo ac sapientissimo cõsilio. Hæc fiunt secundùm quidem prouidētiam Dei,sed nequaquam ex ea: quia non decreuit Deus efficere,sed permittere, vt alij efficiant.Est autem permittere,nõ impedire peccatum in aliqua actione,seu non efficere, vt fit conformis legi & naturæ diuinæ.Sic verò permittit peccatũ Deus,quã-do vel non illuminat mentes suo spiritu, & voluntatis suæ agnitione,vel non flectit animos,vt in actione hûc finem principalem habeant, vt agnitam Dei voluntate exsequantur,& Deum hac obedientiâ honore afficiant. Hæc enim duo,nisi faciat in nobis Deus,quicquid egerimus,quantumuis bonum,iustum,sanctum fuerit,nihil nisi peccatum,nisi βδέλυγμα[?] erit coram Deo.
units.tr: Likewise distinguish the providence of God concerning the good and the evil fault (for evils have the character of good, that is, of justice, and so far are from God). God foresees good things, that is, from eternity He has decreed and wills to bring them about by His decree, at the appointed time, in order and manner. Of these, therefore, He is the cause, the effector and the author. These things happen not only according to providence but also from the providence of God. Evils or sins He foresees from eternity, that is, He has decreed and wills to permit them, or not to hinder, guard against or prevent them from being done by others; but by no means to effect them in them or through them. Of these, therefore, He is by no means the cause, but He allows others to be the cause of them, by a just, best and most wise counsel. These things happen indeed according to the providence of God, but by no means from it; because God did not decree to effect them, but to permit that others should effect them. To permit, however, is not to hinder sin in some action, or not to effect that it be conformed to the divine law and nature. God permits sin in this way when He either does not enlighten minds by His Spirit and by the knowledge of His will, or does not bend the souls so that in the action they have this as their chief end: that, having known the will of God, they carry it out and honour God by this obedience. For unless God works these two things in us, whatever we have done, however good, just and holy it may be, will be nothing but sin, and an abomination before God.

units.la: Iam distingue etiam Deum à creaturis & causis fecū-dis,iis discriminibus, quæ in quæstione de mũdi gubernatione præcipuè sunt spectanda.Primùm: Creaturæ sibi mutuò sunt obligatæ, vt altera alterius salutem promoueat, & interitum impediat vbicunque potest: quia Deus hoc omnibus præcipit, & ipsæ de se inuicem hoc mereri possunt: Et tu conuersus confirma fratres tuos. Deus nulli est obligatus, sicut non ad creandum ex nihilo: ita neque ad seruandum eum, siue vt sit omninò, siue vt in bonitate, & rectitudine, & felicitate, in qua conditus est, maneat: Quia omnia, quæ omnes habent bona, ab ipso habent: ipsi autem à nullo potest quicquam boni, aut felicitatis, aut commodi accedere, propter immensam & perfectissimam ipsius αὐτάρκειαν[?]. Quis est, qui prior dedit Domino, vt retribuat ei? An non licet mihi facere de meo, quod Volo? Secundo: Dei iustitia postulat, cùm ipse sit summum bonum, & author ac finis omnium, vt omnia referat ad suam gloriam, & potius[?] omnes creaturas perire sinat, si res ita postularet, quā illi nō satisfaciat. Creaturę autem se & omnia sua, non sibi, vel aliis, sed Deo debēt. Ideò Paulus optabat etiā ἀνάθεμα[?] esse à Christo, si salute & conuersione fratrum suorum posset gloriam Christi illustrare. Tertio: Deus igitur iustissimè peccatum creaturarum potest permittere, hoc est, non impedire: quia nouit pro sua sapientia, potentia, iustitia, bonitate immensa, illo ad suam gloriam & electorum salutem vti. Hoc non possunt creaturæ: Ideo legi de impediendis, quantum in ipsis est, etiam alienis peccatis sunt subiectæ. Quarto: Deus prima causa est, & effector bonorum omnium in mundo: Creaturæ tantum sunt instrumenta bonorum, quæ fiunt per ipsas, quibus Deus vtitur, pro optima & liberrima voluntate sua, & quælibet pro natura & modo agendo agendi,quem ipsi indidit & praescripsit,& conseruat sua prouidentia.Quinto: Deus solus simpliciter immutabilis est.Deus sum ego & nō mutor.Creaturę omnes mutabiles,aliae suapte natura,quae contingenter tantum agunt: ut fluxus elementaris materiae & motus animaliū: vel contingenter,& insuper etiam liberè,ut voluntates angelorum & hominum:aliae sua quidem natura immutabiles,ac proinde necessariò agentes,sicut agunt:sed tamen Deo æque faciles mutatu ac reliquæ,ut motus solis sua natura est,qualem videmus:Deus tamen cum vult, potest eum sistere,aut abrumpere.Sexto: Deus solus est simpliciter & absolutè liber,hoc est,à seipso mouens omnia,ipse motus & pendens à nullo,in seipso rationem & causam suorum consiliorum habens,& Αὐτοκρατὴς [?] & ἐξουσία summa aliter,si libuisset ei,ab æterno res decernendi:necessitatem & contingentiam omnibus imponès: ipse autem à nullo accipiens.Ephes. 1.9.Secundū beneplacitum,quod proposuit in seipso.Creaturarum autem rationalium libertas non est absoluta,hoc est, à nullo alio pendens, sed licet moueat sese interno principio, intellectu monstrante obiectum, & voluntate illud eligente aut repudiante proprio motu,sine vlla coactione:tamè ab alio agente,nempe à Deo regūtur,qui & obiecta offert,quibus,& quæ,& qualia,& quomodo vult,& ad ea, & per ea afficit & mouet, inclinat & flectit voluntates, quorum,& quando,& quatenus vult. Nimis contumeliosè de Deo sentit,si quis libertatem in Deo,& in creaturis non discernit. Non igitur tollit, sed conseruat, & auget libertatem voluntatis,diuina prouidentia & operatio tam generalis quàm specialis.Quanto enim magis Deus siue mouet,siue deserit eas,tantò maiori impetu, ac proinde tantò liberius & cupidiùs voluntates feruntur ab bona,vel ad mala. Idcirco tū demum liberrimè volemus bona,cum sic Deus erit omnia in omnibus, vt nihil nisi bonum velle possimus, nempe in vita coelesti.
units.tr: Now distinguish also God from creatures and secondary causes, by those differences which are especially to be considered in the question of the government of the world. First: creatures are bound to one another, so that each promotes the salvation of the other and hinders its ruin wherever it can, because God commands this of all, and they themselves can deserve this from one another: "And you, when you have turned, strengthen your brethren" (Luke 22). God is bound to no one, just as He is not bound to create out of nothing; so neither is He bound to preserve anyone, whether so that he simply exists, or so that he remains in the goodness, rectitude and happiness in which he was made. For all have the good things they possess from Him, and no good, happiness or advantage can accrue to Him from anyone, on account of His immense and most perfect self-sufficiency. "Who has first given to the Lord, that he should be repaid by Him? Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own?" (Rom. 11; Matt. 20). Second: the justice of God requires, since He Himself is the highest good, and the author and end of all things, that He refer all things to His own glory, and rather allow all creatures to perish, if the matter so required, than fail to satisfy Him. Creatures, however, owe themselves and all that is theirs not to themselves or to others, but to God. Therefore Paul also wished to be accursed from Christ, if by the salvation and conversion of his brethren he could illustrate the glory of Christ. Third: God therefore most justly can permit the sin of creatures, that is, not hinder it, because He knows, by His wisdom, power, justice and immense goodness, how to use it for His glory and the salvation of the elect. Creatures cannot do this; therefore they are subject to the law of hindering, so far as lies in them, even the sins of others. Fourth: God is the first cause and the effector of all good things in the world. Creatures are only the instruments of the good things which are done through them, and which God uses according to His most excellent and most free will; and each of them acts according to its nature and the mode of acting which He has implanted and prescribed in them, and which He preserves by His providence. Fifth: God alone is absolutely immutable. "I am God, and I do not change" (Mal. 3). All creatures are mutable: some by their own nature, which act only contingently, such as the flux of elemental matter and the motions of animals; or contingently and moreover freely, such as the wills of angels and men; others, indeed, immutable by their own nature, and therefore acting necessarily as they act, yet nonetheless as easily changed by God as the rest, as the motion of the sun is by its nature, such as we see it; yet God, when He wills, can halt it or break it off. Sixth: God alone is simply and absolutely free, that is, moving all things from Himself, Himself moved by no one and dependent on no one, having in Himself the reason and cause of His counsels, and the highest authority and power, if it had pleased Him, from eternity to decree things otherwise; laying necessity and contingency upon all things, but receiving from no one. "According to the good pleasure which He purposed in Himself" (Eph. 1:9). The freedom of rational creatures, however, is not absolute, that is, not dependent on no other; but although they move themselves by an internal principle, the intellect showing the object and the will choosing or rejecting it by its own motion, without any compulsion, yet they are governed by another agent, namely by God, who both offers the objects, which and what and of what kind and in what manner He wills, and by them and through them affects and moves, inclines and bends the wills, whom, and when, and in so far as He wills. He thinks too insultingly of God who does not distinguish freedom in God from freedom in creatures. Therefore divine providence and operation, both general and special, does not take away but preserves and increases the freedom of the will. For the more God either moves or forsakes them, the more forcefully, and therefore the more freely and eagerly, the wills are carried either toward good or toward evil. Hence we will the good most freely only when God will be all in all, so that we are able to will nothing but good, namely in the heavenly life.

units.la: Distingue etiam rationem effectuum: Idem effectus quia procedit à diuersis causis,earum respectu diuersus est. Bonus quatenus à bona,malus quatenus à mala causa exsistit: Contingens & mutabilis,quatenus à contingente agente: Necessarius & immutabilis, quatenus ab immutabili tabili causa procedit. Respectu igitur Dei, in quo su-mus, viuimus, & mouemur, tam mali,quàm boni,bona sunt omnia,quæ fiunt,cùm summè sit bonus & immuta-biliter bonus, ac proinde non nisi bona possit velle & facere,cum natura sua & cum lege, in qua natura & iu-stitiam suam expresserit,congruentia. Respectu creaturarum bona,quatenus bona sunt,& à Deo in bonitate sua conseruantur,mala quatenus mala,& Deo permittente ac deserente à bonitate in qua condita sunt,degenerant, nec in eam à Deo restituuntur. Sic respectu diuinæ libertatis omnia contingenter fiunt, etiam quæ ex causis secundis maximè necessaria sunt, vt motus cœli:respectu immutabilis decreti omnia necessaria, vt cum milites crucifigentes Christum,offa ipsius non frangunt,sed latus aperiunt lancea,quæ respectu causarum secundarum,erant maximè contingentia.
units.tr: Distinguish also the aspect of the effects. The same effect, because it proceeds from different causes, is different in relation to them. It is good insofar as it comes from a good cause, and evil insofar as it comes from an evil cause; it is contingent and changeable insofar as it comes from a contingent agent, and necessary and unchangeable insofar as it proceeds from an unchangeable cause. Therefore, with respect to God, in whom we live, move and have our being, all things that happen, both evil and good, are good, since he is supremely good and unchangeably good, and so can will and do only what agrees with his nature and with the law in which he has expressed his nature and justice. With respect to creatures, things are good insofar as they are good and are preserved by God in their goodness; they are evil insofar as they are evil, and, when God permits and forsakes them, they degenerate from the goodness in which they were created and are not restored to it by God. Thus, with respect to the divine freedom, all things happen contingently, even those which, from secondary causes, are most necessary, such as the motion of the heavens; with respect to the unchangeable decree, all things are necessary, as when the soldiers crucifying Christ did not break his bones but opened his side with a spear, an event which with respect to secondary causes was most contingent.

units.la: Vt igitur Dei consilia & opera, & iudicia non fiunt meliora, si per bonos exsequatur : ita nec deteriora, si per malos,& interrea[?] non corrigente ipsorum mentes & voluntates Deo, peccantes & pœnam per peccata sibi attrahentes. Sic etiam vt libertatem & contingentiam actionis diuinæ non tollit aut minuit ad vnum destinata,& necessariò ages causa secunda:ita prouidentiæ,voluntatis,consilij,decreti diuini immutabilitatem, non infringit mutabilis natura causarum secundarum,& suapte natura ad vtrumque aut diuersum effectum æque propendens & apta:consilio autem & gubernatione diuina ad alterum seu certum vno quoque tempore,secundum suæ naturæ & operationis modum determinata, inclinata,& mota,siue mediatè siue immediatè.
units.tr: Just as the counsels, works and judgments of God do not become better when carried out through good men, so neither do they become worse when carried out through evil men, whose minds and wills God does not correct, since they sin and bring punishment upon themselves through their sins. Likewise, just as the freedom and contingency of divine action is not removed or diminished by a secondary cause that is destined to one thing and acts of necessity, so the unchangeability of divine providence, will, counsel and decree is not broken by the changeable nature of secondary causes, which by their own nature lean equally toward either one effect or the other, and are apt for both; but by the counsel and government of God they are determined, inclined and moved toward one certain effect at each moment, according to the mode of their nature and operation, whether mediately or immediately.

units.la: Discerne & peccata, quorum alia sunt per se & suo genere peccata,videlicet quæ à Deo prohibita sunt, nec ab ipso singulari lege seu exceptione iubentur fieri, vt spoliatio Ægypti,mactatio Isaaci.Alia per accidens,vi-delicet quæ à Deo præcepta, aut saltem concessa sunt, sed à creatura depravata prauè,hoc est,nō ita,vt præce-pta sunt, fiunt,vt impiorum & hypocritarum sacrificia, precatio,& eleemosynæ. Verumque autem, siue per se, siue per accidens peccent homines,suo vitio & sua culpa faciunt. Quod vero Deus in ipsorum actionibus spe-ctat & stat & intendit, semper est bonum & iustum.
units.tr: Distinguish also sins: some are sins in themselves and by their kind, namely those which are forbidden by God and which he does not command to be done by any special law or exception, such as the spoiling of the Egyptians or the slaying of Isaac; others are sins by accident, namely those which God has commanded, or at least permitted, but which the creature corrupts by doing them wrongly, that is, not in the way they were commanded, such as the sacrifices, prayers and alms of the impious and hypocrites. Whether men sin in either way, in themselves or by accident, they do so by their own fault and their own guilt. But what God looks to, stands for and intends in their actions is always good and just.

units.la: Postremò discerne etiā necessitatē coactionis ,& immu-tabilitatis.Hæc enim confundere,nimis agreste esset. Illa enim violenter mouet, externo tantùm principio: hæc secundùm naturam agentis,interno principio mouete & mo-to,sicut moueri aptum est natum.Hæc vbi viderem,postquam oculos mihi Deus aperuit,non feci vnius cassæ nu-cis fabulas illas, Deum fieri causam peccati : tolli contin-gentiam,libertatem. Didici autem hæc ex locis scripturæ infinitis,qualia sunt:Gen.20. Ideò custodiui te, ne peccares in me,nec permisi, vt tangeres eam.Gen.45. Pro salute ses-tra misit me Deus ante vos.Item : Non vestro consilio sed Dei voluntate huc missus sum, qui fecit me quasi patrem Pharaonis.Gen.50.Nolite timere.Num possumus resistere voluntati? Vos cogitastu de me malum,sed Dominus ver-tit illud in bonū,vt exaltaret me,sicut in præsētia cernitis, & seruaret multos populos.Exo.4. 7.10.11.14 Indurabo cor Pharaonis & seruorū illius,& faciam signa mea in eo. Et 9.Ideo posui te,vt ostidam in te fortitudinē meam,& narretur nomen meum in omni terra.Exo.12. Dominus dedit gratiam populo coram Ægyptiis,vt comodarent eis,& spo-liauerunt Ægyptios,Exo.21.Qui non est insidiatus(ei quem interfecit) sed tradidit illū Dominus in manus eius. Dicit de cæde fortuita.Exo.32. Occidat vnusquisque fratrem,vt amicum & proximum suum. Laudatur hoc facientes,qui absque isto mandato pessimè fecissent: nec tamè si Deus non dedisset hoc mandatū, sed alio obiecto admoto illo-tu animos irritasset:minùs iustè puniuisset idololatras per instrumenta peccantia,quàm per iustè facientia , eo quod non occulta prouidentia, sed patefacta Dei voluntate re-gebantur.Exo.33.Miserebor cuius soluero,& clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit.Num.23.Non est Deus quasi homo,vt mentiatur,nec vt filius hominis,vt mutetur. Dixit ergo & non implebitur ? Ad benedicen-dum adductus sum,benedictionē prohibere non saleo.Deu. 5.Quis det eos habere talem mentem vt timeant me,& si-niuersa mādata mea in omni tempore,vt bene sit eis,& fi-lis eorum in aeternum?His & similibus locis ostēdit Deus, quid probet, quo deleētetur , quid placeat ei.Sed Exod.33. Miserebor cuius soluero :& similibus, quid efficere velit in hominib⁹,&in quib.Deu.13.Si dixerit propheta,eam⁹, & sequamur Deos alienos:non audies vocē eius,quia tentat vos Dominus,vt palam fiat,vtrum diligamus eum an non. Et ibidē:Propheta aut ille interficiatur: quia locutus est, vt vos auerteret à Domino Deo vestro. Deu.29 & non dabat vobis Deus cor intelligens & que in praesentem diē. Iof. 11. Domini sententia fuit,vt indurarentur corda eorum,vt pugnarent contra Israel,& caderent,ꝑ non inuenirēt vllā misericordiā,ac perirent,sicut praeceperat Domin⁹ Moysi.Iudic.1. & 3. Dominus reliquit gentes, quas tulerat deleri.1.Reg.2.No audiuerunt vocē patris sui:quia voluit Dominus occidere eos.1bi.c.10.Abiit cū eo pars exercitus,quorū tetigerat Deus corda. Ibi.10. Spiritus Domini recessit à Saul,& exagitabat eū Spiritus malus Domini,seu à Domino.2.Reg.12. Ecce,ego suscitabo super te malum de domo tua,& tollam vxores tuas in oculu tuis,& dabo proximo tuo,& dormiet cum vxoribus tuis in conspectu filius tuus. Tu enim fecisti abscondite.Ego aut faciam hoc in conspectu omnis Israelis.2. Reg. 16.Dominus praecepit ei, vt maledi ceret Dauidi.Et quis est, qui audet dicere,cur sic fecerit? Ib.17.Domini cultu dissipatum est consiliū Achitophel.Ib.24.Addidit furor Domini irasci contra Israelem, conuertitq. Dauidē,vt diceret ad Ioab:Numera Israelē.& 1.Par.21. Surrexit Satan contra Israelē & incitauit Dauidē,vt numeraret populū.2.Reg.12.& 2.Par.10. Noacquieuit Roboā populo: erat n voluntas Dei.& 2.Par.11.Mea hoc gestum est voluntate.3.Reg.22. Dedit Deus spiritū mendacij.1.Par.36.Suscitauit Deus spiritū Cyri.Esd.6 Couertat Dominus cor regis ad eos.Iob.1.Domin⁹ dedit,Domin⁹ abstulit.Iob.12. Adducit consiliarios in stultū finē.Iob.14.Constituisti termi nos eius,qui praeteriri non poterunt.Ps.105. Conuertit cor eorū,vt odissent populū eius.Ps.115. Quaecunque voluit fecit.Prou.16. Omnia fecit Dominus,propter semetipsū,etiam impium ad diē malum.Ib.In sinum proiciuntur sortes,sed à Deo iudicium earū proficiscitur.Ib.21.Cor regis in manu Domini, sicut flumina aquarum,quoquunque voluerit inclinabit.Eccl.7.Considera opera Dei,quē nemo potest corrigere,quē ille despexerit.Sap. 8.Sapientia pertingit ab extremo ad extremū,firmiter & suauiter disponit omnia. Vide eius libri c.12. & 19. Sir.17. Non possunt corda sua ex lapideis facere carnea.Ies.10.Va Assur virga furoris mei, &c. in manu eius indignatio mea mea. Ad gentē fallacē mittā eum, ut auferat spolia, & diripiat prædā. &c. Vide integrū locū: qui sol? sufficit ad refutatione obiectionis de causa peccati. Similia sunt in cap. 13. Icf.14 Dominus exercituum decreuit, & quis poterit infirmare? Ief.43. Omnē qui invocat nomen Domini in gloriā meā creaui eum, formaui eum & feci eum. Ib. Operabor, & quis auertet illud? Ief.45. Ego Dominus faciens pacem & creās malum. Ief.46. Consilium meum stabit, &c. Et locutus sum & adducam illud, creaui & facia illud. Ier.13. Si mutare potest Æthiops pellē suam, & Pardus varietates suas, vos poteritis bene facere, cum didiceritis malum. Ier.50. Aperuit Dominus thesaurum suum & protulit vasa iræ suæ. Thr.3. Quis est, qui dixerit, ut fieret Domino non iubente? Ex ore altissimi nō egredientur, nec bona nec mala? Ezech.12. Loquar verbum & faciam illud. 14. Propheta cum erraverit & locutus fuerit verbum: Ego Dominus decepi Prophetā illum. Eze.18 Nolo mortem morietis. Quale est illud Deut.5. Quis det eos talem, &c. Ezec.20. Dedi eis præcepta non bona. Eze.29. Nebucadnetzar seruus meus seruire fecit exercitum suum seruitute magna aduersus Cyrū. Eze.36. Et dabo vobis cor nouum, & spiritum nouum ponam in medio vestri: Et auferā cor lapideū de carne vestra. Confer cū Syrac,17. & Ier.13. Ezec.38. Circumagam te, & ponam frenum in maxillis tuis, & reducā te. In die illa ascendent sermones super cor tuum, & cogitabit cogitatione pessimā, & dices: Ascendam ad terrā, &c. Confer cū Isa.10. Daniel. 4. Iuxta voluntatem suam fecit, tam in virtutib. cœli, quā in habitationib. terra: Et non est qui resistat manui eius, & dicat ei, quare fecisti? Amos 3 Non est malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecit: dictū de malo pœnæ: sed sæpissimè per accidens etiam est malum culpæ, quod finit Deus concurrere, Mich.4. Gentes multa congregata sunt. Ipsa autem non cognouerunt cogitationes Domini.
units.tr: Finally, distinguish also the necessity of compulsion and of unchangeability. For to confuse these would be too crude. The former moves violently, by an external principle only; the latter moves by the nature of the agent, by an internal principle, and moves that which is naturally apt to be moved. When I saw this, after God had opened my eyes, I did not make those fables of a single rotten nut, that God is the cause of sin and that contingency and freedom are abolished. I learned these things from countless passages of Scripture, such as: Gen. 20. "Therefore I kept you from sinning against me, nor did I allow you to touch her." Gen. 45. "God sent me before you for the preservation of life." Likewise: "It was not by your counsel but by the will of God that I was sent here, who made me as a father to Pharaoh." Gen. 50. "Do not fear. Can we resist the will?" "You planned evil against me, but the Lord turned it into good, to exalt me, as you now see, and to save many peoples." Exod. 4, 7, 10, 11, 14: "I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants, and I will do my signs in him." And ch. 9: "Therefore I have set you up to show in you my strength, and that my name may be declared in all the earth." Exod. 12: "The Lord gave the people grace before the Egyptians, so that they lent to them, and they spoiled the Egyptians." Exod. 21: "He who did not lie in wait for him whom he killed, but God delivered him into his hand." This speaks of accidental slaughter. Exod. 32: "Let each man kill his brother, his friend and his neighbour." This is commended in those who did it, who would have acted most wickedly without this command; yet even if God had not given this command, but had stirred their minds by some other object, he would not have punished the idolaters by instruments that sinned any more justly than by instruments that acted justly, since they were governed not by a hidden providence but by the revealed will of God. Exod. 33: "I will have mercy on whom I shall have mercy, and I will be gracious to whom I please." Num. 23: "God is not as a man, that he should lie, nor as the son of man, that he should change. Has he therefore said, and will he not fulfil it? I have been brought to bless, and I am not accustomed to prohibit a blessing." Deut. 5: "Who will give that they have such a mind as to fear me and keep all my commandments at all times, that it may go well with them and with their children for ever?" By these and similar passages God shows what he approves, what he delights in, what pleases him. But by Exod. 33, "I will have mercy on whom I shall have mercy," and similar passages, he shows what he wills to effect in men, and in whom. Deut. 13: "If a prophet arises and says, let us go and follow other gods, you shall not hear his voice, for the Lord your God tests you, to make it plain whether you love him or not." And in the same place: "That prophet or dreamer shall be put to death, because he has spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God." Deut. 29: "and God has not given you a understanding heart, to this present day." Josh. 11: "It was the sentence of the Lord that their hearts should be hardened, that they should fight against Israel and fall, and find no mercy, and perish, as the Lord had commanded Moses." Judg. 1 and 3: "The Lord left the nations which he had determined should be destroyed." 1 Sam. 2: "They did not listen to the voice of their father, because the Lord willed to slay them." Ibid. ch. 10: "A part of the army went with him, whose hearts God had touched." Ibid. 10: "The Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit of the Lord, or from the Lord, troubled him." 2 Sam. 12: "Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes, and give them to your neighbour, and he shall lie with your wives in the sight of your son. For you did it in secret, but I will do this before all Israel." 2 Sam. 16: "The Lord commanded him to curse David." And who dares to say why he did so? Ibid. 17: "The counsel of Ahithophel was destroyed by the appointment of the Lord." Ibid. 24: "The anger of the Lord was kindled again against Israel, and it moved David to say to Joab: Number Israel." And 1 Chron. 21: "Satan rose up against Israel and stirred David to number the people." 2 Chron. 10 and 2 Sam. 12: "Rehoboam did not listen to the people, for it was the will of God." And 2 Chron. 11: "This was done by my will." 1 Kings 22: "God put a lying spirit." 1 Chron. 36: "God stirred up the spirit of Cyrus." Ezra 6: "May the Lord turn the heart of the king towards them." Job 1: "The Lord gave, the Lord took away." Job 12: "He leads counsellors into a foolish end." Job 14: "You have appointed his bounds, which cannot be passed." Ps. 105: "He turned their heart to hate his people." Ps. 115: "Whatever he willed, he did." Prov. 16: "The Lord made all things for himself, even the wicked for the day of evil." Ibid.: "The lots are cast into the lap, but their judgment comes from the Lord." Ibid. 21: "The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord, like the streams of water; he turns it wherever he will." Eccl. 7: "Consider the works of God, which no one can correct, which he has despised." Wisd. 8: "Wisdom reaches from end to end mightily, and orders all things sweetly." See that book, ch. 12 and 19. Sir. 17: "They cannot make their hearts of stone into flesh." Isa. 10: "Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger, etc.; in his hand is my indignation. I will send him against a deceitful nation, to take away spoils and seize the prey," etc. See the whole passage, which is enough to refute the objection about the cause of sin. Similar things are in ch. 13. Isa. 14: "The Lord of hosts has decreed, and who shall frustrate it?" Isa. 43: "Everyone who calls on the name of my glory, I created him, formed him and made him." Ibid.: "I will work, and who shall turn it back?" Isa. 45: "I am the Lord, making peace and creating evil." Isa. 46: "My counsel shall stand, etc. I have spoken and I will bring it about; I have created and will do it." Jer. 13: "If the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots, you also will be able to do good, when you have learned evil." Jer. 50: "The Lord has opened his treasure and brought forth the vessels of his wrath." Lam. 3: "Who is he who says that a thing comes to pass when the Lord has not commanded it? Do not good and evil come out of the mouth of the Most High?" Ezek. 12: "I will speak the word and do it." Ch. 14: "If a prophet errs and speaks a word, I the Lord have deceived that prophet." Ezek. 18: "I do not desire the death of him who dies." What is that in Deut. 5, "who will give them such a mind," etc.? Ezek. 20: "I gave them commandments that were not good." Ezek. 29: "Nebuchadnezzar my servant made his army serve with great servitude against Cyrus." Ezek. 36: "And I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit in the midst of you, and I will take away the stony heart from your flesh." Compare Sirach 17 and Jer. 13. Ezek. 38: "I will turn you about, and put a bridle in your jaws, and lead you back. In that day thoughts will rise up in your heart, and you will think a most evil thought, and you will say: I will go up to the land, etc." Compare Isa. 10. Dan. 4: "He did according to his will, both among the powers of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; and there is none who can resist his hand or say to him, what have you done?" Amos 3: "There is no evil in the city which the Lord has not done." This is said of the evil of punishment; but very often there is also an evil of guilt by accident, which God allows to concur. Mic. 4: "Many nations have gathered together. But they have not known the thoughts of the Lord."

units.la: Matt.7. Non potest arbor bona malos fructus ferre. Ibi.a- dificati super petrā non corruent. Vide commentarium Philippi super illum locū. Luc.10. Passer ǵnus nō cadit, Mat. 11. Gratias tibi ago Pater, quod hæc abscondisti à sapientib. Matth.13. Vobis datum est nosse: Cæteris autem non est datum. Mat.16. & passim apud Euangelistas Quod oporteret Christum ire Hierosolymam & multa pati. Matth.18. Ne-
units.tr: Matthew 7: "A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit." There: "Built upon the rock they will not fall." See Philip's commentary on that passage. Luke 10: "Not one sparrow falls." Matthew 11: "I thank you, Father, that you have hidden these things from the wise." Matthew 13: "To you it has been given to know; but to the others it has not been given." Matthew 16, and throughout the Evangelists: "That the Christ must go up to Jerusalem and suffer many things." Matthew 18: "Offences must needs come."

units.la: cesse est Venire scandala :Mat.20.Annon licet mihi de iure meo facere quod ego volo? multi vocati, pauci electi. Mat.24[?]. Oportet omnia fieri. Ibi. Electos in errore induci (scilicet finaliter) non est possibile. Ioh.6. Quidquid dat mihi pater, ad me venit, et venientem ad me non ejiciam foras. Ibid. Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater traxerit illum. Ibid. Haec est voluntas Patris, ut quod quod dedit mihi, ex eo non perdam. Ioh.10. Et alias oves habeo, quas oportet me adducere. Ibi. Oves meas nemo rapiet ex manu mea. Ioh.11. Caiphas, cum esset Pontifex, prophetabat. Ioh.12. Propterea non poterant credere, quia excaecauit eorum oculos. Ioh.13. Scio quos elegerim. Ioh.14. Quem Spiritum Mundus non potest accipere. Ioh.15. Non vos me elegistis, sed ego vos. Act.1. Oportuit impleri dicta de Iuda. Act.2. Hunc definito Dei consilio et praescientia traditum per manus impias acceptis, et cruci affixum interemistis. Act.3. Per ignorantiam fecistis, Deus autem, quae praenunciauerat sic impleuit. Act.4. Conuenerunt, ut facerent, quacunque manus tua et consilium tuum prius decreuerant fieri. Act.13. Crediderunt, quotquot ordinati erant ad vitam aeternam. Act.17. Ipse dat omnibus vitam et motum per omnia. Ibi. In ipso viuimus, movemur et sumus. Rom.1. Tradidit illos Deus in reprobam mentem. Ro.8. Diligentibus Deum omnia cooperantur in bonum. Ro.9. Cuius vult miseretur, quem vult indurat. Lege tota disputatione Pauli Ro. xi. Electio obtinuit: reliqui indurati sunt. Ib. χαρίσματα εἰσὶν ἀμεταμέλητα. 1.Co.4. Quid habes quod non accepisti? Eph.1. Elegit nos in ipso ante Mundi creationem, ut essemus sancti. Ib. Praedestinati secundum propositum eius, qui omnia effecit secundum consilium voluntatis suae. Legatur ipsum caput Phil.1. Deus efficit in nobis velle et perficere pro bona voluntate. 2.Thes.2. Immisit eis errores efficaces. Vide locum, &c. 2.Tim.2. firmum stat fundamentum Domini. 1.Ioh.2. Ex nobis egressi sunt, sed ex nobis non erant. 1.Ioh.4. In hoc est dilectio, quia prior dilexit nos. Apoc.17. Deus dabit in corda eorum, ut faciat sententiam suam. Sed ego nimis multa, dum volui pauca tantum delibare. Nam sexcenta similia loca scripturae inuenies.
units.tr: Matthew 20: "Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own?" "Many are called, but few are chosen." Matthew 24: "All these things must come to pass." There: "It is not possible for the elect to be led into error (that is, finally)." John 6: "All that the Father gives me shall come to me, and him that comes to me I will in no wise cast out." Ibid.: "No one can come to me unless the Father draws him." Ibid.: "This is the Father's will, that of all he has given me I should lose nothing." John 10: "And other sheep I have, which I must bring." There: "No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand." John 11: "Caiaphas, being high priest, prophesied." John 12: "For this cause they could not believe, because he has blinded their eyes." John 13: "I know whom I have chosen." John 14: "The Spirit which the world cannot receive." John 15: "You did not choose me, but I chose you." Acts 1: "The things said about Judas had to be fulfilled." Acts 2: "Him, delivered up by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have taken and by lawless hands have crucified and slain." Acts 3: "You did it in ignorance, but God thus fulfilled what he had foretold." Acts 4: "They gathered together to do whatever your hand and your counsel had predestined to be done." Acts 13: "As many as were ordained to eternal life believed." Acts 17: "He gives to all life and breath and all things." There: "In him we live, and move, and have our being." Romans 1: "God gave them over to a reprobate mind." Romans 8: "To those who love God all things work together for good." Romans 9: "He has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens." Read the whole discussion of Paul in Romans 11: "The election obtained it, and the rest were hardened." Ibid.: "The gifts of God are without repentance" [χαρίσματα εἰσὶν ἀμεταμέλητα]. 1 Corinthians 4: "What do you have that you did not receive?" Ephesians 1: "He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy." Ibid.: "Predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will." Let the whole chapter of Philippians 1 be read: "God works in us both to will and to do for his good pleasure." 2 Thessalonians 2: "He sent them strong delusions." See the passage, etc. 2 Timothy 2: "The firm foundation of the Lord stands." 1 John 2: "They went out from us, but they were not of us." 1 John 4: "In this is love, that he first loved us." Revelation 17: "God has put it into their hearts to fulfil his purpose." But I have said far too much, when I meant only to touch on a few points; for you will find six hundred similar passages in Scripture.

units.la: Accedunt his argumenta, quae nemo euertet.
units.tr: To these are added arguments that no one will overturn.

units.la: Omnipotentia Dei non patitur quicquam fieri, quod Deus non aut simpliciter aut secundum quid velit. Quod enim simpliciter non vult, id fieri non potest vllo modo.
units.tr: The omnipotence of God does not allow anything to happen that God does not will, either absolutely or in some respect. For what he does not will absolutely cannot come to pass in any way.

units.la: Infinita ipsius sapientiæ non patitur quicquam in Mundo sine ipsius consilio fieri.
units.tr: The infinite wisdom of God does not allow anything in the world to happen without his counsel.

units.la: Dum fines, quos habet omnium optimos, vult, etiam media vult, saltem secundum quid: non autem quatenus peccata sunt.
units.tr: While he wills the ends, which are of all the best, he also wills the means, at least in some respect, though not insofar as they are sins.

units.la: Bona omnia & res positiuæ in Mundo ab ipso sunt: & eius prouidentia reguntur. Motus igitur quatenus sunt motus à Deo reguntur.
units.tr: All good things and positive realities in the world are from him and are governed by his providence. Motions, therefore, insofar as they are motions, are governed by God.

units.la: Nec Dei consilia à creaturarum operibus, sed contrà creaturarum actiones & motus à Dei consilio pendent.
units.tr: God's counsels do not depend on the works of creatures; rather, the actions and motions of creatures depend on God's counsel.

units.la: Præscit immutabiliter etiam maximè mutabilia. Ergo præscit ex causa immutabili, hoc est, æterno decreto suo. Hæc prouidentiam confirmant vniuersalem omnium particularium.
units.tr: He foreknows immutably even those things that are most mutable. Therefore he foreknows from an immutable cause, that is, from his eternal decree. These considerations confirm the universal providence over all particular things.

units.la: Non minus multa electionem æternâ & immutabilem.
units.tr: No less do many things confirm an eternal and immutable election.

units.la: Nihil in quoquam potest exsistere boni, nisi Deus ab æterno decreuerit hoc efficere.
units.tr: Nothing good can exist in anyone unless God from eternity decreed to bring it about.

units.la: Quos semel amat, eos ab æterno in æternum amat. Ergo non possumus esse certi de præsenti gratia Dei erga nos, nisi certi etiam simus de æterna, nisi Deum mutabilem velimus fingere.
units.tr: Whom he loves once, them he loves from eternity to eternity. Therefore we cannot be certain of God's present grace toward us unless we are also certain of his eternal grace, unless we wish to imagine a changeable God.

units.la: Credere debemus vitam æternam.
units.tr: We ought to believe in eternal life.

units.la: Spes debet esse certa.
units.tr: Hope ought to be certain.

units.la: Petenda salus æterna sine conditione & hæsitatione.
units.tr: Eternal salvation is to be sought without condition and without hesitation.

units.la: Rata est perpetuo Christi pro electis intercessio. Sufficiunt mihi hæc e multis. Forte etiam tibi. Te igitur tandem iam audiamus.
units.tr: The intercession of Christ for the elect is valid forever. These points suffice for me out of many; perhaps they suffice for you too. So let us at last hear you.

units.la: Primum: hæc doctrina hominem abducit à voluntate Dei revelata ad arcanam, à verbo ad impressiones fidei antequam verbo audito credatur. Quid audio? Si vidisti hæc scripta in nostra doctrina, cur non profers aut notas loca? Si sequi putas ex ea, cur non argumentis agis, & deducis consequentias? Quæ hæc est Dialectica, & à quo præceptore tibi tradita, conuitia dicere dira & capitalia in homines innocentes sine vlla vel specie probationis? Si autem nec scripta à nobis monstrare, nec ex revelata doctrina deducere bona aliqua aut saltem apparente consequentia potes (vt te non posse certissimum est) cur nos hoc lotio perfundis? Nunquam hæc nobis in mentem venerunt, omnia docemus contraria. Quid de nobis hæc tibi vel aliis inculcant,mentiuntur sceleratissime & impudentiffime tanquam Diaboli. Apage igitur hæc monstra. Verbum Dei est,ô bone, amplectentes cupido & grato animo, in vera pœnitentia, beneficium Christi in Euangelio oblatum debere statuere,se esse in gratia apud Deum per Christum,& esse certissimos hæredes vitæ æternæ,idque non ex operibus, neque factis,neque præuiisis: sed ex mera, & gratuita Dei misericordia, qua ab æterno ipsos dignatus est præaliis,quod nisi fecisset Deus,vnà cum cæteris fuissent periturî in sua cæcitate & impietate. Verbum confituimus maiorem Syllogismi, Testimonium conscientiæ, quod credamus verbo,& pœnitentiam agamus Minorem hoc modo. Qui credit in filium habet vitam æternam. Ego credo in Filium. Hinc deducimus istam conclusionem de qua est quæstio. Ergo habeo vitam æternam. Est-ne hoc abducere à verbo,aut aliunde atque è verbo iudicare de gratia Dei & salute nostra? Profecto si tu aliter iudicare de te voluerit,in æternum perieris.
units.tr: First: this doctrine draws a man away from the revealed will of God to a hidden one, from the Word to impressions of faith before the Word is heard and believed. What do I hear? If you have seen these things written in our teaching, why do you not produce them or mark the passages? If you think they follow from it, why do you not argue and draw out the consequences? What kind of dialectic is this, and from what teacher did you receive it, to hurl dire and capital insults at innocent men without any show of proof? But if you can neither show these things written by us nor deduce them from revealed doctrine by any good, or at least apparent, consequence (as you most certainly cannot), why do you drench us with this slop? These things never came into our minds; we teach the very opposite. What you and others pile upon us, they lie most wickedly and shamelessly, like devils. Away with these monstrosities! Good man, the Word of God is this: that we, embracing it with eager and grateful hearts, in true repentance, should settle that the benefit of Christ offered in the Gospel is ours; that we are in grace before God through Christ, and are most certain heirs of eternal life; and this not from works, nor deeds, nor foreseen merits, but from the mere and free mercy of God, by which he deigned to choose them before others from eternity; for, unless God had done so, they would have perished along with the rest in their blindness and impiety. We confess the Word as the major premise of the syllogism; the testimony of conscience, that we believe the Word and repent, as the minor premise, in this way: "He who believes in the Son has eternal life. I believe in the Son. From this we draw this conclusion, which is the matter in question: therefore I have eternal life." Is this to draw away from the Word, or to judge concerning the grace of God and our salvation from anywhere other than the Word? Truly, if you wish to judge of yourself otherwise, you will perish for ever.

units.la: Nos textum Pauli torquere & corrupere,arcana scrutari dicis. Exemplum nullum profers, nec potes proferre. Loco autem probationis conuitia putidarum declamationum obtrudis. Si quæreremus, quare hunc potius,quàm illum,Petrum potius quàm Iudam ad vitam æternam elegerit Deus: an alij sint electi, quantus sit numerus electorum: aut similia horum: causam haberet hæc scommata in nos proiiciendi. Hæc enim sunt abyssus imperuestigabilis,de qua Paulus: & nobis ad salutem non necessaria. Sed fontem salutis nostræ esse gratuitam Dei electionem, eámque certam & immutabilem esse, & nobis patefieri ex effectibus in nobis, hoc est,ex fide & pœnitentia,per auditum verbi Dei excitatis. Hæc non voluit Deus nobis ignota esse, sed propter suam gloriam, & nostram consolationem millies in verbo suo inculcauit. Nihil igitur ad nos tua epiphonemata, nihil ad nos, quantumuis tibi bella visa sint.
units.tr: You say that we twist and corrupt Paul's text and pry into hidden things. You produce no example, nor can you produce one. Instead of proof you thrust upon us the insults of foul declamations. If we asked why God chose Peter rather than Judas, or this man rather than that, to eternal life; whether others are elect, or how great the number of the elect is, or things like these, you would have some cause to hurl these jests at us. For these are the unsearchable abyss of which Paul speaks, and they are not necessary to our salvation. But that the source of our salvation is God's free election, and that this election is certain and immutable, and is made known to us from its effects in us, that is, from faith and repentance, roused by the hearing of God's Word: this God did not wish to be unknown to us, but for his own glory and our consolation he has impressed it on us a thousand times in his Word. So your exclamations are nothing to us, nothing to us, however fine they may have seemed to you.

units.la: II. Deliria Stoicorum Manichæorum calumnia obiciuntur.
units.tr: II. The Stoic and Manichaean ravings are thrown at us as a calumny.

units.la: Secundùm: ne ab illis quidem obsoletis & aridis stercori bus abstines,nimirum destitutus aliis telis, quibus nos petas,Stoicis & Manichæis. Exsecramur delirium Stoicum de necessitate in ipsis rebus inhærente, quæ Deum & res alias constringat, & sibi subiectas habeat. Contra verò Deum liberrimum, & summum omnium rerum gubernatorem esse statuimus, qui facit omnia secundum beneplacitum suum, cuius manum nemo potest auertere, qui sit aeternus, immutabilis, perpetuo sibi constans. Huius tu optimum, sapientissimum, liberrimum, immutabile decretum quare iam petulanter derides nomine tabularum fatalium. Futilitatem istaru stropharum ridere quis posset: sed impietatem blasphemam in Deum, quam addis, nemo Christianus riserit, sed ei vehementer indignatus fuerit. An tibi absurdum est, omnia quae fiunt & futura sunt in aeternum, ante lapsum Deo fuisse cognita & decreta? Rides ergo Paulum dicentem, ante conditum Mundum nobis datam esse gratiam in Christo: Et Iacobum dicen-te: Nota sunt Deo opera sua a seculo, quod est, ab aeterno. Te vero tam diu studiis Philosophicis & Theologicis versatum tam ineptire, ut Deum nobis fingas mutabilem. Profecto mente cares, si res agitur tibi seria: rursus fron-te cares, si sic ludis amice. An tu Niniuitis minitantem & parcentem existimas mutari? Parcere volebat tam ante, quam post minas. Cur ergo minabatur? Hanc ipsam ob causam, ut minando eos converteret, & conversos seruaret. Non igitur a se dissentit, aut discedit a sententia. In minis enim subaudiebat conditionem hanc, nisi agerent poenitentiam. Hanc autem in illorum animis minando efficere iam ab aeterno constitutum habebat.
units.tr: Second: you do not even refrain from those obsolete and dry dung-heaps, namely, since you are deprived of other weapons with which to attack us, the Stoics and the Manichaeans. We curse the Stoic madness about a necessity inhering in things themselves, which binds God and other things and holds them subject to itself. On the contrary, we hold that God is most free and the supreme governor of all things, who does all things according to his good pleasure, whose hand no one can turn aside, who is eternal, unchangeable, and constantly consistent with himself. Why do you now wantonly mock his best, wisest, most free and unchangeable decree under the name of fated tables? Anyone could laugh at the futility of those trifles; but no Christian would laugh at the blasphemous impiety against God which you add, rather he would be bitterly indignant at it. Is it absurd to you that all things which happen and will happen to eternity were known and decreed by God before the fall? So you laugh at Paul saying that grace was given to us in Christ before the world was made; and at James saying: "All his works are known to God from the beginning of the age," that is, from eternity. But that you, having been so long engaged in philosophical and theological studies, should be so foolish as to make God mutable for us! Truly you lack reason if you are serious; again you lack a forehead if you are playing thus, friend. Do you think that God, threatening and sparing the Ninevites, was changed? He wished to spare them both before and after the threats. Why then did he threaten? For this very reason, that by threatening he might convert them and, once converted, save them. He therefore does not disagree with himself or depart from his purpose. For in the threats he implied this condition, unless they repented; and he had from eternity determined to bring this about in their minds by threatening.

units.la: Grandem porro dicam nobis impingis, disciplinam, inuocationem, Magistratum, Leges nos euertere ac tollere. O he[?] vero pedet ntim,ne offendas aut decidas de gradibus. Si futurum est, sicut profecto est immutabiliter & necessario, quicquid Deus decreuit: inania sunt illa omnia, scilicet, si fine[?] illis decreuisset, ut fierent ipsius decreta. Si vero per haec media alios seruare, alios coercere, alios item inexcusabiles vult reddere, ac propterea nos illis uti iussit, & per hoc mandatu permouere nos, ut illis utamur, atq. hoc modo bona nobis decreta consequa-mur: quis tu es reformator consiliorum Dei, qui inania illa decreuisse & ordinasse & praecepisse mussites[?]? Decreuit Deus cras diem facere. An igitur tu nobis audiendus eris dicens, frustra oriri Solem? An quia ipse quotannis educit panem e terra, tollendam commoditatem coeli & agri[?] culturam dices? Quæ schola te docuit à positione causæ primæ ad remotionē secundarum concludere? Cum Deus finem decreuit, etiam media ad finem ordinauit & decreuit, atque his vti nos iussit: Si vtimur, ipsius beneficio, si non vtimur, ipsius iudicio, nostra culpa, & periculo fit. Blasphemias Manicheas non nobis, sed Paulo impingis, cui nihil cum Mane est commune. Abvno Deo bono omnes creati sunt boni, illius permissu iustissimo, lapsi sunt ac sese deprauarunt auertendo se à Deo. Ex hac igitur perdita massa elegit & reprobauit ab æterno, quos voluit? Nihil horum Manes. Atrox ergo conuitium est, Deum aliquos reprobasse contra dicta: Deus vult nullos perire, sed omnes saluos fieri, &c. Amore ergo creaturas, & bonitate [illegible, ~6 letters] in destructione suorum operum & mandato, sed vocatione & inuitatione ad pœnitentiam & salutem, nullos perire, omnes salvos esse vult: at no efficacia. Se enim nullius exitio lætari, quatenus exitiu destructio, cruciatus est: omnes ad se inuitare, etsi alios aliter, sæpissime dixit in verbo suo. Effecturum autem, vt omnes obtemperent & feruentur, non modo nusquam dixit, sed plurimis etiam locis contrarium expressit. Sic non pugnat secum scriptura, docens, Deum omnium salute lætari, & tamen aliquos reprobasse.
units.tr: Furthermore, you charge us with a great thing: that we overturn and abolish discipline, invocation, the magistracy, and laws. Oh, but watch your step, lest you stumble or fall from your rungs. If it is going to happen, as it certainly does happen unchangeably and necessarily, whatever God has decreed, then all those things are empty, namely if God decreed them without any end for them to be the means of fulfilling his decrees. But if through these means he wishes to save some, restrain others, and likewise make others inexcusable, and for this reason has commanded us to use them, and by this command moves us to use them, so that in this way we obtain the good things decreed for us: who are you, reformer of God's counsels, that you mutter that he decreed, ordained and commanded those empty things? God has decreed to make the day tomorrow. Shall we then have to listen to you saying that the sun rises in vain? Or because he himself brings forth bread from the earth every year, will you say that the advantage of heaven and the cultivation of the field is to be abolished? What school taught you to conclude from the positing of the first cause to the removal of the secondary causes? When God has decreed the end, he has also ordained and decreed the means to the end, and has commanded us to use them. If we use them, it is by his benefit; if we do not use them, it is by his judgment, and it happens through our own fault and at our own peril. You fling Manichaean blasphemies not at us but at Paul, who has nothing in common with Manes. All were created good by the one good God; by his most just permission they fell and corrupted themselves by turning away from God. Did he therefore choose and reprobate from eternity from this lost mass whomever he wished? Manes has none of this. It is therefore a savage insult to claim that God reprobated some, contrary to the words: "God wishes that none should perish, but that all be saved," etc. Out of love for creatures and goodness he wishes that none perish and all be saved, not in the destruction of his works or by command, but by calling and invitation to repentance and salvation; yet not with efficacy. For he does not rejoice in anyone's ruin, since ruin is destruction and torment; to invite all to himself, though some in different ways, he has very often said in his word. But that he would bring it about that all obey and are saved, he has not only nowhere said, but has even expressed the contrary in very many places. Thus Scripture does not contradict itself, teaching that God rejoices in the salvation of all, and yet has reprobated some.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Tertium: Puto te voluisse multitudine argumentorum vincere, cum robore eorum dissideres, idcirco idem primum & tertio loco posuisse: nisi forte malis amplificationem esse ab Enthusiastarum nomine petitam, vt hoc etiam emblema tibi non perierit. Sed age, quam tandem affinitatem cum iis contraxisti? Neglecto verbo raptus nos expectare dicis. Apud quem vero nostrorum audiuisti, aut legisti hoc? Non minus igitur dicitur hoc verecunde de nobis, quàm primum illud dicebatur, nos discedere à voluntate Dei patefacta: Deum in nobis fidem & conuersionem efficere dicimus, sed per verbum ordinario quidem modo agendi, cui nos alligauit, seruata sibi libertate præter ordinem agendi, si quando velit, sicut etiam per verbum mouendi, quos ipsi est visum, & quando, & quatenus est visum.
units.tr: Third: I think you wished to overcome by a multitude of arguments, since you differed in their strength; therefore you placed the same thing first and third; unless perhaps you prefer that the amplification be taken from the name of the Enthusiasts, so that this emblem too might not be lost to you. But come, what affinity have you finally contracted with them? You say we expect a rapture, neglecting the word. But from whom among our people did you hear or read this? This is said no less shamefully about us than that first charge was made, that we depart from the revealed will of God: we say that God works faith and conversion in us, but through the word, in the ordinary manner of acting to which he has bound us, while keeping for himself freedom beyond the ordinary manner of acting whenever he wills, just as also through the word he moves whom he has pleased, and when, and as far as he has pleased.

units.la: Addis eadem incogitantiâ, & haud scio, an non reclamante conscientia, quam tandiu nostros audiuisti, secundùm nos voluntatem nihil agere. In vtroque rursus argumentaris à positione causæ primæ ad exclusionem secundæ. Agit voluntas, sed mota, & acta, inclinata, emollita, renouata à Deo per verbum, non inquam impulsa, vt lapis, vel truncus, sed obiecto in mente agitato alle & a & inuitata. Dei opus erat in Paulo hæc voluntas Pauli, quod volebat facere, quæ vellet Dominus. Dei iudicium & Iudæorum peccatum, quòd à Christo congregari nolebant. Frustra præcedet gratia nisi comitatum voluntatis efficiat. Quid igitur dicis de pari modo agendi? Cur non potius audis illum doctorem Ecclesiæ, qui dicit: Deus [?] est qui operatur in vobis & velitis, & perficiatis? Rem magnam & verissimam tibi dicam. Nullomodo possumus tueri puritatem articuli de iustificatione gratuita & certa, contra meritum, quod de congruo vocant, & [illegible, ~3 letters] Papistarum, nisi explodatur impium commentum de generali gratia Dei, relinquente in nostra potestate acceptionem & vsum vel repudiationem sui, & æternus atque immutabilis amor Dei erga electos, ab obscuratione & sophismatibus vindicetur.
