units.tr: You add with the same thoughtlessness, and I do not know whether your conscience does not protest, since you have heard our people for so long, that according to us the will does nothing. In both cases again you argue from the positing of the first cause to the exclusion of the second. The will acts, but moved, and acted upon, inclined, softened, renewed by God through the word; not, I say, pushed like a stone or a log, but drawn and invited by an object stirred in the mind. This will of Paul was the work of God in Paul, for he wished to do what the Lord wished. It was God's judgment and the sin of the Jews that they were unwilling to be gathered by Christ. Grace will go before in vain unless it brings about the accompanying will. What then do you say about the same manner of acting? Why do you not rather listen to that teacher of the Church who says: "It is God who works in you both to will and to perform"? I will tell you a great and most true thing. We can in no way defend the purity of the article on justification as gratuitous and certain, against the merit which they call of congruity by the Papists, and [...], unless the impious invention of a general grace of God is exploded, which leaves in our power the acceptance and use, or the rejection, of itself, and unless the eternal and unchangeable love of God toward the elect is vindicated from obscuring and sophisms.

units.la: Quartum [?] agere voluisse videris, dum robur argumentorum in medio collocasti, primum & vltimum argumentum lixis & calonibus complens, contrà quàm scis præcipere declamatores in scholis. Hic est Achilles illorum: Deum fieri causam peccati, si decreuit aliquos in cæcitate, peccato, & morte relinquere, quem tu bene cristatum produxisti. Sed huc nobis pharetram Philo-ctetis. Primum rursus in eo candorem desidero, cum dicis, multorum ex nostris hæc esse verba: Deum in reprobis hoc efficaciter operari, vt peccent. Multos narras, cum ne vnum quidem proferas, nec possis credo proferre. Toto enim pectore hanc vocem & sententiam exsecramur, quod sexcentis testimoniis facile probabunt nostrorum scripta.
units.tr: You seem to have wished to do the fourth thing, while you placed the strength of your arguments in the middle, filling the first and last argument with camp-followers and servants, contrary to what you know the declaimers teach in the schools. Here is their Achilles: that God becomes the cause of sin, if he decreed to leave some in blindness, sin, and death, which you brought forward well crested. But bring here to us the quiver of Philoctetes. Again, in this I miss candor, when you say that these are the words of many of ours: that God efficaciously works this in the reprobate, that they sin. You name many, when you do not produce even one, nor, I believe, could you produce one. For with our whole heart we curse this voice and opinion, which our writings will easily prove by six hundred testimonies.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Sed dixeris, consequi hoc ex nostra doctrina. Qui enim decreuit permittere hominum peccata, est eorum author. Vide quale sit argumentum tuum, quod inuersum sufficit ad causam tibi extorquendam è manibus. Qui enim permittit peccatum, non debens cuiquam eius impedimentum, nedum etiam puniendi ius habens pœna desertionis & abiectionis in pœnas æternas,is ne-quaquam est author vel fautor, sed permiffor & iudex peccati. Si autem permittit peccatum Deus, sequitur,eū nihil minus esse,quā eius authore. Si iniftas: at priuatio illa gratiæ,quam pœnæ loco infligit,est peccatum: paralogifmu accidentis committitis. Per fe.n. quatenus à Deo infligitur, iustissima pœna est:per accidens,hoc est,quia ab hominibus per primum & per subsequentia peccata est attracta: peccatum est. Plus habuisset coloris fi ex prouidentia collegisses hanc peccati effectionem: quantumquā idé est paralogifmus. Volebat vehementissime & efficacissime Deus crucifixione Filij per eos,per quos facta est: nec tamen volebat,sed sinebat concurrere cum suo iustissimo & sapientissimo & omnium maxime admirando & glorioso opere,quod per eos exercebat, ipsorum parricidiū,quod postea horribiliter puniuit. Volebat bella Nebucadnetza-ris,eius interea oderat peccata. Volebat bellum Abfolo-mi contra Dauidem & pollutionem conigij Dauidis.Sed quatenus hæc volebat Deus,erat iustissimæ pœnæ Dauidis: quatenus autem Abfolomus ista faciebat, regni tatū occupandi,& patrem opprimendi causa,minime vero habens mandatum Dei quod sequeretur, erant seditio & incestus. Hæc vero prauitas Abfolomi per accidens cōcur-rit cum iudicio Dei,quod per ipsum exercet.Nec plus egeris,si dicas,tum Deum fieri causam peccati, cū deserti ab ipso non aliud possunt nisi peccare. Scripturam, n.& Deum ipsum accusas, sæpissime hoc dicentem, sed fine huius blasphemiæ periculo: quia genus humanum sponte sibi hanc necessitatem peccandi in Paradiso attraxit.
units.tr: But you will say that this follows from our doctrine: whoever has decided to permit men's sins is their author. See what sort of argument this is; turned around, it is enough to wrest your case from your own hands. For whoever permits sin, without being obliged to anyone to prevent it, and still less having the right to punish, is by no means its author or abettor, but the permitter and judge of sin. If God permits sin, it follows that he is in no way its author. You object: but that privation of grace, which he inflicts as a punishment, is sin. You commit the fallacy of accident. For in itself, insofar as it is inflicted by God, it is the most just punishment; accidentally, that is, because by men it has been drawn into sin through the first and subsequent sins, it is sin. You would have had more colour if you had inferred this effecting of sin from providence, although it is the same fallacy. God most vehemently and most efficaciously willed the crucifixion of the Son through those by whom it was done; yet he did not will it so much as permit it to concur with his most just, most wise and most admirable and glorious work, which he was carrying out through them: the murder of the Son by its own authors, which he afterwards punished dreadfully. He willed the wars of Nebuchadnezzar, yet in the meantime he hated their sins. He willed Absalom's war against David and the defiling of David's concubines. But insofar as God willed these things, they were a most just punishment for David; insofar as Absalom did them, for the sole purpose of seizing the kingdom and oppressing his father, and with no command of God behind them, they were sedition and incest. Absalom's wickedness coincides accidentally with the judgment of God, which God carries out through him. Nor would you gain more if you said that God is then made the cause of sin, since those abandoned by him can do nothing but sin. For you accuse both Scripture and God himself, who says this very often, but without danger of this blasphemy: because the human race of its own accord drew upon itself this necessity of sinning in Paradise.

units.la: Quintum:Dicis legalem esse hanc doctrinam. Quid si esset legalis,an propterea esset falsa? An non æque vera est Lex & Euangelium? Addis: ex ratione sumptam. Perspicacior fuisse te oportet in libris Platonis & Aristotelis, quàm ego & omnes alij fuimus, qui nunquam ibi quaerimus eam inuenire. Breuiter. Ex penetralibus Euangelij eam esse scito. An Paulum ad Romanos 9.10.11.12. Eph.1. Legem prædicare voluisse existimas? Non opinor hoc te credere. Et quid magis ad medullam euangelij pertinet quàm æternus,gratuitus,immutabilis amor Dei erga electos,quem Christus dicit fuisse causam,cur etiam Filium vnigenitum pro nobis daret, ne dum vt huic nos per fidem insitos in æternum seruaret, & opus in nobis inchoatum perficeret? Si hæc non sunt Euangelica, nescio quæ sint. Monere iterum (satis est quod supra de puritate articuli iustificationis retinenda dixi. Partim admiratione, partim indignatione & dolore me perturbauit ista tua vox, quòd scribis: Quam me illa exclamatio perturbat: Cui Deus aliquid debet? Frontem serij hæc legens. Certè aut parum legisti libros sacros, aut nimis occupatus es affectibus & rari diciis, cum verba scripturæ tam audacter damnas. Ann n est Paulina exclamatio Rom.11.13. Quis est qui prior dedit Domino vt retribuat ei? Certè me nihil magis consolatur, quàm hic ineffabilis Dei amor erga me, quòd mihi non plus debens, quàm Iudæ, & Caino, ex hoste suo fecerit mihi filium suum per mortem vnigeniti. Nimis enim est [illegible, ~12 letters], quod affers de obligatione Dei erga nos per promissionem. Quid igitur quæso ante applicationem promissionem obtendes? At promissio cui Deum obligat, nisi qui fide eam accipit? Quis autem accipit, nisi quem Deus hoc beneficio dignatur? Credentibus obligat se, & hæc ipsa obligatio est ex gratuita bonitate. Vbi, vbi, vbi autem legisti in scriptura, quòd vlla promissione se Deus obliger ad fidem & pœnitentiam omnibus dandam? Hæc tu in æternum nobis non monstrabis. Ergo define interea perturbari verbis Christi, ex intimo pietatis & veræ coram Deo humilitatis sensu profectis, nec illis dubitationem Papisticam stabiliri finge, sine quib. fidei certitudo non potest consistere.
units.tr: Fifth: You say that this doctrine is legal. What if it were legal: would it on that account be false? Is not law no less true than gospel? You add that it is drawn from reason. You must have been keener-sighted than I and all the others have been in the books of Plato and Aristotle, who never look for it there. In short, know that it comes from the innermost parts of the gospel. Do you think that Paul in Romans 9, 10, 11, 12 and Ephesians 1 wanted to preach law? I do not suppose you believe that. And what pertains more to the very marrow of the gospel than the eternal, gratuitous, unchangeable love of God towards the elect, which Christ says was the cause why he gave even his only-begotten Son for us, and so that he might preserve us, grafted into him through faith, for ever, and bring to completion the work begun in us? If these are not evangelical, I do not know what are. I must warn you again (I have already said enough above about keeping the purity of the article of justification). Your remark has disturbed me, partly with astonishment, partly with indignation and grief, where you write: "How that exclamation disturbs me: To whom does God owe anything?" I read these words with a straight face. Surely you have either read the sacred books too little, or you are too much governed by feelings and rash judgments, since you so boldly condemn the words of Scripture. Is not the exclamation of Paul in Romans 11:35 this: "Who has first given to the Lord, that he should be repaid?" Certainly nothing comforts me more than this ineffable love of God towards me, that, although he owes me no more than he owed Judas and Cain, he has made me, from his enemy, his son, through the death of his only-begotten. For it is too much [illegible, about 12 letters] that you bring forward concerning God's obligation to us through the promise. What then, I beg you, will you put forward before the application of the promise? But the promise to which God binds himself: is it not to those who receive it by faith? And who receives it, unless the one whom God deigns to honour with this benefit? He binds himself to believers, and this very obligation arises from his free goodness. Where, where, where did you read in Scripture that God binds himself by any promise to give faith and repentance to all? You will never show us this. Therefore cease, meanwhile, to be disturbed by the words of Christ, which proceed from the innermost sense of piety and of true humility before God, nor imagine that the Papistical doubt is established by them, without which the certainty of faith cannot stand.

units.la: Sextum: Pudere ipsos iam dudum debebat argumenti de promissionibus vniuersalibus. Crimen enim quod ipsi committunt, nobis impingunt. Ipsemet soluis argumentum, & tamen eo vteris. Si vniuersalis ad omnes homines pertineret, quantum chaos impietatis & absurditatis sequeretur! Si autem ad credentes restringenda est, vt omnino est, nos veritatem & consolationem vniuersalem tuemur, qui ex verbo Dei didicimus, omnes & solos credentes esse hæredes vitæ æternæ, & sic in gratiam receptos à Deo, vt in ea mansuri sint omnes in æternum: nullus eorum periturus secundum dicta: Nemo rapiet oves meas: Ex eo quod dedit mihi pater non perdam, &c. Vt seducantur, si fieri possit, electi. Quos elegit hos vocauit, iis iustificauit, glorificauit. Hic est consolationis & fidei Christianæ colophon, & articulus iste postremo loco Symboli positus, eo quòd alios omnes propter istum credimus, vt possimus credere vitam æternam, & cum Apostolo triumphalem illum pæana canere: Quis separabit electos? &c. Contrà vero illi Deum manifestissima & grauif-fima contumelia afficiunt, dum ipsius amorem sicut hominum mutabilem esse fingunt: pios autem sua consolatione spoliant, vim, vsum, & consolationem promissionum vniuersalium prorsus eneruant, conspuunt & conculcant, dum fingunt, aliquos vere credentes finaliter excidere & perire: & eos, qui nunc sunt apud Deum in gratia, nec ab æterno fuisse, nec in æternum fore: Id verò cùm sit omni absurdo absurdius, sequitur omninò, cùm de futura atque æterna Dei gratia nolunt esse certi, eos nec de præsenti esse posse. Docet scriptura, omnes credentes seruandos esse. Opponunt isti contradictoriam, quosdam credentes non seruandos esse. Vbi iam tua est consolatio, qua te in vniuersum includas? Hæc sunt occulta Diaboli artificia, quæ animaduertenda & cauenda sunt.
units.tr: Sixth: They ought long since to have been ashamed of the argument about universal promises. For the crime they themselves commit, they charge upon us. You yourself dissolve the argument, and yet you make use of it. If the universal promise pertained to all men, what a chaos of impiety and absurdity would follow! But if it must be restricted to believers, as indeed it is, we maintain the universal truth and consolation, since we have learned from the Word of God that all, and only believers, are heirs of eternal life, and so are received by God into grace that all of them will remain in it for ever; none of them will perish, according to the words: "No one will snatch my sheep" and "What the Father has given me, I will not lose," etc. "that the elect might, if it were possible, be led astray" and "Whom he has elected, these he has also called; those he has justified, those he has also glorified." This is the crown of Christian consolation and faith, and that article placed last in the Creed, because we believe all the others on account of it, so that we may believe in eternal life, and with the Apostle sing that triumphal paean: "Who shall separate the elect?" etc. On the contrary, they inflict the most manifest and most grievous insult upon God, while they pretend that his love is changeable like that of men; they strip the pious of their consolation, utterly enervate the force, use and consolation of the universal promises, spit upon and trample them, while they pretend that some who truly believe fall away and perish in the end, and that those who now are in grace with God were neither from eternity nor will be for ever. Now this, since it is more absurd than any absurdity, it follows altogether that, when they do not want to be certain of the future and eternal grace of God, they cannot be certain of the present either. Scripture teaches that all believers are to be preserved. They oppose a contradictory statement, that some believers are not to be preserved. Where, then, is your consolation by which you include yourself in the universal? These are the hidden crafts of the Devil, which must be noted and guarded against.

units.la: Expositio Augustini ad Timotheum de omnibus ordi-nibus hominum, est propria illius loci, quod scopus & con-textus Paulus ostendit. Sed concentiosis[?] concedere soleo, de omnibus indiuiduis dici, quoad effectum erga omnes homines & vocationem, non autem quoad efficaciam. Pro vniuersali nostrum nemo ne pateretur quidem sub-stitui indefinitam, tantum abest, vt postulet[?].
units.tr: Augustine's exposition to Timothy, concerning all orders of men, is peculiar to that passage, as Paul's scope and context show. But I am accustomed to concede to the quarrelsome that it is said of all individuals as regards effect towards all men and calling, but not as regards efficacy. None of us would even allow the indefinite to be substituted for the universal; so far is it from requiring this.

units.la: Pro vniuersali nostrum nemo ne pateretur quidem sub-stitui indefinitam, tantum abest, vt postulet[?].
units.tr: None of us would even allow the indefinite to be substituted for the universal; so far is it from requiring this.

units.la: Septimum: Responsione de vniuersalibus obturatur etiam coccysmus de contradictoriis voluntatibus. Nulla enim contradictio, Deum omnes credentes velle saluos fieri: nullos non credentes fore saluos. Male etiam con-fundis mandatum ad omnes homines pertinens, vt omnes ad Christum veniant, cùm promissione, quod non omnes homines, sed omnes venientes ad se Christus sit refocillaturus. Itaque sicut nullos homines etiam reprobos, & pereuntes excludit à mandato: ita nullos ad se venientes, hoc est, credentes in ipsum à promissione.
units.tr: Seventh: The answer about universals also stops the cuckoo's cry about contradictory wills. For there is no contradiction in God's willing that all believers be saved, and that no unbelievers will be saved. You also wrongly confuse the command, which pertains to all men, that all come to Christ, with the promise, that Christ will refresh not all men but all who come to him. Therefore, just as he excludes from the command no men, even reprobate and perishing ones, so he excludes from the promise no one who comes to him, that is, who believes in him.

units.la: Etiam [illegible, ~10 letters] æquè putida est exprobratio. Cum ex debito datur, ea committi potest; non autem, cùm ex gratuita & liberrima misericordia, sicut Deus dat. Dives in omnes est, sed non eadem omnibus dona & beneficia dans, quia variam suppellectilem vult esse in sua domo amplissima. Sed cum apostolus petissimum hic de diuitiis æternis loquatur, tu maligne omittis, quod ipse addit: Invocantes eum.
units.tr: Also [illegible, about 10 letters] this reproach is equally foul. When a thing is given as a debt, it can be committed; but not when it is given from free and most liberal mercy, as God gives. He is rich towards all, but does not give the same gifts and benefits to all, because he wants his very ample house to have varied furnishings. But since the Apostle here speaks chiefly of eternal riches, you maliciously omit what he adds: "calling upon him."

units.la: Quæris, quo fundamento statuatur duplex electio? I-mo triplicem monstrabo in scriptura, pro diuersitate re-rum, ad quas fit electio diuina. Primò elegerat Deus po-pulum Israeliticum, vt esset ipsius ecclesia. Secundò ele-gerat Christus xii. Apostolos ad spargendum Euange-lium in mundo. Tertiò neutros horum omnes elegerat ad vitam æternam: quia in illis multi vocati, pauci electi: in his vnus erat Diabolus. Notat autem ipse, quos eleg isset, nempe ad vitam æternam, non tantum ad Apostolatum, ad quem etiam ludam elegerat. Sic & vocatio triplex est: Ad ecclesiam visibilem, de qua dicitur, Multi vocati. Ad Ecclesiam sanctorum, quæ est interna, seu efficax, quam Paulus vocat secundum propositum videlicet saluandi vocatos. Ad certum aliquod officium in vita. Sic mea vocatio est laborare in schola.
units.tr: Why is the double election established? First, I will show that there are three kinds of divine election in Scripture, according to the different matters for which God's election is made. First, God chose the people of Israel to be his church. Second, Christ chose the twelve apostles to spread the Gospel in the world. Third, he chose neither of these groups to eternal life: for among them many were called and few chosen, and among the twelve there was one devil. Moreover, the words make clear what he chose them for, namely eternal life, and not merely the apostleship, for which he also chose Judas. So too the calling is threefold: to the visible church, of which it is said, "Many are called"; to the church of the saints, which is inward or effectual, which Paul calls "according to his purpose," namely to save those who are called; and to a certain office in life. So my calling is to work in a school.

units.la: Voluntatem signi & beneplaciti recte distinxerunt Scholastici, non tanquam contrarias aut tanquam duas voluntates, sed tanquam vnam, partim patefactam, par-tim non probantem, partim efficientem, quæ natu-ræ diuinæ conueniunt.
units.tr: The Scholastics rightly distinguished the will of the sign and the will of good pleasure, not as contrary, or as two wills, but as one will, partly revealed, partly not revealed, partly effective, which agree with the divine nature.

units.la: Obiauum: Graui & pestilenti calumnia concludis: do-strinam de perseuerantia finali, facere homines arroga-tes: An arrogantiam vocas credere vitam æternam? Ni-mis contumeliosè tractas Spiritum sanctum, & nimis a-trox est ista ingratitudo pro summo beneficio, quod Deus in hac vita per Christum nobis confert, nimirum, summa & fundamento consolationis ac pietatis, certitu-dine salutis nostræ, per Christum nobis parta. Quæ e-nim esset consolatio scire, quod semel quidem peperis-set nobis Christus salutem, sed singulis momentis millepericulis amissionis eam obnoxiam esse? Scire igitur nosoportet, ab scondita esse vitam nostram cum Christoin Deo, ibique tam tuto custodiri, quàm tuta est ipsius Christi vita in cœlo regnâtis. Millies hoc in scriptura dictum est. Lege 5. Philippum in 7. cap. it. Matth. loco supra citato. Leg. 5. & 8. cap. ad Rom. Video te non observare discrimen securitatis spiritus & carnis, & hærere in ipsis doctrinæ Christianæ fundamentis, si illa plane ἀπηνὴς dicis ex animo. Quod si ita est, doleo vicem tuam valde, & hortor te, ut legas diligenter scripturam.
units.tr: As for your objection: you conclude with a grave and pestilent slander that the doctrine of final perseverance makes men arrogant. Do you call it arrogance to believe in eternal life? You treat the Holy Spirit with too much insult, and that ingratitude is too monstrous for the highest benefit which God in this life confers on us through Christ, namely the chief foundation of consolation and piety, the certainty of our salvation, won for us through Christ. For what consolation would it be to know that Christ indeed once secured our salvation, but that it is exposed to loss at every moment through a thousand dangers? We must therefore know that our life is hidden with Christ in God, and kept there as safely as the life of Christ himself is safe in heaven, reigning. This has been said a thousand times in Scripture. Read Philippians 5, and Matthew 7 in the passage cited above; read Romans 5 and 8. I see that you do not observe the distinction between the security of the spirit and of the flesh, and that you cling to the very foundations of Christian doctrine, if you truly call those things utterly harsh [apēnḗs] from your heart. If that is so, I grieve greatly for you, and I urge you to read Scripture diligently.

units.la: Etiam illud calumniosum est, quod dicamus, electos non posse excutere Spiritum sanctum. Imò sæpè amittunt plurima dona, sed ea per pœnitentiam recuperant. Non n. deficiunt in vniuersum à Deo, ut fiant hostes agnatæ veritatis, hoc est, non peccant in Spiritum sanctum, ideoque non sic labuntur, ut finaliter in erroribus contra fundamentum, aut peccatis contra conscientiam perfecuerent. Neque hæc consolatio securos facit, quia ad illos tantum pertinet, qui habent propositum cauendi lapsus, & à nulla re magis abhorrent, quàm ab offensione Dei. Est igitur implicatio contradictionis in illo diabolico Sarcasmo impiorum dicentium: Si sum electus, faciam quidquid lubet, quia mihi non obest. Vult enim Deus nos statuere, quòd simus electi. Hoc autem non possumus sine fide & pœnitentia. Omnia cooperantur ad bonum sci.diligentibus Deum. Nulla est condemnatio in iis, qui secundum spiritum ambulant. Hæc duo coniuncta excludunt securitatem. Excitant autem ad alacritatem currendi in stadio nostro secundum præceptum: Firmam facite electionem vestram. Contra vero illi puluinar suis peccatis sternunt, qui fingunt, in manu sua esse, assumere & deponere pœnitentiam, quoties & quando ipsi volunt, & ludere cum Deo pro libidine. Illud verò examen, ad quod nos vocat certitudo salutis, vellem, inquis, declinare. Hoc diabolus quærit.
units.tr: That also is a slander, that we say the elect cannot cast out the Holy Spirit. Indeed they often lose many gifts, but they recover them through repentance. For they do not fall away from God altogether, so as to become enemies of the truth they once knew; that is, they do not sin against the Holy Spirit, and so they do not fall in such a way as to persist finally in errors against the foundation, or in sins against conscience. Nor does this consolation make men careless, because it pertains only to those who have a purpose of avoiding lapses, and who shrink from nothing more than offence against God. There is therefore a contradiction in that devilish sarcasm of the impious who say: "If I am elect, I will do whatever pleases me, because it will not harm me." For God wills that we establish that we are elect. But we cannot do this without faith and repentance. "All things work together for good to those who love God." "There is no condemnation for those who walk according to the Spirit." These two things joined together exclude security. They also stir us to eagerness in running our race, according to the command: "Make your election firm." On the other hand, those who pretend that it is in their own hand to take up and lay down repentance whenever and however they please, and to play with God at their whim, lay pillows under their sins. As for that examination to which the certainty of salvation calls us, you say you would prefer to avoid it. This is what the devil seeks.

units.la: Dicta illa: Qui perseuerauerit usque ad finem, saluus erit. Vincenti dabo coronam, &c. non labefactant certitudinem salutis, sed sunt hortationes, quib. nos Deus in ea certitudine conseruat, excitans in nobis studium pietatis & fugam peccatorum.
units.tr: Those sayings, "He who endures to the end shall be saved," and "To him who overcomes I will give a crown," etc., do not weaken the certainty of salvation, but are exhortations by which God keeps us in that certainty, stirring in us zeal for godliness and flight from sins.

units.la: Verè Ethnica sunt ista, & vestibulum inferni. Itaque bene est, quod Ethnicorum testimoniis confirmas. Nam a verbo Dei haec dicta dissentiunt. Quare sic corrumpis dicta scripturae, quae a timore filiorum, qui manent in domo, detorques ad timorem seruorum? Quae miseria haec est? Quanta est caecitas, vniuersales promissiones astare, & non excutere se ipsum, an sit ex iis, de quibus promissiones loquuntur? Hoc plane est securitatem carnalem, & laruam fidei in hominibus facere, quae in certamine praecipitat nos in desperationem. Non credo, sic docuerunt quenquam promissiones vniuersales blaterare & spumare Lutherus & Philippus. Es sind lauter Teuffels griff, fur denen Gns Gott behute. Sed adstat tabellarius. Et ego totam noctem impendi scriptioni huic summa cum difficultate. Vale. Peto ne me amplius talibus disputationibus lacessas. Bene vale,
units.tr: Truly these are heathen notions, and the vestibule of hell. So it is good that you confirm them by the testimonies of the heathen. For these statements disagree with the Word of God. Why then do you so corrupt the words of Scripture, twisting what is said about the fear of sons who remain in the house into fear of servants? What wretchedness is this! How great is the blindness of those who stand by universal promises and do not examine themselves, whether they are among those of whom the promises speak! This plainly makes carnal security and a mask of faith in men, which in the struggle plunges us into despair. I do not believe that Luther and Philip taught anyone in this way, or babbled and foamed about universal promises. Es sind lauter Teuffels griff, fur denen Gns Gott behute. But the courier is standing by. And I have spent the whole night on this writing with great difficulty. Farewell. I ask that you no longer harass me with such disputations. Farewell,

units.la: 11.Septemb.Anno MDLXXIII.
units.tr: 11 September, in the year 1573.

units.la: EIVSDEM D. ZACHARIÆ VRSINI EPISTOLA AD EVNDEM AMICVM ex Italia reuersum.
units.tr: The same Dr. Zacharias Ursinus's letter to the same friend, returned from Italy.

units.la: Gratulor tibi felicem reditum ex cloaca diabolo-rum, & precor, vt prosit tibi balneum, quod post illam ingressus es. Quod si opus est, etiam pumicem huic fec-dæ[?] inclusum tibi mitto, quo fricatus redeas nobis lautus sat commode. Est enim pumex iste bene aridus ante annum fere missus a me, vt iusseras, Noribergam. Sed i-bi te non offendit. Itaque reuersus ad me, iam ad te pro-ficiscitur, cum alioqui scribendi nec argumentum nec tempus haberem. Noui hic nihil. Augescunt contagia pestilentiæ, vt metuamus dissipationem scholæ. Plurimæ sunt dysenteriæ, quæ etiam nostram domum affligunt. Suasi nostratibus, vt in tempore hinc abeant. Vale. Septemb. 1574.
units.tr: I congratulate you on your happy return from the sewer of the devils, and I pray that the bath you entered after that may do you good. If it is needed, I am also sending you a pumice stone enclosed for that filthy business, so that when you come back to us you will be scrubbed and fairly clean. For this pumice, which I sent you from Nuremberg almost a year ago at your request, is quite dry. But you did not find it there. So it has come back to me and is now setting out for you, since in any case I have neither a subject nor the time for writing. I have no news here. The contagions of the plague are increasing, so that we fear the school will be broken up. There are many cases of dysentery, which are also afflicting our household. I have advised our countrymen to leave here in good time. Farewell. September 1574.

units.la: Fragmentum epistolæ Vrsini ad amicum, de causa peccati.
units.tr: Fragment of Ursinus's letter to a friend, on the cause of sin.

units.la: Vnum habent μορμολύκειον[?] de causa peccati: cætera tam inepta sunt, vt sint indigna responsione. Sed illud etiam puerulis est paralogismus accidentis. Per accidens enim, hoc est, propter defectum & vitium atque aberrationem voluntatis diaboli aut hominis, peccatum est illud opus, quod Deus iustissima[?], & cum natura sua ac legi optime congruente voluntate per instrumentum illud vitiosum & peccans, vult fieri, permittens interea peccata creaturæ, hoc est, non corrigens eam, vt cū Deo iuste agente, & ipsa agat iuste: siue dum non illuminat eam voluntatis suæ agnitione, siue dum non flectit suo spiritu, vt patefactæ Dei voluntati obediendi causa agat quod agit. Atque ita Deus semper agit bene siue per bonos, siue per malos. Creatura verò cum Deo agit bene in bonitate, in qua condita est, à Deo conseruata, aut in eam reflituta: ideoque bonum quod agit, Dei opus est, quod ipse vult & efficit: malum quod agit, creaturæ est. A Deo autem non efficitur, sed permittitur: Dum enim efficit, vt creaturæ voluntas bona sit, & bene cum Deo bene agente agat. Idem enim opus respectu diuer-sarum causarum bonum & malum, immutabile & mutabile, seu contingens aut liberum est, prout causæ diuersæ sunt, quæ in illo producendo concurrunt. Hæc qui non videt, nihil videt. Sed si potero, respondebo tibi aliquando paucis. Neque enim an possim, aut quando possim, scio: ac tædet me tractare ista sophismatum oleta. Disce tacitus & animo otioso illa cogitans: σιγᾶ πόλιν[?] πατρὸς ἐξ ὡς ἡσύχου[?] ὁ καταστάντα[?] μόνου Θεοῦ. Si tacitus pasci didicisset coruus, haberet plus dapis, & rixæ multò minus inuidiæque. 10. Mart. Anno 1573.
units.tr: They have one bugbear concerning the cause of sin; the rest is so silly that it is unworthy of an answer. But even that is a fallacy of accident, which even little boys could see. For the act is sinful accidentally, that is, on account of the defect, the fault and the deviation of the will of the devil or of man. This is the work that God, most justly, and with a will perfectly consistent with its own nature and with the law, wills to be done through that faulty and sinning instrument, while in the meantime he permits the sins of the creature, that is, he does not correct it, so that, with God acting justly, it too may act justly: whether by not enlightening it with knowledge of his own will, or by not bending it by his Spirit, so that it does what it does in order to obey the revealed will of God. And so God always acts well, whether through good or through wicked agents. But the creature acts well together with God, who acts well, in the goodness in which it was created, preserved by God, or restored to it. Therefore the good that it does is God's work, which he himself wills and effects; the evil that it does belongs to the creature. Yet this is not effected by God but permitted: for while he effects that the creature's will be good, and act well together with God acting well... For the same work is good and evil, unchangeable and changeable, or contingent and free, with respect to different causes, according as the different causes are those which concur in producing it. Whoever does not see this sees nothing. But if I am able, I will answer you briefly at some time. For I do not know whether I can, or when I can, and I am weary of handling those mouldy sophisms. Learn in silence, and think on those things with a quiet mind: "Keep silence, the city of the father ... the one God only." If the raven had learned to feed in silence, it would have more food and far less quarrelling and envy. March 10, 1573.

units.la: AN̅ DOCTRINA DE PROVIDENTIA tollat preces.
units.tr: Whether the doctrine of providence abolishes prayer.

units.la: PIA precatio optimè congruit cum doctrina de providentia, eaque confirmatur & stabilitur. Nam ad salutem necessaria petens animo sincero, certò statuit, se illa accipere. Hanc fiduciam labefactat, & ab imis radicibus conuellit contraria opinio, quæ non finit nos credere vltimum articulum symboli. Ea verò petens, sine quibus salus nostra consistere potest: subiicit se patienter & modestè voluntati diuinæ, aliud nec volens quidem impetrare, quam Deus optimo & nobis vtilissimo consilio suo decretum habet. Hanc obedientiam, consolationem & quietem animi nihil magis conturbat, quàm illa vagabunda, Academica & Epicurea contingentia, qua fingitur euentus non regi & determinari diuino consilio. Repete apud animum illud pueris à Philippo nostro traditum, & inculcatum discrimen rerum petendarum, & omnis ista quæstio de precibus tibi erit plana. Cum hoc autem optimè congruit nostra sententia: prorsus ei repugnat contraria opinio, adeò consonat verum vero, falsum neque vero, neque falso. Summa est: debes Deo fidere, ab ipso omnia bona petere, eíque accepta referre, non secus ac si omnia sine te ab ipso existe-rent, & debes officium facere tanto studio & conatu, ac si omnia a te, & per te, sine ipso consequereris. Hic hic frater ligt der haaff vm[?] Pfeffer.Ad hunc scopum, qui non dirigit doctrinâ & disputationem omnem de prouidentia & electione, is euanescit in curiositate sua, & induit se multis laqueis, quos ipse sibi nectit. Quib. dare Deus decreuit bona, iis etiam destinauit spiritum precum. Si igitur precandi animum tibi dat, certò statuas, non frustra tibi datum esse, sed semper exauditionem impetrandam secundum promissiones & consilium Dei. Hoc consequens ex illo antecedente beneficio debes colligere certa consecutione & conclusione. Vides-ne igitur plane contrarium tui istius metus? Nihil enim minus labefactat, & nihil magis confirmat studium, rursum & consolationem piarum precum, quàm doctrina de prouidentia. Mirror te adhuc somniare de spectris particularitatis. Quoties audisti & legisti contrarium eius esse verum, quod isti miserrimi & in densissimis academicæ suæ ἀγνωσίας[?] tenebris palpantes sophistæ cauillantur? Sine enim doctrina de electione & certitudine salutis neque consistere ac defendi potest, neque ad usum & consolationem accommodari universalitas promissæ gratiæ, quæ ad fo-los & omnes credentes pertinet. Quoties tibi inculcatum est, de electione iudicandum esse à posteriori, id est, ex effectis de causa? Ex fide electorum Dei debes statuere, te esse electum. Imò hæc ipsa est vera fides, credere se electum ad vitam æternam propter Christum. Excute igitur sinum tuum. An sit in te fides, pœnitentia & verû desideriû gratiæ Dei, & statue te electû, omissis curiosis disputationibus. Coram Deo affirmo, me nô video, quomodo in multis meis doloribus potuissem consistere, nisi habuissem hanc consolationem immotam: Nemo rapiet oues meas, &c. Quid aliq,nisi hæc accedat: omnia nobis bona & mala non fortuito: sed æterno Dei consilio euenire ad nostram salutem?
units.tr: Devout prayer agrees very well with the doctrine of providence, and is confirmed and made firm by it. For a man who asks with a sincere heart for what is necessary to salvation is certain that he receives it. This confidence is shaken, and torn up from its deepest roots, by the opposing opinion, which does not let us believe the last article of the creed. But when we ask for things without which our salvation can stand, we submit ourselves patiently and modestly to the will of God, not even wishing to obtain anything other than what God has decreed by his most good and most useful counsel for us. Nothing disturbs this obedience, the consolation and the quiet of the mind, more than those wandering, Academic and Epicurean notions of contingency, by which it is imagined that events are not governed and determined by the divine counsel. Keep in mind the distinction between things to be asked for, which our Philip taught and impressed upon the boys, and all that question about prayers will be clear to you. Our opinion agrees very well with this; the opposing opinion is wholly at odds with it, for truth harmonizes with truth, and falsehood with neither truth nor falsehood. In short: you ought to trust God, to ask all good things from him, and to ascribe them to him, just as if all things came into being from him without you; and you ought to perform your duty with as much zeal and effort as if you were to obtain everything from yourself and through yourself, without him. To this end, the doctrine of providence and of election, which directs every discussion, is not in place; whoever neglects it vanishes in his own curiosity and entangles himself in the many snares that he himself weaves. To those to whom God has decided to give good things, he has also appointed the spirit of prayer. If therefore he gives you the desire to pray, be certain that it has not been given to you in vain, but that you will always obtain an answer according to God's promises and counsel. You ought to draw this consequence from that antecedent benefit by a certain sequence and conclusion. Do you not then see that your fear is plainly the opposite? For nothing shakes less, and nothing confirms more, the zeal and the consolation of pious prayers, than the doctrine of providence. I marvel that you are still dreaming of the phantoms of particularity. How often have you heard and read that the contrary of this is true, which those most wretched sophists, groping in the very dense darkness of their academic ignorance, wrangle about? For the universality of the promised grace, which pertains to all the faithful and to each one, can neither stand nor be defended without the doctrine of election and the certainty of salvation, nor be fitted to use and consolation. How often has it been impressed upon you that election must be judged from the a posteriori, that is, from the effects to the cause? From the faith of the elect of God you ought to establish that you are elect. Indeed, this very faith is true faith: to believe that one is elected to eternal life on account of Christ. Search, therefore, your own breast: whether there is in you faith, repentance and true desire for the grace of God, and establish that you are elect, setting aside curious disputations. I affirm before God that I do not see how, in my many sorrows, I could have stood, had I not had this unshaken consolation: "No one will snatch my sheep," etc. What else, unless this is added: that all good and evil things happen to us not by chance, but by the eternal counsel of God, for our salvation?

units.tr: V. FRAGMENT OF A SPEECH, ON THE QUESTION

units.la: AD QVOS FRVCTVS MORTIS ET resurrectionis Christi pertineant: & quomodo Christus pro omnibus sit mortuus: in inclyta Academia Heidelbergensi a quodam S. Theologiae studioso pridie Paschatis, Anno XC. recitata.
units.tr: TO WHOM THE FRUITS OF THE DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF CHRIST PERTAIN: AND HOW CHRIST DIED FOR ALL: recited in the famous Academy of Heidelberg by a certain student of sacred theology, on the eve of Easter, in the year 1590.

units.la: SATIS multa verba fecisse mihi videor de historia, déque fructibus resurrectionis Domini. Restat, vt quod postremo loco instituimus, ad quosnam hi fructus pertineant, explicare pergamus.
units.tr: I seem to have said quite enough about the history and the fruits of the Lord's resurrection. What remains is to go on and explain the last point we set out to treat: to whom these fruits pertain.

units.la: Ad scripturam itaque sanctam, tanquam ad Cynosuram cursum nostrum dirigentes, fructus hos tã pretiosos ad omnes, & solos credentes pertinere, cum eadem scriptura sacra asserimus: Impios vero & incredulos omnes, quoad tales manent, ab illis procul arcemus. Etenim omnes & soli credentes fructuum illorum, iustificationis puta gratuitæ coram Deo, viuificationis à morte peccati & corporis, denique immortalis vitæ & gloriæ, dulcedine sentiunt, omnes & soli percipiunt: quia omnes & soli hi vera fide eos sibi applicant. Hi enim sunt, qui sermonem Christi audiunt, credunt, vitamque æterna habet, nec in condemnatione veniũt. Hi sunt, qui fide iustificatur, Deo reconciliatur, & pacé habet per dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Hi sunt, qui per Spiritũ sanctum regenerati, in nouam vitam cũ Christo excitatur, quorũ corda fide purificantur. Hi denique sunt, quos in Iesu dormientes, Deus tandé ex morte suscitatos, cum eo adducet, vt vitæ cœlestis gloria in æternum fruantur. Impij vero, fide iustificante destituti, quid quæso de his tãtis bonis participarent, qui Deo non placent (sine fide enim Deo placere est impossibile) qui ad Christum nõ pertinent, qui non sunt hæredes, qui neque in re, neque ad rem, quod dicitur, hic ius vllũ habent? Quomodo ad eos pertineret Christus? Quomodo beneficia Christi? Quin potiùs isti oēs ipsius filij Dei voce ab his thesauris procul, procul arcētur, & æternæ maledictioni ac morti adiudicantur.Sic enim ille in euangelio : Qui non credit, iam iudicatus est : & ira Dei manet super eo. Et Paulus: Qui non habet spiritum Christi, non est eius: quae apostoli locu cū primis huc facere arbitror.Si enim infideles ad Christum non pertinent:neque sunt Christi: vtiq. à correlatis firmissimè concluditur, vicissim Christum cum suis beneficiis ad ipsos non pertinere: & sicut ipsi non sunt Christi : ita nec Christum ipsorum esse. Et quomodo, quaeso, ad eos pertineret, quos ipse tandem in iudicio extremo coram vniuerso mundo,alienos à se, à beneficiis suis,à regno suo pronunciabit, quos nunquam cognitos fuisse testabitur, quos denique vt maledictos operarios iniquitatis,à se in gehennam ablegabit?
units.tr: Directing our course, then, to holy Scripture as to the Cynosure, we assert on the authority of that same holy Scripture that these fruits, so precious, belong to all and only believers, while all unbelievers and the impious, so long as they remain such, we keep far away from them. For all and only believers feel the sweetness of those fruits, namely justification freely before God, quickening from the death of sin and of the body, and finally immortal life and glory, and all and only believers receive them, because all and only these by true faith apply them to themselves. For these are they who hear the word of Christ, believe, and have eternal life, and do not come into condemnation. These are they who are justified by faith, reconciled to God, and have peace through our Lord Jesus Christ. These are they who, regenerated by the Holy Spirit, are raised with Christ into new life, whose hearts are purified by faith. Finally, these are they whom God, at last raising them from death, will bring with Jesus, those who sleep in Jesus, so that they may enjoy the glory of heavenly life for ever. But the impious, destitute of justifying faith, what, I ask, would they share of such great goods? They who do not please God (for without faith it is impossible to please God), who do not belong to Christ, who are not heirs, who have, as the saying goes, no right whatever either in the thing or to the thing? How would Christ pertain to them? How would the benefits of Christ? Rather, all of them are driven far, far away from these treasures by the very voice of the Son of God, and are adjudged to eternal curse and death. For thus he says in the gospel: He who does not believe is already judged, and the wrath of God remains upon him. And Paul: He who does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his; which passages of the apostles I judge to bear most directly on this point. For if unbelievers do not belong to Christ, and are not Christ's, it is most firmly concluded from correlatives that, conversely, Christ with his benefits does not belong to them, and just as they are not Christ's, so neither is Christ theirs. And how, I ask, would he pertain to those whom he himself, at the last judgment, before the whole world, will pronounce strangers to himself, to his benefits and to his kingdom; whom he will testify never to have known; whom at last, as workers of iniquity under a curse, he will banish from himself into hell?

units.la: At,inquies,Christus pro omnibus est mortuus. Pro omnibus ergo etiam resurrexit.Responsio duplex est,vtraque vera & certa.Primo:quoties euangelium fructus operum & beneficiorum Christi ad omnes extendit, de vniuersitate fidelium & electorum (vt vocat Ambrosius) id accipiendum esse. Est enim haec perpetua & constans euangelij vox:Qui crediderit,seruabitur,non venit in iudicium:Qui non crediderit, condemnabitur : iam iudicatus est:& ira Dei manet super eo. Arcet ergo euangelium à Christi beneficiis omnes infideles,non modò diserta exclusione, sed & illa fidei ac poenitentiae conditione, sub qua expresse, vel tacitè beneficia sua hominib. remittit,& quà in reprobis,hoc est,perseueratibus & perseueraturis in impietate nunquâ inueniri palàm est. Sic itaque Christus mortuus dicitur pro omnibus nepe fidelibus & electis:pro quibus etiam solis orauit,& in quib. solis fine mortis suae assequitur. Ad infideles verò & reprobos,pro quibus ipse nō orauit,quos pro suis nũquam nouit,super quos ira Dei in æternũ manet,mortis Christi beneficia extendere,quid aliud est,quā contra ipsiusmet præceptū,sanctū canib9 dare, margaritas porcis obiicere? Haec scripturae & orthodoxorũ patrũ autoritate solidè defendi possunt:& ad consolationẽ Christianam faciunt.Sed & altera nō minùs vera responsio est,qua concedimus, tentiofis gratificari possumus,Christũ absolutè pro omnibus mortuũ esse,nepe si & meriti eius sufficientiam spectes.Extra omne est cōtrouersiam, tantū pondus habedus habere mortem filij Dei, vt sufficiat non vnius tantum mundi, sed millium peccatis expiandis: Si modo hanc peccati medicinam omnes fide acciperent. Sed de efficacia & participatione ipsa fructuum est quaestio: quam credulis iuxta & incredulis communem esse, vel in euangelio promitti, & dari, constanter negamus, neque eius respectu Christum pariter pro omnibus electis ac reprobis mortuum recte dici concedimus.
units.tr: But, you will say, Christ died for all. Therefore he also rose again for all. The answer is twofold, and both parts are true and certain. First: whenever the gospel extends the fruits of Christ's works and benefits to all, that must be understood of the whole body of believers and the elect (as Ambrose calls it). For this is the constant and unbroken voice of the gospel: He who believes shall be saved, does not come into judgment; he who does not believe shall be condemned, is already judged, and the wrath of God remains upon him. The gospel therefore excludes all unbelievers from the benefits of Christ, not only by express exclusion but also by that condition of faith and repentance under which he sends his benefits to men, expressly or tacitly, and which is manifestly never found in the reprobate, that is, those who persist and will persist in impiety. Thus Christ is said to have died for all, namely for believers and the elect, for whom alone he prayed, and in whom alone the end of his death is attained. But to extend the benefits of Christ's death to unbelievers and the reprobate, for whom he did not pray, whom he never knew as his own, over whom the wrath of God remains for ever, what else is it than, against his own command, to give what is holy to dogs and to cast pearls before swine? These things can be defended soundly by the authority of Scripture and the orthodox Fathers, and they serve Christian consolation. But there is also a second answer, no less true, by which we concede, so that we may indulge the contentious, that Christ died absolutely for all, namely if you regard the sufficiency of his merit. It is beyond all controversy that the death of the Son of God has such weight that it suffices to expiate the sins not of one world only but of thousands, provided that all should receive this medicine of sin by faith. But the question concerns the efficacy and the very participation in the fruits; and we steadfastly deny that these are common to believers and unbelievers alike, or that they are promised and given in the gospel to both, and with respect to these we do not concede that Christ rightly is said to have died equally for the elect and the reprobate.

units.la: Hic vero male feriati quidam homines, quasi parum controuersiarum habeat ecclesia, plenis buccis virus suum in nos despumant, indignissime ferentes, nos coelestes illos thesauros & margaritas non aequo iure piis & impiis, fidelibus & infidelibus, electis & reprobis, Christi membris & diaboli seruis, ouibus & porcis diuidere. Clamant ergo, nos negare, Christum pro omnibus esse mortuum. Hanc vero esse Saracenicam, Mahumeticam, & plusquam Paganam blasphemiam, qua religio Christiana funditus euertatur.
units.tr: But here certain men, idle and ill-employed, as if the Church lacked controversies, foam their poison against us with cheeks full, indignant beyond measure that we divide those heavenly treasures and pearls not with equal right between the pious and the impious, believers and unbelievers, the elect and the reprobate, members of Christ and servants of the devil, sheep and swine. So they cry out that we deny that Christ died for all. And this, they say, is a Saracen, Mahometan, and more than pagan blasphemy, by which the Christian religion is utterly overthrown.

units.la: Nobis vero, auditores, cum talibus mostris[?] nō est propositum dimicare. De calumnia tantum aliquid monendum est. Quid enim est calumniari, si hoc non est? Hoccine est simpliciter negare Christū pro omnibus mortuum, cum meriti dignitatem ab efficacia & fruitione ipsa beneficiorum distinguimus, hancque ad solam fidelium vniuersitatem ex Iudaeis & gentibus collecta, cum scriptura & orthodoxis patribus restringimus?
units.tr: But with such men, hearers, we have no intention of contending. Only something must be said about the calumny. For what is it to calumniate, if this is not? Is it simply to deny that Christ died for all, when we distinguish the dignity of his merit from the efficacy and enjoyment of the benefits themselves, and restrict this latter to the sole body of believers gathered from Jews and Gentiles, in agreement with Scripture and the orthodox Fathers?

units.la: Caeterum, vt veritas magis elucescat, & contentiosis illis, si possit, aliquo modo a nobis satisfiat: nge[?] paucis rationes grauissimas expedamus, quibus adducti hoc modo distinguendum censeamus.
units.tr: Moreover, so that the truth may shine more clearly, and so that the contentious may, if possible, be satisfied in some way by us, let us briefly set out the most weighty reasons by which we are led to think that a distinction must be made in this way.

units.la: Ac primo quidem ipsa scriptura sacra hoc modo distinguere nō obscurè nos docet & cogit. Inuenias enim in scriptura alicubi absolutè dici, Christum pro omnibus esse mortuum: dedisse se pretiū redemptionis pro omnibus: esse expiationem pro peccatis totius mundi. Rursus inuenias: Christum non orasse, neq. se sanctificasse, hoc est, sacrificasse pro mundo: sed pro electis ipsi datis: pro ouibus vitam posuisse: dedisse se precium redemtionis pro multis: cognitione sui iusti ficaturus multos: sanguinem fudisse pro multis: Mundum non posse accipere spiritum fanctū,cùm eum non agnoscat,ideoq. Christi non esse,&c.Ista speciem haberent repugnantiæ:nisi intelligeremus,priora dicta de λυτρω sufficientia, posteriora de eiusdem efficacia loqui.
units.tr: And first, holy Scripture itself teaches and compels us, not obscurely, to distinguish in this manner. For you will find in Scripture passages where it is said absolutely that Christ died for all, that he gave himself as the price of redemption for all, that he is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world. Again you will find that Christ did not pray, nor sanctify himself, that is, sacrifice himself for the world, but for those given to him by the Father; that he laid down his life for the sheep; that he gave himself as the price of redemption for many; that by the knowledge of himself he would justify many; that he shed his blood for many; that the world cannot receive the Holy Spirit, since it does not know him, and therefore is not Christ's, and so on. These would have the appearance of contradiction, unless we understood the former sayings to speak of the sufficiency of the ransom (λύτρον), and the latter of its efficacy.

units.la: Porrò loca alia occurrunt,quę impiis quoque redemptionis beneficium largiri videntur: vt cum Petrus dicit, eos negare Dominum,qui illos mercatus erat:purgatos fuisse à veteribus peccatis.Et Paulus : Eos sanguine fœderis sanctificatos fuisse:quæ vel de hypocritarum inani redemtionis & sanctificationis gloriatione:vel certè non nisi de λυτρω Christi amplitudine, & sufficientia accipere,scriptura alibi nos cogit,quoties infideles & impœnitentes à redemtionis beneficiis simpliciter excludit,& eos adhuc captiuos teneri laqueis diaboli:ab eodem efficaciter agi ad nequitiam patrandam : iram Dei super eis manere:(manere inquit,non redire, quasi aliquando recesserit,) Denique Christum eos nunquam nouisse,ne dum redemisse constanter asseruerat.
units.tr: Moreover, other passages occur which seem to bestow the benefit of redemption even on the impious: such as when Peter says that those who deny the Lord, who had bought them, were cleansed from their former sins; and Paul says that they were sanctified by the blood of the covenant. These things, Scripture elsewhere compels us to understand either of the empty boasting of hypocrites in redemption and sanctification, or certainly only of the amplitude and sufficiency of Christ's ransom, whenever it simply excludes unbelievers and the impenitent from the benefits of redemption, and says that they are still held captive in the snares of the devil, are efficaciously driven by him to work wickedness, that the wrath of God remains upon them (it says "remains," not "returns," as if it had once withdrawn), and finally that Christ never knew them, much less redeemed them, as it constantly asserts.

units.la: Quòd si orthodoxorum patrum & saniorum scholasticorum sententias producere animus esset,qui scriptuam nobiscum sic interpretantur, in amplissimum sane oratio nis campum vos deducerem. Non tamen abs re fuerit,aliquas saltem in medium afferre.
units.tr: But if I were minded to produce the opinions of the orthodox Fathers and of the saner Schoolmen, who interpret Scripture with us in this way, I would indeed lead you into a very wide field of discourse. Still, it will not be out of place to bring forward at least a few of them.

units.la: Audiamus Cyrillū,Christi verba:Nō oro pro mundo: cū dicto Iohānis:Est propitiatio pro peccatis totius mundi,ita cōciliātē: Iohannes videtur discrepare à saluatore. Saluator enim pro mūdo hic rogare abnuit:Iōhānes autem nō pro nostris solū peccatis propitiatione & paracletū illū esse,sed pro vniuerso affirmat mūdo. Verum beatus Iohannes,quōnia erat Iudæus, ne pro Iudæis tantum paracletus esse Dominus apud patrē videretur,nō autē etiam pro aliis gentibus,quæ vocatæ obsequuta sunt, necessario pro toto mundo adiecit. Dominus autē Iesus eos à nō suis separans,pro eis inquit,tantummodò, qui verba mea seruant, & in gum meum acceperunt,rogo.Nam quorum Mediator atque pontifex est,ipsis tantummodò Mediationis bonum non imuria attribuit.Hæc Cyrillus.
units.tr: Let us hear Cyril, on Christ's words: "I do not pray for the world," reconciling this with John's saying: "He is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world." John seems to differ from the Saviour. For the Saviour here refuses to pray for the world, whereas John affirms that he is the propitiation not only for our sins but for the whole world, and that the Paraclete is there for the whole world. But the blessed John, since he was a Jew, added necessarily "for the whole world," lest the Lord seem to be an advocate with the Father only for the Jews, and not also for the other nations who were called and obeyed. But the Lord Jesus, separating those who were not his from them, says: "I pray only for those who keep my words and have received my commandment." For he rightly attributes the benefit of mediation only to those for whom he is Mediator and High Priest. Thus Cyril.

units.la: Audiamus & Profperū in respōsionib. ad obiectiones Vicetinas,clarius ista distinguentem. Quod ergo (inquit ad obiectionem primā) ad magnitudinē & potentiā pre-
units.tr: Let us hear also Prosper, who distinguishes these things more clearly in his answers to the Vincentian objections. "Therefore (he says in answer to the first objection) as regards the greatness and power..."

units.la: Vide Augustinum, Tom.7. tū, & quod ad unā pertinet causam generis humani: sanguis Christi redeptio est totius mundi: sed qui hoc seculū sine fide, & sine regenerationis sacramento pertrafeunt, redetio-nis alieni sunt. Cum itaque propter omnium causā a Domino nostro in veritate susceptā, rectè omnes dicatur redeti: & tamen non omnes a captivitate sint eruti: redetionis proprietas haud dubie penes illos est, de quibus princeps mundi missus est foras: & iā nō vasa diaboli: sed membra sunt Christi. Cuius mors non ita impēsa est generi humano, ut ad redemtionē eorum etiam, qui regenerandi non erant, pertineret: sed ita, ut quod per unicum exemplum gestum est pro universis, per singulare sacramentum celebraretur in singulis. Poculum quippe immortalitatis, quod confectum est de infirmitate nostrā, & veritate divina habet quidem in se, ut omnibus prosit: sed si non bibitur, non medetur.
units.tr: See Augustine, vol. 7. "...and as far as it concerns the one cause of the human race, the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world; but those who pass through this age without faith and without the sacrament of regeneration are strangers to the redemption." Therefore, although on account of all, the cause undertaken by our Lord in truth, it is rightly said that all are redeemed, yet not all have been rescued from captivity; the peculiar property of redemption doubtless belongs to those of whom the prince of the world has been cast out, and who are no longer vessels of the devil but members of Christ. "His death was not so applied to the human race that it pertained also to the redemption of those who were not to be regenerated; but in such a way that what was accomplished for all through one example is celebrated in each person through a singular sacrament. For the cup of immortality, which was prepared from our weakness and has in itself divine truth, indeed benefits all; but if it is not drunk, it does not heal."

units.la: Idem ad capitula Gallorum respondens, phrasin hanc, Christū tātum pro fidelib. esse mortuū, quam isti ut Saracenicā dānat, diserte approbat his verbis: Cùm itaq. recte dicatur Saluator pro totius mūdi redetione crucifixus, pter vera natura humana suscepcionē, & propter cōmunē in primo homine perditionē: potest tamē dici pro his tantū crucifixus, quibus mors ipsius profuit. Dicit enim euangelista, quia Iesus mortuus erat pro gente, nec tātum pro gente sed etiā ut filios Dei dispersos cōgregaret in unum. Haden5 Prosper.
units.tr: Responding likewise to the chapters of the Gauls, he expressly approves this phrase, that Christ died only for the faithful, which these men condemn as Saracen, in these words: "Since it is rightly said that the Saviour was crucified for the redemption of the whole world, on account of the assumption of true human nature and on account of the common perdition in the first man; yet he can be said to have been crucified only for those to whom his death profited." For the evangelist says: "Because Jesus was going to die for the nation, and not only for the nation but that he might also gather into one the scattered children of God." Thus Prosper.

units.la: Gregorius dicit: Pro electorum vita, usque ad mortem se tradidit author vita.
units.tr: Gregory says: "The author of life gave himself up to death for the life of the elect."

units.la: Innocentius III. qui vixit circa annū Domini 1200. sic scribit: PRO SOLIS PRAEDESTINATIS effusus est Christi sanguis quātū ad efficientiam. Effusio quippe sanguinis tui[?] pro multis tā fuit dignis ad precium: ut si omnes crederet in redemtore, nullum omnino diaboli vincula retinerēt.
units.tr: Innocent III, who lived around the year of the Lord 1200, writes thus: "Christ's blood was poured out for the PREDESTINED ALONE, as far as its efficacy is concerned. For the effusion of your blood for many was so worthy as a price that, if all believed in the Redeemer, the chains of the devil would retain no one at all."

units.la: Bernhardus ait: Christus secundum tempus quidem pro impiis mortuus est: secundum praedestinationem autem pro fratribus & amicis.
units.tr: Bernard says: "Christ indeed died for the impious according to time; but according to predestination, for his brothers and friends."

units.la: Thomas super Apocalypsin ca. 5. De redemtione facta per passionem Dei, est loqui dupliciter: Aut secundum sufficientiam: & sic passio redemit omnes: quia, quātū est de se, omnes liberavit. Omnib. enim redimēdis & saluandis sufficiens est: etiā si esset infiniti mundi: Sic dicit Anshelmus l. 2. Cur Deus homo, &c. cap. 14. Aut secundum efficientiam, & sic non omnes redemit. per passionem: quia non omnes adhaerent redemptori: & ideo non omnes habent efficaciam redemptionis.
units.tr: Thomas, on Revelation chapter 5: "To speak of redemption accomplished by the passion of God is to speak in two ways. Either according to sufficiency, and so the passion redeemed all; for, as far as it is in itself, it has freed all. For it is sufficient for all who are to be redeemed and saved, even if the world were infinite. Thus Anselm says in book 2 of Cur Deus homo, chapter 14. Or according to efficacy, and so it did not redeem all by the passion, because not all adhere to the Redeemer; and therefore not all have the efficacy of redemption."

units.la: Idē summa de verit. mater. 26. quaest. 7. Meritum Christi quantum ad sufficientiam, aequaliter se habet ad omnes: non autem quantum ad efficaciam. Quod accidit partim ex libero arbitrio, partim ex divina electione, per quam quibusdam misericorditer effectus meritorum Christi confertur, quibusdam vero iusto Dei iudicio subtrahitur.
units.tr: The same, in the Summa on the truth of the Catholic faith, book 4 (cited as 26, question 7): "The merit of Christ, as regards sufficiency, stands equally toward all; but not as regards efficacy. This happens partly from free will and partly from divine election, through which the effect of Christ's merits is conferred mercifully upon some, but withdrawn from others by the just judgment of God."

units.la: Lobardus li.3.diftinct.22.cap. Christus se Deo Trinitati obtulit pro omnibus quantum ad precy[?] sufficientiam, sed pro electis tantum, quantum ad efficaciam: quia praedestinatis tantum salutem effecit. Sed plura addere quid attinet? cum haec satis ostendat, minime nova vel impia, sed in ecclesia iam olim recepta & vera haec sacrae scripturae interpre-tatio[?] ne esse? Vnū adiicere libet Petri Galatini, hominis quidem monasticī, sed Theologi & Hebraei doctissimi locum, vt magis videant clamosi isti Theologiae hospites, nō mox inauditum & Sarracenicum esse, quicquid vel ignotum est ipsis, vel moestrosis[?] ipsorum figmentis non patrocinatur. Sic igitur ille in ea Iesaiae verba: Seruus meus iustus iustificabit multos: & c. orthodoxe commentatur: Licet passio Christi ad delenda omnium peccata sufficiens esse debeat: non tamen omnium peccata deletura erat, sed eorum dun-taxat, qui in eum crediturī essent atque pœnitentiam a-sturi[?]. Eam ob rem dicit: Et ipse peccata multorum tulit.
units.tr: Lombard, book 3, distinction 22, chapter: "Christ offered himself to the Triune God for all as regards sufficiency of price, but for the elect only as regards efficacy, because he effected salvation only for the predestined." But what is the point of adding more? Since this shows sufficiently that this interpretation of Holy Scripture is by no means new or impious, but is something long since received and true in the Church? I wish to add one passage of Peter Galatinus, a monk indeed, but a theologian and most learned Hebraist, so that these noisy guests of theology may see that whatever is unknown to them, or does not support their monstrous fictions, is not at once unheard-of and Saracen. He thus interprets orthodoxly those words of Isaiah: "My righteous servant shall justify many," etc.: "Although the passion of Christ ought to be sufficient to blot out the sins of all, yet it was not going to blot out the sins of all, but only of those who were going to believe in him and undertake repentance. Therefore he says: 'And he bore the sins of many.'"

units.la: Nunc missis auctoritatibus ad rationes nos conuer-tamus, quas praecipuè noua haec Pelagianorum progenies impio & absurdo dogmate nobis suggerit.
units.tr: Now, with the authorities set aside, let us turn to the arguments which this new brood of Pelagians especially suggests to us with its impious and absurd dogma.

units.la: Cōtēdūt, Christū pro omnibus mortuū esse. Nemo negat. Hęc enim scripturę locutio est. Addūt pro omnibus & singulis mortuū esse. Ne h c quidē simpliciter insicia mur, licet scriptura sic loqui nō inueniamus. Pergūt ad-dere: Pro omnib. & singulis pariter electis & reprobis, pro Caino & Dauide, pro Iuda & Petro, pro dānatis [?]quē ac seruadis[?], abfq. fidei & infidelitatis ratione mor-tuum esse. Hoc durū est. Pergūt denique pro his omnib. & singulis, non modo quoad sufficientiam, sed & quoad efficaciam gratiae Dei etiā λύτρον[?] mortuū esse. Quid hoc vero? Nēpe Christū sanguine & morte sua omnes ac singulos illos etiā, qui nō saluantur, sed iā inde à Caino dānati sunt, & damnantur, & porro damnabuntur veraciter, vt loquuntur, à morte liberasse, à peccatis purgasse, sanctificasse, Deo reco-ciliasse, inque sinum & gratiâ eius restituisse. Hoc impium & absurdum dogma: quo aliud non minus falsum & absurdum concludunt: Impios ergo, quotquot periere, ac pereunt, ac peribunt, non propter peccata sua (quippe quæ & sanguine Christi expiata fuerint) sed propter solam incredulitatem periisse, ac perire, & perituros esse. Nihil nos hic fingere, vel per calumniam dicere, fatebuntur ij, qui controuersiam hanc non omnino ignorant. Quàm verò hæc sunt portentosa Christianis auribus?
units.tr: They contend that Christ died for all. No one denies this; for this is the language of Scripture. They add that he died for all and each. We do not simply deny even this, although we do not find that Scripture speaks thus. They go on to add: that he died for all and each alike, both elect and reprobate, for Cain and David, for Judas and Peter, for the damned and the saved, without regard to faith or unbelief. This is harsh. Finally they go on to say that he died for all these, and each, not only as regards sufficiency but also as regards the efficacy of God's grace, even as a ransom. What is this, indeed? Namely, that Christ by his blood and death has freed from death, cleansed from sins, sanctified, reconciled to God, and restored into the bosom and grace of God all and each of those who are not saved, but who have been condemned from Cain onward, and are condemned, and will truly be condemned, as they say. This is an impious and absurd dogma, from which they conclude something no less false and absurd: that the impious, as many as have perished, and as are perishing and will perish, did not perish, and are not perishing, and will not perish, on account of their sins (since these have been expiated by the blood of Christ), but on account of unbelief alone. Those who are not wholly ignorant of this controversy will admit that we are not inventing anything here, nor speaking by calumny. But how monstrous are these things to Christian ears!

units.la: Impios & impuros canes omnes, ante & post Christum mortuum, morte eius in sinum & gratia Dei receptos esse, distitant belliis[?]ti impiorum patroni. Nos primò falsum & impium dogma esse dicimus: quia aperte repugnat scripturæ, quæ constanter clamat, impios, quoad sunt absque fide & pœnitentia, nô esse in sinu & gratia Dei, sed esse ac manere filios iræ & æternæ maledictionis: nec esse liberatos à peccato & morte, sed teneri captiues laqueis diaboli & efficaciter agitari: jam iudicatos esse & sub ira Dei manere.
units.tr: The defenders of the impious deny that all impious and unclean dogs, before and after Christ's death, have been received by his death into the bosom and grace of God. First, we say that this is a false and impious dogma, because it openly contradicts Scripture, which constantly proclaims that the impious, so long as they are without faith and repentance, are not in the bosom and grace of God, but are and remain children of wrath and of eternal curse; that they are not freed from sin and death, but are held captive in the snares of the devil and are effectively driven about; that they are already judged and remain under the wrath of God.

units.la: Deinde longè absurdissimum hoc esse figmentum af-ferimus:quia multa principia Christianæ fidei, & se ip-sum turpissimè elidit:Ponamus enim in medio thesin i-stam:OMNES HOMINES nullo excepto,fideles & infideles, ante & post Christum mortuum sanguine Christi vere & indubitanter in gratiam & sinum Dei esse receptos. Quid quæso hinc sequitur?Certè Ilias absurditatum.
units.tr: Next, we assert that this figment is by far the most absurd, because it utterly destroys many principles of the Christian faith. Let us set down in the midst this thesis: "ALL MEN, none excepted, faithful and unfaithful, before and after Christ's death, have truly and undoubtedly been received into grace and into the bosom of God by the blood of Christ." What, I ask, follows from this? Surely a whole heap of absurdities.

units.la: Primò:tolletur peccatum originis: nec ullus eius erit reatus:falsum erit,omnes homines nasci filios iræ:quia omnes nascentur in gratia & sinu Dei. At scriptura nos omnes filios iræ natura proclamat.
units.tr: First, this will remove original sin: no one will bear its guilt. It will be false that all men are born children of wrath, since all would be born in grace and in the bosom of God. Yet Scripture proclaims that by nature we are all children of wrath.

units.la: Secundò:omnes etiam Turcarum,Sarracenorum, Centaurorum,& Canibalum liberi, qui sunt extra fœdus & ecclesiam Dei,nascentur in sinu & gratia Dei. Erit ergo salus etiam extra fœdus Dei:extra ecclesiam Dei.O immanes verò Briareos istos: qui infantes Turcarum extra ecclesiam natos, in gratiam & sinum Dei collocare nô dubitant:Christianorum verò infantes ante baptismum, ex illo Dei sinu & gratia in gehennam crudeliter præcipitare nihil veretur. Quis nescit enim eos baptismo salutem infantum ita alligare, ut ante baptismū mortuos, nisi pię preces parentum vel amicorum inter-uenerint, ab æterna salute suspendant, atque ita è gratia & sinu Dei excutiant. Quòd si vero per baptismum demum in gratiam & sinum Dei recipiuntur : quomodo morte Christi iam olim totum genus humanū in eum esse receptum Theticus ille disputator defendet?
units.tr: Second, all the children of Turks, Saracens, Centaurs and Cannibals, who are outside the covenant and the Church of God, will also be born in the bosom and grace of God. Salvation will therefore exist even outside the covenant of God and outside the Church of God. O monstrous Briareuses, who do not hesitate to place the infants of the Turks, born outside the Church, in the grace and bosom of God, yet have no qualms about cruelly hurling the infants of Christians, before baptism, from that bosom and grace of God into hell! For who does not know that they so bind the salvation of infants to baptism that, unless the pious prayers of parents or friends intervene, those who die before baptism are cut off from eternal salvation and thus cast out from the grace and bosom of God? But if they are received into the grace and bosom of God only through baptism, how will that Theticus disputant defend the claim that the whole human race was long ago received into him through the death of Christ?

units.la: Tertiò: igitur hoc portentum aliud ipsorum dogma de infantibus fidelium extra gratiam nascentibus, imò, ante baptismum à diabolo obsessis, & damnatis manifestè elidit.
units.tr: Third, therefore, their other monstrous doctrine about the infants of believers, who are born outside grace, or even, before baptism, are possessed by the devil and damned, plainly refutes itself.

units.la: Quarto: Omnes impij, qui ante mortem Christi in gehennam inciderunt, morte Christi rursus Deo fuerunt reconciliati, & in sinum atque gratiam eius restituti: quomodo ergo inde rursus exciderunt, qui mortui recepti sunt, quando amplius peccare incredulitate non potuerunt? Ergo aut in sinu Dei impij manebunt, & fine fide seruabuntur: aut fine incredulitate inde rursus præcipitantur: quorum utrumque veritati euangelij, & iustitiæ Dei manifestè repugnat.
units.tr: Fourth: all the wicked who fell into hell before the death of Christ were reconciled to God again through the death of Christ, and restored to his bosom and grace. How, then, do those who were received back in death fall out again, since they could no longer sin by unbelief? Therefore either the wicked will remain in the bosom of God and be kept without faith, or without unbelief they are cast out again from it. Both of these plainly contradict the truth of the gospel and the justice of God.

units.la: Quintò : Incredulitas vel non erit peccatum, vel si sit, non omnia peccata fuerint morte Christi expiata: vel si sint omnia, ea salte[?] efficacia mortis Christi fortior fuerit. Hæc verò falsa & impia sunt omnia. Incredulitas, n. non modò ipsa peccatum est, sed & mater est peccatorum reliquorum: & cum peccatis reliquis subinde etiam renatis adhæret: verum sanguine Christi efficacissimè expiata est illis atque rem[?]sa.
units.tr: Fifth: either unbelief will not be sin, or, if it is sin, not all sins were expiated by the death of Christ, or, if all were, the efficacy of the death of Christ was weaker than they. But these claims are all false and impious. For unbelief is not only itself sin, but is also the mother of the other sins, and it clings to the remaining sins, even to those that are later forgiven in the regenerate; yet it has been most effectively expiated and removed by the blood of Christ.

units.la: Sextò :-Impudens & absurdū mendacium est, impios non propter peccata, sed propter incredulitatem damnari. Quasi vero scriptum non sit 1.Cor. 6.ver.10. Fures, Avari, Ebriosi, &c. regnū Dei hæreditatem non consequentur: Et Christus in iudicio non sit dicturus maledictis: Abite in gehennam, quia non cibastis me, &c. & quasi nō incredulitas in genere peccatorum primas teneat. Imò contrà concludimus, propter peccata damnari, quia propter in-credulitatem damnantur. Quòd enim peccatum incredulitate grauius? Nimis vero futiliter ludit apostata ille. Incredulitatem nunc non consideraři, vt in se pecca-tum tum est,sed vt salutis media respuit.Quid enim est salutis media respuere? Annon cotemtus Dei? Annon graui ssimü peccatum?quia salutem eiusque media respuit?
units.tr: Sixth: it is a shameless and absurd lie that the wicked are damned not on account of their sins, but on account of unbelief. As if it were not written, 1 Cor. 6:10, "Thieves, the covetous, drunkards, etc. shall not inherit the kingdom of God"; and as if Christ, in judgment, were not going to say with curses, "Depart into hell, because you did not feed me, etc."; and as if unbelief did not hold first place among the kinds of sin. Rather, on the contrary, we conclude that they are damned on account of their sins, because they are damned on account of unbelief. For what sin is graver than unbelief? That apostate plays far too frivolously. He says that unbelief is now not to be considered as sin in itself, but as it rejects the means of salvation. For what is it to reject the means of salvation? Is it not contempt of God? Is it not the most grievous sin, because it rejects salvation and its means?

units.la: Septimo : Portentosū hoc dogma tribuit impiis,quòd stante doctrina ecclesiæ de peccato originis , & de impiorum reatu,nullo vnquam momento illis infit,vel de illis vere prædicari possit. Sumamus enim Turcæ infantem,fumamus & barbarum adultum aliquem,qui morte Christi nunquâ vel fando audiuerit:proinde nec incredulitate spreuerit. Dicant iam nobis isti difputatores,quo temporis momento istis,an dū eflent embryones,an recens natis,an pueris,an adolescentibus,an viris,an fœnibus,denique viuis an mortuis tribuere velint, quod sint in sinu & gratia Dei,reconciliati Deo, iustificati,sanctificati? Imò dicant, fi recepti sunt, quomodo excidant,cùm neque peccata, neque actualis incredulitas eos inde præcipitare queat?Hæc enim in tales non cadit.Illa verò morte Christi expiata fuerunt. Quicquid dixerint,audiemus,vel fine fide aliquos Deo placere:vel absque incredulitate actuali aliquos è sinu Dei præcipitari:quæ & falsa & impia sunt & fe mutuo elidunt.
units.tr: Seventh: this monstrous doctrine attributes to the wicked that, while the Church's teaching on original sin and on the guilt of the wicked stands, they never at any moment are, or can truly be said to be, in that state. For let us take a Turkish infant, let us take also some barbarian adult who has never heard even the name of the death of Christ, and so has not despised it through unbelief.
