Let these disputants now tell us at what moment they wish to attribute to these people that they are in the bosom and grace of God, reconciled to God, justified, sanctified: whether while they were still embryos, or newly born, or children, or youths, or men, or women, or finally living or dead? Nay, let them say: if they were received, how do they fall away, since neither sins nor actual unbelief can cast them out from there? For these do not apply to such people. But those were expiated by the death of Christ. Whatever they say, we shall hear either that some please God without faith, or that some are cast out from the bosom of God without actual unbelief; both of which are false and impious and contradict each other.

units.la: Denique quid magis blasphemum dici possit, quàm Deum in gratiam recepisse,& in sinu fouere,omnes infideles,impios,Cainü,Saulé,Iudam,Herodem, Caligulā, denique omnes omninò sceleratos & porcos?Quæ consolatio magis erit ludibrio similis, quàm te esse Christi morte redemtum , in finum & gratiam Dei restitutum: multa vero millia eorum,qui sic fuerunt restituti, nihilominùs æternùm perire? Horret animus hæc monstra pluribus persequi. Dogma ergo tam falsum,impium, absurdum,blasphemum, quis nō censeat procul ab ecclesiæ limitibus arcendum atque exterminandum esse?
units.tr: Finally, what could be said to be more blasphemous than that God has received all unbelievers, the impious, Cain, Saul, Judas, Herod, Caligula, in short all utterly wicked and filthy men, into grace and cherishes them in his bosom? What consolation would be more like a mockery than to be told that you have been redeemed by the death of Christ and restored to the bosom and grace of God, while many thousands of those who were so restored nonetheless perish forever? My mind shudders to pursue these monstrosities at greater length. Who would not judge that a doctrine so false, impious, absurd and blasphemous must be kept far away from the boundaries of the Church and driven out?

units.la: Hic verò mihi videor audire ad rauim vsque clamantes : Promissiones euangelij esse vniuersales : pertinere ad omnes,ad omnes. Nos verò primum quærimus, qualis hæc fit consecutio?Promissiones sunt vniuersales.Ergo etiam reprobi, impuri canes & porci sunt in finum & gratiam Dei restituti. Quin potiùs contra:Promissiones euangelij omnes annexam habent conditionem fidei & pœnitentiæ : Ergo nihil illæ ad canes &porcos. Deinde quoties illi suum omnes, omnes nobis occinunt: toties nos nostrum credentes, credentes regerimus. Sūt n. promissiones vniuersales, sed respectu agentium pœnitentiam, & credentium euangelio. Atque hic ad ipsam promissionum literam coram toto mundo prouocamus. Venite ad me OMNES,inquit Christus:sed addit : qui laboratis & onerati estis, hoc est,sub peccatorum mole fatiscitis,quod fit iis,qui resipiscunt.Et alibi:Sic Deus dilexit mundum,& filium suum vnigenitum daret,& omnis,qui credit non pereat,sed habeat vitā aeternā. Et Paulus:iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes,& super omnes credetes.Et alibi:Conclusit scriptura omnia sub peccato,& promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus. Et Christus:Qui credit in filium,habet vitā aeternā. Et Petrus:Huic testimonium dant omnes prophetae,remissionem peccatorum accepturum per nomen eius omnem qui credit in eū. Similis aliarum promissionum euangelij omniū est ratio.Nam vel expressam,vel tacitam fidei & pœnitentiæ conditionem habent, nec possunt nisi de vniuersitate fidelium citra blasphemiam intelligi.
units.tr: Here indeed I seem to hear people shouting hoarsely: the promises of the gospel are universal; they pertain to all, to all. But we first ask: what kind of inference is this? The promises are universal; therefore even the reprobate, the impure dogs and swine, have been restored to the bosom and grace of God. Rather, on the contrary: the promises of the gospel all have the condition of faith and repentance attached; therefore they do not apply to dogs and swine at all. Moreover, as often as they sing their "all, all" to us, so often do we answer them with our "believing, believing." For the promises are universal, but with respect to those who repent and believe the gospel. And here we appeal to the very letter of the promises before the whole world. "Come to me, all," says Christ, but he adds, "you who labour and are burdened," that is, who faint under the weight of sins, which is the case with those who repent. And elsewhere: "God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, and whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life." And Paul: "the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, unto all and upon all who believe." And elsewhere: "Scripture has concluded all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe." And Christ: "Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life." And Peter: "To him all the prophets bear witness, that through his name everyone who believes in him will receive the forgiveness of sins." The reasoning is the same for all the other promises of the gospel. For they have either an expressed or a tacit condition of faith and repentance, and they cannot be understood, without blasphemy, of anything other than the whole body of believers.

units.la: Excipiūt:Sic statui promissiones particulares. Respō-deat vero pro nobis author librorum de vocatione gen-tium:siue is sit Ambrosius,cuius nomen praeferunt,siue Prosper,quod nonnullis placet.Habet,inquit,populus Dei plenitudinem suam:& quantumuis magna pars hominum saluātur gratiā aut negligat,aut repellat:in electis tamen & praescitu,atq. ab omniū generalitate discretū speciali-bus quadā cefetur[?] vniuersitas,& de toto mundo totus mundus liberatus & de omnibus hominies[?] omnes hominies[?] redeti[?]. Manet ergo promissiones euangelij vniuer-sales fidelibus, etsi ad canes & porcos nihil pertineant. Manet & maior syllogismi practici vniuersalis. Promis-siones ad omnes credentes pertinent. Ergo ad me pertinent. Item Christus pro omnibus credenti-bus orauit & mortuus est. Ergo credo. Ergo pro me ora-uit & mortuus est. Nimis vero frigidi sunt consolatores, qui sic docent afflictas conscientias argumentari: Chri-stus pro omnibus hominibus est mortuus. Ergo sum ho-mo. Ergo etiā pro me est mortuus. Quidni enim etiam Turca, canis,& porcus,in volutabro manens, sic concludat[?] O egregios consolatores, & gratiae Dei praecones! Non hominem esse, sed fide Christo insitum esse, est Christianae consolationis neruus praeclarissimus.
units.tr: They object: thus the particular promises are established. But let the author of the books on the calling of the Gentiles answer for us, whether he is Ambrose, whose name they bear, or Prosper, as some prefer. "The people of God," he says, "has its fullness; and however many people are saved, although the greater part of men neglect or reject grace, yet among the elect and the foreknown, and distinguished from the general mass of all, a certain universality is found by special selection, and from the whole world the whole world is freed, and from all men all men..." Therefore the universal promises of the gospel remain for believers, even if they have nothing to do with dogs and swine. The major premise of the universal practical syllogism also remains: the promises pertain to all believers; therefore they pertain to me. Likewise, Christ prayed for all believers and died for them; therefore I believe; therefore he prayed for me and died for me. But those comforters are far too cold who teach troubled consciences to reason in this way: Christ died for all men; therefore I am a man; therefore he also died for me. For why could not the Turk, the dog and the swine, lying in the mire, reason in just this way? O excellent comforters and heralds of the grace of God! To be not merely a man but grafted into Christ by faith is the most excellent sinew of Christian consolation.

units.la: Obiciunt denique ex Apostolo: Omnes in Christo viuificari, quemadmodum omnes in Adamo moriuntur. Atqui, si absolute omnes in Christo viuificari dicant, scriptura & experientia eos refutabit. Hoc ergo dicit Apostolus, Christum omnibus suis conferre vitam: sicut Adam omnibus suis contulit mortem. Et ille quidem per gratiam, quod maius est: hic per naturalem propagationem, quod facilius. Atque hunc Pauli sensum etiam sequentia verba liquido probant. Cùm enim omnes in Christo viuificari dixisset, statim subiungit: Vnusquisque autem suo ordine. Primitiae Christus: postea qui sunt Christi, hoc est, credentes, qui ipsi a Patre dati sunt, & pro quibus Patrem ardentissime orauit. Nec dissimiliter Augu-stinus interpretatur, ideo dictum esse, omnes in Christo viuificari, non quia omnes, qui in Adamo moriuntur, membra sint Christi: sed quia sicut nemo corpore animali nisi in Adam moritur: ita nemo corpore spirituali, nisi in Christo viuificetur.
units.tr: Finally, they object from the Apostle: all are made alive in Christ, just as all die in Adam. But if they say absolutely that all are made alive in Christ, Scripture and experience will refute them. Therefore the Apostle says this: Christ confers life on all his own, just as Adam conferred death on all his own. And the former indeed through grace, which is greater; the latter through natural propagation, which is easier. And the following words clearly confirm this sense of Paul. For when he had said that all are made alive in Christ, he immediately adds: "But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterwards those who are Christ's," that is, believers, who were themselves given to the Father and for whom he prayed most fervently to the Father. Augustine interprets it similarly: it is said that all are made alive in Christ not because all who die in Adam are members of Christ, but because just as no one dies in an animal body except in Adam, so no one is made alive in a spiritual body except in Christ.

units.la: Neque vero est, quod obstrepere pergant: hac ratione Adamum Christo fortiorem statui: si plures ille in exitium & mortis voraginem praecipitauerit, quam hic seruet, atque ex faucibus mortis eripiat. Potentia enim vtriusque non numero eorum, qui moriuntur, vel viuificantur, sed modo potius quo fit perditio vel viuificatio, itemque magnitudine beneficiorum amissorum & reparatorum aestimatur. Laedere est facile, mederi difficile, iuxta Prouerbium: Citius & facilius sexcentos homines perdas, quam vnum seruēs[?]: citius multos de ponte in profluentem praecipites, quam vnum ex submersionis periculo eripias. Sic multo facilius fuit, totum humanum genus perdere: quam vnicum hominem ex ruina restituere. Illud Satan potuit, Adam potuit: hoc nemo nisi Christus potuit. Nocere, laedere, neci dare homines, bestiae, & res aduersae queunt. At salutem & vitam aeternam reparare, in nullius creaturae situm est facultate: sed solius Dei rerum omnium conditoris potentiae est referre. Fortior igitur mors Christi Adami peccato fuit[?] set, etiamsi vel vnicum hominem vitæ restituisset. Tum etiam certum est & indubitatū, bona illa quæ per Christum sunt reparata, tantum præcellere iis, quorum per Adamum fecerámus iacturam, quantum terrenis & caducis rebus cœlestes & æternæ præstant. Adam enim, teste Apostolo, est terrenus: Christus cœlestis: ille animalis, hic spiritualis: ille ex terreno Paradiso nos eiecit: hic in cœlestem collocauit, æternaque felicitate donauit.
units.tr: Nor should they go on objecting that by this reasoning Adam would be made stronger than Christ, if he cast more people into destruction and the abyss of death than Christ saves and snatches from the jaws of death. For the power of each is measured not by the number of those who die or are made alive, but rather by the manner in which destruction or making alive takes place, and likewise by the greatness of the benefits lost and restored. To harm is easy, to heal difficult, as the proverb has it: you may more quickly and easily destroy six hundred men than save one; you may more quickly throw many from a bridge into a river than rescue one from the danger of drowning. Thus it was far easier to destroy the whole human race than to restore a single man from ruin. Satan could do that, Adam could do that; only Christ could do this. Men, beasts and adverse things can harm, injure and bring death; but to repair salvation and eternal life lies within the power of no creature, and it belongs to the power of God alone, the creator of all things. Therefore the death of Christ was stronger than Adam's sin, even if it had restored only a single man to life. Moreover, it is certain and beyond doubt that the good things restored through Christ surpass those we lost through Adam as much as heavenly and eternal things surpass earthly and perishable ones. For Adam, as the Apostle testifies, is earthly, Christ heavenly; the one is natural, the other spiritual; the one cast us out of the earthly paradise, the other placed us in a heavenly one and endowed us with eternal happiness.

units.la: Hactenus mortis & resurrectionis Christi fructus ad omnes & solos eos, qui fide Christo adhærent, & pœnitentiam agunt, satis ostensum, atque calumniis respondendum esse arbitramur, &c.
units.tr: Thus far we judge that it has been sufficiently shown that the fruits of the death and resurrection of Christ belong to all and only those who cling to Christ by faith and repent, and that objections must be answered, etc.

units.la: VI. ISAGOGE BREVISSIMA AD CONTROVERSIAM EVCHARISTICAM: EXPONENS quæstiones præcipuas non controuersas & controuersas inter euangelicos.
units.tr: VI. A VERY BRIEF INTRODUCTION TO THE EUCHARISTIC CONTROVERSY: SETTING OUT the principal questions, both uncontroversial and controversial, among the evangelicals.

units.la: Davide Pareo Authore.
units.tr: By David Pareus.

units.la: Quatuor ὑποθέσεις generalia.
units.tr: Four general theses.

units.la: I. Meminerint iuniores, discernendas esse quæstiones de Cæremonia seu ritu Cœnæ: & de doctrina, quæ est promissio Euangelij ritui annexa.
units.tr: I. Let the younger readers keep in mind that two sets of questions must be distinguished: those concerning the ceremony or rite of the Supper, and those concerning the doctrine, which is the promise of the Gospel annexed to the rite.

units.la: II. Discant etiam discernere quæstiones tam de ritu quàm de doctrina, non controuersas à controuersis.
units.tr: II. Let them also learn to distinguish, both in the rite and in the doctrine, questions that are uncontroversial from those that are controversial.

units.la: III. Sciant quæstiones controuersas de ritu esse minus principales & magna ex parte κατ' ἀπεχθείαν decidi posse ac debere, ex temporum, locorum & hominum circumstantiis: semper tamen ad ædificationem.
units.tr: III. Let them know that the controversial questions concerning the rite are less important, and for the most part can and ought to be settled by a kindly disposition (kat' apecheian), according to the circumstances of times, places and persons; yet always for the sake of edification.

units.la: IV. Sciant quæstiones præcipuas de doctrina cœnæ non controuersas esse tres: & controuersas totidem: ad quas omnes aliæ facilè referri possunt. De vtrisque iuniores hic monebo breuissimè.
units.tr: IV. Let them know that the principal questions concerning the doctrine of the Supper are three that are uncontroversial and as many that are controversial, to which all the others can easily be referred. I will here briefly advise the younger readers about both kinds.

units.la: Tres quæstiones non controuersæ de doctrina Cœnæ.
units.tr: Three questions not in dispute concerning the doctrine of the Supper.

units.la: I. Quid sit Cœna Domini?
units.tr: I. What is the Lord's Supper?

units.la: Consentiunt de hac omnes Euangelici, quòd Cœna Domini sit noui Testamenti Sacramentum à Christo institutum, in quo sumpto pane & vino, sumitur verum corpus & sanguis Christi, atque obsignatur fidelibus κοινωνία Christi & beneficiorum eius.
units.tr: All evangelical Christians agree on this: the Lord's Supper is a sacrament of the New Testament, instituted by Christ, in which, when bread and wine are taken, the true body and blood of Christ are received, and the fellowship [κοινωνία] of Christ and his benefits is sealed to believers.

units.la: II. Quæ sint fines & usus Cœnæ à Christo institutæ?
units.tr: II. What are the ends and uses of the Supper instituted by Christ?

units.la: Consentiunt hîc quoque omnes euangelici, quòd sumtio hæc confirmet fidem promissionis gratiæ: tum quia hic est communis sacramentorum vsus: tum quia Christus de hoc sacramento dixit: Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Et: Hoc poculum est nouum fœdus in meo sanguine.
units.tr: Here too all evangelical Christians agree that this partaking strengthens faith in the promise of grace, both because this is the common use of the sacraments and because Christ said of this sacrament: Do this in remembrance of me. And: This cup is the new covenant in my blood.

units.la: III. Quid in Cœna Domini exhibeatur & percipiatur?
units.tr: III. What is offered and received in the Lord's Supper?

units.la: Consentiunt & hic Euangelici panem & vinum visibiliter corpus & sanguinem Domini cum omnibus beneficiis, inuisibiliter exhiberi & percipi.
units.tr: Here too evangelical Christians agree that the bread and wine visibly offer and the body and blood of the Lord with all his benefits are invisibly offered and received.

units.la: De his, inquam, consensus est inter Theologos euangelicos. Contentiosis verò matæologis, neque de his, neque de aliis conuenit: quorum rixæ non debent esse mensura iudicij de ecclesiarum euangelicarum consensu, vel controuersiis.
units.tr: On these points, I say, there is agreement among the evangelical theologians. But among the contentious word-quibblers, there is agreement neither on these points nor on others; and their squabbles should not be taken as the measure of the agreement or the controversies of the evangelical churches.

units.la: Quæstiones verò tres controuersæ sunt hæ.
units.tr: The three questions that are in dispute, however, are these.

units.la: PRIMA QVÆSTIO.
units.tr: FIRST QUESTION.

units.la: Quid sit vnio signi & res signatæ in Cœna Domini: num transsubstantiatio: an consubstantiatio: an verò relatio mystica?
units.tr: What is the union of the sign and the thing signified in the Lord's Supper: is it transubstantiation, or consubstantiation, or rather a mystical relation?

units.la: De his tribus propositionibus orthodoxè respondetur, duabus negantibus, vna affirmante.
units.tr: These three propositions are answered orthodoxly: two denying, one affirming.

units.la: PROPOSITIO I. Signa & res non vniuntur transsubstantiatione, hoc est, talis mutatione, qua substantia signorum transeat in substantiam rerum, manentibus tantum accidentibus.
units.tr: PROPOSITION I. Signs and things are not united by transubstantiation, that is, by such a change whereby the substance of the signs passes into the substance of the things, only the accidents remaining.

units.la: Ratio 1.Quia ex regula Irenæi duæ sunt res habentes analogiam sacramentalem in eucharistia: quam accidentia panis & vini,& substantia corporis ac sanguinis Christi habere non possunt.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because, according to the rule of Irenaeus, there are two things having a sacramental analogy in the Eucharist; the accidents of bread and wine and the substance of the body and blood of Christ cannot have this analogy.

units.la: Ratio 2.Ex verbis Christi: Hoc est corpus meum. Non dixit: Hoc est, aut fiat corpus meum.
units.tr: Reason 2. From the words of Christ: "This is my body." He did not say: "This is, or let it become, my body."

units.la: Ratio 3.Panis nominatur panis in actione, ante & post actionem.
units.tr: Reason 3. Bread is called bread in the action, both before and after the action.

units.la: Ratio 4.Patres orthodoxi panem in cœna retinent: & cum [illegible, ~5 letters] de panis mutatione loquuntur, sacramentaliter intelligi volunt: ut Theodoretus Dial. 1. Voluit Christus sacramentis [?] non intentos esse in naturam eorum quae cernuntur, sed per nominu permutationem credere ei, quae ex gratia facta est mutationi. Hic mutationem sacramentalem intelligendam esse, ipse eodem dialogo docet, sic inquies: Christus visibilia symbola corporis & sanguinis appellatione honoravit, non naturam mutans, sed naturæ gratiam adducens.
units.tr: Reason 4. The orthodox Fathers retain the bread in the Supper; and when [illegible, about 5 letters] they speak of the change of the bread, they want it understood sacramentally: as Theodoret, Dialogue 1: "Christ wished that those not intent on the nature of the things that are seen should believe, by the exchange of names, in the change that has been made by grace." That this change is to be understood sacramentally, he himself teaches in the same dialogue, thus you will say: "Christ honoured the visible symbols with the appellation of body and blood, not changing their nature, but adding grace to their nature."

units.la: Propositio II. Signa & res signata non uniuntur consubstantiatione, hoc est, reali duorum corporum in eodem loco existentia: aut unius in altero latentia: qualis est avena in sacco: pecunia in crumena: infantis in cunis: vini in cantharo. Hæc enim sunt consubstantiatorum similia.
units.tr: Proposition II. Signs and the thing signified are not united by consubstantiation, that is, by the real existence of two bodies in the same place, or by the hiding of one in the other: such as oats in a sack, money in a purse, an infant in a cradle, wine in a cup. For these are the likenesses of the consubstantiators.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia Christi verba: Hoc est corpus meum, sonant, non sit corpus Christi: neque quid in, cum, sub pane sit: sed quid ipse panis sit, esseque debeat piis in hoc usu.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because the words of Christ, "This is my body," do not mean that the body of Christ is in, with, or under the bread, but what the bread itself is, and what it ought to be for the pious in this use.

units.la: Ratio 2. Corpus Christi est verum, organicum, finitum, & visibile corpus: post ascensionem non in terris vel ubique præsens, sed in cœlo existens & manens, usque ad reditum extremum.
units.tr: Reason 2. The body of Christ is a true, organic, finite and visible body; after the ascension it is not present on earth or everywhere, but exists and remains in heaven until the final return.

units.la: Ratio 3. Orthodoxi patres corpus & sanguinem Christi in pane & vino esse docent, non in latibulis, sed ut in mysterio & per mysterium. Chrisost. in opere imperfecto Matt. homil. 11. In Vatis sanctificatis non verum Christi corpus, sed mysterium corporis Christi continetur.
units.tr: Reason 3. The orthodox Fathers teach that the body and blood of Christ are in the bread and wine not in hiding places, but as in a mystery and through a mystery. Chrysostom, in the unfinished work on Matthew, Homily 11: "In the sanctified vessels is contained not the true body of Christ, but the mystery of the body of Christ."

units.la: Propositio III. Signa & res cohærent in cœna unione sacramentali. Ea vero est, quæ toti sacramentorum generi communis est: alioqui non sacramentalis, sed cœnalis effet.in omnibus vero sacramentis aliis, unio est relatiua, hoc est, mystica rei signatæ per signum significatio, obsignatio, præbitio & perceptio in usu legitimo: qui non est sine fide & conuersione utentium.
units.tr: Proposition III. Signs and things cohere in the Supper by sacramental union. This union is common to the whole genus of sacraments; otherwise it would not be sacramental but merely a supper. In all other sacraments the union is relative, that is, the mystical signifying, sealing, offering and receiving of the thing signified through the sign, in lawful use; which is not without faith and the conversion of those who use it.

units.la: Ratio 1. à genere. In omnibus sacramentis talis est unio; Ergo etiam in cœna. Antecedens ex definitione & principali sacramentorum sine patet.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the genus. In all sacraments there is such a union; therefore also in the Supper. The antecedent is plain from the definition and the principal nature of sacraments.

units.la: Ratio 2. Panis est corpus Christi aut rei veritate (ut loquitur Augustinus in sententia Prosperi:) aut significante mysterio. Non rei veritate seu essentialiter: quia non fit transsubstantiatio. Ergo significante mysterio.
units.tr: Reason 2. Bread is the body of Christ either in truth of the thing (as Augustine speaks in the sentence of Prosper), or by a signifying mystery. Not in truth of the thing or essentially, because there is no transubstantiation. Therefore by a signifying mystery.

units.la: Ratio 3. Huc pertinent omnia argumenta, quibus probatur sacramentalis locutio in verbis cœnæ. Unio enim sacramentalis phrases sacramentales parit.
units.tr: Reason 3. All the arguments by which sacramental speech in the words of the Supper is proved belong here. For sacramental union produces sacramental phrases.

units.la: Ratio 4. Testimonia patrum, quod panis fit signum, figura, sacramentum corporis Christi, non utique absentis, sed præsentis: præsentis autem non in elementis, sed in verbo elementis annexo: non ori, sed cordi: nec oraliter, sed mystice & spiritualiter.
units.tr: Reason 4. The testimonies of the Fathers, that the bread becomes a sign, figure and sacrament of the body of Christ, not of an absent body but of a present one: present, however, not in the elements but in the word joined to the elements; present not to the mouth but to the heart, and not orally but mystically and spiritually.

units.la: Obiectio papistarum pro transsubstan-tiatione ex verbis Cœnæ.
units.tr: The objection of the Papists for transubstantiation from the words of the Supper.

units.la: Hoc quod dabat Christus, & sacerdos consecrat, est corpus Christi. Ergo non est panis. Valet à disparatis. Hæc res est homo. Ergo non est bos. Respon. Negatur, quod fit argumentum à positione unius speciei ad remotionem disparatæ eiusdem generis: quia est processus vitiosus à positione relationis sacramentalis, ad negationem subiecti seu substantiæ: qualis est, si dicam. Hic homo est pater. Ergo nō est homo. Sic illi: Hic panis est corpus Christi. Ergo non est panis. Est ergo fallacia accidentis non minus absurda, quàm si à positione formæ ad negationem materiæ sic argumenteris: Hæc res est mensa: Ergo non est lignum. Licet enim corpus Christi non sit forma vel accidens panis: ipsa tamen relatio, quam panis, vi promissionis, ad Corpus Christi habet ac sustinet, forma est sacramenti. Sic non valet: Columba est spiritus sanctus. Ergo nō est columba. Circumcisio est fœdus Dei: Ergo non est circumcisio.Poculum est nouum testamentum. Ergo non po-culum.
units.tr: What Christ gives, and the priest consecrates, is the body of Christ. Therefore it is not bread. The inference is from disparates: This thing is a man. Therefore it is not an ox. Answer. It is denied: this is an argument from the positing of one species to the removal of a disparate of the same genus, because it is a faulty process from the positing of a sacramental relation to the denial of the subject or substance; such as if I say: This man is a father. Therefore he is not a man. So they say: This bread is the body of Christ. Therefore it is not bread. It is thus a fallacy of the accident, no less absurd than if you argued from the positing of a form to the denial of the matter: "This thing is a table: therefore it is not wood." For although the body of Christ is not a form or accident of the bread, yet the very relation which the bread, by virtue of the promise, has and sustains toward the body of Christ, is a form of the sacrament. So this does not hold: "The dove is the Holy Spirit. Therefore it is not a dove." "Circumcision is the covenant of God. Therefore it is not circumcision." "The cup is the new testament. Therefore not a cup."

units.la: Ad testimonia patrum,quę papistæ de mutatione symbolorū obiiciunt, responsio communis est, ea de mutatio-ne sacramentali, non de essentiali intelligenda esse, quod ex orthodoxo patrum consensu de hoc sacramento est manifestum.
units.tr: The common answer to the testimonies of the Fathers, which the Papists object concerning the change of the symbols, is that they are to be understood of a sacramental change, not of an essential one; which is manifest from the orthodox consensus of the Fathers concerning this sacrament.

units.la: SECUNDA QUÆSTIO. Quomodo tum symbola, tum res cœlestes in cœna exhibeantur & percipiantur?
units.tr: SECOND QUESTION. In what way are both the symbols and the heavenly things exhibited and received in the Supper?

units.la: Hæc quæstio nobis controuersa est cum pontificiis simul & vbiquitariis, quia utrique volunt res in signis, vel signorum speciebus latenter & miraculose præsentes manu ministrorum gestari, tractari, & in ora fumetium ingeri. Nos contra docemus, res cū symbolis exhiberi & percipi quidem coniunctim in legitimo cœnæ usu: sed diffimiliter: symbola manu ministrorum tractari, ore fumentium accipi. Res vero à summo pontifice Christo ipso præberi, ac fide à nobis percipi. Similiter vero tribus propositio-nibus explicari potest: duabus negantibus una affirmante.
units.tr: This question is in dispute with the Papists and also with the ubiquitarians at the same time, because both want the things, present in the signs or under the species of the signs in a hidden and miraculous way, to be carried and handled by the hands of the ministers and put into the mouth of the communicants. We teach on the contrary that the things are indeed exhibited and received together with the symbols in the lawful use of the Supper, but in a different way: the symbols are handled by the hand of the ministers and received by the mouth of the communicants; the things, however, are offered by Christ himself, the highest pontiff, and received by us through faith. This can be explained similarly in three propositions: two negative and one affirmative.

units.la: PROPOSITIO I. Res signatæ, corpus & sanguis Domini, neque tractantur, neque exhibentur manu ministrorum in symbolis corporaliter percipienda.
units.tr: PROPOSITION I. The signified things, the body and blood of the Lord, are neither handled nor exhibited by the hand of ministers in the symbols to be received bodily.

units.la: Ratio 1. à toto sacramentorum genere negatiue: In nullo sacramento ministri manu tractant & conferunt res spirituales significatas. Ergo nec in cœna.
units.tr: Reason 1, from the whole genus of sacraments, negatively: In no sacrament do ministers handle with their hands and confer the spiritual things signified. Therefore neither in the Supper.

units.la: Antecedens probatur tum inductione quæ etiam aduersariorum confessione patet: tum ex analogia sacramentorum & verbi, Marc. 1. Ego vox[?] clamans, Ioh. 1. Ego baptizo aqua: qui post me venit, baptizabit vos spiritu sancto & igni. 1 Cor. 3.7. Neque qui rigat, neque qui plantat est aliquid, sed qui dat incrementum Deus. Ergo sic etiam in sacramentis, quæ sunt verbum visibile.
units.tr: The antecedent is proved both by induction, which is evident even from the admission of our opponents, and from the analogy of the sacraments and the Word: Mark 1. I am the voice crying, John 1. I baptize with water; he who comes after me will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire. 1 Cor. 3.7. Neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but God who gives the increase. Therefore likewise in the sacraments, which are the visible Word.

units.la: Ratio 2. Res signatæ non sunt IN, CUM, SUB symbolis præsentes corporaliter, ut est ostensum. Non ergo manu ministri tractantur vel distribuuntur.
units.tr: Reason 2. The signified things are not present bodily IN, WITH, UNDER the symbols, as has been shown. Therefore they are not handled or distributed by the hand of the minister.

units.la: Ratio 3. Res signatæ in cœna sunt spirituales, quæ in promissione gratiæ symbolis annexæ offeruntur. Promissio autem gratiæ non tractatur manibus, &c.
units.tr: Reason 3. The signified things in the Supper are spiritual, which are offered in the promise of grace annexed to the symbols. But the promise of grace is not handled with hands, etc.

units.la: Ratio 4. Testimonia patrum, vt Chrysost. sermone de euch. in encæn. Ne putetis accedentes ad hæc mysteria, quod accipiatis diuinum corpus ex homine: id est, ministro: & similia multa.
units.tr: Reason 4. The testimonies of the Fathers, as Chrysostom in his sermon on the Eucharist in the Encaenia: Do not think, as you approach these mysteries, that you receive the divine body from a man, that is, from a minister; and many similar things.

units.la: PROPOSITIO 11. Res signata corpus & sanguis Domini non percipiuntur cum, in, sub pane & vino, oraliter seu ore corporeo.
units.tr: PROPOSITION II. The signified thing, the body and blood of the Lord, is not received with, in, or under the bread and wine orally, or with the bodily mouth.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia non sunt cum, in, sub symbolis corporaliter præsentes, vt est ostensum, quæst. 1. propos. 2.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because they are not bodily present with, in, under the symbols, as has been shown, question 1, proposition 2.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia non ingrediuntur ventrem, qui destinatus est escis corporeis. 1. Corint. 6. 13. Omne autem, quod ingreditur in os, in ventrem cedit. Matth. 15.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because they do not enter the belly, which is destined for bodily food. 1 Cor. 6.13. Yet whatever enters the mouth passes into the belly. Matt. 15.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia promissio, in qua res offeruntur, non capitur ore.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because the promise, in which the things are offered, is not grasped by the mouth.

units.la: PROPOSITIO III. Res signata, corpus & sanguis Domini, percipiuntur fide, spiritualiter.
units.tr: PROPOSITION III. The signified things, the body and blood of the Lord, are received by faith, spiritually.

units.la: Ratio 1. à genere: quia in omnibus sacramentis res signatæ percipiuntur fide: qua sola vt iustificamur, ita omnia beneficia noui testamenti accipimus.
units.tr: Reason 1. From the genus: because in all sacraments the signified things are received by faith, which alone justifies us, and by which we receive all the benefits of the New Testament.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia promissio gratiæ non nisi fide percipitur: corporis vero & sanguinis Christi κοινωνία est promissio gratiæ. Vide volum. 1. Vrsini. pag. 103.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because the promise of grace is received only by faith; but the communion [κοινωνία] of the body and blood of Christ is a promise of grace. See Ursinus, vol. 1, p. 103.

units.la: Pro orali manducatione argumentum cuiusdam nobilis disputatoris.
units.tr: On behalf of oral manducation, the argument of a certain noble disputant.

units.la: Cuicunque instrumento conuenit manducatio snius rei in cœna Domini, eidem etiam alterius conueniat, oportet. Sed ori corporis manducatio snius, hoc est, panis in cœna conuenit. Ergo & alterius, hoc est, corporis Christi.
units.tr: If the manducation of one thing in the Supper of the Lord belongs to some instrument, it must also belong to another instrument. But the manducation of one thing, that is, of bread, belongs in the Supper to the mouth of the body. Therefore also of the other, that is, of the body of Christ.

units.la: Resp. Maior vera est de cibis physicè copulatis, aut sese continentibus, vt est artocreas. At non ita copulantur panis & corpus Christi. De his igitur falsa est.
units.tr: Answer: The major is true of foods that are physically joined or that contain themselves, as is artocreas [bread-and-meat pie]. But bread and the body of Christ are not so joined. Therefore the major is false in respect of these.

units.la: Probat ille maiorem. Quicunque panem & vinum, corpus & sanguinem Christi eidem manducationis vocabulo includit, is eodem etiam instrumento utraque sumi affirmat: Sed Christus panem & vinum, corpus & sanguinem suum eidem manducationis vocabulo includit. Ergo Christus utraque eodem etiam manducationis instrumento sumi affirmat.
units.tr: He proves the major: Whoever includes bread and wine, the body and blood of Christ, under the same word of manducation, affirms that both are taken by the same instrument. But Christ includes bread and wine, his body and blood, under the same word of manducation. Therefore Christ affirms that both are taken by the same instrument of manducation.

units.la: Resp. 1. Probatio maioris deficit, quia affirmans vniuerfalis concluenda erat in Barba ra.
units.tr: Answer 1. The proof of the major fails, because an affirmative universal was to be concluded in Barbara.

units.la: 2.Maior principium petit: & negatur. Falsitas patet ex Ioh.3.vbi Christus eodem nati uitatis vocabulo includit spiritum & carnem : nec tamen sequitur, eodem modo vel instrumento vtrumque nasci.
units.tr: 2. The major begs the question, and is denied. The falsehood is evident from John 3, where Christ includes spirit and flesh under the same word of birth; yet it does not follow that both are born in the same way or by the same instrument.

units.la: 3.Etiam minor est falsa. Verbum enim manducare, ad panem sacrum,non ad corpus refertur,nisi ex consequenti.Proprie enim ad id pertinet, quod Dominus manibus accepit & fregit:quod erat panis:non corpus eius. Ratio notatu digna haec est,quia secundum papistas & simplices consubstantiatores , corpus Christi ante pronunciata verba consecrationis,quae vocant,nondum adest,sed in vlti-mo prolationis instanti: Hoc est enim corpus meum,adesse incipit.Secundum vbiquitarios vero,qui sunt quasi chymici consubstantiatores,adest quidem,vt in quovis pane, sed nondum est manducabile : nisi post consecrationem. Non ergo iussit Christus & ore manducare in pane,quod in pane nondum fuit,vel manducabile fuit.
units.tr: 3. The minor is also false. For the verb to eat, as applied to the sacred bread, refers to the bread, not to the body, except by consequence. For properly it pertains to that which the Lord took in his hands and broke, which was bread, not his body. This is a remarkable point, because according to the Papists and the simple consubstantiators, the body of Christ is not yet present before the pronouncing of the words of consecration, as they call them, but begins to be present at the last instant of the utterance: This is my body. According to the ubiquitarians, who are as it were chemical consubstantiators, it is indeed present, as in any bread, but it is not yet eatable until after the consecration. Therefore Christ did not command that what was not yet in the bread, or was not yet eatable, be eaten orally in the bread.

units.la: Rursus probat maiore profyllogismi:Vocabulum unam habens significationem, in una est accipiendum. Maduca-tio tā de pane, quàm de corpore Christi unā habet significationem: nempe oralem. Ergo in una de utroq. est accipienda.
units.tr: Again, he proves the major by a prosyllogism: A word having one meaning is to be understood in one sense. Manducation, both of bread and of the body of Christ, has one meaning: namely oral. Therefore it is to be understood in one sense of both.

units.la: Resp. Rursus deficit probatio maioris' universalis affirmantis, quae erat concludenda in Barbara. 2. minor est petitio principii.
units.tr: Answer. Again the proof of the major, an universal affirmative which was to be concluded in Barbara, fails; the minor is a begging of the question.

units.la: TERTIA QUAESTIO. Quibus res offerantur, & à quibus percipiantur?
units.tr: THIRD QUESTION. To whom are the things offered, and by whom are they received?

units.la: Ad hanc duabus propositionibus respondetur, utraque affirmante.
units.tr: This is answered by two propositions, both affirmative.

units.la: PROPOSITIO I. Res signata à solis fidelibus percipiuntur.
units.tr: PROPOSITION I. The signified thing is received by the faithful alone.

units.la: Ratio 1. Quia soli credentes fide promissionem accipiunt.
units.tr: Reason 1. Because only believers receive the promise by faith.

units.la: Ratio 2. Quia soli credentes habent Spiritum Christi, à quo caro eius vivifica non potest separari.
units.tr: Reason 2. Because only believers have the Spirit of Christ, from whom his life-giving flesh cannot be separated.

units.la: Ratio 3. Quia in solis credentibus Christus manet, & ipsi in Christo, Ephes.3.17.
units.tr: Reason 3. Because Christ abides in believers alone, and they in Christ, Eph. 3.17.

units.la: Ratio 4. Quia soli credentes percipiunt, & habent vitam, Ioh.3.&6.
units.tr: Reason 4. Because only believers partake and have life, John 3 and 6.

units.la: Propositio II. Impij sine fide accedentes symbola sine rebus percipiunt.
units.tr: Proposition II. The impious, approaching without faith, receive the signs without the things.

units.la: Rationes vide Expli cat.catech.pag.515.
units.tr: For the reasons, see Explicatio catechetica, p. 515.

units.la: Obiectiones pro impiorum manducatione, vide ibid. pag.517.
units.tr: For the objections in favour of the eating of the wicked, see ibid., p. 517.

units.la: VII. COMPENDIOSA EXPLICATIO TOTIVS DE COENA DOMINI CONTROVERSIAE inter Synusiastas & orthodoxos.
units.tr: VII. A CONCISE EXPLANATION OF THE WHOLE CONTROVERSY ABOUT THE LORD'S SUPPER between the Synusiastae and the orthodox.

units.la: Capita Explicationis.
units.tr: Heads of the Explanation.

units.la: 1. Quos errores Synusiastae nobis impingant?
units.tr: 1. What errors do the Synusiastae charge against us?

units.la: 2. Synusiastarum argumenta contra nostram de coena doctrinam.
units.tr: 2. The arguments of the Synusiastae against our doctrine of the Supper.

units.la: 3. Synusiastarum effugia, et quasdam nostras obiectiones eludant.
units.tr: 3. The evasions of the Synusiastae, and their refutation of some of our objections.

units.la: 4. Argumenta contrapraesentiae et manducationem oralem corporis Christi, in, cum, sub pane.
units.tr: 4. Arguments against the presence and oral eating of the body of Christ in, with, and under the bread.

units.la: 5. Argumenta, quibus dogma of bisquistarum refellitur, et sana doctrina veritas confirmatur.
units.tr: 5. Arguments by which the dogma of the bisquistae is refuted and sound doctrine and truth are confirmed.

units.la: I. Errores quos Synusiastae falso nobis impingunt, cum refutatione.
units.tr: I. The errors which the Synusiastae falsely charge upon us, with refutation.

units.la: In doctrina de coena Domini duo (inquiunt Synusiastae) extrema sunt citanda: siquidem omnis virtus et veritas consistit inter duo extrema. Unum est pontificiorum, alterum sacramentariorum: et apparet hoc ex quadruplici. Pontificiorum errores sunt: 1. Transubstantiatio. 2. ἐμπλα-σία. 3. sacrificium missae. 4. mutilatio sacramenti.
units.tr: In the doctrine of the Lord's Supper, the Synusiastae say, two extremes must be cited, since all virtue and truth consist between two extremes. One is that of the Papists, the other that of the sacramentarians; and this appears from a fourfold consideration. The errors of the Papists are: (1) transubstantiation; (2) [the eating of the body of Christ]; (3) the sacrifice of the mass; (4) the mutilation of the sacrament.

units.la: Resp. Papistarum errores notant quidem, sed non possunt refutare: quia ipsorum sententia cum papistarum opinione magis consentit, quam nostra.
units.tr: Reply: They do indeed note the errors of the Papists, but they cannot refute them, because their own opinion agrees more closely with the opinion of the Papists than ours does.

units.la: Nam 1. etsi non docent transubstantiationem: docent tamen consubstantiationem, de qua ipsa nihil in verbo Dei docetur.
units.tr: For, (1) although they do not teach transubstantiation, they do teach consubstantiation, about which nothing is taught in the Word of God.

units.la: 2. Cū docent corporale Christi praesentiam: necesse est, ut Christū, quem in, sub, cum, ad panē corporaliter adesse statuunt, etiam in pane adorent: quod aequē est idololatricū, ac si ipsum panem adorent. Ubicunque enim Christus est, sive visibili sive invisibili modo, ibi est adorandus.
units.tr: (2) Since they teach a corporeal presence of Christ, they must necessarily adore Christ, whom they hold to be bodily present in, under, with, or at the bread, also in the bread; and this is no less idolatrous than if they adored the bread itself. For wherever Christ is, whether in a visible or an invisible manner, there he is to be adored.

units.la: 3. Sacrificium missae stabiliunt, quia ut iam dictum est, dū Christum tenentur ad panem adorare: coguntur a Deo petere, ut sua peccata remittantur, propter illum Christum, quem in manibus habent: quod nihil aliud est, nisi pontificia Christi oblatio.
units.tr: (3) They establish the sacrifice of the mass, because, as has already been said, while they are bound to adore Christ in the bread, they are compelled to ask God that their sins be forgiven for the sake of that Christ whom they hold in their hands; which is nothing other than the Papist offering of Christ.

units.la: 4. Mutilationem sacramenti admittant necesse est, quo enim rei eius fundamento nituntur pontifici, id ipsi retinent. Nam cum statuant corporalem Christi praesentiam, in, cum, sub, vel ad panem: nec esse est, ut vel calicem accedentibus coenam negent, cum sanguis Christi in ipsius sit corpore: vel, quo nihil absurdius, sanguinem Christi ab eius corpore diuellunt.
units.tr: (4) They must admit the mutilation of the sacrament, for they retain the very foundation on which the Papists rest their case. For since they hold a corporeal presence of Christ in, with, under, or at the bread, it is necessary either that they deny the cup to those who approach the Supper, since the blood of Christ is in his body; or, which is nothing more absurd, that they tear the blood of Christ away from his body.

units.la: Nos in defectu non peccamus: sed verum medium tenemus. Docemus enim spiritualem praesentiam & participationem omnes nimirum fideles, qui panem & vinum edunt & bibunt, omnium Christi beneficiorum & ipsius Christi vere participes fieri, & ita ipsi uniri, ut caro fiunt de carne eius & os de ossibus eius. Ipsi vero, ut iam demonstratum est, cum papistis in excessu peccant.
units.tr: We do not sin by defect, but we hold the true middle way. For we teach a spiritual presence and participation: all faithful persons, namely, who eat and drink the bread and wine, become truly partakers of all the benefits of Christ and of Christ himself, and are so united to him that they become flesh of his flesh and bone of his bones. But they, as has already been shown, sin with the Papists by excess.

units.la: Sacramentariorum vero (inquiunt) errores sunt, 1. Esse tantum nuda signa & symbola. Resp. Docemus res significatas una cum signis in usu legitimo exhiberi & communicari, licet non corporaliter, sed eo modo qui sacramentis competit.
units.tr: The errors of the sacramentarians, however (they say), are: (1) that the elements are merely bare signs and symbols. Reply: We teach that the things signified are exhibited and communicated together with the signs in lawful use, although not corporeally, but in the manner which belongs to sacraments.

units.la: 2. Adesse Christum tantum modo secundum efficaciam. Resp. Docemus adesse & vniri nobis per Spir. S. etsi corpus eius longe a nobis absit, sicut & ministerio totus adest, licet aliter secundum alteram naturam.
units.tr: (2) That Christ is present only according to his efficacy. Reply: We teach that he is present and united to us through the Holy Spirit, even though his body is far from us, just as he is wholly present also in the ministry, although in a different way according to his other nature.

units.la: 3. Adesse corpus Christi ταυτικόν, τυπικόν, πνευματικόν, imaginarium figuratum, spirituale, non essentiale. Resp. De corpore τῶν nunquam fumus locuti, sed de vera Christi carne, quae nobis adest, etsi in coelis maneat. Deinde dicimus, nos accipere panem & corpus: sed vtrumque suo modo.
units.tr: (3) That the body of Christ is present tautikon, typikon, pneumatikon [identically, typically, spiritually]: figurative, imaginary, spiritual, not essential. Reply: We have never spoken of a body of this kind, but of the true flesh of Christ, which is present to us, although it remains in heaven. Next, we say that we receive the bread and the body, but each in its own way.

units.la: 4. Distribui Verum corpus Christi quod in cruce pependit, & verum sanguinem qui pro nobis effusus est, sed spiritualiter. Accipi a dignis solummodo: indignos nihil sumere praeter nuda signa ad iudicium. Resp. Concedimus totū, ut verbo Dei, naturae sacramentorum, analogiae fidei, & communioni cum Christo conueniens.
units.tr: (4) That the true body of Christ which hung on the cross, and the true blood which was poured out for us, are distributed, but spiritually; and that they are received only by the worthy, while the unworthy receive nothing but bare signs, to their judgment. Reply: We grant the whole of it, so far as it agrees with the Word of God, with the nature of the sacraments, with the analogy of faith, and with communion with Christ.

units.la: II. Synuasiastarum argumenta, quibus nostram de cœna Domini doctrinam euertere conantur, additis refutationibus.
units.tr: II. The arguments of the Synusiastae, by which they try to overturn our doctrine of the Lord's Supper, with refutations added.

units.la: Argument.1. Verba institutionis sunt perspicua & plana. Hoc est corpus meum. Hic est sanguis meus. RES. Citant ea verba contra seipsos. Dicunt enim, in sub, cum pane accipi realiter corpus Christi: cum Christus dicat, ipsum panem esse suum corpus. Duplici ergo iniuria afficiunt Ecclesiam. 1. Dum obtrudunt ei sua pro Christi verbis. 2. Dum putant eam non videre, quod diuersæ sint locutiones, in pane est corpus: & panis est corpus. Accusant etiam Christum mendacij: negant enim panem esse ipsius corpus, sed dicunt, corpus esse in pane. Videant igitur, quomodo in extremo iudicio de hac blasphemia & calumnia sint Christo responsuri. Papistæ magis retinent verba Christi, quam isti. Docent enim panem, ita esse corpus Christi, ut in illud mutetur. Isti vero τὸ ῥῆμα[?] non tenent, sed sequuntur δι-αιοῦσιν[?]. Videndum ergo, utri verum sequantur. Nostra probabitur in fine.
units.tr: Argument 1. The words of institution are clear and plain. This is my body. This is my blood. REPLY: They cite these words against themselves. For they say that the body of Christ is received really in, under, or with the bread, whereas Christ says that the bread itself is his body. They therefore wrong the Church in a twofold way: (1) by thrusting their own words upon her in place of the words of Christ; (2) by thinking that she does not see that the expressions differ, the body is in the bread and the bread is the body. They also accuse Christ of lying, for they deny that the bread is his body, but say that the body is in the bread. Let them see, then, how they will answer to Christ for this blasphemy and calumny at the last judgment. The Papists hold more firmly to the words of Christ than these men do. For they teach that the bread is so the body of Christ that it is changed into it. These men, however, do not keep the word [ῥῆμα], but follow their own interpretation [διαίουσιν]. We must consider, therefore, which of the two follows the truth. Ours will be proved at the end.

units.la: Inst. Additur declaratio: Quod pro vobis datur, & qui pro vobis effunditur. Resp. Est petitio principij. Sumút. n. pro confesso, panem proprie dici corpus, quod tamen est probandum. Sacramentalis enim est locutio. 2. Per innuer-sionem. Corpus Christi proprie dictum est pro nobis tra-ditū. Panis autem non est pro nobis traditus. Ergo, &c. Ita, sicut panis est corpus fractum, sic fractio panis est fractio corporis. Sed fractio panis improprie seu symbolice est fractio corporis Christi. Fractio enim corporis est eius crucifixio. Ergo panis fractus symbolice est corpus fractum.
units.tr: Objection. A declaration is added: which is given for you, and which is poured out for you. Reply. This is a begging of the question. For they take for granted that the bread is properly called the body, which nevertheless must be proved. For the expression is sacramental. 2. By inversion. The body of Christ properly so called was delivered for us. But the bread was not delivered for us. Therefore, etc. Thus, just as the bread is the broken body, so the breaking of the bread is the breaking of the body. But the breaking of the bread is improperly or symbolically the breaking of the body of Christ. For the breaking of the body is his crucifixion. Therefore the bread broken symbolically is the broken body.

units.la: Argum.2. Ab authore, qui est Verax: Resp. Est petitio principij, quia debent probare, quod Christus dixerit in, sub, cum pane esse corpus suum. Imo potest quis figurate loqui, & tamen perspicæ.
units.tr: Argument 2. From the author, who is truthful. Reply. This is a begging of the question, because they ought to prove that Christ said his body is in, under, or with the bread. Indeed, someone may speak figuratively and yet clearly.

units.la: Inst. Est etiam omnipotens. Ergo potest esse ubique & in pane. Resp. 1. Etsi posset facere ut duo contradictoria simul essent vera: tamen non vult. 2. Deus ne potest quidem contradictoria efficere, quia est verax. Velle autem contradictoria est mendacis. Non ergo negamus veritatem & omnipotentiam Dei, sed istorum mendacia: imo eam defendimus, dicentes Deum facere quae dixit. Ipsi vero eam oppugnant, statuentes in Deo voluntates contrarias. Inst. Christi corpus habet multas prerogativas, alienas a nostris corporibus. Vt quod nascitur ex Virgine, ambulat super mare, semel & simul fuit in sepulchro, inferno & paradiso: transfuit per ianuas clausas. Resp. Exempla haec partim sunt dissimilia, partim falsa. Dissimilia, quia possunt etiam in creaturam cadere, vt ambulare super aquas in Petrum: transire per ianuas clausas in spiritum.
units.tr: Objection. He is also almighty. Therefore he can be everywhere and in the bread. Reply. (1) Even if he could make two contradictories true at the same time, yet he does not will to do so. (2) God cannot even bring about contradictories, because he is truthful. But to will contradictories belongs to a liar. We therefore do not deny the truth and omnipotence of God, but the lies of these men; indeed, we defend God's truth, saying that God does what he has said. They, however, assail it, by positing contrary wills in God. Objection. The body of Christ has many prerogatives foreign to our bodies: that it was born of a virgin, walked upon the sea, was at once and at the same time in the tomb, in hell and in paradise, and passed through closed doors. Reply. These examples are partly unlike, partly false. Unlike, because they can also fall upon a creature: walking upon the waters belonged to Peter, passing through closed doors to a spirit.

units.la: 2. Quia implicant contradictionem. nam dum dicitur natus esse ex virgine, non simul dicitur non natus ex virgine. Sed simul finitum & infinitum esse, implicant contradictionem. Falsum est, quod transierit per ianuas clausas, cum ei cedere potuerint: item quod transierit per ostium sepulchri, cum dicatur id ab Angelo apertum: item quod Christi corpus simul & semel fuerit in pluribus locis, id ex Augustino sumsisse videntur. Sed is dixit corpus in sepulchro, animam in inferno, deitatem vbique fuisse.
units.tr: (2) Because they involve a contradiction. For when it is said that he was born of a virgin, it is not at the same time said that he was not born of a virgin. But to be at once finite and infinite involves a contradiction. It is false that he passed through closed doors, since they could yield to him; likewise that he passed through the opening of the tomb, since it is said to have been opened by an angel. Likewise, that the body of Christ was at once and at the same time in several places: they seem to have taken this from Augustine. But he said that the body was in the tomb, the soul in hell, and the deity everywhere.

units.la: Argu. 3. A circumstantia temporis: in ea nocte in qua traditus est. Nullus loquens serio loquitur figurate. Christus instituens coenam, est serio locutus. Ergo sine tropo. Resp. 1.
units.tr: Argument 3. From the circumstance of time: on the night in which he was betrayed. No one speaking seriously speaks figuratively. Christ, instituting the Supper, spoke seriously. Therefore without a trope. Reply 1.

units.la: Nego maiore: quia alioqui nullus loquens figurate loquetur serio, quod est salsissimum. Deus enim in omnib. sacramentis, etsi figurate, serio tamen loquitur. Desiderio de-sideravi[?] (inquit Christus) hoc pascha manducare vobiscum[?]. Ego vitis, vos palmites. Transeat a me calix iste. Si hoc fit in viridi ligno, quid fiet in arido? Citauit Psal. 22. & tamen serio, licet figurate omnia illa dixerit. 2. Resp. ad minorem.
units.tr: I deny the major premise: for otherwise no one speaking figuratively would speak seriously, which is most absurd. For God, in all sacraments, although figuratively, nevertheless speaks seriously. I have earnestly desired (says Christ) to eat this passover with you. I am the vine, you are the branches. Let this cup pass from me. If this is done in the green wood, what will be done in the dry? He cited Psalm 22, and yet he said all those things seriously, although figuratively. 2. Reply to the minor premise.

units.la: Non vtitur figuris iocosis aut obscuris. Haec figura est perspicua, quia trita, & discipuli sic loquuntur: Vbi vis paremus tibi pascha? Vsitata est in omnibus sacramentis. Emphatica est, quia exprimit similitudinem signi & significatae rei, & certitudinem coniunctionis eorum in vsu legitimo. 3. Per inuersionem, imo quia Christus serio locutus est, ideo vsus est figura rem bene declarante. Inst. Dixit: Hoc poculum est nouum Testamentum. Intestamentis loquuntur proprie. Christus hic instituit sacramentum. Ergo, &c. Resp. Nego maiorem, & inuerto: quia cum vellet instituere sacramentum, ipse figurate locutus est, vocans cœnam testamentum, quòd figuratè est accipiendum, 1. quia alioqui essent duo fœdera: alterum proprium, & alterum cœna. 2. alioqui excluderentur à fœdere Dei, qui non possent accedere ad cœnam, & omnes ea vtentes essent in fœdere.
units.tr: He does not use jocular or obscure figures. This figure is clear, because it is familiar, and the disciples speak in this way: "Where do you want us to prepare the Passover for you?" It is customary in all the sacraments. It is emphatic, because it expresses the likeness of the sign and the thing signified, and the certainty of their conjunction in lawful use. (3.) By inversion: indeed, because Christ spoke seriously, he therefore used a figure that declares the thing well. Objection: He said, "This cup is the New Testament." In testaments they speak properly. Christ here instituted a sacrament. Therefore, etc. Answer: I deny the major and invert it: because when he wished to institute a sacrament, he himself spoke figuratively, calling the supper a testament, which is to be taken figuratively, (1.) because otherwise there would be two covenants: one proper, and another the supper. (2.) Otherwise those who could not come to the supper would be excluded from the covenant of God, and all who used it would be in the covenant.

units.la: Obiect. In sanguine meo: Ergo in cœna est realis Christi sanguis, & ore bibitur. Resp. Per inuersionem: quia Nouum Testamentum initum est per sanguinem Christi in cruce fusum,& fide nobis applicatum:non ore haustum: Alioqui enim ab eo excluderentur, qui ad hoc sacramentum non possunt accedere.
units.tr: Objection: "In my blood." Therefore in the supper there is the real blood of Christ, and it is drunk with the mouth. Answer: By inversion: because the New Testament was entered into through the blood of Christ poured out on the cross, and applied to us by faith, not drunk with the mouth. Otherwise those who cannot come to this sacrament would be excluded from it.

units.la: Inst. Emphasis est in Vocabulo Nouû. Quod in Veteri Testamento fiebat typicè, ad in nouo fit realiter. Resp. Si addat: Ergo ore corporis: plus est in conclusione: quia nullus in Veteri Testamento fuit typus, qui oralem Christi manducationem significaret. 1. per inuersionem. Non aliter manducatur Christi corpus in Nouo Testamento, quàm in veteri. Sed in veteri manducabatur spiritualiter tantum. Ergo & in nouo.
units.tr: Objection: The emphasis is on the word "New." What was done typically in the Old Testament is done really in the New. Answer: If he adds, "Therefore with the mouth of the body": the conclusion goes further than the premise, because in the Old Testament there was no type signifying an oral eating of Christ (1. by inversion). The body of Christ is not eaten in the New Testament otherwise than in the Old. But in the Old it was eaten only spiritually. Therefore also in the New.

units.la: Inst. Nouum Testamentû distat à Veteri[?], quia in eo fuerunt typi, in nouo ipsum corpus. Heb. 9. Col. 2. Resp. 1. Nunquam est expressum in scriptura hoc veteris & noui Testamenti discrimen, quòd in veteri non oraliter, in nouo oraliter edatur Christus. In dictis Apostoli, quæ citant, corpus significat vmbratum Veteris Testameti per Christum factam esse impletionem: quia corpus illis vmbris ibi opponitur: item, quia dicit corpus esse Christi: quæ phrasis docet, à Christo factam esse typorum impletionem. 2. per concessionem. Etsi in nouo Testamento exhibitum habeamus Christum, & natus sit homo: tamen hinc idcirco non sequitur, corpus eius esse in pane: sed tantum esse in Nouo Testamento.
units.tr: Objection: The New Testament differs from the Old, because in the one there were types, in the other the body itself. Heb. 9; Col. 2. Answer (1.): It has never been expressed in Scripture that this distinction between the Old and New Testament is that in the one Christ is not eaten orally, while in the other he is eaten orally. In the words of the Apostle that they cite, "body" signifies that the shadow of the Old Testament has been fulfilled by Christ: because "body" is there set over against those shadows; and also because he says it is the body of Christ, which phrase teaches that the fulfilment of the types was accomplished by Christ. (2.) By concession: although we have Christ presented in the New Testament, and he was born a man, nevertheless it does not follow from this that his body is in the bread, but only that it is in the New Testament.

units.la: Argu.4. A consensu Euangelistarum & Pauli: Matthaeus, vt Theophylactus supputat, scripsit Euangelium Iuda[?] anno 8. post ascensionem. Marc. anno 10. Luc. 15. Paulus 20. & omnes [illegible, ~6 letters] eisdem verbis. Oratio sapius eisdem verbis prolata non est tropica. Talis est locutio de Cœna Domini, &c. Resp. Negatur maior, quia quàdo figura aliqua est illustris, nota, & emphatica, vt hæc, retinetur. Item Euangelistæ repetunt verba Christi, qui tropicè fuerat locutus. Sæpius illud, etsi tropicum repetitur: Baptizabit Spiritu sancto & igni. Ioh.1. Mat.3. Item ex fallacia à non causa: quia non ideo oratio aliqua repetitur, quòd figurata aut propria sit: sed vt auditorib. melius inculcetur. Deinde, negatur minor. 1. quia Matthæus & Marcus dicunt, Hic est sanguis novi Testamenti. Lucas dicit, hic calix est novum Testamentum in meo sanguine. 2. Matthæus & Marcus dicunt, hoc est corpus meum. Lucas & Paulus addunt: quod pro vobis traditur. Lucas dicit: quod pro vobis traditur. Paulus, quod pro vobis frangitur. Paulus dicit: Panis est κοινωνία corporis Christi.
units.tr: Argument 4: From the agreement of the Evangelists and Paul: Matthew, as Theophylact reckons, wrote his Gospel in the eighth year after the ascension; Mark in the tenth; Luke in the fifteenth; Paul in the twentieth; and all [illegible, about six letters] in the same words. A speech repeated often in the same words is not tropical. Such is the saying about the Lord's Supper, etc. Answer: The major is denied, because when some figure is famous, well known, and emphatic, as this one is, it is retained. Likewise the Evangelists repeat the words of Christ, who had spoken tropically. Often that saying, though tropical, is repeated: "He will baptize with the Holy Spirit and with fire." John 1; Matt. 3. Likewise it is a fallacy from a non-cause: for a speech is not repeated because it is figurative or proper, but so that it may be more effectively impressed on the hearers. Next, the minor is denied. (1.) Because Matthew and Mark say, "This is the blood of the New Testament." Luke says, "This cup is the New Testament in my blood." (2.) Matthew and Mark say, "This is my body." Luke and Paul add, "which is given for you." Luke says, "which is given for you." Paul, "which is broken for you." Paul says: the bread is the communion [κοινωνία] of the body of Christ.

units.la: Etsi autem hoc loco non agit ex professo de coena, ad ea tamen provocat. Inst. Est tamen eadem sententia. Res.
units.tr: Although indeed in this place he does not treat of the supper professedly, he nevertheless refers to those things. Objection: Nevertheless it is the same sense. Answer.

units.la: Iam non de verborum sententia, sed de verborum identitate quaeritur. Inst. 2. Nulla Vnquam fit mentio tropi. Ibi non fit mentio tropi. Ergo,&c. Resp. Negatur maior: quia ineptum esset, & viderentur homines ostentare suam artem, si dicerent se vtos esse egregia figura. Scriptura etiam sæpe loquitur tropicè, tamen non addit se tropicè loqui. Nego etiam minorem, quia tropi faciunt mentionem, dum eum declarant: quod constat 1. ex natura subiecti & praedicati: corpus natum est ex virgine, cru-cifixum, &c. panis est e farina mixtus. 2. Iubet hoc fieri in sui memoriam: ergo panis dicitur corpus, sicut memoriale. 3. Matthæus & Marcus dicunt: Hoc est sanguis novi Testamenti. Paulus & Lucas: Hoc est novum Testamentum in meo sanguine. Novū autē testamentū est obligatio Dei ad recipiendos credentes & respiscentes in gratiam, & horum ad fidem & obedientiam ipsi praestandam. 4. Paulus dicit, panem esse κοινωνίας corporis Christi, quae non est oralis manducatio, 1. quia fideles ea sunt unum corpus in Christo. 2. confert eam cum κοινωνία altaris in Veteri Te-stamento, quae non erat corporalis. 3. Quia solis fideli-bus, nō impiis potest competere. 4. Iohannes communionem eam declarat per remissionem peccatorum. Si in luce ambulamus, communionem habemus cum eo & sanguis Iesu Christi filij Dei purgat nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: Now the question is not about the sense of the words, but about the identity of the words. Objection 2: There is never any mention of a trope. There is no mention of a trope there. Therefore, etc. Answer: The major is denied, because it would be absurd, and men would seem to show off their skill, if they said they had used an excellent figure. Scripture also often speaks tropically, yet does not add that it speaks tropically. I deny the minor too, because tropes do make mention of themselves, while they declare the thing; which is clear (1.) from the nature of subject and predicate: the body was born of a virgin, crucified, etc.; bread is mixed from flour. (2.) He commands this to be done in his memory: therefore the bread is called the body, as a memorial. (3.) Matthew and Mark say: "This is the blood of the New Testament." Paul and Luke: "This is the New Testament in my blood." Now the New Testament is the obligation of God to receive believers and the repentant into grace, and of these to render to him faith and obedience. (4.) Paul says the bread is the communion [κοινωνία] of the body of Christ, which is not an oral eating: (1.) because the faithful are, by it, one body in Christ; (2.) he compares it with the communion [κοινωνία] of the altar in the Old Testament, which was not bodily; (3.) because it can belong only to the faithful, not to the impious; (4.) John declares that communion to be the remission of sins: "If we walk in the light, we have communion with him, and the blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cleanses us from all sin."

units.la: Imo Paulus ponit tria vocabula, quae sunt tres demonstrationes: 1. κοινωνία. Resp. Sed hæc communio est vnio cum Christo, & fruitio omnium eius beneficiorum per fidem. Huc pertinet similitudo corporis & membrorum, vitis & palmitum, quibus nihil cum manducatione corporali. Hæc communio omnibus piis fuit &, est communis à condito orbe, ad eius finem. Illi autem non potuerunt oraliter edere: Vt crescamus in eo, ex quo totum corpus coagmentatur. Qui adhæret Domino, est unus spiritus cum eo. Et omnes per unum spiritum baptizati sumus in unum corpus. Per hoc cognoscimus nos in eo habitare, et ipsum in nobis, quod de spiritu suo dedit nobis. Hæc igitur unio est κοινωνία, quæ fit per spiritum sanctum. Ergo spiritualis. Panis enim non potest esse hæc κοινωνία, nisi μετοχῆς[?].
units.tr: Indeed Paul sets down three words, which are three demonstrations: (1.) κοινωνία. Answer: But this communion is union with Christ, and the enjoyment of all his benefits through faith. To this belong the likeness of the body and the members, the vine and the branches, with which bodily eating has nothing to do. This communion has been common to all the pious from the foundation of the world to its end. But those men could not eat it orally. "That we may grow up into him, from whom the whole body is joined together." "He who cleaves to the Lord is one spirit with him." "And we have all been baptized by one Spirit into one body." "By this we know that we dwell in him, and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit." This union, therefore, is κοινωνία, which takes place through the Holy Spirit. Therefore it is spiritual. For bread cannot be this κοινωνία, except by participation [μετοχῆς].

units.la: 2. Qui sit reus corporis Christi, illud edit. Indignè sumentes, fiunt rei corporis Christi. Ergo illud corporaliter edunt. Spiritualiter enim non possunt: nā si sic ederent, non fierent rei.
units.tr: (2.) Whoever is guilty of the body of Christ eats it. Those who eat unworthily become guilty of the body of Christ. Therefore they eat it bodily. For they cannot eat it spiritually: for if they ate it so, they would not become guilty.

units.la: RES. Nego maiorem. Is enim reus est corporis Christi, qui suis peccatis illud in crucem agit, & Christi beneficium spernit. Ad reatum autem non est opus orali manducatione, sed Christum oblatum nolle fide recipere. Sic iniuria illata arcæ, illata dicitur Iehouæ.
units.tr: ANSWER: I deny the major. For he is guilty of the body of Christ who, by his sins, crucifies it again and despises the benefit of Christ. Guilt, however, does not require oral eating, but refusing to receive Christ offered in faith. So an injury done to the ark is said to be done to Jehovah.

units.la: 3. Non diiudicans corpus Domini. Qui non discernunt corpus Domini, illud comedunt. Rei non discernunt. Ergo, &c.
units.tr: (3.) Not discerning the body of the Lord. Those who do not discern the body of the Lord eat it. The guilty do not discern. Therefore, etc.

units.la: RES. Per concessionē si maior sacramentaliter sumatur, videlicet, de pane, qui corpus Christi nominatur, vera est: sin proprie, falsa. Nam non discernere, est non afficere honore ipsi debito, contemnere, & rem significatam non accipere. Sic Heb.10.v.29. Filium Dei conculcare, & sanguinem fœderis communem ducere dicuntur, qui eum contemnunt.
units.tr: ANSWER: By concession, if the major is taken sacramentally, namely, of the bread, which is called the body of Christ, it is true; but if taken properly, it is false. For not to discern is not to regard with the honour due to it, to despise, and not to receive the thing signified. So in Heb. 10:29, those who despise the Son of God are said to trample him underfoot and to count the blood of the covenant a common thing.

units.la: Argumentum V. A testimoniis patrum, &c. pia[?] antiquitatis in puriore ecclesia.
units.tr: Argument V. From the testimonies of the Fathers, etc., of the purer antiquity of the Church.

units.la: RES. Patrum dicta sunt sacramentaliter vel de communione spirituali accipienda. Dicunt sæpe, cum pane & vino dari nobis corpus & sanguinem Domini. Ergo si statuunt corporalem præsentiam, statuat etiam vel concomitantiam papisticam, vel diuisionem sanguinis à corpore.
units.tr: REPLY. The sayings of the Fathers must be taken sacramentally, or of spiritual communion. They often say that the body and blood of the Lord are given to us with the bread and wine. Therefore, if they posit a corporal presence, let them also posit the Papists' concomitance, or a division of the blood from the body.

units.la: Augustinus dicit: Hoc accipis in pane, quod pependit in cruce: hoc in calice, quod de Christi latere effusum est. Resp. In pane tanquam symbolo, id est, cum symbolo simul accipi rem significatam. Accipientes panem, certi sumus Christum habere.
units.tr: Augustine says: What you receive in the bread is what hung on the cross; what you receive in the cup is what flowed out from the side of Christ. Reply. In the bread as in a symbol, that is, the thing signified is received together with the symbol. Receiving the bread, we are sure that we have Christ.

units.la: Cyrillus super Iohannem inquit: naturali participatione, non tantum spiritualiter, sed etiam corporaliter: non tantum secundum spiritum, sed etiam secundum carnem: corporaliter & essentialiter.Resp. Cyrillus non loquitur de modo edendi, sed de re edenda. Docet non tantum spiritus, sed etiam humanae Christi naturae nos fieri participes. Intelligit autem spiritualem κοινωνικῶς[?]. 1.Quia de ea citat locos. Iohan.6.54.& 1.Cor.6.15.vbi nulla fit mentio corporalis manducationis. 2. Loquitur de praesentia Christi non in pane, sed in nobis. 3. Hanc mansionem Christi probat ex usu coenae, non ex corporali manducatione. 4. Ita eam describit, ut dicat duraturam esse in vita aeterna. 5. Loquitur de communione, quae est sanctorum propria. Haec autem spiritualis est, alioqui enim etiam impiis contingeret.
units.tr: Cyril, on John, says: by natural participation, not only spiritually but also corporally; not only according to the Spirit but also according to the flesh; corporally and essentially. Reply. Cyril is not speaking of the manner of eating but of the thing to be eaten. He teaches that we are made partakers not only of the Spirit but also of the human nature of Christ. He understands, however, a spiritual [participation] (koinōnikōs). (1) Because he cites passages on it: John 6:54 and 1 Cor. 6:15, where there is no mention of corporal eating. (2) He speaks of the presence of Christ not in the bread but in us. (3) He proves this indwelling of Christ from the use of the Supper, not from corporal eating. (4) He describes it in such a way that he says it will endure into eternal life. (5) He speaks of the communion which is proper to the saints. But this is spiritual; otherwise it would also happen to the impious.

units.la: III. Effugia Synusiastarum, ut quasdam nostras (non omnes, plures etenim illis opponuntur) obiectiones eludant.
units.tr: III. The evasions of the Synusiastae, by which they elude some of our objections (not all, for more are opposed to them).

units.la: 1.Non statuimus (inquiunt) physicam & Capernaitica manducationem.Resp. Hoc eis non obiicimus, sed tantum quaerimus, an Christus oraliter manducetur, sive crasso, sive subtili modo. Ut ut respondeant, in ipsa eorum opinione plus satis est idololatriae. Christus enim refutas Capernaitas, non distinguit sui manducationem in crassum & subtilem modum, sed simpliciter dicit, non posse suum corpus edi ore corporis. Dicit enim se ascensurum: & verba quae loquitur esse spiritum & vitam.
units.tr: 1. We do not posit (they say) a physical and Capernaitic eating. Reply. We do not object this to them, but only ask whether Christ is eaten orally, whether in a gross or in a subtle manner. However they answer, in their own opinion there is more than enough idolatry. For Christ, refuting the Capernaites, does not distinguish his eating into a gross and a subtle manner, but simply says that his body cannot be eaten with the mouth of the body. For he says that he will ascend, and that the words he speaks are spirit and life.

units.la: II.Ubiquitatem non asserimus: De ea enim non exstat verbum. Resp. Notanda hic est adversariorum de Ubi-quitate dissensio. Sed neque de eo exstat verbum, quod corpus Christi sit simul pluribus in locis. Nam solius divinae naturae est, tota simul esse in pluribus locis. Deinde ex hac ipsorum opinione sequitur ubiquitas. Nam qui simul & semel est pluribus in locis, necesse est, ut sit infinitus, ac proinde, ac proinde sit ubique.
units.tr: II. We do not assert ubiquity: for there is no word about it in Scripture. Reply. The disagreement of our opponents about ubiquity is to be noted here. But there is no word in Scripture that the body of Christ is in several places at once. For it belongs to the divine nature alone to be whole at once in several places. Moreover, from this their own opinion, ubiquity follows. For whoever is in several places at once and at the same time must be infinite, and therefore must be everywhere.

units.la: III.Non tollimus articulum de ascensione.Resp. Imo in eum impingunt. Etenim dum statuunt, quoties celebratur coena, Christum corporaliter edi: necesse est dicant, eum invisibiliter in terris mas[?]isse: (Atqui dicitur reliqui-sse mundum, ascendisse de loco inferiore in superio-rem, mansurus in coelo, donec veniat ad iudicium) vel descendere de coelo, quoties administratur coena: quod iam est refutatum. Quomodo igitur est in pane?
units.tr: III. We do not remove the article on the ascension. Reply. Indeed they strike against it. For while they maintain that, whenever the Supper is celebrated, Christ is eaten corporally, they must say either that he has remained invisibly on earth (yet it is said that he left the world, ascended from a lower place to a higher, and will remain in heaven until he comes to judgment), or that he descends from heaven whenever the Supper is administered, which has already been refuted. How then is he in the bread?

units.la: IV. Non tollimus doctrinā de proprietatibus humanā na-tura. Resp. Omnino tollunt. Volunt enim humanam naturam talem esse, quae non videatur, nec palpetur, nec sit circumscripta.
units.tr: IV. We do not remove the doctrine of the properties of the human nature. Reply. They remove it altogether. For they want the human nature to be such that it is not seen, nor touched, nor circumscribed.

units.la: Inst. Atqui Christus deposuit istas infirmitates, proprie-tates essentiales retinuit. Resp. Imo hæ sunt essentiales proprietates, quibus sublatis tollitur veritas naturæ hu-manæ. Augustinus: Tolle spatia corporibus & nusquam erunt.
units.tr: Objection. Yet Christ laid aside those infirmities; he retained the essential properties. Reply. Indeed these are the essential properties, and with them removed the truth of the human nature is taken away. Augustine: Take away space from bodies and they will be nowhere.

units.la: V. Non abolemus doctrinam de communicatione proprie-tatum. Resp. Imo in eam impingunt. Proprietates enim naturæ divinæ de tota persona in concreto dictæ, ipsi ad utramque naturam applicant: Ergo Vobiscum Usque ad consummationem seculi: accipiunt de utraq. natura: quod perinde est, ac si dictum, Christus est circumcisus, ita acci-perem: Christus deitate & carne est circumcisus.
units.tr: V. We do not abolish the doctrine of the communication of properties. Reply. Indeed they strike against it.
