Neque immutabilis Dei prouidentia, vsum doctrinæ, & studium nostrum rectè faciendi tollit, quasi hæc essent inania: siquidem nec posita prima causa, oportet remoueri secundas, nec primam, positis secundis. Et Deus non sine his mediis, sed per illa efficturum se nobis salutaria promisit, iisque nos vti iussit, profectum eorum ab ipso exspectantes.
units.tr: XVI. Nor does the unchangeable providence of God take away the use of doctrine and our zeal for acting rightly, as if these were in vain; for just as, when the first cause is posited, the secondary causes need not be removed, so also, when the secondary causes are posited, the first cause need not be. Nor did God promise that he would effect what is salutary for us without these means, but through them, and he has commanded us to use them, expecting their progress from him.

units.la: XVII. Cùm autem Deus negatur in scriptura velle actiones diabolorum aut hominum peccatiū[?],id intelligendum est, quatenus peccata sunt,siue eo fine,quo ab hominib.aut diabolis fiunt:nō autē quatenus actiones sunt, aut quatenus fiunt eo fine,quę Deus in ordine suę prouidetię spectat. Fines enim faciunt actionum discrimina.
units.tr: XVII. But when it is denied in Scripture that God wills the actions of devils or of sinning men, this is to be understood insofar as they are sins, either with the end for which they are done by men or devils, but not insofar as they are actions, or insofar as they are done with the end which God regards in the order of his providence. For the ends make the distinctions of actions.

units.la: XVIII. Haec doctrina in ecclesia propter gloriam Dei retinenda est, vt videlicet constet Deũ esse omniũ rerũ gubernatore, nec tamen peccati authore, sed liberrimum atque optimum bonorũ omniũ effectorem & datorem.
units.tr: XVIII. This doctrine must be retained in the Church for the glory of God, so that it is clear that God is the governor of all things, and yet not the author of sin, but the most free and best maker and giver of all good things.

units.la: XIX. Necessaria est etiā ad doctrinā & consolatione nostrā, vt grati simus Deo tanquam bonorum omnium fontis: mala, vt quæ ipsius voluntate nobis eueniunt, patiêter [?] feramus, certi simus, omnia nostræ saluti seruitura: poenarum authore Deum agnoscentes, emendemur, non desperemus de auxilio diuino, etiamsi nos causæ secundæ destituat: nō fidamus nobis ipsis, sed bona omnia in timore Dei ab ipso petamus: sciamus ecclesiā precipuè Deo curæ esse: nō temere de operibus & consiliis Dei iudicemus: propter dona nobis gratuita bonitate à Deo concessa, ne contemnamus alios: voluntatem & ordinem nobis à Deo præscriptum vbique sequamur.
units.tr: XIX. It is also necessary for our teaching and consolation: that we be thankful to God as the fount of all good things; that we bear evils, which come to us by his will, patiently; that we be certain that all things will serve our salvation; that, recognising God as the author of punishments, we amend ourselves; that we do not despair of divine help, even if secondary causes fail us; that we do not trust in ourselves, but seek all good things from him in the fear of God; that we know the Church is above all under God's care; that we do not rashly judge the works and counsels of God; that, on account of the gifts freely granted to us by God's goodness, we do not despise others; and that we follow everywhere the will and order prescribed to us by God.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: De prouidentia Dei.
units.tr: Concerning the providence of God.

units.la: I. Non tantum doctrina prophetica & apostolica, sed etiam testimonia de Deo in rerum natura lucentia confirmant, mundum conseruari & regi Dei prouidentia, nimirum, ordo in præcipuis naturæ partibus: Mens humana reges actiones hominum sua prouidentia: Lex naturæ, indita hominibus, vt sit regula vitæ: præmia & pœnæ: Conscientia: ordo politicus, Motus & virtutes heroicæ: prædictiones futurorum euentuū: Fines ad quos res sunt ordinatæ: ac denique ipsa Dei omnipotentis, sapientissimi, iustissimi, atque optimi natura.
units.tr: I. Not only prophetic and apostolic teaching, but also the testimonies about God shining forth in the nature of things, confirm that the world is preserved and governed by the providence of God: namely, the order in the chief parts of nature; the human mind, which governs the actions of men by its providence; the law of nature, implanted in men so as to be the rule of life; rewards and punishments; conscience; political order; movements and heroic virtues; predictions of future events; the ends to which things have been ordained; and finally the very nature of God, almighty, most wise, most just and best.

units.la: II. Docet autem sacra scriptura, Dei prouidentiam esse consilium Dei æternum, liberrimum, immutabile, sapientissimum & iustissimum, secundũ quod Deus bona omnia in omnibus creaturis efficit, peccata autem fieri permittit, & bona ac mala vniuersa ad suam gloriam & electorum salutem dirigit.
units.tr: II. Sacred Scripture teaches, moreover, that the providence of God is the eternal, most free, immutable, most wise and most just counsel of God, according to which God brings about all good things in all creatures, permits sins to occur, and directs all good and evil things to his own glory and the salvation of the elect.

units.la: III. Sic igitur sentiens & docens ecclesia de prouidentia Dei, prorsus damnat & detestatur furores Epicureorum & Academicorum, & aliorum figmenta, qui Dei nullam, vel non omnium rerum in mundo prouidentiam, vel notitiam tantum in Deo, ac non etiam decretum diuinum, & eius exsecutionem, eam esse volunt.
units.tr: III. Thus the Church, thinking and teaching so about the providence of God, utterly condemns and detests the frenzies of the Epicureans and Academics, and the fictions of others, who want God to have no providence over all things in the world, or only a knowledge in God, and not also a divine decree and its execution.

units.la: I v. Nec minus etiam repugnat blasphemiis & erroribus Manichæorum, Stoicorum, Libertinorum & aliorum, qui Deum fingunt peccati authorem, aut libertatem, qua ab æterno sua decreta fecit, ipsi adimunt, aut operationes atque usum, vel discrimina causarum secundarum, necessario vel contingenter, vel voluntarie & libere agentium tollunt.
units.tr: IV. Nor does it less oppose the blasphemies and errors of the Manichaeans, Stoics, Libertines and others, who feign that God is the author of sin, or who take away from him the freedom by which he made his decrees from eternity, or who abolish the operations and use, or the distinctions, of secondary causes acting by necessity, by chance, or voluntarily and freely.

units.la: v. Causæ, propter quas in Ecclesia exstare ac defendi hanc de providentia doctrinâ necesse est, gravissimæ sunt, vt videlicet, Deo sua gloria, & nobis consolatio solida con-stet, atque in timore & invocatione Dei contineamur.
units.tr: V. The reasons why it is necessary that this doctrine of providence be upheld and defended in the Church are most weighty: namely, that the glory of God and our solid consolation may stand firm, and that we may be kept in the fear and invocation of God.

units.la: XI. De peccato.
units.tr: XI. On sin.

units.la: I. Sola ecclesiæ doctrina integrè ostendit naturam, causas & effectus peccati.
units.tr: I. Only the teaching of the Church sets out fully the nature, causes and effects of sin.

units.la: II. Peccatum est, quicquid cum lege divina pugnat, hoc est, defectus vel inclinatio, vel actio contra legem Dei, offendens Deum & peccantem faciens reum pœnarum temporalium & æternarum, nisi fiat remissio propter filium Dei mediatorem.
units.tr: II. Sin is whatever conflicts with the divine law: that is, a defect, or an inclination, or an action against the law of God, which offends God and makes the sinner liable to punishments, temporal and eternal, unless remission is granted on account of God's Son as Mediator.

units.la: III. Omne peccatum aut originale aut actuale est.
units.tr: III. Every sin is either original or actual.

units.la: IV. Peccatum originale est reatus totius generis humani propter lapsum primorum parentum, & privatio agnitionis Dei, voluntatis divinæ in mente, & inclinationis ad obediendum Deo in voluntate & corde, & in his inclinatio ad repugnandum legi divinæ, secuta lapsum primorum parentum, & ab illis deriuata in omnes posteros, ac totam eorum naturam sic depravans, vt omnes propter hanc prauitate rei sint æternæ iræ Dei, neq. Deo placés facere quicquā possint, nisi fiat remissio propter filium Dei mediatorem, & renouatio naturæ per spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: IV. Original sin is the guilt of the whole human race on account of the fall of our first parents, and the privation of the knowledge of God in the mind, of the divine will, and of the inclination to obey God in the will and heart; and in these, the inclination to resist the divine law, which followed the fall of our first parents and is derived from them into all their posterity, so depraving their whole nature that, on account of this depravity, all are liable to the eternal wrath of God, and can do nothing pleasing to God unless remission is granted on account of God's Son as Mediator, and nature is renewed by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: V. Actuale peccatum est omnis actio in mente, voluntate aut corde, aut in membris externis, aberrans à lege divina, aut omissio eorum, quæ lex Dei iubet facere.
units.tr: V. Actual sin is every action in the mind, will or heart, or in the external members, that strays from the divine law, or the omission of those things which the law of God commands to be done.

units.la: VI. Omne peccatum est aut regnans, aut non regnans, quod aliqui dixerunt mortale aut veniale.
units.tr: VI. Every sin is either reigning or non-reigning; some have called these mortal or venial.

units.la: VII. Peccatum regnans est, cui peccans non repugnat per gratiam spiritus sancti, regenerantis enim ad vitam æternam, ideoque est obnoxius morti æternæ, nisi pœnitentiam agat & veniam per Christum consequatur.
units.tr: VII. Reigning sin is that to which the sinner does not resist through the grace of the Holy Spirit, who regenerates him to eternal life; and therefore he is liable to eternal death, unless he repents and obtains pardon through Christ.

units.la: viii. Peccatu non regnans est, cui peccans repugnat per gratiam spiritus sancti, regenerantis eum ad vitam aeternam, ideoque non est obnoxius morti aeternae: quia poenitentiam agit, & veniam per Christum consequitur.
units.tr: VIII. Non-reigning sin is that to which the sinner resists through the grace of the Holy Spirit, who regenerates him to eternal life; and therefore he is not liable to eternal death, because he repents and obtains pardon through Christ.

units.la: ix. Omne peccatum sua natura est mortale, hoc est, mortem aeternam meretur: fit autem veniale, id est, non accersit mortem aeternam in renato, ex gratia propter Christum.
units.tr: IX. Every sin is by its nature mortal, that is, it deserves eternal death; but it becomes venial, that is, it does not bring eternal death upon the regenerate, by grace on account of Christ.

units.la: x. Omne peccatum aut est contra conscientiam, aut non contra conscientiam.
units.tr: X. Every sin is either against conscience, or not against conscience.

units.la: xi. Peccatum contra conscientiam est, cum sciens Dei voluntatem, ex proposito contra eam facit.
units.tr: XI. Sin against conscience is when a person, knowing the will of God, acts against it deliberately.

units.la: xii. Peccatum non contra conscientiam est, quod velab i-gnorante voluntatem Dei committitur, vel peccatum quidem esse agnoscitur & deploratur a peccante, sed tamen vitari non potest perfecte in hac vita, ut peccatum originale & multa peccata ignorantiae & infirmitatis.
units.tr: XII. Sin not against conscience is what is committed by one ignorant of the will of God, or what is indeed recognised and deplored by the sinner as sin, but cannot be perfectly avoided in this life, such as original sin and many sins of ignorance and weakness.

units.la: xiii. Omne peccatum aut est irremissibile sive in spiritum sanctum, aut est remissibile sive non in spiritu sanctu.
units.tr: XIII. Every sin is either unforgivable, that is, against the Holy Spirit, or forgivable, that is, not against the Holy Spirit.

units.la: xiv. Peccatum irremissibile sive in spiritum sanctum est, oppugnatio aut abiectio veritatis divinae, destinato consilio facta, postquam de veritate testimonio spiritus sancti mens edocta & confirmata est: quod peccatum qui committunt caecitate a Deo puniuntur, ita ut nunquam resipiscant, ac proinde nec remissionem consequantur.
units.tr: XIV. The unforgivable sin, that is, against the Holy Spirit, is the assault upon or rejection of divine truth, done with settled purpose, after the mind has been taught and confirmed concerning the truth by the testimony of the Holy Spirit. Those who commit this sin are punished by God with blindness, so that they never repent, and consequently do not obtain forgiveness.

units.la: xv. Peccata remissibilia, sive non in spiritum sanctum, sunt omnia alia peccata, quorum aliqui agunt, aliqui non agunt poenitentiam.
units.tr: XV. Forgivable sins, that is, sins not against the Holy Spirit, are all other sins, of which some repent and some do not repent.

units.la: xvi. Omnes electi a Deo ad vitam aeternam, sic ab ipso servantur, ut nunquam peccent in spiritum sanctum.
units.tr: XVI. All the elect, whom God has chosen to eternal life, are so preserved by him that they never sin against the Holy Spirit.

units.la: xvii. In omnib. renatis, quamdiu sunt in hac vita, manent reliquiae peccati: primo, peccatum originale: secundo, multa peccata actualia, ignorantiae, omissionis & infirmitatis, quae tamen ipsi agnoscunt & deplorant, eisque repugnant, ideoque retinent bonam conscientiam & remissionem peccatorum: Tertio, aliqui ruunt etiam aliquando in errores pugnantes cum fundamento, aut in peccata contra conscientiam, propter quae amittunt bonam conscientiam, consolationem & dona spiritus sancti, & damnarentur, si in illis usq.ad finem vitae perseverarent: sed[?] in illis non pereunt, quia in hac vita poenitentiam agunt.
units.tr: XVII. In all the regenerate, as long as they are in this life, remnants of sin remain: first, original sin; second, many actual sins of ignorance, omission and weakness, which nevertheless they themselves recognise and deplore, and resist, and therefore they retain a good conscience and the remission of sins; third, some sometimes fall even into errors contrary to the foundation, or into sins against conscience, on account of which they lose a good conscience, consolation and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and would be condemned if they persisted in these until the end of life; but they do not perish in them, because in this life they repent.

units.la: xviii. Triplex est discrimen, quo peccantes renati differunt ab impiis: Primum, in Deo propositum perpetuum eos seruandi: Secundum, certa poenitentia finalis: Tertium, etiam in ipsis peccatis aliquod initium verae fidei & conuersionis, quod alias est maius ac firmius, & sic reluctatur peccato, ut in errores contra fundamentum, aut in peccata contra conscientiam non labantur: alias est minus & languidius, & vincitur ad tempus tentationib. sed tamen facit, ne in universum à Deo deficiant, qui semel fuerunt vere conversi. Idcoque peccatum in renatis aut non regnans tantum est appellandum: aut si errores contra fundamentum & peccata contra conscientiam regnantia peccata vocentur, (ut aliqui loquuntur), necesse est, regnum illud peccati in renatis & non renatis diligenter distingui, quòd nimirum grauiter quidem etiam renatis labentib. irascatur Deus, sed tamen universaliter cum proposito eos corrigendi & seruandi, & quòd semper in ipsis maneat aliqua scintilla fidei & conversionis, & aliquod odiū peccati, quod aduersatur peccato, ut non simpliciter sine vlla repugnantia sese dedant peccato, atque eo delectentur, sicut impij sine omni lucta, siue toto animo peccantes.
units.tr: XVIII. There is a threefold difference by which the regenerate who sin differ from the impious: first, in God there is a perpetual purpose to preserve them; second, a certain final repentance; third, even in their sins there is some beginning of true faith and conversion, which in the one case is greater and firmer, and so struggles against sin that they do not fall into errors contrary to the foundation, or into sins against conscience; in the other case it is smaller and weaker, and is overcome by temptations for a time, yet it keeps them from wholly falling away from God, who once were truly converted. Therefore sin in the regenerate ought to be called only non-reigning; or, if errors contrary to the foundation and sins against conscience are called reigning sins (as some speak), it is necessary to distinguish carefully this reign of sin in the regenerate and in the unregenerate: namely, that God is indeed angered by the regenerate when they fall gravely, yet universally with a purpose of correcting and preserving them; and that in them there always remains some spark of faith and conversion, and some hatred of sin, which opposes sin, so that they do not simply, without any resistance, give themselves over to sin and delight in it, as the impious do, sinning without any struggle or with their whole mind.

units.la: xix. Omne peccatum aut per se, aut per accidens peccatum est.
units.tr: XIX. Every sin is either sin in itself, or sin by accident.

units.la: xx. Per se siue suo genere peccata sunt omnia quae legę diuina prohibentur.
units.tr: XX. Sins in themselves, or by their own kind, are all those things forbidden by the divine law.

units.la: xxi. Per accidens peccata sunt actiones non renatorum, quae praeceptae quidē sunt à Deo, sed tamen Deo displicet, propter defectus & vitia in impiis concurrentia: aut actiones adiaphorae, quae fiunt cum scandalo.
units.tr: XXI. Sins by accident are actions of the unregenerate which indeed are commanded by God, but nevertheless displease God, on account of the defects and vices concurring in the impious; or indifferent actions which are done with scandal.

units.la: xxii. Deus nullius peccati causa est, sed omnium peccatorum efficiens causa est voluntas diabolorum & hominum, sua sponte se avertentes à Deo: originalis vitij in homi-nib. causa efficiens est lapsus primorum parentum: originale autem peccatum causa est [illegible, ~8 letters] omnium peccatorum actualium, quae primum lapsum secuta sunt.
units.tr: XXII. God is the cause of no sin, but the efficient cause of all sins is the will of devils and men, turning themselves away from God of their own accord; the efficient cause of original vice in men is the fall of our first parents; and original sin is the cause of all actual sins which followed the first fall.

units.la: xxiii. Effectus peccati sunt poenae temporales & aeternę: & quia Deus peccatis punit peccata, etiam sequentia peccata praecedentium effectus sunt.
units.tr: XXIII. The effects of sin are temporal and eternal punishments; and because God punishes sins by sins, even subsequent sins are effects of preceding ones.

units.la: xxiv. Etsi autem omnia peccata mereantur aeternam damnationem, non tamen omnia peccata sunt paria: Sed sicut pœnarum, ita & peccatorum gradus sunt[?] etiam in iudicio diuino.
units.tr: XXIV. Although all sins deserve eternal damnation, not all sins are equal; but as there are degrees of punishments, so also there are degrees of sins, even in the divine judgment.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: De libero arbitrio.
units.tr: On Free Will.

units.la: I. Libertas voluntatis in Deo & in creaturis rationalibus est facultas eligendi aut repudiandi proprio ac suo motu sine vlla coactione, id quod ratio eligi aut repudiari suadet.
units.tr: I. The freedom of the will, in God and in rational creatures, is the faculty of choosing or rejecting by its own motion and without any compulsion, that which reason suggests should be chosen or rejected.

units.la: II. Ac liberum vocatur, quod ea facultate præditum est: Arbitrium significat ipsam voluntatem: sed quæ mentis iudicium in eligendo sequitur aut repudiat: atque idcirco facultatem utramque complectitur, intelligendi nimirum & volendi.
units.tr: II. It is called free because it is endowed with this faculty. The arbitrium (free choice) signifies the will itself, but one which follows or rejects the judgment of the mind in choosing; and so it embraces both faculties, namely understanding and willing.

units.la: III. Est igitur liberum arbitrium facultas seu potentia volendi aut nolendi, eligens aut repudians sine coactione, proprio motu & aptitudine ad alterutrum, id quod intellectus eligendum aut repudiandum esse dictat.
units.tr: III. Free choice, therefore, is the faculty or power of willing or not willing, choosing or rejecting without compulsion, by its own motion and with an aptitude for either alternative, according as the understanding dictates that it is to be chosen or rejected.

units.la: IV. Duo sunt ergo, quæ communia habet libertas voluntatis in Deo & creaturis rationalibus: primum, quod ex deliberatione agunt & consilio, siue intellectu monstrate[?] obiecta: Alterum, quod voluntas sua sponte, ac vi sibi insita, sine coactione vult aut nö vult quod mens[?] cogitauit.
units.tr: IV. There are therefore two things which the freedom of the will has in common in God and in rational creatures: first, that they act from deliberation and counsel, or from the objects shown by the understanding; second, that the will, of its own accord and by the power implanted in it, without compulsion, wills or does not will what the mind has thought.

units.la: V. Discrimina vero libertatis in Deo & creaturis tria sunt: primum in intellectu, quod Deus ex seipso perfectissime omnia ab æterno intelligit atque intuetur, nec vlla in eum ignorantia vllius rei, aut vllus error iudicij unquam potest cadere. Secundum, est in voluntate: quod videlicet Dei voluntas à nulla alia causa regitur, aut flectitur, aut pendet quâ à seipsa: angelorum vero & hominum voluntates sic sunt actionum & motuum suorum causæ, vt nihilominus, arcano Dei consilio, vt ubique & semper præsenti vti & efficacia obiectorum ad electionem aut repudiationem flectantur, siue immediate à Deo, siue per instrumenta seu media, alias bona, alias mala, quibus vti Deo est visum: ac præter æternum ac immutabile Dei consilium quicquam eas agere fit impossibile. Tertium est simul in intellectu & in voluntate, quod Deus sicut immutabiliter omnia scit, sic etiam decreuit ab æterno & vult immutabiliter omnia quæ fiunt, quatenus bona sunt, & permittit, quatenus peccata sunt: creaturarum autem sicut notitiæ, & iudicia de rebus, sic etiam voluntates mutabiles sunt.
units.tr: V. The differences of freedom in God and in creatures are three. The first is in the understanding: God knows and perfectly beholds all things from himself from eternity, and no ignorance of anything, nor any error of judgment, can ever fall upon him. The second is in the will: the will of God is governed by no other cause, is not bent or dependent on anything except himself; but the wills of angels and men are causes of their own actions and motions, yet nevertheless, by the secret counsel of God, they are bent by the present and effective influence of objects, which God uses everywhere and always, toward choosing or rejecting, whether immediately by God or through instruments or means, some good and some evil, as God has seen fit; and it is impossible for them to do anything outside the eternal and unchangeable counsel of God. The third is at once in the understanding and in the will: God, just as he knows all things unchangeably, so also has decreed from eternity and unchangeably wills all things that come to pass, insofar as they are good, and permits them insofar as they are sins; but the knowledge and judgments of creatures about things are changeable, and so too are their wills.

units.la: VI. In hominibus libertas hæc per peccatū, quod ad o-pera Deo placentia attinet, amissa est: in regeneratione autem instaurari incipit & in vita æterna perfectè resti-tuitur. Unde quatuor illius gradus, quatuor distincti status hominum efficiunt, qui temporibus distincti sunt.
units.tr: VI. In human beings this freedom was lost through sin, as far as works pleasing to God are concerned; it begins to be restored in regeneration and is perfectly restored in eternal life. Hence its four degrees make up four distinct states of human beings, which are distinguished by times.

units.la: VII. Primus gradus libertatis fuit in natura nondum lapsa, in qua voluntas erat idonea ad præstandam integram obedientiam legi diuinæ, non tamen ita confirmata, quin tentata à diabolo specie alicuius boni, deficere ab illa obedientia posset, suo & spontaneo motu.
units.tr: VII. The first degree of freedom was in nature not yet fallen, in which the will was fit to render complete obedience to the divine law, yet not so confirmed that, when tempted by the devil under the appearance of some good, it could not fall away from that obedience by its own spontaneous motion.

units.la: VIII. Et tamen, quia non aliunde potest existere perseverantia creaturæ in obedientia, nisi ex confirmatione diuina, volens quidem, sed tamen necessariò tentationi voluntas hominum cessit, & in peccatum prolapsa, libertatem, quam ad bonū vel malū eligendū habebat, ad bonū amisit, ad malum verò auersa & alienata à Deo, retinuit.
units.tr: VIII. And yet, since the perseverance of a creature in obedience can arise from no other source than divine confirmation, the human will, though willing, nevertheless of necessity yielded to temptation, and having fallen into sin, it lost the freedom it had to choose good or evil with respect to good, but retained it with respect to evil, being turned away and alienated from God.

units.la: IX. Secundus igitur gradus libertatis est minimus, in natura lapsa & nondum regenerata, in qua etsi voluntas idonea est ad præstandam externam disciplinam decalogi, ta-men quia internam & spiritualè obedientiam ne inchoa-re quidem potest, sine qua vniuersa, etiam optima in spe-ciem, opera externa sunt peccata damnata à Deo, liberè quidem voluntas eligere non definit, sed nihil eligere po-test, quàm peccatum, propter inhærentem sibi prauita-tem & auersionem à Deo.
units.tr: IX. The second degree of freedom, therefore, is the least, in nature fallen and not yet regenerated, in which, although the will is fit to render the external discipline of the decalogue, yet because it cannot even begin the internal and spiritual obedience, without which all external works, even the best in appearance, are sins condemned by God, the will indeed does not cease to choose freely, but it can choose nothing except sin, on account of the depravity inherent in it and its aversion from God.

units.la: X. Tertius gradus est in homine renato, sed nondū glorificato: in quo voluntas libertate sua utitur partim ad bene, partim male operandum. Quia enim per spiritum sanctum regeneratus est, inclinatur quidem rursus ad obedi-endum Deo, sed quia regeneratio nondum est perfecta, reliquæ sunt etiam inclinationes prauæ: ideo inchoat quidem spiritualem & Deo placentem obedientiam: sed eam perfectā in hac vita præstare non potest. Tunc autem & eatenus agit bene, & in bono perseverat, quādo & quatenus à spiritu sancto gubernatur.
units.tr: X. The third degree is in the regenerate man, but not yet glorified; in him the will uses its freedom partly to act well and partly to act badly. For since he has been regenerated by the Holy Spirit, he is indeed inclined again to obey God, but because regeneration is not yet perfect, the remaining depraved inclinations also remain; therefore he indeed begins a spiritual obedience pleasing to God, but cannot render it perfectly in this life. Then, and insofar, he acts well and perseveres in good, when and insofar as he is governed by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: XI. Quartus gradus est summus & perfectissimus, in vita æterna, siue post glorificationem, in qua voluntas libertate sua uti poterit tantùm ad bonum, & non ad malum eligendum, propter agnitionem perfectissimam & dilectionem ardentissimam Dei, & summam inclinationem ad iustitiam & auersionem à peccato, & perpetuam spiritus sancti gubernationem.
units.tr: XI. The fourth degree is the highest and most perfect, in eternal life, or after glorification, in which the will will be able to use its freedom only to choose good and not evil, on account of the most perfect knowledge and most ardent love of God, the supreme inclination to righteousness and aversion from sin, and the perpetual governance of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: xi.Doctrinam hanc de libertate voluntatis in ecclesia retineri necesse est:ut soli Deo summa & perfectissima libertas & immutabilitas,& effectio omnium bonorum in nobis,tanquam primae causae tribuatur : peccantib.omnis excusatio detrahatur:agnitione miseriae & pravitatis nostrae,vere coram Deo humiliati,ab ipso solo nostrae salutis confectionem &consummationem petamus,& convicti testimoniis divinis ad credendum & obtemperandum voci ipsius permoveamur.
units.tr: XII. It is necessary that this doctrine of the freedom of the will be retained in the Church, so that supreme and most perfect freedom and immutability, and the effecting of all good things in us, may be ascribed to God alone as the first cause; that all excuse be removed from sinners; and that, truly humbled before God by the recognition of our misery and depravity, we may seek the accomplishment and consummation of our salvation from him alone, and, convinced by the divine testimonies, be moved to believe and obey his voice.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: De fide, disputatae xii. Augusti, anno MDLXXII.
units.tr: On faith, disputed on the 12th of August, in the year 1572.

units.la: i. Fides, late sumendo vocabulum, significat notitiam certam ex assueratione testium, qui non fallere existimantur.
units.tr: i. Faith, taking the word broadly, signifies a certain knowledge arising from the assertion of witnesses who are thought not to deceive.

units.la: ii. In doctrina ecclesiae de quatuor fidei speciebus fit mentio, historica, temporaria, miraculorum, & iustificante.
units.tr: ii. In the teaching of the Church, mention is made of four kinds of faith: historical, temporary, of miracles, and justifying.

units.la: iii. Fides historica, est notitia statuens, ea vera esse, quae in libris prophetarum & apostolorum tradita sunt.
units.tr: iii. Historical faith is the knowledge that holds those things to be true which are handed down in the books of the prophets and apostles.

units.la: iv. Fides temporaria est notitia doctrinae ecclesiae coniuncta cum laetitia, propter veritatis cognitionem, aut alia sive vera sive apparentia bona, sine applicatione promissionis gratiae ad credentem, ac proinde sine vera conversione, & finali perseverantia.
units.tr: iv. Temporary faith is the knowledge of the Church's teaching joined with joy, on account of the knowledge of the truth or some other good, whether real or apparent, without the application of the promise of grace to the believer, and therefore without true conversion and final perseverance.

units.la: v. Fides, quae eduntur miracula, est notitia certa ex singulari revelatione voluntatis Dei, de edendo certo miraculo, ad petitionem vel praedictionem eius, per quem credendum est.
units.tr: v. Faith by which miracles are wrought is the certain knowledge, derived from a singular revelation of God's will, that a particular miracle will be performed at the request or prediction of the one by whom it is to be believed.

units.la: vi. Fides iustificas est notitia, qua quis firmiter assentitur omni verbo Dei sibi patefacto, & statuit, promissione gratiae Dei, propter Christum, ad se pertinere, & fiducia huius favoris Dei erga se omne tristitiam & metum superat.
units.tr: vi. Justifying faith is the knowledge by which someone firmly assents to every word of God revealed to him, and determines that the promise of God's grace, on account of Christ, pertains to him; and by trust in this favour of God toward him, overcomes all sorrow and fear.

units.la: vii. Est enim Fiducia Dei iustificantis motus voluntatis & cordis, compositus ex laetitia propter certitudinem praesentis gratiae Dei erga nos: & spe futurae liberationis ab omnibus malis.
units.tr: vii. For the trust of justifying God is a movement of the will and heart, composed of joy on account of the certainty of God's present grace toward us, and of hope for future deliverance from all evils.

units.la: viii. Nulla igitur fides est, nisi quae voluntate Dei patefacta nititur.
units.tr: viii. No faith is therefore faith unless it rests upon the will of God as revealed.

units.la: ix. Fide[?] omnem in hominibus efficit spiritus sanctus,
units.tr: ix. The Holy Spirit produces faith in all human beings,

units.la: Vsus doctrina de libero arbitrio. siue per vocem doctrinæ cælestis, siue per immediatam reuelationem.
units.tr: The use of the doctrine concerning free will: either through the voice of the heavenly teaching, or through immediate revelation.

units.la: x. Cùm autem ordinariè fidem in nobis accedere & fovere atque confirmare velit Deus per doctrinam ecclesiæ: omnes ad eam audiendam & meditandam obligantur.
units.tr: x. Since God ordinarily wishes to bring faith into us, to foster it and to confirm it, through the teaching of the Church, all are bound to hear and to meditate upon it.

units.la: xi. Fides temporaria multis in ecclesia hypocritis contingit: historica & miraculorum piis & impiis communis est: iustificans solis & omnibus ad vitam æternam electis in hac vita datur.
units.tr: xi. Temporary faith befalls many hypocrites in the Church; historical faith and the faith of miracles are common to the pious and the impious; justifying faith is given in this life to the elect alone and to all the elect for eternal life.

units.la: xii. Iustificans fides semper historicam in se complectitur: cum miraculorum fide non semper est coniuncta: sicut etiam fides miraculorum semper historicam aut temporariam coniunctam habet, iustificantem vero non semper.
units.tr: xii. Justifying faith always includes historical faith within itself; it is not always joined with the faith of miracles; just as the faith of miracles always has historical or temporary faith joined with it, but not always justifying faith.

units.la: xiii. Fides etiam in sanctissimis hominibus est in hac vita imperfecta & languida: sed tamen quisquis serium cre-dendi propositum, & luctam cum dubitationibus in corde suo sentit, vera fide se præditum esse certò statuere potest ac debet.
units.tr: xiii. Faith, even in the most holy men, is imperfect and weak in this life; yet whoever feels in his heart a earnest purpose of believing, and a struggle with doubts, can and ought to determine with certainty that he is endowed with true faith.

units.la: xiv. Vera fides semel in cordibus accensa, etsi sæpe admodum languescit & obscuratur: tamen nunquam tota exstinguitur.
units.tr: xiv. True faith, once kindled in hearts, though it often grows very faint and obscured, is nevertheless never wholly extinguished.

units.la: xv. Post hanc vitam autem in pleniorem ac certiorem Dei ac diuinarum rerum cognitionem commutatur, sensum nimirum & experientiam præsentis in Deo beatitudinis, quam cognitionem per speciem, & à facie ad faciem scriptura nominat.
units.tr: xv. After this life, however, it is changed into a fuller and clearer knowledge of God and of divine things, namely a sense and experience of the present blessedness in God, which Scripture calls knowledge through sight, and face to face.

units.la: xvi. Fides quæ tantum historica est, desperationem & iudicij diuini grauitatem quamuis per accidens, efficit.
units.tr: xvi. Faith that is merely historical produces despair and the gravity of divine judgment, though only incidentally.

units.la: xvii. Fides temporaria lætitiam quandam, sed non pacantem conscientias: quia non ex vera causa profestam: confessionem, ac speciem aliquam bonorum operum efficit, sed tantum ad tempus.
units.tr: xvii. Temporary faith produces a certain joy, but one that does not pacify consciences, because it does not arise from a true cause; it produces a confession and some appearance of good works, but only for a time.

units.la: xviii. Fides miraculorum ea, de quibus est, miracula à Deo impetrat.
units.tr: xviii. Faith in miracles obtains from God the miracles of which it speaks.

units.la: xix. Sola fide applicante singulis promissionem gratiæ, iustitiam coram Deo, & Christi, omniumque eius beneficiorum communionem accipimus.
units.tr: xix. By faith alone, applying the promise of grace to each person, we receive righteousness before God, and communion in Christ and in all his benefits.

units.la: xx. Eandem fidem, ut non possunt antecedere, ita non possunt non comitari vera conversio, & obedientiæ no-væ [?], secundùm omnia mandata, inchoatio.
units.tr: xx. True conversion and the beginning of obedience to all the commandments cannot precede this same faith, and yet cannot fail to accompany it.

units.la: XIV. THESES DE OFFICIO ET PERSONA vnici mediatoris inter Deum & Homines, Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: XIV. THESES ON THE OFFICE AND PERSON OF THE ONLY MEDIATOR BETWEEN GOD AND MEN, OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST.

units.la: In Academia Heidelbergensi pro Doctoratu disputata a D. Zacharia Vrsino anno 1561. PROOEMIVM.
units.tr: Disputed in the Academy of Heidelberg for the Doctorate by D. Zacharias Ursinus, in the year 1561. PREFACE.

units.la: Cum Deus non tantum verbi sui ministerium in ecclesia instituerit, & vocationem ad docendi officium, quae fit per ecclesiam, praeceperit & approbet: verum & munus hoc longe omnium, quae ab hominibus administrantur, summum, & periculi plenissimum, iis commendari, qui & cognitionem doctrinae coelestis, & eam explicandi facultate mediocrem habent, & vitae innocentia eorum, quae docuerint, exemplum auditoribus praebent: & quidem eos, qui non idoneos, hoc est, vita vel doctrina mala damnum dantes ecclesiae, in hanc statione collocarint, aut collocantibus assenserint, alienae culpae reos fore per os Pauli pronun-ciet, sic dicetis 1.Tim.5. Manus cito nemini imponas, neque communices peccatis alienis. Haec, inquam, cum ita sint, haud dubie necessarium est, ut partem laborum docendi in ecclesiis vel scholis subituri, & audiantur prius ab iis, qui de doctrinae veritate iudicare possunt, & libenter se hominum examinibus & censuris subiiciant. Ego itaque ta-men[?] mei aliqua fiducia in publicum hunc virorum doctorum & studiosae iuuentutis conspectum prodire adeo non potuerim, ut neq. eruditione, neq. rerum usum, neque iudicium, neq. ulla omnino re, quae oculos mihi & aures doctorum hominum patientes impetrare queat, praeter trepidationem summam, & opis divinae, vestrasque beneuolentiae implorationem, huc afferam: tamen cum examina detrectare, qui aliquandiu in scholis versati sunt, non debeant, & pars ingenuitatis ac fidei sit, etiam tenuitatem suam non occultare: & officij faciendi, & mei erudiendi causa, mandata eorum, qui in hunc locum venire me voluerunt, pertinaciùs repugnandum non esse iudicaui.
units.tr: Since God has not only instituted the ministry of his Word in the Church, and has commanded and approved the calling to the office of teaching, which is effected through the Church, but also has entrusted this office, by far the highest of all those administered by men and most full of danger, to those who have both knowledge of heavenly doctrine and a moderate ability to explain it, and who offer their hearers an example of innocence of life in what they have taught; and since he says through the mouth of Paul, 1 Tim. 5: "Lay hands hastily on no one, nor share in the sins of others," indeed declaring that those who have placed in this station, or have assented to those placing, persons who are not fit, that is, who by bad life or bad doctrine do harm to the Church, will be guilty of another's fault; given these things, it is without doubt necessary that those who are to undertake a share of the labours of teaching in churches or schools should first be heard by those who can judge the truth of doctrine, and should willingly submit themselves to the examinations and judgements of men. Accordingly, although I could not come forward before this public gathering of learned men and studious youth with any confidence at all, bringing nothing here (neither learning, nor experience of affairs, nor judgement, nor anything at all that could win the eyes and ears of learned men who are patient), except very great trepidation and an imploring of divine help and of your goodwill, nevertheless, since those who have spent some time in the schools ought not to shrink from examinations, and since it is part of candour and faithfulness not to conceal even one's own slightness, I judged that for the sake of performing my duty and of my own instruction I should not stubbornly resist the commands of those who wished me to come to this place.

units.la: Quia vero colloquiorum istorum ratio & finis postu-lat, ut de praecipuis aliquibus doctrinae Christianae capitib. instituantur: visum est sententiam in verbo Dei tradita de officio & persona vnici mediatoris inter Deum & homines Domini nostri Iesu Christi, in praesentia repetendam & expendendam. pendedam[?] proponere:tū quia fundamentum & summam breuem Christianæ religionis complectitur:tum quia omnibus temporibus externa & domestica ecclesiæ certamina solent hanc potissimum attingere. More igitur visitato propositionum sententiam, aliquas rationes & testimonia è sacris literis petita,quæ potero breuitate & simplicitate recitabo.
units.tr: But since the nature and purpose of these colloquies require that some of the principal heads of Christian doctrine be treated, it seemed fitting to repeat and weigh now the teaching handed down in the Word of God concerning the office and person of the only mediator between God and men, our Lord Jesus Christ. We do so both because it embraces the foundation and brief summary of the Christian religion, and because at all times the external and domestic conflicts of the Church are wont to touch this point especially. Therefore, following the customary method, I shall set out the sense of the propositions and recite, as briefly and simply as I can, some arguments and testimonies drawn from the sacred letters.

units.la: THESIS I.
units.tr: THESIS I.

units.la: Postquā homo per peccatum à Deo auulsus erat:summa & perfectissima Dei{a} iustitia illum reconciliari cū Deo non sinebat,nisi aliquis{b} verus homo ex eo,quod peccauerat,genere humano natus,{c}ab omni tamen peccati labe immunis, pœnam pro peccatis sufficientem lueret,atque integram diuinæ legis obedientiam præstaret.
units.tr: Since man had been torn away from God through sin, God's supreme and most perfect justice did not allow him to be reconciled with God unless some true man, born of the human race from which he had sinned, yet free from every stain of sin, should pay a penalty sufficient for sins and render a complete obedience to the divine law.

units.la: {a} Genef.2.17. Quocunque die comederis, morte morieris. Deu.27.26. Maledictus omnis, qui non, &c. Mat.5.26. Non exibis inde, donec persoluueris extremum quadrantem. Ro.8.3. Deus missō filio proprio condemnauit peccatum in carne, & nos &c.
units.tr: {a} Gen. 2:17. On whatever day you eat of it, you shall surely die. Deut. 27:26. Cursed is everyone who does not, etc. Matt. 5:26. You will not get out of there until you have paid the last penny. Rom. 8:3. God, sending his own Son, condemned sin in the flesh, and us, etc.

units.la: {b} Ro.5.12.15.[?] Sicut per vnū hominem peccatū introiit in mundum, &c. 1. Cor.15.21. Per hominem mors, & per hominem resurrectio. 1. Tim.2.5. Hebr.2.14.15.16. Aug. de Vera relig. Ipsa natura suscipienda erat, quæ liberanda.
units.tr: {b} Rom. 5:12, 15. As through one man sin entered the world, etc. 1 Cor. 15:21. Through a man came death, and through a man the resurrection. 1 Tim. 2:5. Heb. 2:14, 15, 16. Augustine, on True Religion. Nature itself had to be taken up, which was to be freed.

units.la: {c} 2. Cor.5.21. Fecit eum qui non nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum, &c. Heb.7.26. Talis nobis conueniebat Pontifex, pius, innocens, impollutus.
units.tr: {c} 2 Cor. 5:21. He made him who knew no sin to be sin for us, etc. Heb. 7:26. Such a High Priest was fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: At nullius personæ meritum, quæ Deus non esset, culpæ totius generis humani æquale, nec dum ea maius esse potuisset.{d}
units.tr: But no merit of any person who was not God could be equal to the guilt of the whole human race, nor could that merit be greater than it.

units.la: {d} Actor.20.28. Deus ecclesiam proprio suo sanguine acquisiuit. Rom.8.3. Cum legis impotentia nihil posset in carne, Deus &c.
units.tr: {d} Acts 20:28. God obtained the Church with his own blood. Rom. 8:3. Since the law was powerless in the flesh, God, etc.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Persona etiam, quæ tantum creatura fuisset, grauitatem pœnæ, & molem iræ diuinæ aduersus peccata generis humani sustinere, & ex ea emergere nunquam potuisset.{e}
units.tr: Likewise, a person who was merely a creature could never have borne the weight of the punishment and the mass of the divine wrath against the sins of the human race, nor have emerged from it.

units.la: {e} Psal.30.3. Si iniquitates obseruaueris Domine, quis co-sisteret? Deut.4.24. Dominus Deus tuus ignis consumens est.
units.tr: {e} Ps. 130:3. If you, Lord, should mark iniquities, who could stand? Deut. 4:24. The Lord your God is a consuming fire.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Eundem præterea & merito intercessioneque suâ[?] impetrare,& potentia sua iustitiam & vitam amissam reddere,nofq.à peccato & morte liberare,& vsque ad perfectam restitutionem tueri & seruare oportebat. f
units.tr: Moreover, the same one had to obtain by his merit and intercession, and restore by his power, the justice and life that were lost, and to rescue us from sin and death, and to protect and preserve us until perfect restoration. f

units.la: f 1.Cor.15.21.Per hominem resurrectio mortuorum.Ioh. 10.28. Ego omnibus meis do vitam æternam.Io 6. 39. & 15. 26.Mat.11.27.Ephef.4.8.9.10.Heb.7.16. 1.Cor.15.22.23.
units.tr: f 1 Cor. 15:21. Through a man came the resurrection of the dead. John 10:28. I give to all my own eternal life. John 6:39 and 15:26. Matt. 11:27. Eph. 4:8, 9, 10. Heb. 7:16. 1 Cor. 15:22, 23.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Denique saluandos omnes,per fidem insitos huius mediatoris corpori,ab ipso gestari in æternum, & viuificari necesse est. g
units.tr: Finally, all who are to be saved, who are engrafted by faith into the body of this mediator, must necessarily be borne by him for ever and quickened. g

units.la: g Ephef.3.17. Vt inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordib. Vestris.Ioh.15.4.Manete in me & ego in vobis. Sicut palmes non potest ferre fructum a semetipso, nisi manserit in vite: ita nec vos, nisi in me manseritis. Rom.8.9.Qui spiritum Christi non habet,is non est eius.
units.tr: g Eph. 3:17. That Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith. John 15:4. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me. Rom. 8:9. Whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: His igitur de causis in mediatore Christo est natura diuina,quæ est secunda persona diuinitatis, & nominatur λόγος,& filius æterni patris vnigenitus,vnus cū patre & Sp. sancto Deus, patri consubstantialis, & æqualis per omnia. h
units.tr: For these reasons, then, the nature of the divine is in the mediator Christ. It is the second person of the Deity, is called Logos, and is the only-begotten Son of the eternal Father, one God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, consubstantial with the Father and equal to him in all things. h

units.la: h Ioh.1.In principio erat λόγος,& λόγος erat apud Deum,& λόγος erat Deus.Rom.9.5.Qui est Deus super omnes laudandus in secula.Phil.2.6.Qui cum esset in forma Dei,non rapinam duxit,pare esse Deo,&c.Col.2.9.In ipso habitat omnis plenitudo deitatis corporaliter.1 Tim.3.16.Deus manifestatus est in carne.Heb.1.8.Ad filium autem dixit: thronus tuus Deus in seculū seculi.1.Ioh.5.20.Et simus in verace illo filio eius Iesu Christo. Hic est verus Deus & vita æterna.
units.tr: h John 1. In the beginning was the Word [λόγος], and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Rom. 9.5. Who is God over all, blessed for ever. Phil. 2.6. Who, being in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal with God, etc. Col. 2.9. In him dwells all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. 1 Tim. 3.16. God was manifested in the flesh. Heb. 1.8. But to the Son he says: Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever. 1 John 5.20. And we are in his true Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Est etiam in eo ι natura humana vera & integra,constans anima & corpore,de Mariæ matris virginis substantia,virtute Spiritus Sancti formato,& vnà cum anima perfectè sanctificato,inde à conceptionis articulo.
units.tr: In him there is also a human nature, true and complete, consisting of soul and body, taken from the substance of Mary his virgin mother, formed by the power of the Holy Spirit, and perfectly sanctified together with the soul from the moment of conception. i

units.la: i Gen.3.Semen mulieris.Gen.12.Semen Abrahami.Mat.1.Filius Abrahami & Dauidis.Rom.1.Ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem.Luc.1.Fructus ventris Mariæ.Heb.2.Particeps carnis & sanguinis: Semen Abrahæ assumpsit.Mat.26.Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem.
units.tr: i Gen. 3. The seed of the woman. Gen. 12. The seed of Abraham. Matt. 1. Son of Abraham and David. Rom. 1. Of the seed of David according to the flesh. Luke 1. The fruit of Mary's womb. Heb. 2. Partaker of flesh and blood: he took on the seed of Abraham. Matt. 26. My soul is sorrowful even unto death.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Sic autem sola hæc persona diuinitatis, quæ nominatur [?]λόγος assumsit humanam naturam, vt hæ duæ naturæ inde à conceptione esse coeperint, & postea inseparabiliter maneant vna persona, & massa humanæ naturæ à diuinitate gestetur ac sustentur.{k}
units.tr: Thus only this person of the Deity, who is called [?]Logos, assumed human nature, so that these two natures began to be from the conception, and afterwards remain inseparably one person, and the mass of human nature is borne and sustained by the divinity. k

units.la: {k} Ioh.1. Λόγος ἐστὶ caro factum. Col.2. In eo habitat omnis plenitudo deitatis corporaliter. Heb.2. Assumsit semen Abrahæ. Actor.20. Deum proprio sanguine acquisiuit ecclesiam.
units.tr: {k} John 1. The Word was made flesh [ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο]. Col. 2. In him dwells all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. Heb. 2. He took on the seed of Abraham. Acts 20. He obtained the Church with his own blood.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Neque tamen hac vnione vna natura in alteram est mutata, sed vtraque distinctas proprietates retinet perpetuò, quibus natura creatrix à creatura discernitur.{l}
units.tr: Yet by this union one nature has not been changed into the other, but each keeps its distinct properties perpetually, by which the creating nature is distinguished from the created nature. l

units.la: {l} Rom.1. Factus ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem. 1. Pet.3. Mortificatus carne, viuificatus spiritu. 1. Pet.4. Christus est passus carne. Phil.2. Formam serui assumsit.
units.tr: {l} Rom. 1. Made of the seed of David according to the flesh. 1 Pet. 3. Put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit. 1 Pet. 4. Christ has suffered in the flesh. Phil. 2. He took the form of a servant.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Hinc est, quòd nomina, quæ significant Christi officiū, tam vtrique naturæ seorsum, quàm toti personæ rectè attribuuntur: Proprietates verò vni tantùm naturæ conuenientes, de altera natura seorsum dici verè non possunt: de tota autem persona rectè dicuntur, ea loquendi forma, quam [?]κοινωνίαν ἰδιωμάτων vocant.{m}
units.tr: Hence it is that the names which signify Christ's office are rightly attributed both to each nature separately and to the whole person; but the properties belonging to one nature only cannot truly be said separately of the other nature, though they are rightly said of the whole person, in that mode of speaking which they call the [?]communication of properties [κοινωνία τῶν ἰδιωμάτων]. m

units.la: {m} Leo ad Flauian. c.4. Agit in utraque forma cum alterius communione, quod proprium est, verbo scilicet operante quod verbi est, & carne exsequente quod carnis est. Vide Damascenum de fide orthod. lib. 3.c.4.
units.tr: {m} Leo, to Flavian, c. 4. He acts in each form in communion with the other, that which is proper to it: the Word working what belongs to the Word, and the flesh carrying out what belongs to the flesh. See Damascene, on the Orthodox Faith, book 3, c. 4.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Totus itaque Christus vbique est, etsi natura ipsius humana post ascensionem vsque ad nouissimi iudicij diem non alibi, quàm in cœlo est.{n}
units.tr: Thus the whole Christ is everywhere, although his human nature, from the ascension until the day of the last judgment, is in no place other than heaven. n

units.la: {n} Matt.28.6. Surrexit, nō est hic. Mat.26.11. Me nō semper habebitis. Ioh.16.28. Relinquo mundum, & vado ad patrem. Act.3.21. Quem oportet quidem cœlo contineri usque ad tempora restitutionis omnium.
units.tr: {n} Matt. 28.6. He is risen, he is not here. Matt. 26.11. You will not always have me. John 16.28. I leave the world and go to the Father. Acts 3.21. Whom heaven must indeed receive until the times of the restoration of all things.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Et sancti, in quocunq. cœli vel terræ loco existentes, massæ humanæ assumptæ à filio Dei habitâte eodē Sp.S. in Christo per vnitatem essentiæ cum verbo, & in sanctis per gratiam, sicut membra capiti suo vniti sunt.{o}
units.tr: And the saints, wherever they exist in any place of heaven or earth, dwell by the same Holy Spirit in Christ, the human mass assumed by the Son of God, through the unity of essence with the Word, and in the saints through grace, just as members are united to their head. o

units.la: {o} 1.Cor.12.13. Per vnum spiritum omnes in vnum corpus baptizati sumus. Eph.4.4. Vnum est corpus, & vnus spiritus. 1.Ioh.4.13. Per hoc cognoscimus, nos in ipso manere, & ipsum in nobis, quod de spiritu suo dedit nobis, Rom. 8. 11. Si spiritus eius, qui excitavit Iesum a mortuis, habitat in vobis, etc. Iren. lib. 3. cap. 19. Sicut de arido tritico massa unam fieri non potest sine humore, neque unus panis: sic nec nos multi unum fieri in Christo Iesu poterimus, sine aqua, quae de caelo est.
units.tr: {o} 1 Cor. 12.13. By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. Eph. 4.4. There is one body and one Spirit. 1 John 4.13. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. Rom. 8.11. If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, etc. Irenaeus, book 3, ch. 19. As from dry wheat a mass cannot be made into one without moisture, nor one loaf; so we who are many cannot be made one in Christ Jesus without the water which is from heaven.

units.la: Gratiarum actio post disputationem.
units.tr: Thanksgiving after the disputation.

units.la: Non dubium est, nullum cordatum hominem posse non admirari et honorifice sentire de scholasticis congressibus, qui causas, propter quas illi fiunt, gravissimas intelligat: nimirum, ut doctrina de Deo et aliis rebus, quarum cognitione vita hominum praecipue indiget, publice sonet atque explicetur, multorum bonorum de veritate colloquia ostendantur et foveatur, et verae sententiae in diversarum animis illustrentur et confirmentur. Pulcherrimum est illud vetus a Platone recitatum: οὔτε χρυσὸς οὔτε ἀδάμας οὔτως ἀγεγέσθαι πρὸς ὑμῶν ὥσπερ ἀγαθῶν αἰσθάνονται ὁμολογούμενον νόμος. Sed multo pulchrior et gratior est hominibus virtute praeditis ipsius rei, de qua hoc dicitur, in placidis bonorum et recte sentientium colloquiis. Nam ideo servat Deus schola s et ecclesias, quod doctrina de se et voluntate sua professione publica celebrari vult. Et verissimum illud est, ὁμοίως λέγειν ἐπει oftedut exempla multorum, qui ingeniis non destituuntur, sed quia sunt αὐτοὶ δέ, non modo in multis hallucinantur, sed etiam αὐθαδείας et aliorum, quae collationis neglectus parit, vitiorum raro sunt expertes. His ob causas merito illorum voluntas laudata est, qui hos cōuentus fouere atque ornare sua collocatione, vel praesentia, vel opera, vel auctoritate et approbatione student.
units.tr: There is no doubt that no sensible man can fail to admire and think highly of scholastic gatherings, if he understands the very weighty reasons for which they are held: namely, that doctrine concerning God and other matters, of which the knowledge especially is needed by human life, may be publicly proclaimed and explained, that the discussions of many good people about the truth may be shown and encouraged, and that true opinions may be illuminated and confirmed in the minds of different people. That old saying, recorded by Plato, is most beautiful: "Neither gold nor adamant is so esteemed by you as good men who think rightly are esteemed, a law being agreed upon." [οὔτε χρυσὸς οὔτε ἀδάμας οὕτως ἀγαπᾶσθαι ὑφ' ὑμῶν ὥσπερ ἀγαθῶν αἰσθάνονται ὁμολογούμενον νόμος] But far more beautiful and more pleasing to men endowed with virtue is the very thing of which this is said, in the peaceful conversations of good men who think rightly. For God preserves schools and churches for this reason: that he wishes doctrine about himself and his will to be celebrated by public profession. And that saying is most true, that "to speak alike" [ὁμοίως λέγειν] ... the examples of many show, who are not lacking in talent, but because they are themselves [αὐτοὶ δέ], not only go astray in many things, but are also rarely free from the faults of self-conceit [αὐθαδεία] and of others, which the neglect of discussion brings forth. For these reasons, rightly, the will of those is praised who strive to foster and adorn these gatherings by their arrangement, or by their presence, or by their work, or by their authority and approval.

units.la: Primo itaque gratias agimus aeterno Deo et patri nostro et filio eius domino nostro Iesu Christo, quod scholas et earum hospitia servat ac tuetur, et cum in aliis tum etiam in hoc nostro coetu puram evangelii lucem voluit effulgere, eamque optimarum artium studiis alit atque exsuscitat. Ago etiam gratias magnifico domino Rectori, aliisque clarissimis et reverendis viris, doctissimis dominis magistris, et studiosae inventuti, qui partim suis monitionibus nos erudierunt, partim sua praesentia coetum nostrum ornarunt, et suam erga nos benevolentiam declararunt: Deum quoque oro, ut quae hactenus nobis elargitus est beneficia, porro etiam omnibus et singulis ad gloriam suae illustrationem, et nostra & multorum hominum salutem feruet atque augeat, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Amen.
units.tr: First, therefore, we give thanks to the eternal God, our Father, and to his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, because he preserves and protects the schools and their hospitality, and has willed the pure light of the gospel to shine not only in others but also in this our assembly, and nourishes and rouses it by the study of the best arts. I also give thanks to the magnificent Rector, and to the other most distinguished and reverend men, the most learned masters, and the studious youth, who partly instructed us by their admonitions, partly adorned our assembly by their presence, and showed their goodwill towards us. I also pray God that the benefits he has hitherto bestowed on us he may further, to all and each, cherish and increase, to the glory of his own illustration and to the salvation of us and of many people, through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

units.la: Gratiarum actio post actum promotionis.
units.tr: Thanksgiving after the act of promotion.

units.la: Summa Dei beneficia, & longè anteferenda sunt omnibus aliis huius vitæ bonis, quòd colligit & seruat sibi æternam ecclesiam, & nos ciues illius facit: pacem dat mediocrib. politiis, quæ sunt ecclesiæ hospitia: & his præficit gubernatores vera ipsum pietate colentes, fouentes ecclesiam, & doctrinæ studia, seruat scholas, eisque tribuit doctores idoneos, & aliquorum animos discendi, & veritatem ad posteros transmittendi studio accendit: præcipuè vero, quòd euangelij lucem inter nos excitat & repurgat ab idolis, & tenebris antichristi nos liberat, ex ore infantium & lactentium robur perfici[?], ad cuius vocem solam portæ inferorum, quantumuis feroces, contremiscunt, & ruinam æternam trahunt. Hæc bona nō casu nobis euenire, nec humana prudentia, sed singulari Dei prouidentia & bonitate donari & conseruari, partim ex ipsa magnitudine & præstantia harum rerum est manifestum, partim inde, quòd inter tantos diabolorum & mundi furores, & in tanta nostra imbecillitate ea retineri non possent.
units.tr: The greatest of God's benefits, and far to be preferred to all other goods of this life, is that he gathers and preserves for himself an eternal Church and makes us its citizens. He gives peace to the middling commonwealths, which are the hospices of the Church, and sets over them governors who worship him in true piety, who foster the Church and the study of doctrine, who maintain schools, and who grant them fit teachers, and who kindle in some the zeal for learning and for handing down the truth to posterity. Above all, he kindles among us the light of the gospel and cleanses it of idols, and frees us from the darkness of the Antichrist, so that strength is perfected out of the mouth of infants and sucklings, at whose voice alone the gates of hell, however fierce, tremble and draw down eternal ruin. That these goods have not come to us by chance, nor been bestowed and preserved by human prudence, but by the singular providence and goodness of God, is clear partly from the very greatness and excellence of these things, and partly from the fact that they could not have been kept amid such great rages of the devils and the world, and in such great weakness of our own.

units.la: Primum itaque Deo gratias agimus æternas, quòd his tantis beneficiis nos affecit. Deinde suâ quoque laude tribuimus illis, qui sua pietate & virtute hæc bona nobis & generi humano coseruare studêt. Gratias itaq; agimus reuerenter illustrissimo Principi & Electori, Domino nostro clementissimo, quòd eximia clemetia schola hanc, & pietatis atque optimarum artium studia fouet atque ornat. Tū etiam aliis viris nobilitate & virtute præstantibus, ac præsertim magnifico domino Rectori. Tum clarissimis & doctissimis viris dominis doctoribus & magistris, præceptoribus & patronis nostris omni pietate obseruantia colendis, ceterisque doctis & honestis viris, qui hanc testimonij publici renunciatione sua præsentia ornates, beneuolentia ergà nos & studia nostra testati sunt, & vocationem nostram Deo communib. votis commendatam voluerunt: Deumque oro toto pectore, vt bona, quæ hactenus largitus[?] est, feruet atque augeat, ijsque ad ipsius gloriam & ecclesiæ suæ salutē vtendi facultatem omnib. concedat, per Iesum Christum dominum nostrum, Amen.
units.tr: First, therefore, we give eternal thanks to God, because he has favoured us with such great benefits. Next, we also render praise to those who, by their piety and virtue, have taken pains to preserve these goods for us and for the human race. We therefore give thanks with reverence to the most illustrious Prince and Elector, our most merciful Lord, because by his singular clemency he fosters and adorns this school and the study of piety and of the best arts. Then also to the other men who excel in nobility and virtue, and especially to the magnificent Lord Rector; then to the most distinguished and learned men, the lords doctors and masters, our teachers and patrons, to be honoured with all piety and respect, and to the other learned and honourable men who have graced this public declaration of the testimony by their presence, have shown their goodwill towards us and our studies, and have wished our calling commended to God by common vows. And I pray God with my whole heart that he may foster and increase the goods he has so far bestowed, and grant to all of them the opportunity of using them for his own glory and the salvation of his Church, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

units.la: XV. DE CONVERSIONE HOMINIS.
units.tr: XV. CONCERNING THE CONVERSION OF MAN.

units.la: Disputata 19. Martij Anno 1575.
units.tr: Disputed 19 March, in the year 1575.

units.la: THESIS I.
units.tr: THESIS I.

units.la: Nemo, nisi in hac vita pœnitentiam agens, seu conuersus à peccatis ad Deum, vitam & beatitudinem æternam habiturus est. Ioh.3.Ver.5[?]. Nisi quis renatus fuerit desuper. Luc.13. Nisi pœnitentiam egeritis, similiter peribitis. Gal.5.21. Qui talia faciunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt.
units.tr: No one will obtain life and eternal blessedness unless he lives in this life, doing penance, that is, converted from sins to God. John 3.5[?]. Unless someone is born again from above. Luke 13. Unless you repent, you will likewise perish. Gal. 5.21. Those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God.

units.la: Est autem vera pœnitentia, seu resipiscentia, seu conuersio, mutatio seu renouatio hominis, à Spiritu S. effecta, qua homo ex vera Dei & voluntatis diuinæ (in lege & euangelio patefactæ) & suæ prauitatis & culpæ agnitione, serio expauescit iram & iudicium Dei aduersus peccatum: & dolet, quod peccatis suis offenderit & offendat Deum: & tamen obtemperans mandato de fide in Christum, & emendatione vitæ acquiescit in misericordia Dei & promissione gratiæ fiducia Christi mediatoris: & quia per hunc placatum sibi esse Deum statuit, sese ipsi dedit & subiecit, tanquam filius benigno patri, & pro hac in gratiam receptione gratum in omnem æternitatem se Deo exhibere studet. Eph.4.21. Si modo eum audistis, & per eum edocti fuistis, sicut est veritas in Iesu: nēpe deponere quod ad pristinam conuersationem attinet, veterem illum hominem, qui deceptricibus cupiditatibus corrumpitur: renouari verò spiritu mentis vestræ, & induere nouum illum hominem, qui secundum Deum conditus est ad iustitiam & sanctimoniam veram. Tit.3.5. Seruauit nos per lauacrum regenerationis & renouationem spiritus sancti. Rom.7.18. Noui non habitare in me, id est, in carne mea bonum: Vsque[?] ad finem cap. Iesa.5.16. Lauamini, mundi estote.
units.tr: True repentance, or repentance-of-mind (resipiscentia), or conversion, is a change or renewal of the man, effected by the Holy Spirit, by which a man, from a true knowledge of God and of the divine will (revealed in law and gospel), and from a knowledge of his own depravity and guilt, seriously dreads the wrath and judgment of God against sin, and grieves that he has offended and does offend God by his sins; and yet, obeying the command concerning faith in Christ and amendment of life, he rests in the mercy of God and in the promise of grace, by trust in Christ the mediator; and because he holds that God has been appeased toward him through this mediator, he gives and submits himself to God, as a son to a kind father, and for this reception into grace he strives to show himself grateful to God for all eternity. Eph. 4.21. If indeed you have heard him and have been taught by him, as truth is in Jesus: namely, to put off, as concerns your former conduct, the old man who is corrupted by deceitful lusts; but to be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and to put on the new man, who after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. Titus 3.5. He saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit. Rom. 7.18. I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, there dwells no good thing. [To the end of ch.] Isa. 5.16. Wash yourselves, be clean.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Constat hæc resipiscentia duabus partibus, quas scriptura vocat mortificationem veteris, & viuificatione seu resuscitatione noui hominis. Ro.6.6. Vetus homo noster simul crucifixus est. Gal.2.19. Per legē legi mortuus sum, ut Deo viuam: cum Christo cruci fixus sum, &c. Col.2.12. Cōsepulti cum eo in baptismo, in quo etiam resurrexistis per fidē efficacia Dei (quam Deus effecit, & per quam Deus est efficax) cax)Col.3.5.Mortificate igitur membra Vestra super terram,&c.
units.tr: This repentance consists of two parts, which Scripture calls the mortification of the old man and the vivification or resurrection of the new man. Rom. 6.6. Our old man was crucified together with him. Gal. 2.19. Through the law I died to the law, that I might live to God; I have been crucified with Christ, etc. Col. 2.12. Buried with him in baptism, in which also you were raised up through faith in the working of God (which God effected, and through which God is effective). Col. 3.5. Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth, etc.

units.la: IV.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Est autem homo Vetus, seu non renatus, qui ignorantia & dubitatione de Deo, & prauis cupiditatibus laborat, iisque indulget. Nouus vero seu renatus, qui recte agnoscens Deum, & vera iustitia & sanctitate ipsi seruit. Ephes.4.24.
units.tr: The old man is the man who is not reborn, who labors under ignorance and doubt concerning God and depraved desires, and indulges in them. The new man, however, is the reborn man, who rightly acknowledges God and serves him in true righteousness and holiness. Eph. 4.24.

units.la: V
units.tr: V.

units.la: Mortificatio erga Veteris hominis est, ex agnitione nostrae prauitatis, & irae Dei propter eam nobis incumbentis, expauescere, & dolere, quod Deum offenderimus, ac propterea omne peccatum ex animo odisse ac fugere.
units.tr: The mortification of the old man consists in this: from the recognition of our depravity and of the wrath of God that hangs over us because of it, to dread and to grieve that we have offended God, and therefore from the heart to hate and flee every sin.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: Vivificatio autem noui hominis est, ex agnitione miseri-cordiae Dei erga nos in Christo laetari, & acquiscere in Deo, & habere ardens desiderium & studium, Deo secundum omnia praecepta eius obtemperandi. Rom.7.22. Dele-stor[?] lege Dei secundum interiorem hominem.
units.tr: The vivification of the new man, however, consists in this: from the recognition of God's mercy toward us in Christ, to rejoice and rest in God, and to have an ardent desire and zeal to obey God in all his commandments. Rom. 7.22. I delight in the law of God according to the inner man.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: Renouatio haec in infantibus, qui sanctificantur spiritu Dei, tantum est quod ad principium, hoc est, qualitates seu inclinationes nouas attinet: ac proinde regeneratio potius quam poenitentia seu resipiscentia dici potest. In adultis autem est etiam quod ad motus & actiones bonas in mente & voluntate, & corde. Luc.1.15. Replebitur Spiritu S.in-de ab Utero. Mat.19. Talium est regnum coelorum.
units.tr: This renewal in infants, who are sanctified by the Spirit of God, concerns only the beginning, that is, the new qualities or inclinations; and therefore it may be called regeneration rather than repentance or repentance-of-mind. In adults, however, it also concerns the good motions and actions in the mind, the will, and the heart. Luke 1.15. He shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from the womb. Matt. 19. Of such is the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: Sed neque in adultis ante finem huius vitae perficitur, ideoque couersi partim noui partim adhuc veteres homines sunt: donec totam naturae vetustatem seu prauitatem, Vnà cum hac vita deponat. Ro.7.23. Video aliam legem in membris meis. 1.Joh.1.10. Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere, mentimur.
units.tr: But in adults it is not perfected before the end of this life; therefore the converted are partly new and partly still old men, until he lays aside the whole old nature or depravity together with this life. Rom. 7.23. I see another law in my members. 1 John 1.10. If we say that we have no sin, we lie.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Itaque tota piorum vita debet esse, & est, continua quaedam poenitentia seu conuersio, in qua vsque ad finem vitae aduersus diabolum & carnem suam pugnando confirmari & proficere debent. 1.Cor.9.24. Sic currite, vt comprehe-datis. Phil.1.13. Ego meipsum nondum arbitror assecutum vitam. Apoc.22.11. Qui sanctus est, sanctificetur amplius.
units.tr: Therefore the whole life of the pious ought to be, and is, a continual repentance or conversion, in which, until the end of life, they must be strengthened and make progress by fighting against the devil and their own flesh. 1 Cor. 9.24. So run that you may obtain. Phil. 1.13. I do not yet consider myself to have attained life. Rev. 22.11. He who is holy, let him be made holy still more.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Neque dubia est in hoc certamine victoria. In quib.e-nim semel vera conuersio est inchoata,in iis, etiamsi aliquando grauiter labantur ex infirmitate humana,& reliquiis veteris hominis seu peccati,quasin hac vita circumferunt: nunquam tamen ita extinguitur, quin rursus elu-ctentur ex lapsibus,& tandem salui fiant. Matt.7.24. Aedificati super petram non corruunt. Phil.1.6. Qui coepit in vobis bonum opus,perficiet. 1.Ioh.2.19. Si fuissent ex nobis,permansissent utique nobiscum. 1.Ioh.3.9. Qui ex Deo natus est, peccatum non facit: sed femen Dei manet in eo.
units.tr: Nor is victory in this struggle doubtful. For in those in whom true conversion has once begun, even if at times they fall grievously through human weakness and the remnants of the old man or sin which they carry about in this life, yet it is never so extinguished that they do not again struggle up from their falls and at last become saved. Matt. 7.24. Those built upon the rock do not fall. Phil. 1.6. He who began a good work in you will complete it. 1 John 2.19. If they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us. 1 John 3.9. He who is born of God does not commit sin, but the seed of God remains in him.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Interea vero non licet ulli homini neque peccandi licentiam ex hac Dei voluntate arripere,neque poenitentiam suorum peccatorum in futurum tempus reiicere.Ad viuentes enim non in securitate carnali,sed in vera poenitentia & timore Dei,pertinet promissio praesentis & aeternae gratiae Dei:ac non tantum propter incertam vitae prorogationem: sed multo etiam maxime propter iram Dei aduersus securos & contra conscientiam abutentes ipsius misericordia, periculum est omnibus securis, ne iusto iudicio Dei deserti & indurati, sine poenitentia ex hac vita abrepti in aeternum pereant. Matt.24.28. Si dixerit seruus malus: tardat Dominus, &c. Item 9.14. Vigilate: quia nescitis diem & horam, &c. Rom 2.4. An coptam[?] benignitatis eius & tolerantia contemnu?&c.
units.tr: Meanwhile, however, it is not permitted to any man either to seize from this will of God a license to sin, or to postpone repentance of his sins to a future time. For the promise of present and eternal grace of God pertains to those who live not in carnal security but in true repentance and the fear of God; and there is danger for all who are secure, not only because of the uncertain prolongation of life, but much more especially because of the wrath of God against those who are secure and abuse his mercy contrary to conscience, lest, deserted and hardened by the just judgment of God, they be snatched from this life without repentance and perish forever. Matt. 24.28. If that evil servant says: the lord delays, etc. Likewise Matt. 9.14 [?]. Watch, because you know not the day or the hour, etc. Rom. 2.4. Or do you despise the riches of his goodness and forbearance? etc.

units.la: XII.
units.tr: XII.

units.la: Conuersionis causa efficiens principalis est spiritus sanctus: nec sine illius singulari beneficio quisquam convertitur: sed ea in adultis efficit potissimum per cognitionem verbi Dei: & per fidem verbo Dei adhibitam: quae est in omnibus & solis poenitentiam agentibus: ita ut neque fides sine conuersione, neque conuersio sine fide sit. P/.51.12. Cor mundum crea in me Deus. Item 9.15. Docebo iniquos vias tuas. Ier.31.18. Conuerte me & conuertar: Quia postquam conuersus sum me, egi poenitentiam. 1.Cor.4.15. Per euangelium vos genui. Act.15.9. Fide purificantur corda. Heb.4.2. Non ihil profuit eis sermo sine fide. Iac.2.17. Fides sine operibus est mortua. Rom.14.23. Quod non est ex fide, peccatum est.
units.tr: The principal efficient cause of conversion is the Holy Spirit, and no one is converted without his singular benefit; but he effects this in adults chiefly through the knowledge of the word of God, and through faith applied to the word of God; and this faith is in all, and only in those who repent, so that there is neither faith without conversion nor conversion without faith. Ps. 51.12. Create in me a clean heart, O God. Likewise Ps. 9.15. I will teach the wicked your ways. Jer. 31.18. Convert me and I shall be converted, for after I was converted I did penance. 1 Cor. 4.15. Through the gospel I begot you. Acts 15.9. Hearts are purified by faith. Heb. 4.2. The word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith. James 2.17. Faith without works is dead. Rom. 14.23. Whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: XIII.
units.tr: XIII.

units.la: Sicut ergo ad fidem:sic etiam ad poenitentiam in homi-nibus nibus efficiendam & exercendam seu perficiendam, mediis seu causis adiuuantibus externis variis Deus vtitur: Vt bonis exemplis aliorum: poenis impiorum: praemiis piorū:ac praesertim cruce & castigatione. Mat.5.16. Luceat lux vestra,&c. Rom.11.11. Eorū ruinā salus obtigit gentibus,vt eos ad aemulationē prouocaret. Itē Verf.21. Si Deus naturalibus ramis non pepercit,vide ne tibi quoq. non parcat. Psal.98.12. Et dicit homo: Vtique est fructus iusto: Vtiq. est Deus iudicans in terra. Psa.119.71. Bonum mihi, quod humiliasti me,vt discerem iustificationes tuas. 1.Cor.11.37. Cum punimur: a Domino erudimur.
units.tr: Therefore, just as for faith, so also for bringing about, exercising, or completing repentance in men, God uses various external means or aiding causes: such as the good examples of others, the punishments of the wicked, the rewards of the pious, and especially the cross and chastisement. Matt. 5.16. Let your light shine, etc. Rom. 11.11. By their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, so as to provoke them to emulation. Likewise v. 21. If God did not spare the natural branches, see that he also does not spare you. Ps. 98.12 [?]. And man says: Surely there is fruit for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges on earth. Ps. 119.71. It is good for me that you have humbled me, that I might learn your statutes. 1 Cor. 11.32. When we are punished, we are instructed by the Lord.

units.la: XIV.
units.tr: XIV.

units.la: Effectus proprij & perpetui verę poenitentię sunt, confessio indignitatis suae,& miserieordię Dei,&omnia bona opera. Res autem adiaphorae,vt ieiunia,depositio ornatus,&c. adminicula vel signa sunt poenitentię nō perpetua aut simpliciter necessaria,sed quae pro commoditate & affectu piorum possunt suscipi.
